questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A mother asks the barangay health nurse for a herbal remedy for her child's cough. Which DOH-approved herbal medicine should the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Lagundi (Vitex negundo) is the DOH-approved herbal medicine for cough.
explanations: Sambong is for kidney stones and is a diuretic.
Correct: lagundi is used for cough.
Akapulko is for ringworm and other fungal infections.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Lagundi

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A client is using a sambong decoction for kidney stones. Which instruction about fluids should the nurse give?
options: Limit water to 4 glasses a day
Drink the decoction only once a week
Drink 12 or more glasses of water daily
Avoid water for an hour after each dose
questions.rationale: Sambong (Blumea balsamifera) is used for kidney stones. The decoction is divided into 3 portions taken 3 times a day, with 12 or more glasses of water daily.
explanations: The decoction is taken 3 times a day.
Correct: high fluid intake is part of the instructions.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Sambong

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A mother will use akapulko leaf extract on her son's buni (ringworm). How should the nurse tell her to apply it?
options: Twice a day, every day, for 3 weeks
Once a week for a month
Every hour until the itching stops
questions.rationale: Akapulko (Senna alata) extract is applied to the affected skin twice a day, daily for 3 weeks, to fully kill the fungus.
explanations: Too short to kill the fungus.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Akapulko

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How many niyog-niyogan seeds should a 9-year-old with intestinal worms chew as a single dose?
questions.rationale: Niyog-niyogan (Quisqualis indica) seeds are dosed by age: 4 to 5 seeds (4 to 6 years), 6 to 7 seeds (7 to 12 years), and 8 to 10 seeds (13 years and above). The dose may be repeated after 1 week if no worms are expelled.
explanations: This is the dose for 4 to 6 years old.
This is the dose for 13 years and above.
Correct: the dose for 7 to 12 years old.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Niyog-niyogan

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A mother plans to give tsaang-gubat tea to her 5-year-old for stomach pain. What is the nurse's BEST response?
options: 'Give 3 tablespoons of leaves boiled in water.'
'Tsaang-gubat is not recommended for children below 7.'
'Give it with milk to protect the stomach.'
'Use lagundi instead; it also relieves stomach pain.'
questions.rationale: Tsaang-gubat (Carmona retusa) is used for stomach pain but is not recommended for children below 7 years old. If the pain persists, the client should consult a doctor.
explanations: Three tablespoons is the dose for 13 years and older.
Correct: it is not recommended under 7 years.
This is not part of the guidance.
Lagundi is for cough, not stomach pain.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Tsaang-gubat

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which DOH-approved herbal medicine is used to help control uric acid levels in gout?
questions.rationale: Ulasimang bato or pansit-pansitan (Peperomia pellucida) helps control uric acid, used under a doctor's advice. Ampalaya is for diabetes, bawang for high cholesterol, and yerba buena for pain.
explanations: Ampalaya helps control blood sugar in diabetes.
Bawang (garlic) is for high blood cholesterol.
Correct: used to help control uric acid.
Yerba buena is an analgesic for toothache and headache.
questions.sourceLabel: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Ulasimang bato

questions.stem: Using IMCI, which finding in a sick child aged 2 months to 5 years is a GENERAL DANGER SIGN?
questions.rationale: The general danger signs are: unable to drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, history of convulsions, lethargic or unconscious, and convulsing now.
explanations: Correct: vomiting everything is a general danger sign.
Fever is assessed under its own main symptom.
Cough is assessed under cough or difficult breathing.
A cold is not a danger sign.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 2

questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: How should Nurse Joy classify Migo's dehydration?
questions.rationale: Two or more of these signs mean SOME DEHYDRATION: restless or irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly or thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly. Severe dehydration needs signs such as lethargy, inability to drink, or a very slow skin pinch.
explanations: Severe dehydration needs lethargy, poor drinking, or a very slow skin pinch.
He has more than enough signs for dehydration.
Persistent diarrhea is 14 days or more.
Correct: he has two or more 'some dehydration' signs.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 3

questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: Under Plan B, about how much ORS should Migo receive in the clinic over the first 4 hours?
questions.rationale: The approximate ORS amount for the first 4 hours is weight (kg) × 75 mL: 12 × 75 = 900 mL. Give more if the child wants more.
explanations: This is 100 mL/kg, the Plan C amount.
This is 150 mL/kg, far too much.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12

questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: Migo vomits while drinking the ORS. What should Nurse Joy tell his mother?
options: Stop the ORS and give a soft drink instead
Wait 10 minutes, then continue more slowly
Give the ORS faster to replace the loss
questions.rationale: If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes, then continue giving ORS in small, frequent sips from a cup, more slowly.
explanations: Soft drinks are not appropriate rehydration fluids.
Correct: pause, then continue more slowly.
Faster intake makes vomiting more likely.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12

questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: After 4 hours of Plan B, what should Nurse Joy do next?
options: Reassess Migo, reclassify, and choose Plan A, B, or C
Start IV fluids as routine follow-through
Repeat Plan B for 4 more hours automatically
questions.rationale: After 4 hours, the nurse reassesses and reclassifies the child's dehydration, chooses the plan that fits the new classification, and begins feeding in the clinic.
explanations: Correct: reassess and reclassify before choosing a plan.
IV fluids are only for severe dehydration (Plan C).
The next plan depends on the reassessment.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12

questions.stem: An 8-month-old with severe dehydration is started on IV Ringer's lactate under Plan C. How is the 100 mL/kg given?
options: 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg in 2½ hours
70 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 30 mL/kg in 5 hours
30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours
questions.rationale: For infants under 12 months, give 30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours. Children 12 months to 5 years get 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg in 2½ hours.
explanations: This schedule is for children 12 months up to 5 years.
The order of the volumes is reversed.
Correct: the infant schedule under Plan C.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 13

questions.stem: A 4-week-old infant has a respiratory rate of 64 breaths per minute on a repeat count. How does the nurse classify this using IMCI for the sick young infant?
questions.rationale: In a young infant (birth to 2 months), fast breathing of 60 or more per minute is a sign of POSSIBLE SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTION, which needs a first dose of IM antibiotics and urgent referral.
explanations: Local infection involves the umbilicus, skin, or eyes only.
Correct: 60 or more breaths per minute in a young infant.
This classification applies to older children without signs.
Sixty or more is fast breathing at this age.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 22

questions.stem: Under IMCI, a young infant's diarrhea is classified as SEVERE PERSISTENT DIARRHEA when it has lasted:
questions.rationale: Diarrhea lasting 14 days or more is persistent; in a young infant it is classified as severe persistent diarrhea and referred, after treating any dehydration.
questions.sourceLabel: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 23

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The community health nurse plans tuberculosis case-finding. Which group should be targeted as HIGH RISK?
options: Residents of a home for the aged
questions.rationale: Older adults, especially those in long-term care, are at high risk for TB. So are children 5 and under and people who are malnourished, immunosuppressed, or economically disadvantaged.
explanations: Correct: older adults in long-term care are high risk.
Healthy working adults are not a high-risk group.
Healthy adolescents are not a high-risk group.
Age and marital status alone are not risk factors.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 901)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A mother asks how long her child with chickenpox must be kept away from other children. What should the nurse say?
options: For 24 hours after the rash appears
Until all the vesicles have dried and crusted
Isolation is not needed once antipyretics are given
questions.rationale: Varicella is communicable from 1 to 2 days before the rash until the vesicles have crusted, about 6 days after the first crop. It spreads through vesicle fluid and respiratory secretions.
explanations: The child stays contagious after the fever resolves.
The child stays contagious for several more days.
Correct: contagious until all lesions crust.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 601)

questions.stem: During a women's health class in the barangay, the nurse discusses cervical cancer. Which is a risk factor?
options: Early age at first sexual intercourse
questions.rationale: Risk factors include HPV infection, multiple sexual partners (or a partner with multiple partners), smoking, and early first intercourse.
explanations: A single partner is not a risk factor.
Condoms reduce the risk of HPV transmission.
Correct: early first intercourse is a risk factor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 840)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: At a community health screening, which client should the nurse prioritize for teaching on preventing respiratory disease?
options: A nonsmoker who works in an air-conditioned office
A smoker who works in a paint factory
A nonsmoker who jogs every morning
A former smoker who quit 20 years ago
questions.rationale: Smoking greatly raises respiratory risk, and exposure to chemicals, airborne toxins, dust, or fumes adds to it. The client with both risk factors is the priority.
explanations: This client has no major risk factor.
This client has no identified risk factor.
This client's risk has decreased with years of not smoking.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 862)

questions.stem: The nurse helps a repeatedly abused woman recover from the physical and emotional effects of the abuse and prevent future abuse. Which level of prevention is this?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention is needed once a woman has been repeatedly abused. It focuses on overcoming the effects of the abuse and preventing it from happening again.
explanations: Primary prevention acts before any abuse occurs.
Secondary prevention is early detection and prompt treatment.
Primordial prevention addresses root social conditions before risk factors appear.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 886)

questions.stem: The duty not to inflict harm, and to prevent and remove harm, is the ethical principle of:
questions.rationale: Nonmaleficence is the duty not to inflict harm and to prevent and remove harm. Beneficence is doing good, veracity is truth-telling, and autonomy is self-determination.
explanations: Beneficence is the duty to do good.
Correct: the duty to do no harm.
Autonomy is the client's right to choose.
questions.sourceLabel: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key

questions.stem: A competent adult client refuses a procedure after a full explanation, but the physician tells the staff to proceed anyway. Which ethical principle is being violated?
questions.rationale: Autonomy is the right to make a choice free from external constraints. Overriding a competent client's informed refusal violates it.
explanations: Correct: the client's informed choice is overridden.
Justice is the fair distribution of care.
questions.sourceLabel: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key

questions.stem: Which is an INTERDEPENDENT nursing action?
options: Assessing the apical pulse on admission
Teaching a client about discharge care
Giving mouth care to an unconscious client
Giving an IV fluid bolus as prescribed
questions.rationale: Interdependent actions carry out prescribed treatments and need a health care provider's order, such as IV fluids, pain medication, or wound irrigation. Assessment, teaching, and basic care are independent nursing actions.
explanations: Assessment is an independent nursing action.
Teaching is an independent nursing action.
Hygiene care is an independent nursing action.
Correct: IV fluids require a prescription.
questions.sourceLabel: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key

questions.stem: A physician tells a client, in front of other patients, that the nurse 'does not know anything.' The statement is false and harms the nurse's reputation. This is an example of:
questions.rationale: Defamation is a falsehood that injures a person's good name: spoken defamation is slander, and written defamation is libel. Assault is a threat of harm, and battery is unconsented touching.
explanations: Assault is putting someone in fear of harm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 604)

questions.stem: Under RA 9173 (Philippine Nursing Act of 2002), which activity is within the scope of nursing practice?
options: Providing health education to families and communities
Dispensing prescription medicines without an order
questions.rationale: Sec. 28 lists the nurse's duties: nursing care through the nursing process, linkages with community resources, health education to individuals, families and communities, teaching nursing students, and training and research.
explanations: Prescribing is outside the nurse's legal scope.
Correct: health education is listed in Sec. 28.
Dispensing prescription drugs without an order is not a nursing function.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 28 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 9173, how many members, including the Chairperson, compose the Professional Regulatory Board of Nursing?
questions.rationale: The Board is composed of a Chairperson and six members, seven in all.
explanations: Six is the number of members besides the Chairperson.
Correct: a Chairperson plus six members.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 3 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: A nurse wants to be appointed to the Board of Nursing. Under RA 9173, how many years of continuous nursing practice must the nurse have before appointment?
questions.rationale: A Board member must have at least 10 years of continuous practice before appointment, the last 5 of them in the Philippines.
explanations: Five years refers to the most recent practice that must be in the Philippines.
Correct: at least 10 years of continuous practice.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 4 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 9173, what is the longest period for which a nurse's certificate of registration may be suspended?
questions.rationale: The Board may revoke or suspend a license, and a suspension cannot exceed four years.
explanations: Correct: suspension shall not exceed 4 years.
Six years is the maximum prison term under the penal provision, not the suspension period.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 23 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Which penalty does RA 9173 set for a violation of the Act?
options: A fine of P10,000 to P20,000 with no imprisonment
Imprisonment of 6 months to 1 year with no fine
A fine of P50,000 to P100,000, 1 to 6 years in prison, or both
Permanent revocation of the license with no fine
questions.rationale: Violators face a fine of not less than P50,000 nor more than P100,000, imprisonment of 1 to 6 years, or both, at the discretion of the court.
explanations: The prison term is 1 to 6 years.
Correct: this is the penal provision of RA 9173.
Revocation is an administrative sanction, not the penal provision.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 35 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 9173, a chief nurse or director of nursing service must have at least how many years of experience in a supervisory or managerial position in nursing?
questions.rationale: Nursing service administrators need at least 2 years of experience in general nursing service administration; a chief nurse or director of nursing service needs at least 5 years in a supervisory or managerial position.
explanations: Two years is for nursing service administrators in general.
Correct: 5 years in a supervisory or managerial position.
Ten years is the Board member requirement.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9173, Sec. 29 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the Universal Health Care Act (RA 11223), who is covered by the National Health Insurance Program?
options: Only employed Filipinos who pay premiums
Only indigent families listed by the DSWD
Only senior citizens and persons with disability
questions.rationale: RA 11223 automatically includes every Filipino citizen in the NHIP.
explanations: Coverage is not limited to paying members.
Coverage is not limited to indigents.
Correct: inclusion is automatic for every citizen.
These are only some of the groups covered.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11223, Sec. 5 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under RA 11223, members of the National Health Insurance Program are classified into which two types?
questions.rationale: Membership has two types. Direct contributors can pay premiums or are gainfully employed; indirect contributors are all others.
explanations: Correct: the two membership types under UHC.
Dependents are covered, but this is not the membership classification.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11223, Sec. 8 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under UHC, a client without an emergency wants to go straight to a tertiary hospital specialist. Who should coordinate the client's access to that higher level of care?
questions.rationale: The primary care provider is the navigator, coordinator, and initial and continuing point of contact. Except in emergency or serious cases, access to higher levels of care is coordinated by the primary care provider.
explanations: The barangay captain does not manage clinical referrals.
PhilHealth pays for care but does not coordinate referrals.
Correct: the primary care provider acts as gatekeeper and navigator.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11223, Sec. 6(c) (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under RA 11223, which is an example of a POPULATION-BASED health service?
options: Consultation for a child with fever
Dengue vector control in a barangay
Prenatal checkup of a pregnant woman
Teleconsultation for a client with diabetes
questions.rationale: Population-based services such as health promotion, disease surveillance, and vector control target whole communities. Individual-based services are given to one person at a facility or remotely.
explanations: Correct: vector control serves the whole population.
Remote care for one person is individual-based.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11223, Sec. 4(q) (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: RA 11223 describes primary care as initial-contact care that is also:
options: Limited to the treatment of illness
questions.rationale: Primary care is initial-contact, accessible, continuous, comprehensive, and coordinated care that is available when needed.
explanations: Primary care is for every Filipino.
Primary care also covers promotion and prevention.
Correct: these are the features named in the law.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11223, Sec. 4(r) (lawphil.net)

questions.situation: Nurse Lea is in charge of the immunization program at a rural health unit. A mother brings her healthy baby, born 6 weeks ago, for the first visit since birth. The baby received BCG and the hepatitis B birth dose.
questions.stem: Which vaccines should the baby receive today under the routine schedule?
options: Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV first doses
BCG booster and hepatitis B second dose
questions.rationale: Pentavalent (DPT-HepB-Hib), OPV, and PCV are each given at 6, 10, and 14 weeks. IPV is given at 14 weeks, and the measles-containing vaccine at 9 months and 1 year.
explanations: MMR is given at 9 months and 1 year; IPV at 14 weeks.
BCG has no booster in the routine schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: PIDS, Philippine EPI vaccination schedule (pidswebs.pids.gov.ph, 2020)

questions.situation: Nurse Lea is in charge of the immunization program at a rural health unit. A mother brings her healthy baby, born 6 weeks ago, for the first visit since birth. The baby received BCG and the hepatitis B birth dose.
questions.stem: The mother asks which diseases the pentavalent vaccine protects against. Nurse Lea answers:
options: Measles, mumps, rubella, varicella, and polio
Tuberculosis, polio, measles, hepatitis B, and pneumonia
Diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, and Hib
Rotavirus, pneumococcus, measles, polio, and tetanus
questions.rationale: The pentavalent vaccine combines DPT, hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type B.
explanations: These are covered by MMR, varicella, and polio vaccines.
Tuberculosis is covered by BCG, measles by MCV.
These are covered by separate vaccines.
questions.sourceLabel: PIDS, Philippine EPI vaccination schedule (pidswebs.pids.gov.ph, 2020)

questions.situation: Nurse Lea is in charge of the immunization program at a rural health unit. A mother brings her healthy baby, born 6 weeks ago, for the first visit since birth. The baby received BCG and the hepatitis B birth dose.
questions.stem: At which ages will the baby receive the two doses of measles-containing vaccine?
questions.rationale: The measles-containing vaccine (MCV/MMR) is given in two doses, at 9 months and at 1 year.
explanations: These are pentavalent, OPV, and PCV ages.
Six months is too early in the routine schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: PIDS, Philippine EPI vaccination schedule (pidswebs.pids.gov.ph, 2020)

questions.stem: Under RA 10152 (Mandatory Infants and Children Health Immunization Act), up to what age do children receive basic immunization free in government facilities?
questions.rationale: RA 10152 provides free basic immunization for infants and children up to five years of age, and requires the hepatitis B birth dose within 24 hours of birth.
explanations: Correct: up to five years of age.
School-age vaccines are separate from this provision.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10152 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 10152, when must the hepatitis B birth dose be given to infants born in a health facility?
questions.rationale: The law requires the hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours after birth for all infants born in hospitals, infirmaries, health centers, or lying-in centers.
explanations: Six weeks is when the pentavalent series starts.
Waiting for a later visit misses the birth dose.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10152 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: A nurse studies whether home-visit breastfeeding counseling increases exclusive breastfeeding rates in a barangay. What is the DEPENDENT variable?
options: The barangay where the study is done
The number of home visits made
questions.rationale: The dependent variable is the outcome being measured (the exclusive breastfeeding rate). The independent variable is the intervention (counseling).
explanations: The setting is not a variable here.
questions.sourceLabel: Basic research design principles (no excerpt in your materials yet — please verify)

questions.stem: Halfway through a community survey, a respondent says she no longer wants to take part. What should the nurse researcher do?
options: Respect her decision to withdraw without penalty
Remind her that she already signed the consent form
Offer extra incentives so she will continue
questions.rationale: Under respect for persons, research participants may withdraw at any time without penalty. Signed consent does not bind them to continue.
explanations: Correct: the right to withdraw is part of informed consent.
Consent can be withdrawn at any time.
questions.sourceLabel: Research ethics: respect for persons and informed consent (no excerpt in your materials yet — please verify)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client starting TB treatment under DOTS is prescribed rifampin. Which side effect should the nurse tell the client to expect?
questions.rationale: Rifampin turns urine, sweat, and tears orange; soft contact lenses can be permanently stained. Rifampin is hepatotoxic, so yellow sclera would be a warning sign, not an expected effect.
explanations: Jaundice suggests hepatotoxicity and must be reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q353 (PDF p. 521)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on rifampin for TB has new laboratory results. Which finding suggests an adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Rifampin can cause hepatotoxicity, hepatitis, and jaundice. Rising liver enzymes and bilirubin signal an adverse effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1130 (PDF p. 1415)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Tonio, 58, a farmer, has sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. He is enrolled in the TB-DOTS program at the rural health unit, and his regimen includes streptomycin.
questions.stem: Which test result would indicate a TOXIC effect of streptomycin?
questions.rationale: Streptomycin is nephrotoxic, so BUN and creatinine are monitored. Vision testing is for ethambutol, and liver enzymes for isoniazid.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1425 (PDF p. 1734)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Tonio, 58, a farmer, has sputum-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. He is enrolled in the TB-DOTS program at the rural health unit, and his regimen includes streptomycin.
questions.stem: Mang Tonio's regimen also includes ethambutol. Which test should the nurse expect to be done during therapy?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, so vision testing is done. Isoniazid requires liver monitoring, and streptomycin requires kidney monitoring.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1425 (PDF p. 1734)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the MOST common complication of mumps?
options: Orchitis with a red, swollen testicle
questions.rationale: Aseptic meningitis is the most common complication of mumps (nuchal rigidity, lethargy, vomiting). Mumps can cause one-sided deafness, but this is uncommon.
explanations: It occurs, but is not the most common.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q115 (PDF p. 265)

questions.stem: A preschooler has an immunocompromising condition. Which type of vaccine should generally be AVOIDED?
questions.rationale: An immunocompromised child generally should not receive live or attenuated vaccines (oral polio, MMR, varicella). Inactivated vaccines such as DTaP and inactivated influenza are recommended.
explanations: Correct: live vaccines can cause disease in these children.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q775 (PDF p. 1005)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child with rubeola (measles) has Koplik's spots. What does the nurse expect to see?
options: Red spots on the soft palate
questions.rationale: Koplik's spots appear about 2 days before the measles rash. They are small blue-white spots with a red base on the buccal mucosa, last about 3 days, and then slough off. Measles spreads by airborne particles.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1089 (PDF p. 1372)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: An infant is admitted with pertussis. Which problem is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Copious, thick secretions in an infant's small airways make air exchange the priority. Fluid volume deficit, not overload, is more likely because of secretions and vomiting.
explanations: Correct: airway clearance is the priority.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1158 (PDF p. 1445)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Parents worry that their son with mumps will develop orchitis. Which sign should the nurse teach them to watch for?
questions.rationale: About a week after parotitis, orchitis begins abruptly with testicular pain and tenderness, fever, chills, headache, and vomiting. It is usually one-sided, and sterility is rare.
explanations: Correct: abrupt fever and testicular pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1347 (PDF p. 1650)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A sputum culture grows Mycobacterium tuberculosis. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Needs a skin test to confirm
questions.rationale: Culturing M. tuberculosis from sputum or tissue confirms active TB. A skin test helps but does not confirm active disease.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q354 (PDF p. 522)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which findings suggest pulmonary tuberculosis?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary TB causes cough, anorexia and weight loss, fatigue, low-grade fever, chills, night sweats, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and chest pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1322 (PDF p. 1624)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with newly diagnosed TB will be in respiratory isolation for 2 weeks. Which action BEST prevents psychosocial distress?
options: Tell staff not to touch him
Limit nurse visits to save masks
questions.rationale: Visitors and social contacts give positive stimulation, and touch helps the client feel socially acceptable. A client in respiratory isolation is in a private room.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q963 (PDF p. 1210)

questions.stem: Which nursing action is an example of client advocacy?
options: Giving information for an informed decision
questions.rationale: As an advocate, the nurse protects the client's human and legal rights and gives the information the client needs to make an informed decision. Obtaining consent is the provider's responsibility.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q401 (PDF p. 571)

questions.stem: A family friend calls the home health nurse offering to help a newborn's family. What is the BEST action?
options: Ask the friend to call the family
Invite the friend to the teaching
questions.rationale: The nurse gives no information about a client's care to anyone not directly involved in that care. Inviting the friend to teaching would violate the family's privacy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q420 (PDF p. 597)

questions.stem: A nurse gives a client's medical information to someone wrongly assumed to be family. Which rights were violated?
questions.rationale: Discussing a client's condition without permission violates the client's rights to privacy and confidentiality and puts the nurse in legal jeopardy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q449 (PDF p. 629)

questions.stem: Which situation is an example of assault?
questions.rationale: Assault puts a person in fear of a harmful act. Battery is touching without permission, false imprisonment is unlawful restraint, and libel is a written falsehood.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q452 (PDF p. 632)

questions.stem: After colon resection, a client with an NG tube is served solid food and asks for the doctor to be called. The nurse insists he eat, and he later needs more surgery. Which describes this?
questions.rationale: Negligence requires a duty, a breach of duty, injury caused by the breach, and damages. All four elements are present.
explanations: Correct: all four elements are present.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q454 (PDF p. 634)

questions.stem: A client asks how to become an organ donor. What should the nurse tell him?
questions.rationale: Anyone 18 years or older may donate by written consent without the family's permission or presence. This matches the Philippine Organ Donation Act (RA 7170).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q457 (PDF p. 638)

questions.stem: Who is responsible for explaining a procedure and obtaining informed consent?
questions.rationale: Informed consent rests on full disclosure of risks, benefits, alternatives, and the consequences of refusal. The provider doing the procedure gives that information; the nurse may witness the signature.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q464 (PDF p. 646)

questions.stem: After the doctor explains a colonoscopy, the nurse finds the client cannot write. What is BEST?
options: Have two witnesses as he signs an X
questions.rationale: A client who cannot write may sign with an X in front of two witnesses. The nurse witnesses the signature, not whether the client was informed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q506 (PDF p. 701)

questions.stem: An adult with severe dementia is scheduled for gallbladder surgery. What should the nurse do FIRST about consent?
questions.rationale: A mentally impaired client cannot give consent. Verifying the legal guardian avoids improperly signed documents and directs the surgeon to the right person.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q549 (PDF p. 750)

questions.stem: A home care client says she does not want CPR. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: A client may refuse resuscitation. A written DNR order from the provider is needed so that her wishes are followed.
explanations: Correct: a DNR order is needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q481 (PDF p. 670)

questions.stem: A client wants to leave the hospital before the doctor discharges him. What should the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: Informing the supervisor helps the nurse manage the situation safely and completely, including having the client sign a release (discharge against advice) form.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q581 (PDF p. 786)

questions.stem: A post-op client gets no pain relief from opioids only when one coworker is assigned. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Before acting on a suspicion, the nurse needs more data, which the record provides. Policies and drug laws then guide reporting.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q446 (PDF p. 626)

questions.stem: A client dies of gunshot wounds. Which action properly preserves evidence?
options: Bag the hands in paper bags
questions.rationale: Paper bags on the hands and feet protect trace evidence. Items go in paper bags, clothing is cut around holes, and evidence is not released to the family.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q497 (PDF p. 690)

questions.stem: A client with stab wounds arrives in the ER. Which action BREAKS the rules for handling evidence?
options: Giving his wallet to the family
questions.rationale: Potential evidence is never released to the family. A chain of custody log tracks it, access is limited, and clothing is removed carefully.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q597 (PDF p. 805)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: During a disaster, which victim needs IMMEDIATE (red tag) care?
questions.rationale: Arterial bleeding from the neck is life-threatening and is tagged red. Green (minimal) victims can wait.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q598 (PDF p. 806)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Beds are needed for disaster victims. Which client should STAY in the hospital?
questions.rationale: Ongoing ventricular dysrhythmias need continued treatment because they can be fatal. Stable conditions can be managed at home with referrals.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q599 (PDF p. 807)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A client with suspected smallpox arrives in the ER. What should the plan include FIRST?
questions.rationale: With a communicable disease such as smallpox, the client is isolated immediately and staff put on protective equipment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q491 (PDF p. 682)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which action is correct for a client exposed to anthrax?
questions.rationale: Decontamination includes having the client remove contaminated clothing, handling it minimally, and storing it in a labeled paper bag.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q540 (PDF p. 738)

questions.stem: A dying client asks, 'Will you be the executor of my will?' What is the BEST reply?
questions.rationale: The question does not show why the client is asking. Seeking clarification acknowledges the request and keeps communication open.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q832 (PDF p. 1068)

questions.stem: Which factor places an older adult MOST at risk for abuse?
questions.rationale: Elder abuse may come from frustrated adult children caring for dependent parents. Growing demands can cause resentment. Abuse is not tied to income level.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q831 (PDF p. 1067)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: According to Ruth B. Freeman, what is the focus of community health nursing services?
questions.rationale: Freeman described CHN as a service rendered by a professional nurse with communities, groups, families, and individuals in homes, health centers, clinics, schools, and workplaces for health promotion, illness prevention, and care of the sick at home and rehabilitation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Dr. C.E. Winslow defined public health as the science and art of which three aims?
questions.rationale: Winslow defined public health as the science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting health and efficiency through organized community effort.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla motivates barangay residents and starts community development activities. Which PHN role is she performing?
questions.rationale: As community organizer, the PHN motivates and enhances community participation and initiates and participates in community development activities.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla trains the rural health midwives in her catchment area. Which role is this?
questions.rationale: The health educator/counselor/trainer role includes health teaching, counseling, and training and educating rural health midwives.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 80)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla updates the RHU database and analyzes the data for interpretation. Which role is she performing?
questions.rationale: The reporter/recorder/statistician records nursing interventions, updates the database, and makes statistical analysis of data for interpretation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 80)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160), what happened to health services from the provincial level down to the barangay?
options: They were devolved to the LGUs
questions.rationale: RA 7160 devolved all structures, personnel, and budgetary allocations from the provincial health level down to the barangays to the local government units.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Local Health System (PDF p. 81)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: What is the ideal population size of an inter-local health zone (health district)?
questions.rationale: An ideal health district has a population of 100,000 to 500,000 for optimum efficiency and effectiveness.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Local Health System (PDF p. 81)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Primary health care was adopted in the Philippines through which issuance?
questions.rationale: PHC was adopted through Letter of Instruction 949, signed by President Marcos on October 19, 1979.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 81)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is one of the four cornerstones (pillars) of primary health care?
questions.rationale: The four cornerstones are active community participation, intra- and inter-sectoral linkages, use of appropriate technology, and support mechanisms made available.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is an element of primary health care in the ELEMENTS mnemonic?
questions.rationale: ELEMENTS: Education for health, Locally endemic disease control, EPI, Maternal and child health and family planning, Essential drugs, Nutrition, Treatment, and Sanitation of the environment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A trained barangay health worker is which level of primary health care worker?
questions.rationale: Village/barangay health workers include trained community health workers, health auxiliary volunteers, and traditional birth attendants or healers. PHNs, midwives, and rural health physicians are intermediate level.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A rural health unit and a barangay health station belong to which level of care?
questions.rationale: Primary care facilities include barangay health stations, rural health units, community hospitals, health centers, and puericulture centers.
explanations: Not in the PH referral levels.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Health Care (PDF p. 82)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A district hospital that does minor surgery and simple laboratory tests and receives RHU referrals is at which level?
questions.rationale: Secondary care serves as the referral center for primary facilities, can do minor surgery and simple laboratory exams, and includes district and provincial hospitals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Health Care (PDF p. 82)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Sputum AFB testing of a coughing client is which level of prevention?
questions.rationale: Secondary prevention is early detection and prompt treatment, such as diagnostic tests (AFB) and breast self-examination.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 83)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Teaching crutch walking to a client after a leg amputation is which level of prevention?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention is rehabilitation to prevent further disability and restore optimum function, such as crutch walking and physical therapy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 83)

questions.stem: A family's breadwinner is about to retire with no other income source. In family assessment, this is a:
questions.rationale: A foreseeable crisis is an anticipated period of unusual demand on the family in terms of resources and adjustment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)

questions.stem: A family keeps an open drum of stagnant water where mosquitoes breed. This is a:
questions.rationale: A health threat is a condition that promotes disease or injury and keeps people from reaching their health potential.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)

questions.stem: A child in the family has a developmental lag. This is a:
questions.rationale: A health deficit is a gap between actual and achievable health, such as an existing disease, disability, or developmental lag.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In the community health nursing process, when are the evaluation parameters developed?
questions.rationale: Developing evaluation parameters is done in the planning stage, as part of the operational plan.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which management function establishes standards, measures performance, and corrects deviations?
questions.rationale: Controlling measures and corrects activities and sets standards so objectives are met: establish standards, measure performance, and correct deviations.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Management Functions of the CHN (PDF p. 84)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: During an RHU clinic day, which case does the nurse refer to the physician during triage?
options: A child with simple diarrhea under IMCI
A TB client on DOTS refill
questions.rationale: In triaging, program-based cases are managed according to protocols, and all non-program-based cases are referred to the physician.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Clinic Visit (PDF p. 84)

questions.stem: Before measuring BP at the health center, how long should the client have avoided smoking and caffeine?
questions.rationale: The client should rest for 5 minutes and should not have smoked or taken caffeine within 30 minutes before BP measurement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Pressure Measurement (PDF p. 85)

questions.stem: On a client's first BP visit, the readings differ between arms. Which arm is used for later readings?
options: The arm with the higher reading
The arm with the lower reading
questions.rationale: On the first visit, BP is taken in both arms; subsequent readings use the arm with the higher reading.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Pressure Measurement (PDF p. 85)

questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important in deciding how often to make home visits?
questions.rationale: The needs of the family are the most important factor in home visit frequency, followed by the family's acceptance.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Home Visit (PDF p. 86)

questions.stem: During a home visit, what does the nurse do right after stating the purpose of the visit?
questions.rationale: Steps: greet and introduce self, state the purpose, observe the client and determine needs, place the bag and do bag technique, give care and teaching, record, and set a return visit.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Home Visit (PDF p. 86)

questions.stem: What is the MAIN principle of bag technique?
questions.rationale: Bag technique should minimize, if not prevent, the spread of infection. It may vary with agency policy or the home situation as long as this principle is observed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bag Technique (PDF p. 86)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which type of epidemiology tests hypotheses to find the causes of a disease?
questions.rationale: Analytical epidemiology analyzes causes or determinants of disease through hypothesis testing. Descriptive covers distribution and frequency.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Epidemiology (PDF p. 87)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which rate is considered a good index of the general health condition of a community?
questions.rationale: The infant mortality rate is a good index of the general health condition of a community.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which measure is the index of the killing power of a disease?
questions.rationale: The case fatality ratio indexes the killing power of a disease. It is affected by incomplete reporting and poor morbidity data.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A barangay counts ALL existing dengue cases, new and old, on one day. Which measure is this?
questions.rationale: Prevalence measures the proportion of the population with a disease at a particular time, counting new and old cases. Incidence counts new cases only.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which rate measures pregnancy wastage?
questions.rationale: The fetal death rate measures pregnancy wastage: death of the product of conception before complete expulsion, regardless of pregnancy duration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which record is the fundamental building block of the Field Health Services Information System (FHSIS)?
questions.rationale: The Family Treatment Record is the fundamental building block of FHSIS. The Target Client List is the second building block. Reporting forms are the only routine way data move between facilities.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, FHSIS (PDF p. 88)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In FHSIS, what is the ONLY mechanism by which data are routinely sent from one facility to another?
questions.rationale: Reporting forms, prepared monthly or quarterly, are the only mechanism through which FHSIS data are routinely transmitted between facilities.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, FHSIS (PDF p. 88)

questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Aling Rosa gets her third tetanus toxoid dose today. How long does TT3 protect her?
questions.rationale: TT2 (4 weeks after TT1) gives 80% protection for 3 years. TT3 (6 months after TT2) gives 95% protection for 5 years. TT4 gives 10 years and TT5 lifetime.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)

questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Which tetanus toxoid dose gives Aling Rosa LIFETIME protection?
questions.rationale: TT5, given 1 year after TT4, gives 99% protection for life.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)

questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Which iron/folic acid supplement does the nurse give Aling Rosa?
questions.rationale: Pregnant women receive a 60 mg iron/400 mcg folic acid tablet daily, continued up to 2 months postpartum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Micronutrient Supplementation (PDF p. 88)

questions.stem: During FP counseling, what birth spacing interval does the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Family planning counseling in the maternal health program promotes proper spacing of births at 3- to 5-year intervals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)

questions.stem: A man had a vasectomy last week. What should the nurse tell him about its effectiveness?
questions.rationale: Vasectomy is very effective 3 months after the procedure, so another method is used until then. He keeps sexual ability and ejaculation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 89)

questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother wants to use the Lactational Amenorrhea Method. For how long is LAM effective at most?
questions.rationale: LAM is a temporary postpartum method effective for a maximum of 6 months. It depends on full or nearly full breastfeeding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)

questions.stem: Which FP method encourages male participation and protects against sexually transmitted infections?
questions.rationale: The male condom has no hormonal effect, protects against microorganisms during intercourse, and encourages male participation in family planning.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)

questions.stem: Which family planning method uses color-coded cycle beads?
questions.rationale: In the Standard Days Method, couples use color-coded cycle beads to mark fertile and infertile days. It suits women whose cycles are usually 26 to 32 days long.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: Which method identifies fertile days by combining cervical mucus, basal body temperature, and other signs of ovulation?
questions.rationale: The sympto-thermal method combines observations of cervical mucus, basal body temperature, and other ovulation signs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)

questions.stem: A woman says family planning will make her sterile. How should the nurse view this belief?
questions.rationale: Common FP misconceptions include that FP causes abortion, makes couples sterile, or causes loss of sexual desire. The nurse corrects these through counseling.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: Which is a key IYCF message the nurse teaches a new mother?
questions.rationale: Key IYCF messages: initiate breastfeeding within 1 hour after birth, breastfeed exclusively for 6 months, add complementary food at 6 months, and continue to 2 years and beyond.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Infant & Young Child Feeding (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: A mother gives her 3-month-old breast milk plus a little water on hot days. Is this exclusive breastfeeding?
options: No, only breast milk is given
Yes, if under 30 mL a day
questions.rationale: Exclusive breastfeeding means giving only breast milk, with no other liquids or solids, not even water.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Infant & Young Child Feeding (PDF p. 91)

questions.stem: Which law promotes rooming-in and protects and supports breastfeeding in health facilities?
questions.rationale: The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act of 1992 (RA 7600) promotes rooming-in and protects and supports breastfeeding. Mother and baby stay together 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws that Protect IYCF (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: The Food Fortification Law (RA 8976) requires mandatory fortification of which staple foods?
questions.rationale: RA 8976 mandates fortification of rice, flour, edible oil, and sugar, with voluntary fortification of processed foods.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws that Protect IYCF (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: A child missed his second pentavalent dose by 2 months. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The vaccine schedule is not restarted, and no extra dose is given to a child who missed a dose. The nurse continues with the next dose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: Which statement about giving several EPI vaccines on one day is correct?
options: Give them all at one site
questions.rationale: It is safe and effective to give all EPI vaccines on the same day at different sites.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: A child due for vaccines has a mild cough and low-grade fever. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Malnutrition, low-grade fever, mild respiratory infection, cough, diarrhea, and vomiting are false contraindications.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, False Contraindications (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: Which is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to the next DPT-containing dose?
questions.rationale: DPT2 or DPT3 is not given to a child who had convulsions or shock within 3 days of the previous dose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Absolute Contraindications (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: For which child is BCG contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Live vaccines such as BCG must not be given to people immunosuppressed by malignant disease. The others are false contraindications.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Absolute Contraindications (PDF p. 92)

questions.stem: How should the nurse reconstitute freeze-dried vaccines?
options: Only the diluent supplied with it
questions.rationale: EPI strictly follows the principle of never reconstituting freeze-dried vaccines with anything other than the diluent supplied.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)

questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: How does Nurse Ana give BCG?
questions.rationale: BCG for infants is 0.05 mL intradermal in the right deltoid region.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)

questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: Where does Nurse Ana inject the hepatitis B vaccine for an infant?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis B and DPT-containing vaccines are 0.5 mL IM in the upper outer thigh (vastus lateralis).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)

questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: By which route does Nurse Ana give the measles-containing vaccine?
questions.rationale: Measles vaccine is 0.5 mL subcutaneous in the outer upper arm.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)

questions.situation: Nurse Ana is vaccinating infants at the RHU on immunization day.
questions.stem: What is the minimum interval between pentavalent doses?
questions.rationale: Pentavalent starts at 6 weeks, with 3 doses at 4-week intervals. Shorter intervals may lessen the antibody response.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Routine Schedule (PDF p. 93)

questions.stem: Which three micronutrient deficiencies does the DOH nutrition program target?
questions.rationale: The common nutritional deficiencies addressed are vitamin A, iron, and iodine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nutrition Program (PDF p. 93)

questions.stem: Applying pit and fissure sealant to a child's molars is which type of oral intervention?
questions.rationale: Preventive oral interventions include oral exams, oral hygiene, pit and fissure sealant, and fluoride use. Fillings and extractions are curative.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Health Program (PDF p. 93)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Barangay San Isidro has scattered houses. The PHN is reviewing the water supply.
questions.stem: The barangay uses a protected well with no distribution system. What level of water facility is this?
questions.rationale: Level I (point source) is a protected well or developed spring without a distribution system, suited to rural areas with scattered houses.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Barangay San Isidro has scattered houses. The PHN is reviewing the water supply.
questions.stem: The farthest Level I user should be no more than how far from the source?
questions.rationale: A Level I source serves 15 to 25 households, and the farthest user must be no more than 250 meters away.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A water system with a reservoir, piped network, and communal faucets for 4 to 6 households each is which level?
questions.rationale: Level II (communal faucet system) has a piped network and communal faucets, with one faucet per 4 to 6 households and no more than 25 meters from the farthest house.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Water Supply Facilities (PDF p. 94)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which water source is UNAPPROVED?
questions.rationale: Unapproved water facilities include open dug wells, unimproved springs, and wells that need priming.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Unapproved Water Facility (PDF p. 94)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: When must a water supply source be disinfected?
questions.rationale: Disinfection is required for newly constructed water supply facilities and for facilities that have been repaired or improved.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Water Quality Surveillance (PDF p. 95)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A household uses a pour-flush toilet. What level of toilet facility is this?
questions.rationale: Level I includes non-water carriage facilities (pit latrines, reed odorless earth closets) and those needing small amounts of water (pour-flush toilets, aqua privies).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Approved Toilet Facilities (PDF p. 95)

questions.stem: Which law is the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines?
questions.rationale: PD 856 is the Sanitation Code. RA 9003 is Ecological Solid Waste Management, RA 9275 is the Clean Water Act, and RA 8749 is the Clean Air Act.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Health and Sanitation Laws (PDF p. 94)

questions.stem: A barangay starts waste segregation and a materials recovery facility. Which law mandates this?
questions.rationale: RA 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, governs solid waste management, including segregation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Health and Sanitation Laws (PDF p. 94)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under DOH AO 1-2006, which stool test is required for food handlers?
questions.rationale: DOH AO 1-2006 requires laboratories to use the formalin ether concentration technique (FECT) instead of direct fecal smear for food handlers' stool analysis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Food Sanitation Program (PDF p. 95)

questions.stem: In teaching food safety, to what temperature should all parts of cooked or reheated food reach?
questions.rationale: Food should be cooked thoroughly so all parts reach 70°C, and reheated to at least 70°C.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 96)

questions.stem: How long can cooked food stay at room temperature?
questions.rationale: Under right storage, cooked food should be left at room temperature for no more than 2 hours. 'When in doubt, throw it out!'
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 96)

questions.stem: Which teaching belongs to 'right source' in the four rights of food safety?
options: Keep raw and cooked food apart
questions.rationale: Right source includes buying fresh food, checking expiry dates, avoiding dented or bulging cans, and boiling water for at least 2 minutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Four Rights in Food Safety (PDF p. 95)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How long is a Sentrong Sigla certification valid?
questions.rationale: Sentrong Sigla certification is valid for 2 years. Facilities that keep their status get renewal stickers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sentrong Sigla Certification (PDF p. 96)

questions.stem: In what kind of pot should herbal decoctions be boiled?
questions.rationale: Medicinal plants are boiled in enamelware or clay pots, not aluminum, and the pots are cleaned well before and after.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine Guidelines (PDF p. 97)

questions.stem: A mother has given an herbal remedy 3 times with no improvement. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: If there is no improvement after two or three doses, the client should consult a physician. Only one plant is used at a time.
explanations: Use one plant at a time.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine Guidelines (PDF p. 97)

questions.stem: How many tablespoons of FRESH lagundi leaves are boiled for a 9-year-old with cough?
questions.rationale: For lagundi, fresh leaves are 6 tbsp for adults, 3 tbsp for ages 7–12, and 1½ tbsp for ages 2–6. Boil in 2 cups of water for 15 minutes and divide into 3 doses.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lagundi (PDF p. 97)

questions.stem: Which DOH-approved herbal medicine is used to clean wounds and as a mouthwash for swollen gums?
questions.rationale: Bayabas (Psidium guajava) leaves are boiled and used to clean wounds twice a day, or lukewarm as a mouthwash for mouth infections and swollen gums.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Bayabas (PDF p. 98)

questions.stem: How should a client take bawang (garlic) to help lower cholesterol?
questions.rationale: For cholesterol, two cloves of garlic are eaten with meals three times a day. It may be sauteed, boiled, infused, or mixed with vinegar.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Bawang (PDF p. 98–99)

questions.stem: A client with mild diabetes asks how to take ampalaya leaf decoction. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Two cups of chopped leaves are boiled in two glasses of water for 15 minutes on low fire; the client drinks ½ glass three times a day before eating.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Ampalaya (PDF p. 99)

questions.stem: Yerba buena is used for body pain. How is the decoction prepared?
questions.rationale: Chopped leaves are boiled in two glasses of water for 15 minutes without covering the pot, then cooled and strained. Fresh leaves may also be squeezed onto the painful part.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Yerba Buena (PDF p. 97)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which law strengthened Philippine disaster control capability and set up community disaster preparedness?
questions.rationale: PD 1566 (1978) strengthened the Philippine disaster control capability and established the National Program on Community Disaster Preparedness.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response (PDF p. 99)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In disaster management, what is the FIRST priority?
questions.rationale: The first priority is protecting people at risk. The second is protecting the critical resources and systems communities depend on.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response (PDF p. 99)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A serious disruption causing losses that exceed the community's ability to cope with its own resources is a:
questions.rationale: A disaster is a serious disruption of a society causing widespread human, material, or environmental losses that exceed its ability to cope using its own resources. A hazard is a phenomenon with potential to cause damage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Disaster and Health Emergency Management (PDF p. 99)

questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: What is the minimum weight to donate 450 mL of blood?
questions.rationale: Donors must weigh more than 45 kg for 250 mL and 50 kg (110 lb) for 450 mL of donated blood.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)

questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: A 17-year-old student wants to donate. What does Nurse Ben need?
questions.rationale: Donors may be 16 to 65 years old; those aged 16 and 17 need parental consent.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)

questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: Which volunteer should Nurse Ben DEFER from donating?
questions.rationale: Contraindications include malaria, diabetes, cancer, heart disease, epilepsy, STIs, kidney or liver disease, and prohibited drug use. Hemoglobin must be at least 12.5 g/dL.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)

questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: Which after-donation instruction should Nurse Ben give?
options: Carry heavy items with that arm
questions.rationale: After donating: keep the dressing on 3 to 12 hours, avoid heavy lifting with that arm, no smoking for 2 hours, no alcohol for 12 hours, and eat regular meals with more fluids.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Whose commitment is required to supervise the operations of a Botika ng Barangay?
questions.rationale: A Botika ng Barangay requires a commitment from a licensed pharmacist to supervise its operations, plus at least 2 trained BHWs as aides.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Botika ng Barangay (PDF p. 101)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How much of a Botika ng Barangay's initial capital must come from the community?
questions.rationale: At least one-third of the initial capital must be community-sourced, and at least one-third from the LGU or other government officials.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Botika ng Barangay (PDF p. 101)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: In which COPAR phase do the students select the site and do a preliminary social investigation?
questions.rationale: The pre-entry phase is done before going to the community: site selection criteria, site selection, preliminary social investigation, and networking with LGUs and NGOs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Process (PDF p. 102)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: Which criterion should guide site selection for COPAR?
questions.rationale: Criteria: a socio-economically depressed, underserved community, inaccessible health services, poor health status, relative peace and order, and acceptance of the program.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Process (PDF p. 102)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: The students live with the residents and share their hardships to build trust. Which COPAR activity is this?
questions.rationale: Integration is establishing rapport by immersing in community life and sharing the people's hopes and hardships to build mutual trust and cooperation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, 10 Critical Activities in COPAR (PDF p. 103)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: The students go house to house, motivating residents one-on-one to act on an issue. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Ground working, also called agitation, means going around and motivating people one-on-one to do something about community issues.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, 10 Critical Activities in COPAR (PDF p. 103–104)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: Which criterion is used to choose core group members?
options: Respected and from the poor sector
questions.rationale: Core group members should be respected, from the poor sector, responsible and committed to social change, willing to learn, and able to communicate.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Entry Phase (PDF p. 102)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How are leaders identified in COPAR?
questions.rationale: COPAR is group-oriented, not leader-oriented. Leaders emerge and are tested through action rather than being appointed by an external entity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Principles (PDF p. 101)

questions.stem: How does participatory action research differ from traditional research?
questions.rationale: In PAR, community members define the research problem as experts of their own reality and carry out the research, and the purpose is empowerment. In traditional research, external experts define and control it.
