questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Participatory Action Research (PDF p. 104)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A food vendor harbors Salmonella typhi and can spread it but has no symptoms. What is she?
questions.rationale: A carrier harbors the organism and can transmit it to a susceptible host without showing signs of the disease. A contact is someone in close association with an infected person.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The nurse disinfects a patient's sputum cup right after he coughs into it while he is still infectious. This is:
questions.rationale: Concurrent disinfection is done immediately after the infected person discharges infectious material, while the patient is still the source of infection. Terminal disinfection is done after discharge.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Exposed persons have their movement limited for the longest incubation period of the disease. This is:
questions.rationale: Quarantine limits the movement of exposed persons or animals for the longest incubation period. Isolation separates infected persons during the period of communicability.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Schistosomiasis is always present at a fairly constant level in Leyte and Samar. This pattern is:
questions.rationale: Endemic means continuous occurrence of the usual number of cases in a locality, such as schistosomiasis in Leyte and Samar, filariasis in Sorsogon, and malaria in Palawan.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Patterns of Occurrence (PDF p. 143)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A town has a few isolated, unrelated rabies cases this year. Which pattern is this?
questions.rationale: Sporadic occurrence is the intermittent appearance of a few isolated, unrelated cases in a locality, such as rabies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Patterns of Occurrence (PDF p. 143)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which link in the chain of infection is the EASIEST to break?
questions.rationale: The mode of transmission is the easiest link to break, for example through handwashing and barriers. Contact is the most common mode.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chain of Infection (PDF p. 143)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Droplet transmission is generally limited to what distance?
questions.rationale: Droplet spread from coughing, sneezing, or talking is limited to about 3 feet. Airborne particles stay suspended and travel farther.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mode of Transmission (PDF p. 144)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A newborn has antibodies received through the placenta. Which type of immunity is this?
questions.rationale: Natural passive immunity is acquired through placental transfer. Natural active comes from recovering from disease.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Immunity (PDF p. 144)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A dog-bite victim receives rabies immunoglobulin. Which type of immunity does this give?
questions.rationale: Artificial passive immunity comes from antitoxin, antiserum, convalescent serum, or immunoglobulins. Vaccines and toxoids give artificial active immunity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Immunity (PDF p. 144)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is true of attenuated (live, weakened) vaccines compared with inactivated ones?
questions.rationale: Attenuated vaccines usually need a single dose and give long-lasting immunity. Inactivated vaccines need multiple doses and boosters.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Type of Antigen (PDF p. 144)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on chemotherapy is placed in a room to protect HIM from infection. Which isolation is this?
questions.rationale: Reverse or neutropenic isolation separates an immunocompromised client to prevent him from getting an infection from the environment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Isolation (PDF p. 145)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which statement about transmission-based precautions is correct?
options: They are the second tier of precautions
questions.rationale: Transmission-based precautions are the second tier, added to standard precautions for highly contagious patients. The three types are contact, airborne, and droplet.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Isolation (PDF p. 145)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A pregnant woman with no history of chickenpox was exposed. Within how many days should VZIG be given?
questions.rationale: Varicella-zoster immune globulin (VZIG) should be given within 10 days of exposure.
explanations: Earlier is fine but not the limit.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chicken Pox (PDF p. 146)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which statement about chickenpox scabs is correct?
questions.rationale: The main source is respiratory secretions; lesions are of little consequence, and scabs are not infective.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chicken Pox (PDF p. 145)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: During the pre-eruptive stage, the nurse sees a red line on Bea's lower conjunctiva. What is this?
questions.rationale: Stimson's line, a red line on the lower conjunctiva, appears in the pre-eruptive stage of measles along with fever, catarrhal symptoms, and photophobia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Measles (PDF p. 146)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Bea is sensitive to light. Which nursing care is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Measles causes photophobia, so eye care includes protecting the child from bright light.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Measles (PDF p. 147)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Which precautions should the nurse use for Bea?
questions.rationale: Measles is airborne, so standard and airborne precautions are used, ideally in a negative-pressure room.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Measles (PDF p. 147)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Which complication of measles should the nurse watch for MOST in Bea?
questions.rationale: Complications of measles include bronchopneumonia, otitis media, pneumonia, nephritis, and encephalitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Measles (PDF p. 147)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: For which person is measles vaccine contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Measles vaccine is not given to pregnant women or to people with active TB, leukemia, lymphoma, or depressed immunity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Measles (PDF p. 147)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Which EARLY sign of leprosy does Mang Isko show?
questions.rationale: Early signs include skin color change, loss of sensation, less sweating and hair over the lesion, and thickened, painful nerves. Madarosis, clawing, and a sunken nose bridge are late signs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leprosy (PDF p. 148)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Mang Isko is classified as multibacillary. Which MDT regimen will he receive?
questions.rationale: Multibacillary (infectious) leprosy is treated with rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone for 12 months. Paucibacillary leprosy uses rifampicin and dapsone for 6–9 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leprosy (PDF p. 148)

questions.situation: Mang Isko, 45, a farmer, has a pale skin patch on his forearm that he cannot feel.
questions.stem: Mang Isko has an anesthetic foot. What should the nurse teach him?
options: Test bath water before stepping in
Soak feet in hot water daily
Put full weight on the foot
questions.rationale: With an anesthetized limb, the client avoids injury by not overloading it, testing water before entering to prevent scalds, and wearing proper footwear.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leprosy (PDF p. 148)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with leprosy cannot close his eyelids completely. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Lagophthalmos, the inability to close the eyelids, is a late sign. The client uses a tear substitute and protects the eyes to prevent corneal ulceration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leprosy (PDF p. 148)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Which condition does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Scabies causes intense itching that worsens at night, with burrows in the finger webs, wrists, and elbows.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Scabies (PDF p. 149)

questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Who should be treated for scabies in this case?
questions.rationale: All household members, including close contacts, should be treated to prevent reinfestation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Scabies (PDF p. 149)

questions.situation: A school child has intense itching that is worse at night and lesions between his fingers.
questions.stem: Permethrin cream is prescribed. How long should it stay on the skin?
questions.rationale: Permethrin cream is left on the skin for 8 to 12 hours. Fingernails are cut short and contaminated linens are boiled or dry-cleaned.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Scabies (PDF p. 149)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child has a mild rash, low fever, and postauricular lymph nodes. The nurse sees pinkish spots on the soft palate. What are these?
questions.rationale: Forchheimer spots, a pinkish rash on the soft palate, appear in rubella (German measles), along with postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is rubella especially dangerous for pregnant women?
options: It is teratogenic to the fetus
questions.rationale: Rubella is teratogenic. Congenital rubella can cause cataracts, deafness, heart defects such as PDA, microcephaly, and intellectual disability.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which classic finding of congenital rubella syndrome affects the skin?
questions.rationale: Classic congenital rubella syndrome includes growth retardation, low birth weight, and thrombocytopenic purpura known as 'blueberry muffin' skin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, German Measles (PDF p. 150)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where are head lice and nits MOST commonly found?
questions.rationale: Head lice and nits are most commonly found behind the ears and on the hair of the neck and occiput.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pediculosis (PDF p. 151)

questions.stem: How should a family prevent head lice reinfestation?
questions.rationale: Clothes and bed linens are washed in hot water, ironed, or dry-cleaned to prevent reinfestation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pediculosis (PDF p. 152)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Dodong, 4, unvaccinated, has a sore throat, low fever, and a swollen neck.
questions.stem: The nurse sees a grayish membrane on Dodong's tonsils. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Diphtheria forms a grayish pseudomembrane and may cause bull neck, a swelling of the soft tissues of the neck.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diphtheria (PDF p. 154)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Dodong, 4, unvaccinated, has a sore throat, low fever, and a swollen neck.
questions.stem: Which type of diphtheria is MOST fatal in children aged 2 to 5?
questions.rationale: Laryngeal diphtheria is most common in ages 2 to 5 and the most fatal because of airway anatomy. The voice becomes hoarse and is finally lost.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diphtheria (PDF p. 154)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child's Schick test shows induration at the injection site. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: A positive Schick test (inflammation or induration) means the person lacks antibodies to diphtheria and is susceptible.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diphtheria (PDF p. 154)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which nursing care is appropriate for a child with diphtheria?
questions.rationale: Care includes absolute bed rest for at least two weeks (to protect the heart from myocarditis), a soft diet with small frequent feedings, and an ice collar to the neck.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diphtheria (PDF p. 154)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the MOST dangerous complication of pertussis?
questions.rationale: Bronchopneumonia is the most dangerous complication of pertussis. Others include convulsions, otitis media, hernia, and malnutrition.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pertussis (PDF p. 155)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which equipment must be at the bedside of an infant with pertussis?
questions.rationale: Suction equipment should be at the bedside to clear thick secretions during paroxysms.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pertussis (PDF p. 155)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with influenza is recovering at home. Which finding should prompt referral for possible pneumonia?
questions.rationale: The nurse watches for developing pneumonia: crackles, another temperature rise, or coughing with purulent or bloody sputum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Influenza (PDF p. 157)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A farmer who butchered a sick carabao has a painless sore with a black scab and purplish vesicles. Which disease is suspected?
questions.rationale: Cutaneous anthrax, over 90% of cases, starts as a pimple that ulcerates and forms a black scab surrounded by purplish vesicles. It comes from contact with tissues of animals dying of the disease.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anthrax (PDF p. 157)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hand hygiene is needed after caring for a client with anthrax?
questions.rationale: Alcohol-based hand sanitizers do not kill anthrax spores, so hands are washed with soap and water.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anthrax (PDF p. 158)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which form of anthrax is the MOST fatal?
questions.rationale: Inhalational anthrax begins abruptly like the flu, then causes dyspnea, cyanosis, shock, and usually death in 2–6 days.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anthrax (PDF p. 157)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Before starting antibiotics for suspected anthrax, what should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Culture specimens are obtained before antibiotic therapy starts.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anthrax (PDF p. 158)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which sputum characteristic is classic for pneumococcal pneumonia?
questions.rationale: Pneumococcal pneumonia causes productive cough with rusty sputum, high fever, chest pain, and dullness on percussion over the affected lobe.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pneumonia (PDF p. 159)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Which test CONFIRMS pulmonary TB in Mang Rudy?
questions.rationale: Sputum analysis for AFB is confirmatory. Tuberculin tests show exposure, and a chest X-ray supports the diagnosis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis (PDF p. 160)

questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Mang Rudy will take isoniazid. Which supplement should the nurse encourage?
questions.rationale: Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy, so vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) intake is increased. Alcohol is avoided because of hepatotoxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Isoniazid (PDF p. 161)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Rudy, 52, a tricycle driver, has had a cough for 3 weeks with afternoon fevers and night sweats.
questions.stem: Mang Rudy develops joint pain on pyrazinamide. Which lab result should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia and can be hepatotoxic, so uric acid and liver function are monitored.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Pyrazinamide (PDF p. 161)

questions.stem: A woman starting rifampicin for TB uses oral contraceptives. What should the nurse teach?
options: The pill may be less effective
Stop TB drugs on pill days
questions.rationale: Rifampin can make oral contraceptives less effective, so a backup method is advised.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis (PDF p. 161)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of DOTS in TB control?
questions.rationale: Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course is a strategy to prevent non-compliance by having a treatment partner watch the client take each dose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis (PDF p. 161)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which TB drug should be AVOIDED in children under 6 because of optic neuritis?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis and is not recommended for children below 6, who cannot reliably report visual changes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuberculosis – Ethambutol (PDF p. 161)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Bird flu is found in a poultry farm. Which control measure is used?
options: Cull birds and disinfect the farm
questions.rationale: Control includes rapid destruction and proper disposal of birds, quarantine and rigorous disinfection of farms, and restrictions on moving live poultry.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bird Flu (PDF p. 162)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the initial sign of SARS?
questions.rationale: The prodromal phase of SARS begins with fever above 38°C, then chills, malaise, myalgia, and headache. A dry cough follows.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, SARS (PDF p. 162)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: A client passes stools that look like rice water and has wrinkled fingertips. Which disease is suspected?
questions.rationale: Cholera causes profuse rice-watery stool and 'washer-woman's hands' from severe dehydration, which can lead to hypovolemic shock.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholera (PDF p. 163)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: What is the incubation period of cholera?
questions.rationale: Cholera has a short incubation period of 6 to 48 hours. Cases are infectious during diarrhea and up to 7 days after.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholera (PDF p. 163)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: After a flood, a barangay reports many cases of profuse diarrhea.
questions.stem: Which isolation is used for a hospitalized client with cholera?
questions.rationale: Cholera spreads through feces and vomitus, so enteric isolation with handwashing and accurate I&O is used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholera (PDF p. 163)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Typhoid fever is characterized by ulceration of which tissue?
questions.rationale: Typhoid fever is a systemic Salmonella typhi infection with continued fever, anorexia, and involvement of lymphoid tissue, especially ulceration of Peyer's patches.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 15, has had a stepwise-rising fever for a week, headache, and rose spots on his abdomen.
questions.stem: Which disease does the nurse suspect in Jun-jun?
questions.rationale: Typhoid fever begins with headache, nausea and vomiting, a ladder-like (stepwise) fever, and rose spots on the abdomen.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 15, has had a stepwise-rising fever for a week, headache, and rose spots on his abdomen.
questions.stem: Jun-jun suddenly has right lower abdominal pain and a rigid abdomen. What complication is MOST likely?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage and perforation are the most dreaded complications. The nurse watches for sudden right lower abdominal pain and abdominal rigidity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Typhoid Fever (PDF p. 164–165)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug should be AVOIDED in a client with bacillary dysentery (shigellosis)?
questions.rationale: Antidiarrheal drugs are contraindicated in shigellosis because they delay fecal excretion of the organism and can prolong fever.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bacillary Dysentery (PDF p. 166)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client from Sorsogon has had blood-streaked sputum for months that does not respond to TB drugs. He often eats raw crabs. What is suspected?
questions.rationale: Paragonimiasis (lung fluke) comes from eating raw or undercooked crabs or crayfish. It causes a long cough and blood-streaked sputum that look like TB but do not respond to TB drugs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Paragonimiasis (PDF p. 166)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which lab test is MOST useful for an early presumptive diagnosis of mumps?
questions.rationale: An elevated serum amylase is the most useful test for an early presumptive diagnosis of mumps.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mumps (PDF p. 167)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: When is mumps MOST communicable?
questions.rationale: The 48 hours just before parotid swelling begins is the period of highest communicability. Cases are infectious up to a week before until 9 days after.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mumps (PDF p. 167)

questions.stem: A child with mumps has painful parotid glands. Which food should the mother AVOID giving?
questions.rationale: Soft, bland, semi-solid food is easier to manage. Acidic foods such as fruit juices increase discomfort.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mumps (PDF p. 168)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After eating home-canned food, a client has double vision, droopy eyelids, and trouble swallowing. Which paralysis pattern is expected?
questions.rationale: Botulism is a neurotoxin illness of descending flaccid paralysis with blurred vision, ptosis, dry mouth, and difficulty swallowing and breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Botulism (PDF p. 168)

questions.stem: How should a family make home-canned food safer to eat?
questions.rationale: Clients who eat home-canned food are taught to boil it for 10 minutes before eating to make sure it is safe.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Botulism (PDF p. 169)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Before giving botulinum antitoxin, what must the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Before botulinum antitoxin, the nurse checks the client's allergies and does a skin test first.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Botulism (PDF p. 169)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which stage of Entamoeba histolytica is the infective stage?
questions.rationale: The cyst is the infective stage. It resists environmental conditions and survives a few days outside the body. Trophozoites invade tissue.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amoebiasis (PDF p. 169)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: How should the nurse handle a stool specimen for amoebiasis?
options: Send it to the lab immediately
questions.rationale: No oil preparation for 48 hours before collection; collect a large portion with blood and mucus, label it, and send it to the laboratory immediately.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amoebiasis (PDF p. 170)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is the intermediate host of Schistosoma japonicum in the Philippines?
questions.rationale: S. japonicum, endemic in the Philippines, uses the snail Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi as its intermediary host. Cercariae penetrate the skin in infested water.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Schistosomiasis (PDF p. 171)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A farmer from Leyte has an itchy rash a day after wading in a rice field. What is this early sign called?
questions.rationale: The first stage of schistosomiasis is a pruritic rash ('swimmer's itch') about 24 hours after cercariae penetrate the skin. Katayama fever comes in the second stage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Schistosomiasis (PDF p. 171)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test CONFIRMS schistosomiasis?
questions.rationale: The circumoval precipitation test (COPT) is confirmatory for schistosomiasis. Fecalysis, biopsy, and ELISA are also used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Schistosomiasis (PDF p. 171)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which community measure reduces the snail population to control schistosomiasis?
questions.rationale: Snail density is reduced with molluscicides and stream cleaning, which exposes snails to sunlight. Footbridges over infested streams also help.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Schistosomiasis Prevention (PDF p. 172)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which lesion is typical of PRIMARY syphilis?
questions.rationale: Primary syphilis presents a painless chancre at the site of entry with swollen glands. It disappears in 3 to 6 weeks even without treatment. Rash on the palms and soles is secondary.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Syphilis (PDF p. 172)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the drug of choice for syphilis?
questions.rationale: Syphilis is treated with IM penicillin G benzathine; tetracycline or doxycycline are alternatives. The client completes treatment even after symptoms subside.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Syphilis (PDF p. 173)

questions.stem: A woman is prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis. What must the nurse teach?
questions.rationale: Alcohol is avoided while taking metronidazole and for 48 hours after, as the combination causes severe nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, and flushing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Trichomoniasis (PDF p. 174)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which vaginal discharge is typical of trichomoniasis?
questions.rationale: Trichomoniasis causes a white or greenish-yellow odorous discharge with itching, soreness, and painful urination.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Trichomoniasis (PDF p. 173)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A mother with untreated chlamydia delivers vaginally. Which newborn problem should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: Complications of chlamydia include infant eye infections and pneumonia, prematurity, and stillbirth. The newborn is assessed for chlamydial infection.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chlamydia (PDF p. 174)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is gonorrhea often missed in women?
questions.rationale: About 80% of women with gonorrhea are asymptomatic, so case finding and partner treatment matter. Untreated infection can cause sterility and pelvic infection.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gonorrhea (PDF p. 175)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: An infant has white curd-like patches on the tongue that bleed when scraped. What is this?
questions.rationale: Oral candidiasis (thrush) shows cream or bluish-white curd-like patches that reveal bloody engorgement when scraped. Milk curds wipe off easily.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Candidiasis (PDF p. 176)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: In the classic HIV testing sequence, which test is confirmatory?
questions.rationale: ELISA is the presumptive (screening) test and Western blot is the confirmatory test.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, HIV/AIDS (PDF p. 176)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which vector transmits dengue?
questions.rationale: Dengue is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Aedes aegypti mosquito.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 177)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which medicine should Kaye's mother AVOID for her fever?
questions.rationale: Aspirin is not given in dengue because it increases bleeding risk. An analgesic such as paracetamol and fluid replacement are used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 178)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Kaye develops a nosebleed. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: For nosebleed in dengue, an ice bag is applied on the forehead and the bridge of the nose. The nurse also watches for shock.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 178)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Kaye, 8, has had a high fever for 3 days. The barangay has many dengue cases.
questions.stem: Which lab finding suggests plasma leakage in Kaye?
questions.rationale: Hemoconcentration, an increase of at least 20% in hematocrit, together with a falling platelet count, indicates plasma leakage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dengue Fever (PDF p. 177)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which mosquito transmits malaria?
questions.rationale: Malaria is transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, and also by blood transfusion and across the placenta.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Malaria (PDF p. 178)

questions.stem: A worker will go to a malaria-endemic area in Palawan. When should chloroquine prophylaxis start?
questions.rationale: Chloroquine is taken weekly, starting 1 to 2 weeks before entering the endemic area.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Malaria Chemoprophylaxis (PDF p. 179)

questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent malaria?
questions.rationale: Prevention includes insecticide-treated nets, house spraying, stream seeding and clearing, covering arms and legs in the evening, and avoiding outdoor night activity from 9 PM to 3 AM.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Malaria Prevention (PDF p. 179)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: When is blood collected for the nocturnal blood examination (NBE) for filariasis?
questions.rationale: Microfilariae circulate at night, so NBE blood is taken at the client's residence from 8 PM. The ICT antigen test can be done in the daytime.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Filariasis (PDF p. 179)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug is used to treat filariasis?
questions.rationale: Filariasis is treated with diethylcarbamazine citrate (Hetrazan), given as a yearly dose in mass treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Filariasis (PDF p. 180)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After wading through floodwater with leg wounds, a man has fever, myalgia, and calf pain. What is suspected?
questions.rationale: Leptospirosis is a zoonosis spread when animal urine (mostly rats) contaminates water and enters through open skin. It is also called flood fever.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leptospirosis (PDF p. 180)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug is given as prophylaxis to people exposed to floodwater against leptospirosis?
questions.rationale: Doxycycline is used as prophylaxis for leptospirosis. Penicillin and tetracycline are used for treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leptospirosis (PDF p. 181)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the usual incubation period of rabies?
questions.rationale: Rabies usually incubates 3 to 8 weeks but ranges from 9 days to 7 years, depending on the virus dose, wound severity, and closeness to the brain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies (PDF p. 181)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Tonton, 10, was bitten on the leg by a stray dog an hour ago.
questions.stem: What is the FIRST thing to do for Tonton's bite wound?
options: Wash with soap and running water
questions.rationale: First aid for animal bites is to wash the wound with soap and water. An antiseptic such as povidone-iodine may then be applied.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies (PDF p. 182)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Tonton, 10, was bitten on the leg by a stray dog an hour ago.
questions.stem: The owner of the biting dog is found. For how long should the dog be confined and observed?
questions.rationale: Any dog that has bitten a person is confined and observed for 10 to 14 days.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies Prevention (PDF p. 182)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why should there be no running water in the room of a client with rabies?
questions.rationale: Rabies (hydrophobia) causes painful throat spasms at the sight or sound of water. The client is not bathed and there is no running water in the room.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies (PDF p. 182)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test gives the MOST definitive diagnosis of rabies?
questions.rationale: The fluorescent rabies antibody test is the most definitive diagnosis. Negri bodies in the dog's brain also indicate rabies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rabies (PDF p. 182)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: Which disease is suspected in Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: Tetanus causes trismus (lockjaw), painful spasms of the chewing muscles, and risus sardonicus. Spores enter through dirty wounds.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetanus (PDF p. 182)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: What room environment is best for Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: The room is kept quiet and dim, and visitors are told not to stimulate the client, because stimuli can trigger spasms.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetanus (PDF p. 183)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: Which product neutralizes circulating tetanus toxin in Mang Pido?
questions.rationale: Treatment includes tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG), an antibiotic such as metronidazole, sedatives, and airway support.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetanus (PDF p. 183)

questions.situation: Mang Pido, 60, stepped on a rusty nail a week ago. He now has trouble opening his mouth and a fixed grin.
questions.stem: How often should Mang Pido get a tetanus toxoid booster after recovery?
questions.rationale: Active immunization is maintained with a tetanus toxoid booster every 10 years.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetanus (PDF p. 183)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child with polio lets his head fall back when his shoulders are lifted. What is this sign?
questions.rationale: In polio, Hoyne sign is the head falling back when the shoulders are elevated. The tripod sign is sitting with arms extended behind for support.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Poliomyelitis (PDF p. 184)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which pain medication should be AVOIDED in a client with polio?
questions.rationale: Analgesics are given, but not morphine, which depresses respiration in a client at risk of respiratory failure. Moist heat helps muscle pain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Poliomyelitis (PDF p. 184)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which specimen is used for viral culture in suspected polio?
questions.rationale: Poliovirus spreads through oropharyngeal secretions and feces. Viral culture uses a stool sample.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Poliomyelitis (PDF p. 184)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which Mantoux test result is POSITIVE in a client with no special risk factors?
questions.rationale: Positivity is based on induration, not redness. Under Philippine TB guidelines, induration of 10 mm or more is positive for most clients (5 mm or more if HIV-positive or immunosuppressed). A wheal only shows correct injection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q67 (PDF p. 212)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where should the nurse inject a tuberculin skin test?
options: Inner forearm near a burn scar
questions.rationale: Intradermal tests are usually given on the inner forearm in an area that is not heavily pigmented and is free of lesions, scars, and hair.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q222 (PDF p. 377)

questions.stem: Which reason for a restraint shows a need for MORE staff education?
options: Immobilize a limb for a procedure
Keep the client in bed at night
questions.rationale: Restraints limit movement when a limb must be immobilized. They are not used to keep a client in bed at night or as punishment or convenience.
explanations: Correct answer: not a valid reason.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q405 (PDF p. 579)

questions.stem: Which measure prevents intestinal parasite spread in a preschool?
options: Keep sick children at home only
questions.rationale: Intestinal parasites spread by the fecal-oral route; standard precautions with handwashing prevent transmission.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q411 (PDF p. 587)

questions.stem: Which finding is a NEGATIVE outcome of wrist restraints?
questions.rationale: Negative outcomes include impaired skin, poor circulation, agitation, and incontinence.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q465 (PDF p. 647)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a restraint was applied UNSAFELY?
questions.rationale: A restraint is never applied snugly because it impairs circulation. Slip knots and a reachable call bell are correct.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q512 (PDF p. 707)

questions.stem: Which is a safety guideline for physical restraints?
questions.rationale: Restraints need a prescription, are secured to the bed frame with a quick-release knot, and are checked often.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q570 (PDF p. 775)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Besides handwashing, what should the nurse do before entering the room of a client with active TB?
questions.rationale: TB is airborne, so the nurse wears a particulate (HEPA/N95) respirator; hands are washed before and after care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q533 (PDF p. 731)

questions.stem: During a home visit, which finding needs counseling about injury risk?
questions.rationale: Stairs increase fall risk. A tucked-away cord and good lighting are not hazards.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q580 (PDF p. 785)

questions.stem: Which parent plan to prevent childhood obesity needs correction?
questions.rationale: Food is not used as a reward. Consistent meal and snack times and no eating while watching TV are encouraged.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q606 (PDF p. 817)

questions.stem: A client with recurrent trichomoniasis asks about treatment during menses. What is correct?
questions.rationale: Treatment continues through menses because the vagina is more alkaline then and flare-ups are likely.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q614 (PDF p. 827)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is a source of histoplasmosis the client should avoid?
questions.rationale: Histoplasmosis comes from soil contaminated with bird (especially chicken and pigeon) and bat droppings. Grape arbors do not harbor it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q619 (PDF p. 834)

questions.stem: How can women prevent pelvic inflammatory disease?
questions.rationale: Primary prevention of PID is avoiding unprotected intercourse. Douching increases risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q625 (PDF p. 842)

questions.stem: Which statement by a teenager treated for an STI needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: All sexual contacts must be notified and treated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q715 (PDF p. 937)

questions.stem: Which student comment about tobacco needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: All forms of tobacco, including chewing tobacco, are health hazards.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q732 (PDF p. 957)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: After a month of TB drugs, which finding shows isolation is no longer needed?
questions.rationale: A negative sputum culture shows treatment is effective and the client is no longer infectious.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q736 (PDF p. 961)

questions.stem: What is the BEST advice to a coach for preventing dehydration in hot weather?
questions.rationale: Hot weather speeds fluid and electrolyte loss, so fluid breaks every 30 minutes are scheduled.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q742 (PDF p. 969)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A tuberculin skin test is given Monday. When should it be read?
questions.rationale: The test is read in 48 to 72 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q748 (PDF p. 977)

questions.stem: An occupational health nurse learns of a large layoff in 2 weeks. What should she do FIRST to prepare?
questions.rationale: Identifying available services gives immediate avenues for help when the layoff occurs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q917 (PDF p. 1160)

questions.stem: A recently widowed man's tidy home is now in chaos and he smells of alcohol. What should the home nurse say?
options: 'It seems you're having a hard time.'
questions.rationale: Reflection that he seems to be having a difficult time helps him explore and express his feelings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q928 (PDF p. 1172)

questions.stem: What is the MOST immediate concern when planning care for a group of homeless people?
questions.rationale: The first community health concern is always basic physiological needs: food, shelter, and clothing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1023 (PDF p. 1296)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: An older couple's home was flooded. What does the community health nurse plan FIRST?
questions.rationale: Initial disaster concerns are basic physiological needs: food, shelter, and clothing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1027 (PDF p. 1300)

questions.stem: Which factor contributes to health disparities?
questions.rationale: Disparities arise from age, ethnicity, education, provider attitudes, geography, income, occupation, and health literacy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1060 (PDF p. 1340)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client treated for TB understands discharge teaching?
questions.rationale: Close contacts must be tested and treated if positive. Drugs are completed; dishes need no special handling.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1063 (PDF p. 1343)

questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of home fire safety?
options: 'Smoke alarms and quick exit save lives.'
questions.rationale: Early smoke detection and immediate evacuation reduce deaths, since alarms sound before flames appear.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1068 (PDF p. 1350)

questions.stem: An older client asks the home nurse to buy her groceries. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The nurse completes the assessment and then finds immediate and long-term solutions with the client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1289 (PDF p. 1590)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where should a client with active TB be placed?
options: A ward with other TB clients
questions.rationale: Active TB requires a private room with good ventilation (6 to 12 air exchanges per hour).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1307 (PDF p. 1609)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A healthy client (HIV-negative) has 8 mm induration on a Mantoux test. How is this read?
questions.rationale: For people without immunosuppression, 8 mm is below the positive cutoff (10 mm under PH guidelines). 5 mm or more is positive only for HIV or immunosuppressed clients.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1325 (PDF p. 1627)

questions.stem: Which home instruction is correct for an adult with influenza?
questions.rationale: Influenza spreads by droplets; handwashing and staying home prevent spread. Fluids and rest help.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1424 (PDF p. 1733)

questions.stem: Which method effectively prevents STIs?
questions.rationale: Effective measures are abstinence, correct condom use, and avoiding multiple partners.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1335 (PDF p. 1637)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What should the nurse do before giving a Mantoux test?
questions.rationale: The nurse explains the test and asks about prior positive reactions; it is not given if there was one. It is given intradermally with a tuberculin syringe.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1550 (PDF p. 1863)

questions.stem: Which problem should adoptive parents be counseled about?
options: No need to tell the child
questions.rationale: Adoptive parents may set unrealistically high standards and may lack the child's biological history.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q615 (PDF p. 828)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A man treated for syphilis before has a new penile lesion. Which feature suggests reinfection?
questions.rationale: The syphilis chancre is painless and indurated. Warts are cauliflower-like; herpes causes painful vesicles.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1378 (PDF p. 1681)

questions.stem: Florence Nightingale's theory focuses on using which factor to help the patient recover?
questions.rationale: Nightingale's Environmental Theory uses the patient's environment (fresh air, pure water, drainage, cleanliness, light) to assist recovery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Which theorist described 14 fundamental needs the nurse helps the client meet toward independence?
questions.rationale: Henderson's Nature of Nursing Model has the nurse assist people to gain independence in meeting 14 fundamental needs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Which theorist identified 21 nursing problems?
questions.rationale: Abdellah's Patient-Centered Approaches to Nursing identifies 21 nursing problems.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 1)

questions.stem: Imogene King's theory views nursing as an interaction leading to what?
questions.rationale: King's Goal Attainment Theory sees nursing as nurse-patient interaction leading to goal attainment, with personal, interpersonal, and social systems.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Which theory says caring is universal but its expression varies by culture?
questions.rationale: Leininger's Cultural Care Diversity and Universality theory holds that caring is universal but culturally expressed, with three intervention modes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Myra Levine's model proposes conservation of which?
questions.rationale: Levine's four conservation principles: energy, structural integrity, personal integrity, and social integrity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Which theorist classified stressors as intrapersonal, interpersonal, and extrapersonal?
questions.rationale: Neuman's Health Care Systems Model addresses stressors within, between, and outside the person; nursing maintains system stability.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: A client unable to perform any self-care after a stroke needs which Orem nursing system?
questions.rationale: Wholly compensatory care is for those unable to control their environment and process information; partly compensatory for some activities; supportive-educative for learning self-care.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: A new diabetic needs teaching to give his own insulin. Which Orem system applies?
questions.rationale: Supportive-educative care is for clients who need to learn self-care measures with assistance.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Which theorist views the person as an irreducible energy field, greater than the sum of parts?
questions.rationale: Rogers' Science of Unitary Human Beings sees the person as an irreducible, four-dimensional energy field.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: Which is one of Roy's four adaptive modes?
questions.rationale: Roy's adaptive modes are physiologic, self-concept, role-function, and interdependence.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: In Lydia Hall's model, which circle involves the therapeutic use of self?
questions.rationale: Care is nurturance exclusive to nursing; core is therapeutic use of self and reflection; cure is nursing related to physician's orders.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Ida Orlando's three elements of the nursing situation are client behavior, nurse reaction, and:
questions.rationale: Orlando's Dynamic Nurse-Patient Relationship: client behavior, nurse reaction, and nurse action.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Which theorist made caring the central, unifying focus of nursing with 10 carative factors?
questions.rationale: Watson's Human Caring Theory centers practice on caring, using 10 carative factors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 3)

questions.stem: Which nurse role helps clients exercise their rights and speak for themselves?
questions.rationale: The advocate protects the client and helps them exercise their rights.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Roles of a Nurse (PDF p. 5)

questions.stem: Who may read a client's chart?
questions.rationale: Only health professionals participating in the client's care may read the chart.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: Within what period should a physician countersign a telephone order?
questions.rationale: Telephone orders are countersigned by the ordering physician within the prescribed time, usually 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Telephone Orders (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: Who is the PRIMARY source of assessment data?
questions.rationale: The client is the primary source; family, records, and other professionals are secondary.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessment (PDF p. 9)

questions.stem: In an emergency, which interview approach is used?
questions.rationale: The directive interview is structured with closed questions and is used in emergencies to get specific data.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Interviewing (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Which stage of the interview is MOST important for building rapport?
questions.rationale: The opening is the most important stage; it establishes rapport and orients the client.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Interview (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Checking a client's hydration status every 15 minutes is which type of assessment?
questions.rationale: Problem-focused assessment determines the status of a specific problem, such as hydration every 15 minutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Assessment (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: A home nurse compares a client's status now with data from 6 months ago. Which assessment is this?
questions.rationale: Time-lapsed assessment is done months after the initial one to compare with baseline.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Assessment (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Double-checking data to confirm accuracy is called:
questions.rationale: Validating is verifying data to confirm it is accurate and factual.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Validating Data (PDF p. 10)

questions.stem: Which nursing diagnosis is written in the 3-part PES format?
questions.rationale: PES includes the problem, etiology, and signs/symptoms ('as manifested by').
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: A problem is not present, but risk factors make it likely. Which diagnosis type is this?
questions.rationale: A risk diagnosis is a judgment that a problem is likely to develop unless nurses intervene.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: 'Readiness for enhanced family coping' is which type of nursing diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Wellness diagnoses describe readiness for enhancement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: How should collaborative problems be labeled?
questions.rationale: Collaborative problems begin with 'Potential complications', e.g., PC: increased ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: To be useful for evaluation, how should goals be written?
questions.rationale: Goals are stated in behavioral, measurable terms (SMART) and involve the client and family.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 11)

questions.stem: When does discharge planning begin?
questions.rationale: Discharge planning begins at first client contact with ongoing assessment of needs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Discharge Planning (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do just before implementing an intervention?
questions.rationale: Implementation includes reassessing the client before an intervention.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Implementation (PDF p. 12)

questions.stem: Evaluation done at or just before discharge to see if goals were met is:
questions.rationale: Terminal or summative evaluation determines whether goals are met, partially met, or unmet.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Evaluation (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: In Becker's Health Belief Model, which is an individual perception?
questions.rationale: Individual perceptions include perceived susceptibility, seriousness, and threat; age, peers, and media are modifying factors or cues.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Health Belief Model (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: In Smith's models, defining health as the ability to perform one's work is the:
questions.rationale: Role performance model defines health by ability to perform work; eudemonistic is self-actualization.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Smith's Model of Health (PDF p. 13)

questions.stem: Travis's illness-wellness continuum moves toward high-level wellness through which steps?
questions.rationale: Movement right of the neutral point occurs through awareness, education, and growth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Travis's Continuum (PDF p. 13)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client stays home from work, and family confirms he is ill. Which stage of illness is this?
questions.rationale: In assuming the sick role, the person accepts illness and is excused from usual duties, with confirmation from family.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Illness (PDF p. 14)

questions.stem: Physical therapy after a stroke is which level of prevention (Leavell and Clark)?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention halts disease progression and rehabilitates, such as PT after CVA or speech therapy after laryngectomy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 15)

questions.stem: A male nurse examines a female client. What ethical safeguard is needed?
questions.rationale: A female nurse must be present when a male examines a female client.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which disease requires AIRBORNE precautions?
questions.rationale: Airborne precautions are for measles, varicella (including zoster), and pulmonary TB.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child has diphtheria. Which precautions are used?
questions.rationale: Droplet precautions apply to diphtheria, pertussis, mumps, rubella, strep pharyngitis, and pneumonic plague.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which condition requires CONTACT precautions?
questions.rationale: Contact precautions apply to scabies, pediculosis, impetigo, C. difficile, hepatitis A, RSV, and MDROs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: For droplet precautions, when must staff wear a mask?
questions.rationale: Under droplet precautions, a mask is worn when working within 3 feet of the client.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Droplet Precautions (PDF p. 36)

questions.topicName: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In color-coded waste segregation, which container receives infectious items?
questions.rationale: Yellow is for infectious waste; black non-biodegradable, green biodegradable, orange radioactive, red sharps.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Disposal of Equipment (PDF p. 37)

questions.stem: Which Philippine law defines and penalizes rape?
questions.rationale: RA 8353 (Anti-Rape Law of 1997) defines rape; RA 9262 is anti-VAWC; RA 7610 child abuse; RA 9165 dangerous drugs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rape (PDF p. 256)

questions.stem: A gold miner with silicosis has a positive tuberculin test. The nurse anticipates:
questions.rationale: Silicosis increases TB risk; give prophylactic INH if tuberculin-positive.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Occupational Lung Diseases (PDF p. 330)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test confirms active pulmonary tuberculosis?
questions.rationale: Sputum smear and culture confirm TB; PPD shows infection; x-ray shows extent.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Tuberculosis (PDF p. 334)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is pyridoxine (vitamin B6) given with isoniazid?
questions.rationale: Pyridoxine prevents INH-associated peripheral neuritis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, TB Management (PDF p. 334)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which anti-TB drug requires periodic visual acuity and color vision tests?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-TB Drugs (PDF p. 335)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on pyrazinamide reports joint pain. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia, arthralgia, and hepatotoxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-TB Drugs (PDF p. 334)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: When should anti-TB drugs be taken for best absorption?
questions.rationale: Take on an empty stomach or at least 1 hour before meals; food interferes with absorption.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, TB Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 335)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on INH should avoid which food to prevent flushing and palpitations?
questions.rationale: INH users should avoid tyramine and histamine foods (aged cheese, tuna, skipjack).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, TB Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 335)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Hepatitis A is transmitted mainly by:
questions.rationale: Hepatitis A and E: fecal-oral; B, C, D: blood and body fluids.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis is very severe in pregnant women?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis E resembles A but is very severe in pregnancy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis most often leads to chronic liver disease and a carrier state after transfusion?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis C frequently becomes chronic, with cirrhosis and liver cancer risk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Jaundice, dark urine, and clay-colored stools appear in which hepatitis stage?
questions.rationale: Icteric stage brings jaundice; pre-icteric is flu-like; post-icteric is convalescence.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatitis Stages (PDF p. 349)

questions.stem: Under RA 7170 (Organ Donation Act of 1991), who may donate body parts by legacy?
questions.rationale: Any individual at least 18 years old and of sound mind may donate.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Transplant (PDF p. 393)

questions.stem: Under RA 7170, the donor's death must be diagnosed by:
questions.rationale: Death is diagnosed separately by two physicians who are not on the removal team.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Transplant (PDF p. 393)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with meningococcal meningitis is kept on respiratory isolation for:
questions.rationale: Droplet precautions until 24 hours of effective antibiotics.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis (PDF p. 426)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test confirms bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: CSF Gram stain and culture via lumbar puncture.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis (PDF p. 426)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which environment is best for a client with meningitis?
questions.rationale: Photophobia and irritability; keep room dark and quiet.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meningitis Nursing (PDF p. 426)

questions.stem: Under RA 9173, a foreign nurse may be licensed without examination through:
questions.rationale: Section 20: registration by reciprocity if requirements are substantially the same.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Registration (PDF p. 498)

questions.stem: A special/temporary permit under RA 9173 may be given to a foreign nurse who is:
questions.rationale: Permits cover specialists, medical missions (free), and exchange professors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Special Permit (PDF p. 498)

questions.stem: Which law is the Continuing Professional Development Act?
questions.rationale: RA 10912 (2016) is the CPD Act; RA 9173 is the Nursing Act; RA 8981 is the PRC Modernization Act.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CPD (PDF p. 498)

questions.stem: 'The right thing to do is the good thing to do' reflects which ethical approach?
questions.rationale: Teleology focuses on outcomes; deontology on duty; virtue ethics on character.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Ethics (PDF p. 499)

questions.stem: Not revealing confidential information that would harm a patient's reputation illustrates:
questions.rationale: Non-maleficence: do no harm.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Biomedical Ethics (PDF p. 499)

questions.stem: A nurse keeps her promise to return in 15 minutes. This shows:
questions.rationale: Fidelity is keeping promises and loyalty.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Biomedical Ethics (PDF p. 499)

questions.stem: Allowing a dying patient's relative to visit outside visiting hours applies the principle of:
questions.rationale: Epikia is a reasonable exception to the general rule.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principle of Epikia (PDF p. 499)

questions.stem: In the principle of double effect, which condition is required?
questions.rationale: Action is good, good intended, bad only allowed, good not from evil, good greater than bad.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Two-fold Effect (PDF p. 500)

questions.stem: Revocation or suspension of a nursing license is what type of case?
questions.rationale: License actions are administrative; appeals go to the PRC.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Legal Aspects (PDF p. 500)

questions.stem: Where does a nurse file a case for illegal dismissal?
questions.rationale: Illegal dismissal cases are filed with DOLE; no lawyer needed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Illegal Dismissal (PDF p. 501)

questions.stem: A sponge is left inside a patient after surgery. Which doctrine applies?
questions.rationale: 'The thing speaks for itself': injury would not occur without negligence.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Res Ipsa Loquitor (PDF p. 501)

questions.stem: The hospital shares liability for a staff nurse's negligence under:
questions.rationale: 'Let the master answer': employer shares liability with employee.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respondeat Superior (PDF p. 501)

questions.stem: An unconscious accident victim needs emergency surgery and no relative is present. Consent is:
questions.rationale: In emergencies consent is implied, since delay may cause greater harm.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Who Must Consent (PDF p. 502)

questions.stem: Who gives consent for surgery of a married 17-year-old?
questions.rationale: A married or emancipated minor may consent without parents.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Who Must Consent (PDF p. 502)

questions.stem: A nurse tells a patient, 'I'll restrain you if you don't take your medicine.' This is:
questions.rationale: Assault is a threat of harmful contact; battery is actual unconsented touching.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assault (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: A nurse gives an injection after the patient refused it. The nurse may be charged with:
questions.rationale: Battery is intentional unconsented physical touching.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Battery (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: A competent patient insists on leaving against advice. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Detaining him is false imprisonment; explain consequences and allow discharge against advice.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, False Imprisonment (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: Closing the curtains during a physical examination protects the patient's:
questions.rationale: Privacy relates to the person; confidentiality relates to information.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Right to Privacy (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: A nurse posts false, damaging written statements about a colleague. This is:
questions.rationale: Libel is written defamation; slander is spoken; a third party must receive it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Defamation (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: Under the Revised Penal Code, a felony is frustrated when the offender:
questions.rationale: Frustrated: all acts performed but not produced for reasons independent of the offender.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Felony Degrees (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: A person who knows of a crime and later helps the offender escape is an:
questions.rationale: Accessories act after the crime; accomplices cooperate before or during.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Conspiracy (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: Self-defense with all its elements present is a:
questions.rationale: Justifying: no liability; incomplete self-defense becomes mitigating.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Justifying Circumstance (PDF p. 504)

questions.stem: Voluntary surrender to authorities is which type of circumstance?
questions.rationale: Mitigating circumstances reduce liability (voluntary surrender, confession).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mitigating Circumstance (PDF p. 504)

questions.stem: Looting during a calamity is which type of circumstance?
questions.rationale: Crimes in times of calamity, cruelty, treachery, and premeditation increase liability.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Aggravating Circumstance (PDF p. 504)

questions.stem: Which law is the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers?
questions.rationale: RA 7305; RA 7160 is Local Government Code; RA 6713 ethics of officials; RA 7875 PhilHealth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.stem: Which law mandates rooming-in and breastfeeding in health facilities?
questions.rationale: RA 7600 (Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act, amended by RA 10028).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.stem: The Generics Act of the Philippines is:
questions.rationale: RA 6675 Generics Act; RA 7719 Blood Services; RA 9262 VAWC; RA 8749 Clean Air Act.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.stem: Which law governs the National Blood Services program?
questions.rationale: RA 7719 promotes voluntary blood donation and safe blood supply.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laws Related to Nursing (PDF p. 505)

questions.stem: A study testing whether breastfeeding reduces infant pain during injections is:
questions.rationale: Applied research solves existing practice problems; basic research builds theory.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Research (PDF p. 522)

questions.stem: In 'number of prenatal classes and anxiety about labor,' the dependent variable is:
questions.rationale: Dependent variable is the presumed effect; independent is the presumed cause.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Variables (PDF p. 522)

questions.stem: Which characteristic describes qualitative research?
questions.rationale: Qualitative: narrative, subjective, inductive, theory development, field setting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Quantitative vs Qualitative (PDF p. 522)

questions.stem: A true experiment requires manipulation, control, and:
questions.rationale: True experiments have manipulation, control group, and random assignment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, True Experimental Design (PDF p. 523)

questions.stem: A study with an intervention but no random assignment is:
questions.rationale: Quasi-experiments lack randomization.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Quasi-experimental (PDF p. 523)
