questions.stem: In-depth interviews exploring the lived experience of women after pelvic surgery is:
questions.rationale: Phenomenology studies lived experience; ethnography studies cultures.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Phenomenological Research (PDF p. 523)

questions.stem: Studying the health lifeways of an indigenous community through fieldwork is:
questions.rationale: Ethnography studies cultural groups holistically.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ethnographical Research (PDF p. 523)

questions.stem: 'There is no significant relationship between anxiety and duration of infertility' is a:
questions.rationale: Null hypothesis states no relationship between variables.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothesis (PDF p. 524)

questions.stem: Which literature source is most recommended for a review?
questions.rationale: Primary sources are written by the original researchers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Literature Review (PDF p. 524)

questions.stem: Following premature infants' development from birth through childhood is a:
questions.rationale: Longitudinal: data collected at multiple points over time.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Research Design (PDF p. 525)

questions.stem: Selecting every 10th patient from a list is which sampling method?
questions.rationale: Systematic sampling selects every nth case.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Probability Sampling (PDF p. 525)

questions.stem: Asking early participants to refer others who meet criteria is:
questions.rationale: Snowball (network) sampling uses referrals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Non-probability Sampling (PDF p. 526)

questions.stem: Staff perform better because they know they are being observed. This is the:
questions.rationale: The Hawthorne effect is a disadvantage of overt observation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Observation (PDF p. 526)

questions.stem: Levels of anxiety (mild, moderate, severe, panic) are measured on which scale?
questions.rationale: Ordinal ranks categories; nominal only classifies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Measurement (PDF p. 527)

questions.stem: Which statistical test compares the means of two groups?
questions.rationale: t-test: two means; ANOVA: three or more; chi-square: categories.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Statistical Tests (PDF p. 528)

questions.stem: The most frequently occurring score in a distribution is the:
questions.rationale: Mode: most frequent; median: middle; mean: average.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Central Tendency (PDF p. 528)

questions.stem: Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true is a:
questions.rationale: Type I is a false positive; Type II is accepting a false null.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothesis Testing (PDF p. 529)

questions.stem: Using multiple data sources to confirm findings is:
questions.rationale: Triangulation uses multiple referents to establish truth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Research Quality (PDF p. 529)

questions.stem: A participant may withdraw from a study at any time without penalty. This upholds the right to:
questions.rationale: Self-determination: voluntary participation without penalty.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Research Ethics (PDF p. 529)

questions.stem: The most secure way to protect participant confidentiality is:
questions.rationale: Anonymity: even the researcher cannot link participants to data.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Right to Privacy (PDF p. 530)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which drug is an anthelminthic used in school deworming?
questions.rationale: Albendazole and mebendazole treat intestinal worms.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antiparasitics (PDF p. 140)

questions.topicName: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on long-term antimalarials needs regular:
questions.rationale: Antimalarials can cause visual disturbances; give with food.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antiparasitics (PDF p. 140)

questions.stem: While the nurse measures the fundal height of a client at 36 weeks' gestation lying flat, the client becomes pale and lightheaded. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Raise her legs on two pillows
Turn her onto her left side
Have her breathe into a paper bag
questions.rationale: Late in pregnancy, the uterus can compress the inferior vena cava and aorta when the client lies supine (supine hypotension syndrome). Turning her to the left side, or wedging the right hip, relieves the compression.
explanations: Raising the legs does not lift the uterus off the vena cava.
Correct: the left lateral position relieves vena cava compression.
This treats hyperventilation, not supine hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 243)

questions.stem: A client pregnant with twins comes for a prenatal checkup. Which complication should the nurse monitor for as a PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Two fetuses demand more iron, so maternal anemia is common and is the priority concern. Twin pregnancies tend to end preterm, not post-term.
explanations: Hemorrhoids can occur but are a lower priority.
Twin pregnancies usually end in preterm birth.
Correct: iron demand from two fetuses causes anemia.
This is not a typical priority problem of a twin pregnancy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 244)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why does the nurse closely monitor the weight, vital signs, and fluid status of a pregnant client with rheumatic heart disease?
options: Pregnancy raises blood volume and cardiac output
Pregnancy slows the maternal heart rate
Blood volume drops in the third trimester
questions.rationale: Blood volume rises during pregnancy, increasing cardiac output (stroke volume × heart rate). A diseased heart may not meet this added workload and can decompensate.
explanations: Correct: the extra volume and output strain a diseased heart.
Stroke volume increases with higher blood volume.
Blood volume peaks late in pregnancy; it does not drop.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 245)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client with diabetes at 36 weeks' gestation has had reactive nonstress tests for 3 weeks. Today the test is nonreactive after 40 minutes. What should the nurse prepare for next?
options: Sending her home to repeat the test in 2 days
questions.rationale: A nonreactive NST needs further evaluation, and the contraction stress test is the next step. There is not enough data to justify immediate delivery, and waiting 2 days may endanger the fetus.
explanations: Delay may put the fetus at risk.
Data do not yet justify emergency surgery.
Data do not yet justify immediate induction.
Correct: a CST further assesses fetal well-being.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 290)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client with gestational hypertension is admitted in early active labor. Which finding does the nurse MOST expect?
questions.rationale: Elevated blood pressure is the major sign of gestational hypertension. As it progresses, reflexes may become brisk, urine output falls, and fetal heart rate variability decreases.
explanations: Correct: hypertension is the defining finding.
Reflexes become hyperactive as the disease progresses.
Fluid retention leads to weight gain, not loss.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 211)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A laboring client has sickle cell anemia. Which nursing action helps prevent a sickling crisis during labor?
options: Pushing early in the first stage
questions.rationale: Labor raises oxygen demand, which a client with sickle cell anemia may not meet. Oxygen and IV hydration lower the risk of crisis.
explanations: Hydration helps prevent sickling, so fluids are not restricted.
Early pushing is exhausting and inappropriate.
Correct: oxygen meets the higher demands of labor.
Lying flat does not prevent sickling and may compress the vena cava.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 286)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Ana, a 24-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks, is in active labor on an oxytocin infusion. The nurse is watching the fetal monitor tracing.
questions.stem: The tracing shows late decelerations. The nurse understands that these are caused by:
questions.rationale: Late decelerations come from reduced blood flow and oxygen transfer through the placenta during contractions, causing fetal hypoxemia. Oxygen and repositioning are needed.
explanations: Correct: late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency.
Sleep cycles reduce variability; they do not cause late decelerations.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 176)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Ana, a 24-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks, is in active labor on an oxytocin infusion. The nurse is watching the fetal monitor tracing.
questions.stem: Which nursing measure helps prevent fetal heart rate decelerations during Ana's labor?
options: Keep her lying flat on her back
questions.rationale: Side-lying and upright positions (walking, standing, squatting) improve venous return and uterine blood flow. Lying supine compresses the vena cava.
explanations: The supine position reduces placental blood flow.
More oxytocin can overstimulate the uterus.
Walking is an upright position that helps.
Correct: these positions improve venous return and placental flow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 289)

questions.stem: Twelve hours after a vaginal delivery, where does the nurse expect to palpate the fundus if involution is progressing normally?
options: At the level of the umbilicus
Midway between the umbilicus and symphysis
questions.rationale: Within 6 to 12 hours after birth the fundus rises to the umbilicus, stays there about a day, then descends about one fingerbreadth daily. It is no longer palpable by about day 10.
explanations: Correct: the fundus is at the umbilicus at 6 to 12 hours.
This is where the fundus sits right after the placenta is delivered.
This level is reached several days later.
The uterus is no longer palpable only by about 10 days.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 536)

questions.stem: On the second postpartum day, which lochia does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Lochia rubra is dark red and lasts from delivery to about day 3. Lochia serosa (pinkish-brown) follows, then lochia alba (white to yellowish).
explanations: Alba appears in the later weeks.
Alba appears in the later weeks.
Correct: rubra lasts from delivery to about day 3.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 542)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which postpartum client has the HIGHEST risk of puerperal infection?
options: A client with a 6-hour labor and spontaneous vaginal birth
A client with a history of two miscarriages
A client with cesarean birth after prolonged rupture of membranes
A client who delivered twins vaginally
questions.rationale: Risk factors include cesarean birth, prolonged rupture of membranes, prolonged labor, many vaginal examinations, trauma, retained placental fragments, and past infections.
explanations: A short labor with vaginal birth is low risk.
Past miscarriages are not a risk factor.
Correct: cesarean birth and prolonged rupture are major risk factors.
Twin vaginal delivery alone is not a listed risk factor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 251)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A postpartum client with heart disease is told to call the nurse before getting out of bed or caring for her baby. What is the reason for this instruction?
options: To promote bonding with the newborn
To reduce stress on her heart
To allow the perineum to heal
questions.rationale: Right after delivery, fluid shifts from the tissues back into the circulation and hormones change, adding stress to the heart. The priority is to limit cardiac workload.
explanations: Bonding matters but is not the reason for this instruction.
Correct: fluid shifts after birth add cardiac stress.
This does not address the cardiac risk.
Perineal healing is not the main concern here.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 705)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding in a term newborn increases the risk of developing jaundice?
questions.rationale: As a cephalhematoma is reabsorbed, the broken-down red cells add to the bilirubin load. A negative Coombs test means no antibody-mediated hemolysis.
explanations: Rh incompatibility involves an Rh-negative mother and Rh-positive infant, not the reverse.
Normal birth weight is not a risk factor.
A negative Coombs test shows no immune hemolysis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 174)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The mother's hepatitis B surface antigen test is positive. Which does the nurse anticipate for the newborn?
options: Hepatitis B vaccine and HBIG within 12 hours
Repeat maternal test before any newborn treatment
questions.rationale: Infants of HBsAg-positive mothers receive both the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours of birth. Antibiotics do not treat viral infection.
explanations: Breastfeeding is not prohibited when the infant is immunized.
Antibiotics do not act against hepatitis B virus.
Correct: vaccine plus HBIG gives active and passive protection.
Delaying protection increases the risk of infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 237)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which medication is applied to a newborn's eyes to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum?
questions.rationale: Erythromycin 0.5% eye ointment is effective against Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis, which the newborn can acquire in the birth canal.
explanations: Penicillin eye drops are not the standard prophylaxis.
Correct: erythromycin covers gonococcal and chlamydial infection.
Vitamin K is given IM to prevent bleeding.
Silver sulfadiazine is a burn cream.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 250)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 3-day-old preterm neonate has respiratory distress syndrome. Which finding shows the condition is improving?
options: Edema of the hands and feet
questions.rationale: As alveoli open, lung fluid moves into the bloodstream and is excreted by the kidneys, so normal urination (2 to 5 mL/kg/hour) is an early sign of improvement.
explanations: Edema appears early in RDS and does not show improvement.
Correct: increased voiding is an early sign of improvement.
Grunting is a sign of respiratory distress.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 173)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which safety teaching is MOST appropriate for the mother of a 1-month-old infant?
options: Place the baby on the back to sleep
questions.rationale: At 1 month, the key instructions are back-to-sleep positioning and never shaking the baby. Outlet covers, locked chemicals, and gates matter once the infant starts moving around, at about 6 months.
explanations: Correct: back-sleeping reduces the risk of sudden infant death.
Outlets become a hazard when the infant is mobile.
Poisoning becomes a risk once the infant explores.
Stairs become a hazard with crawling.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 693)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which is the HIGHEST priority in the care of a hospitalized toddler?
options: Adapting the toddler to hospital routines
questions.rationale: A toddler's mobility, curiosity, and the unfamiliar environment create a high risk of injury. Consistency and play matter, but safety comes first.
explanations: Important for separation anxiety, but safety comes first.
Toddlers do better when their home routines are kept.
Helpful, but not the top priority.
Correct: safety is the highest priority.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 732)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which personal-social milestone should the nurse tell a mother to expect in her 3-year-old?
questions.rationale: A 3-year-old puts on articles of clothing, brushes teeth with help, washes hands, knows their own name, and begins to take turns.
explanations: Tying shoelaces is a skill of about 5 to 6 years.
Correct: dressing in simple clothing is expected at 3.
Bicycle riding comes at school age.
Printing a name comes at about 5 to 6 years.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 813)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Under RA 9288 (Newborn Screening Act), when should newborn screening be done for a healthy term baby?
options: Immediately after the cord is cut
Within the first 6 hours of life
After 24 hours of life but not later than 3 days
questions.rationale: Screening is done after 24 hours of life but not later than 3 days. A baby who needs intensive care may be tested later, but by 7 days of age.
explanations: Too late; the window closes at 3 days.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9288, Sec. 6 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A preterm baby has been in the NICU since birth. By what age must the baby's newborn screening be done?
questions.rationale: A newborn who must be placed in intensive care may be exempted from the 3-day requirement but must be tested by seven days of age.
explanations: Three days applies to healthy newborns.
Thirty days is the legal definition of the newborn period.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9288, Sec. 6 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: The parents of a newborn refuse newborn screening because of their religious beliefs. What must the nurse ensure?
options: The screening is done anyway since it is mandatory
The parents sign an acknowledgment of the risk
The baby is kept until the parents agree to it
The refusal is reported to the barangay police
questions.rationale: Parents may refuse on religious grounds, but they must acknowledge in writing that refusal places the newborn at risk. The document goes into the baby's record and the refusal is noted in the national database.
explanations: The law allows refusal on religious grounds.
Holding the baby would be unlawful.
Refusal is documented, not reported to the police.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9288, Sec. 7 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 9288, when must the health practitioner who will deliver the baby inform the parents about newborn screening?
options: Only if the baby looks sick
questions.rationale: Any health practitioner who delivers or assists in delivering a newborn must, before delivery, inform the parents or guardian of the availability, nature, and benefits of newborn screening.
explanations: All newborns are screened, not only sick ones.
Too late to support an informed decision.
Too late; the screening window has passed.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 9288, Sec. 5 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is assigned in the delivery room of a district hospital that follows the Essential Intrapartum and Newborn Care (EINC) protocol, also known as Unang Yakap.
questions.stem: A baby is delivered and is crying. What is the FIRST step of the EINC protocol?
options: Weigh the baby on the warmer
Dry the baby immediately and thoroughly
questions.rationale: EINC has four steps done in sequence: immediate and thorough drying, early skin-to-skin contact, properly timed cord clamping, and non-separation of mother and baby for early breastfeeding.
explanations: Routine suctioning is no longer done.
Cord clamping is the third step.
Weighing is delayed so the baby stays with the mother.
questions.sourceLabel: Bull World Health Organ 2023;101(8):499–500 (interview with M. A. Silvestre on EINC)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is assigned in the delivery room of a district hospital that follows the Essential Intrapartum and Newborn Care (EINC) protocol, also known as Unang Yakap.
questions.stem: After drying the baby and placing it skin-to-skin on the mother's abdomen, when should Nurse Carla clamp the cord?
options: After cord pulsations stop, about 1 to 3 minutes
After the first breastfeeding is completed
questions.rationale: Properly timed (delayed) cord clamping waits until pulsations stop, about 1 to 3 minutes after birth. Even a one-minute delay gives the baby more blood and warmth.
explanations: Immediate clamping deprives the baby of placental blood.
questions.sourceLabel: Bull World Health Organ 2023;101(8):499–500 (interview with M. A. Silvestre on EINC)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is assigned in the delivery room of a district hospital that follows the Essential Intrapartum and Newborn Care (EINC) protocol, also known as Unang Yakap.
questions.stem: Which routine practice was DISCONTINUED for healthy newborns under EINC?
questions.rationale: EINC stopped routine suctioning, early bathing, early weighing and footprinting, and early separation of mother and baby, because these practices harm newborns.
explanations: Skin-to-skin contact is a core EINC step.
Early breastfeeding is a core EINC step.
Non-separation is a core EINC step.
questions.sourceLabel: Bull World Health Organ 2023;101(8):499–500 (interview with M. A. Silvestre on EINC)

questions.stem: A nurse returns to work after maternity leave and is still breastfeeding. Under RA 10028, what lactation break is she entitled to?
options: Breaks only during her meal time
questions.rationale: Nursing employees get lactation breaks, on top of meal time, of not less than 40 minutes for every 8-hour working period. These count as compensable hours worked.
explanations: Correct: at least 40 minutes per 8 hours, paid.
The breaks are compensable, not unpaid.
The breaks are in addition to meal time.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10028, Sec. 12 (lawyerly.ph)

questions.stem: A hospital is setting up a lactation station for its employees. Which plan violates RA 10028?
options: Placing it in a well-ventilated room
Providing a refrigerator to store milk
Placing it inside a staff toilet
Providing a sink for washing up
questions.rationale: A lactation station must be private, clean, sanitary, and well ventilated, and it must not be located in the toilet.
explanations: Storing expressed milk is part of its purpose.
Correct: the law prohibits lactation stations in toilets.
Washing facilities are part of the station.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10028, Sec. 11 (lawyerly.ph)

questions.stem: Under RA 10028, rooming-in means the newborn stays in the same room as the mother:
options: Right after delivery up to discharge
questions.rationale: Rooming-in places the newborn in the same room as the mother right after delivery up to discharge, which supports breastfeeding on demand.
explanations: Rooming-in is continuous, not only during feeds.
Rooming-in is continuous, day and night.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10028, Sec. 3(v) (lawyerly.ph)

questions.stem: A 16-year-old who has never been pregnant asks the health center nurse for a modern family planning method. Under RA 10354, what is required?
options: Written consent from her parents or guardian
Only her own verbal consent at the clinic
A court order allowing the method
Written consent from her sexual partner
questions.rationale: Minors cannot access modern family planning methods without written parental or guardian consent, unless the minor is already a parent or has had a miscarriage.
explanations: Correct: written parental or guardian consent is required.
A minor's own consent is not enough unless an exception applies.
Partner consent is not the legal requirement.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10354, Sec. 7 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: A nurse has religious objections to providing artificial contraception. Under RA 10354, what must the nurse do when a client asks for it in a non-emergency?
options: Refuse and tell the client to stop asking
Provide it anyway despite the objection
Refer the client to another provider
Report the client to the parish priest
questions.rationale: The law respects conscientious objection based on ethical or religious beliefs, but the objector must refer the client to another provider. Emergencies and serious cases must still be attended to.
explanations: The law respects the nurse's conscience.
Correct: refer the client to another provider.
This breaches confidentiality and is inappropriate.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10354, Sec. 23 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: RA 10354 defines modern methods of family planning as methods that are safe, effective, legal, and:
options: Artificial methods only, such as pills
Given free of charge in all facilities
questions.rationale: Modern methods are safe, effective, non-abortifacient, and legal, whether natural or artificial.
explanations: Natural methods can also be modern methods.
Cost is not part of the definition.
Religious approval is not part of the definition.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10354, Sec. 4(l) (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 10354, when may nurses and midwives give lifesaving drugs during an obstetric emergency?
options: Never; only physicians may give them
Only with the family's written consent
questions.rationale: The law allows midwives and nurses to administer lifesaving drugs in emergencies when no physicians are available, as part of ensuring skilled birth attendance.
explanations: The law makes an exception for emergencies.
Emergency drugs are not conditioned on family consent.
The provision applies wherever no physician is available.
Correct: when no physicians are available.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 10354, Sec. 5 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: According to Erikson, which nursing action BEST supports the psychosocial task of a 2-year-old?
options: Letting the toddler choose between two shirts
Dressing the toddler quickly to save time
Praising the toddler for sharing toys
Encouraging the toddler to join group games
questions.rationale: Toddlers are in Erikson's stage of autonomy versus shame and doubt. Offering simple, limited choices builds a sense of autonomy.
explanations: Doing everything for the toddler limits autonomy.
Sharing is not yet expected; toddlers play in parallel.
Cooperative group play fits older children.
questions.sourceLabel: Erikson's psychosocial theory (standard developmental theory; no excerpt in your materials yet — please verify)

questions.stem: A 10-month-old searches under a blanket for a toy that was just hidden. In Piaget's theory, this shows:
questions.rationale: Object permanence, knowing an object still exists when out of sight, develops in Piaget's sensorimotor stage (birth to 2 years).
explanations: Conservation develops in the concrete operational stage.
Egocentrism is typical of the preoperational stage.
Abstract reasoning belongs to formal operations.
questions.sourceLabel: Piaget's cognitive development theory (standard developmental theory; no excerpt in your materials yet — please verify)

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy says he will marry his mother when he grows up. According to Freud, this child is in which stage?
questions.rationale: In Freud's phallic stage (about 3 to 6 years), the child is attached to the opposite-sex parent (the Oedipus or Electra complex).
explanations: The anal stage is the toddler years.
Correct: the phallic stage, with the Oedipus complex.
questions.sourceLabel: Freud's psychosexual theory (standard developmental theory; no excerpt in your materials yet — please verify)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.situation: Aling Joy, G2P1 at 35 weeks, is admitted with severe preeclampsia and started on a magnesium sulfate infusion.
questions.stem: Which medication must the nurse keep at the bedside during the infusion?
questions.rationale: Calcium gluconate is the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity and is kept at the bedside throughout the infusion.
explanations: Correct: the antidote for magnesium toxicity.
Oxytocin stimulates contractions; it is not an antidote.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q141 (PDF p. 291)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.situation: Aling Joy, G2P1 at 35 weeks, is admitted with severe preeclampsia and started on a magnesium sulfate infusion.
questions.stem: Why should the nurse check Aling Joy often for signs of labor while she is on magnesium sulfate?
options: Magnesium raises the risk of infection
Its sedative effect may keep her from noticing labor
Labor always starts within hours of the drug
questions.rationale: Magnesium sulfate is a CNS depressant and anticonvulsant. Its sedative effect may keep the client from perceiving labor, so the nurse checks for signs of labor.
explanations: Magnesium relaxes, rather than stimulates, the uterus.
Infection risk is not increased by this drug.
Correct: sedation can mask the onset of labor.
Labor onset is not predictable from the drug.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q141 (PDF p. 291)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which statement by a mother shows she understands why her newborn needs a vitamin K (phytonadione) injection?
options: 'The baby's liver cannot make vitamin K at all.'
'Newborns lack the gut bacteria that make vitamin K.'
questions.rationale: The newborn gut lacks the normal flora that synthesize vitamin K, causing a temporary clotting deficiency in the first days of life. The injection prevents bleeding.
explanations: The liver uses vitamin K; the problem is the lack of gut flora.
Correct: there are no intestinal bacteria yet to produce vitamin K.
Vitamin K prevents bleeding, not jaundice.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q344 (PDF p. 512)

questions.stem: Methylergonovine is prescribed for a postpartum client. Which finding should make the nurse verify the order with the physician?
options: Continuous trickle of bright red blood
questions.rationale: Methylergonovine treats uterine atony but is contraindicated in hypertension. Heavy lochia and a boggy fundus are the very signs it treats.
explanations: A sign of atony that the drug treats.
A sign of atony that the drug treats.
Bleeding from atony is an indication for the drug.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q505 (PDF p. 700)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Miguel, 8 months old, has congestive heart failure from a ventricular septal defect. He is going home on oral digoxin, and the nurse is teaching his parents.
questions.stem: Which statement by the mother shows she understands how to give the digoxin?
options: 'I will mix it with his milk so he takes it.'
'I will check his pulse before each dose.'
'If he vomits, I will repeat the dose.'
'If I miss a dose, I will give two next time.'
questions.rationale: Digoxin is not mixed with food or formula (the full dose may not be taken). The pulse is checked before each dose, and a dose is not repeated after vomiting or doubled when missed.
explanations: Mixing with milk may mean an incomplete dose.
Correct: check the pulse before giving digoxin.
Do not repeat a dose after vomiting.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q637 (PDF p. 855)

questions.stem: Which statement shows that a client starting oral contraceptives understands the teaching?
options: 'I won't need any other method from the first day.'
'I will use a backup method during the first pill cycle.'
'I can skip a pill if I have sex less often.'
'If I miss a pill, I'll wait for the next pack.'
questions.rationale: A second method is used during the first cycle. Pills are taken at the same time daily, and a missed pill is taken as soon as remembered.
explanations: Protection is not reliable during the first cycle.
Correct: backup is needed in the first cycle.
A missed pill is taken as soon as remembered.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q639 (PDF p. 857)

questions.stem: A woman with a family history of heart disease wants to start oral contraceptives. What should the nurse ask about NEXT?
questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives are a risk factor for heart disease, especially combined with cigarette smoking. Exercise and cholesterol control are general measures.
explanations: Correct: smoking plus OCPs greatly raises cardiovascular risk.
A general measure, not the key risk.
A general measure, not the key risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q647 (PDF p. 865)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A postpartum client recovering from DIC goes home on a low-dose anticoagulant. What should the nurse tell her to avoid?
questions.rationale: Aspirin is an antiplatelet drug that interacts with anticoagulants and raises the bleeding risk. She can brush gently with a soft toothbrush and stay active.
explanations: She should use a soft toothbrush, not stop brushing.
Correct: aspirin increases the bleeding risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q738 (PDF p. 963)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child recovering from a head injury goes home on tapering doses of dexamethasone. What should the nurse tell the parents?
options: 'It will be stopped after two doses.'
'Facial swelling means the drug must stop.'
'Stopping it suddenly can bring back brain swelling.'
questions.rationale: Stopping dexamethasone abruptly can cause cerebral edema to rebound, so it is tapered. It reduces inflammation, not infection, and facial swelling is a common side effect that resolves.
explanations: Facial edema is common and goes away after therapy.
Correct: abrupt withdrawal causes rebound edema.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q769 (PDF p. 999)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child treated for scarlet fever now has puffy eyes, poor appetite, and scant tea-colored urine. What does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Scarlet fever is caused by group A beta-hemolytic streptococci. Periorbital edema, reduced tea-colored urine, and anorexia point to acute glomerulonephritis, which must be reported.
explanations: Not signs of a penicillin allergy.
Correct: classic signs of post-streptococcal AGN.
Dehydration does not cause facial edema.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q771 (PDF p. 1001)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Ate Liza, G1P0 at 41 weeks, is being induced with an IV oxytocin infusion. Nurse Rica is monitoring her closely.
questions.stem: Which contraction pattern shows the oxytocin dose is ADEQUATE?
options: Three to five contractions in 10 minutes, with dilation
Continuous contractions with no rest between
questions.rationale: The goal is the lowest dose that gives 3 to 5 contractions in 10 minutes with cervical dilation. Contractions more often than every 2 minutes reduce their quality and stress the fetus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1218 (PDF p. 1511)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.situation: Ate Liza, G1P0 at 41 weeks, is being induced with an IV oxytocin infusion. Nurse Rica is monitoring her closely.
questions.stem: Which finding should make Nurse Rica suspect water intoxication from the oxytocin?
questions.rationale: Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect. Signs of water intoxication include tachycardia, dysrhythmias, shortness of breath, nausea, and vomiting.
explanations: Not a sign of water intoxication.
Not a sign of water intoxication.
Not a sign of water intoxication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1104 (PDF p. 1388)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with a seizure disorder takes carbamazepine. Which plasma level is in the therapeutic range?
questions.rationale: The therapeutic plasma level of carbamazepine is 5 to 12 mcg/mL. Lower levels may need a dose increase; higher levels risk toxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1127 (PDF p. 1411)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with von Willebrand disease is prescribed intranasal desmopressin. Which instruction should the nurse give the parents?
options: Reduce fluid intake during early treatment
Keep the spray in the freezer
questions.rationale: Desmopressin reduces urine output, so fluids are reduced during initial treatment to prevent fluid buildup. The spray is refrigerated, not frozen.
explanations: Correct: limit fluids during early treatment.
Extra doses are not given without orders.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1342 (PDF p. 1645)

questions.stem: Methylergonovine is given IM to a mother right after delivery. What is its purpose?
options: To maintain a normal blood pressure
questions.rationale: Methylergonovine is an oxytocic that contracts the uterus to prevent or control postpartum hemorrhage. It may raise blood pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1363 (PDF p. 1666)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A laboring client receives butorphanol for pain. Which item must be readily available?
questions.rationale: Butorphanol is an opioid analgesic. Naloxone and resuscitation equipment are kept ready in case of respiratory depression.
explanations: Another opioid; it would add to depression.
May be useful, but not the priority.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1365 (PDF p. 1668)

questions.stem: A mother receives the rubella vaccine 2 days after delivery. Which instruction is MOST important?
options: Stay out of the sun for 3 days
questions.rationale: Rubella vaccine is a live attenuated virus that can harm a developing fetus, so the woman avoids pregnancy for the period advised after vaccination. Immunity lasts about 15 years.
explanations: Correct: the live vaccine is potentially teratogenic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1368 (PDF p. 1671)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Andrea was born with a cleft lip and palate. The lip was repaired at 3 months, and the palate repair is planned later.
questions.stem: On the first day after the cleft lip repair, how should the nurse care for the incision?
options: Rinse it with sterile water after feedings
Clean it only when exudate forms
Rub it gently to remove crusts
Remove the Logan bar to clean it
questions.rationale: The incision is rinsed with sterile water after every feeding and patted dry, never rubbed. The Logan bar protects the suture line and stays in place.
explanations: Cleaning is routine, not only when exudate forms.
Removing it adds tension to the incision.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q144 (PDF p. 294)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Andrea was born with a cleft lip and palate. The lip was repaired at 3 months, and the palate repair is planned later.
questions.stem: Years later, at a preschool checkup after her palate repair, which question BEST screens for a long-term complication?
options: 'Does she play with an imaginary friend?'
'Does she sometimes not respond when called?'
'Does she still eat soft food only?'
questions.rationale: Children with cleft palate get frequent otitis media, which can lead to hearing loss. Not responding may mean she cannot hear well. Imaginary friends are normal at this age.
explanations: Unrelated to cleft palate after repair.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q44 (PDF p. 183)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After spinal rod insertion for scoliosis, which assessment is MOST important in the immediate postoperative period?
questions.rationale: Spinal manipulation can impair neurovascular status, so circulation, sensation, and motion are checked at least every 2 hours. Pain and urine output matter but come second.
explanations: Correct: neurovascular checks are the priority.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q58 (PDF p. 199)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 2-year-old has just had a hip spica cast applied. Which action BEST protects the child's skin?
options: Change the diaper at least every 2 hours
Leave the genital area open to air
Check the skin only once a day
questions.rationale: The spica cast leaves the genital area open. Diapers are changed at least every 2 hours by day (3 to 4 hours at night) so urine and stool do not soil the cast and damage the skin.
explanations: Correct: frequent changes protect skin and cast.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q61 (PDF p. 206)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with decorticate posturing suddenly shows decerebrate posturing. How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: A change from decorticate (flexor) to decerebrate (extensor) posturing usually means neurologic function is deteriorating, and the provider is notified.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q84 (PDF p. 230)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 3-year-old admitted with croup has a respiratory rate of 28. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A normal respiratory rate for a 3-year-old is about 20 to 30 breaths per minute, so the nurse documents it. Nasal flaring, retractions, and stridor would signal distress.
explanations: Not needed for a normal rate.
Correct: the rate is normal for the age.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q86 (PDF p. 232)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which food or drink is BEST to offer a child after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Clear, cool liquids are best. Citrus, carbonated, and very hot or cold drinks irritate the throat. Milk coats the throat and causes throat clearing, which can cause bleeding. Red liquids look like blood.
explanations: Correct: clear, cool, and not red.
Red color can be mistaken for blood.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q106 (PDF p. 255)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant is HIV-positive. Which home-care action BEST reduces the infant's risk of complications?
options: Check the fontanel daily for bulging
Feed only in an upright position
questions.rationale: Meticulous skin care protects an HIV-infected infant from secondary infections. The other actions are unrelated to HIV.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q112 (PDF p. 261)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement about brain tumors in children younger than 3 years is accurate?
options: Radiation is the treatment of choice
Headache and vomiting are the classic symptoms
The head is never shaved before surgery
questions.rationale: Headache and vomiting are classic. Total surgical removal is the treatment of choice. Radiation is avoided under age 3 because of its toxic effects on the developing brain.
explanations: Radiation is avoided at this age.
Only as much hair as needed is shaved.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q117 (PDF p. 267)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a child with viral pneumonia ask about treatment. Which statement shows they need MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Treatment of viral pneumonia is supportive: oxygen, chest physiotherapy, and IV fluids. Antibiotics are not given unless the pneumonia is bacterial.
explanations: Correct answer: antibiotics do not treat viruses.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q118 (PDF p. 268)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Nurse Bea plans a tepid tub bath for 4-year-old Kiko, who has a temperature of 39.6°C.
questions.stem: How should Nurse Bea prepare the bath?
options: Add rubbing alcohol to the water
Start warm and add cool water gradually
questions.rationale: Adding cool water to a warm bath lowers the temperature gradually, so the child adjusts without chilling. Alcohol is toxic and causes vasoconstriction. The bath lasts 20 to 30 minutes.
explanations: Too short; 20 to 30 minutes is needed.
Cold water causes shivering, which raises heat production.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q143 (PDF p. 293)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Nurse Bea plans a tepid tub bath for 4-year-old Kiko, who has a temperature of 39.6°C.
questions.stem: What should Nurse Bea do right after the bath?
options: Dress Kiko in a light cotton shirt
Cover Kiko with a heavy blanket
questions.rationale: Light cotton keeps the child from chilling. Blankets raise body temperature, and the temperature is rechecked about 30 minutes after the bath.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q345 (PDF p. 513)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After surgical closure of a meningomyelocele, how should the infant be positioned?
options: Supine with a binder over the dressing
questions.rationale: The prone position keeps pressure off the surgical site on the back. The nurse watches closely for CSF leakage.
explanations: Supine puts pressure on the site.
Correct: prone protects the operative site.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q155 (PDF p. 305)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has Reye's syndrome. Which complication should the nurse monitor for MOST closely?
questions.rationale: Reye's syndrome is an acute encephalopathy after a viral illness, with cerebral edema and fatty liver changes. Increased ICP is a major problem, and hypoglycemia (not hyperglycemia) occurs.
explanations: It follows viral, not bacterial, illness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q162 (PDF p. 313)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 8, is admitted with suspected rheumatic fever three weeks after an untreated sore throat.
questions.stem: Which laboratory result BEST supports the diagnosis?
questions.rationale: An elevated antistreptolysin-O (ASO) titer shows a recent streptococcal infection and is the most reliable test supporting rheumatic fever. A high WBC count is not specific.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q173 (PDF p. 326)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 8, is admitted with suspected rheumatic fever three weeks after an untreated sore throat.
questions.stem: Which finding is a MAJOR manifestation of rheumatic fever the nurse should prepare to manage?
options: Cool, pale skin over the joints
White, painful lesions on the trunk
Carditis with a new heart murmur
questions.rationale: Rheumatic fever is a delayed inflammatory reaction to group A beta-hemolytic streptococcal infection. Major manifestations include carditis (murmur, cardiac enlargement) and subcutaneous nodules over bony prominences.
explanations: Correct: carditis is a major manifestation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q289 (PDF p. 448)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 5-year-old with tetralogy of Fallot has clubbed fingers. What does this finding reflect?
questions.rationale: Clubbing, a thickening and flattening of the fingertips, results from chronic tissue hypoxia and polycythemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q174 (PDF p. 327)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which stool characteristic does the nurse expect in a child with celiac disease?
questions.rationale: Gluten intolerance causes malabsorption, giving malodorous, pale, bulky, loose stools with excess flatus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q210 (PDF p. 365)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding suggests an inguinal hernia in a child?
questions.rationale: An inguinal hernia appears as painless groin swelling when the child cries or strains. A dribbling stream suggests phimosis; absent testes suggest cryptorchidism.
explanations: Suggests partial obstruction of a herniated loop.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q214 (PDF p. 369)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding in a newborn supports a diagnosis of esophageal atresia?
questions.rationale: The esophagus ends in a blind pouch, so swallowed saliva cannot reach the stomach. It collects and flows out of the mouth, causing continuous drooling.
explanations: Correct: saliva cannot pass into the stomach.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q218 (PDF p. 373)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has diarrhea. Which is an EARLY sign of dehydration?
options: Apical pulse of 200 beats per minute
questions.rationale: As fluid is lost, the pulse rises first to maintain circulation. Peripheral signs (cool, mottled skin and slow capillary refill) come later as circulatory failure develops.
explanations: A later sign of circulatory failure.
Correct: tachycardia is an early compensatory sign.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q346 (PDF p. 514)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has a new plaster cast on the arm. Which instruction helps the cast dry properly?
options: Lift the cast with the fingertips
Keep the cast covered with a blanket
Point a fan toward the cast
Keep the arm still in one position
questions.rationale: A fan speeds drying. The cast is lifted with the palms (fingertips leave dents), elevated on pillows, left uncovered, and repositioned every 2 to 4 hours. A dry cast sounds hollow.
explanations: Fingertips cause dents and pressure points.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q365 (PDF p. 533)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which group of findings is typical of nephrotic syndrome in a child?
questions.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome causes edema, proteinuria, and hypoalbuminemia, with weight gain, anorexia, and abdominal pain. Blood pressure is usually normal or slightly low.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q367 (PDF p. 535)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with intussusception passes a normal, formed brown stool. What should the nurse do?
options: Report it to the physician at once
questions.rationale: A normal brown stool usually means the intussusception has reduced itself. This is reported at once because the plan may change.
explanations: The finding needs to be reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q455 (PDF p. 635)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with autism spectrum disorder will attend a day care center. What is the PRIORITY when planning the child's activities?
questions.rationale: A child with autism may not anticipate danger, may self-injure, and has sensory-perceptual deficits, so safety comes first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q495 (PDF p. 688)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Maya, 6, is admitted for tonic-clonic seizures. Nurse Gino is preparing her room and care plan.
questions.stem: Which items should Nurse Gino place at the bedside?
questions.rationale: Airway obstruction and increased oral secretions are the main complications during and after a seizure. Suction prevents choking, and oxygen prevents hypoxia.
explanations: Not routinely needed at the bedside.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q498 (PDF p. 691)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Maya, 6, is admitted for tonic-clonic seizures. Nurse Gino is preparing her room and care plan.
questions.stem: Which planned intervention is UNSAFE for Maya?
options: Keep the bed in the low position
Restrain her limbs during a seizure
Pad the side rails of the bed
Turn her to her side during a seizure
questions.rationale: Restraints can injure a child during a seizure. The bed is kept low, side rails are padded, and the child is turned to the side so saliva drains out.
explanations: Correct answer: restraints can cause injury.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q496 (PDF p. 689)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child is admitted for removal of a malignant brain tumor. Which action ensures a safe environment?
options: Use a wheelchair for all activity
Assist with walking at all times
questions.rationale: Seizure precautions are used before and after surgery for any child with a brain tumor. Mobility aids are needed only if deficits exist.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q507 (PDF p. 702)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An adolescent with conjunctivitis wears contact lenses. Which instruction is MOST appropriate?
options: Get a new set of contact lenses
questions.rationale: A new set of lenses prevents reinfection. Eye makeup is replaced, not banned. Cool compresses ease pain, and isolation lasts 24 hours after starting antibiotics.
explanations: Makeup is replaced, not avoided forever.
Cool, not hot, compresses are used.
Isolation is needed for 24 hours on antibiotics.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q522 (PDF p. 717)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which home-care plan by a mother of a child with croup is CORRECT?
options: Give sips of warm fluids during an attack
questions.rationale: Warm fluids relax the vocal cords and thin mucus. Cough syrups and cold medicines dry and thicken secretions. A cool-mist humidifier is safer than a steam vaporizer.
explanations: Risk of burns; use cool mist.
Correct: warm fluids ease the attack.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q635 (PDF p. 853)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which discharge instruction is correct after a child's heart surgery?
options: Rub lotion and powder on the incision
Play outside every day after discharge
questions.rationale: A fever above 38°C (100.5°F) is reported. No lotions or powders go on the incision until it heals, outdoor play is restricted for several weeks, and school resumes about 3 weeks after discharge.
explanations: Nothing is applied until it is healed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q638 (PDF p. 856)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement by the parent of a 3-year-old with hemophilia shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll pad the corners of our tables.'
questions.rationale: Immunizations, dental hygiene, and routine well-child care are important in hemophilia. Supervision and a safe home environment prevent injury.
explanations: Correct answer: immunizations are still needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q650 (PDF p. 868)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An 8-year-old who had a tonsillectomy loves crispy tacos. When can the child safely eat rough, scratchy foods again?
options: Right away if there is no pain
questions.rationale: Rough, scratchy, and spicy foods are avoided for 3 weeks after tonsillectomy. Citrus is avoided for 10 days. Full liquids start on day 2, then soft foods as tolerated.
explanations: Correct: avoid rough foods for 3 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q699 (PDF p. 921)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child awaiting umbilical hernia repair goes home. Which sign of strangulation should make the parents call the physician immediately?
questions.rationale: Signs of strangulation include vomiting, pain, and an irreducible mass at the umbilicus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q701 (PDF p. 923)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a child with celiac disease asks how long the special diet is needed. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a lifelong intolerance to gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats). Treatment is mainly dietary management with a gluten-free diet.
explanations: Gluten must stay excluded even after symptoms settle.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q703 (PDF p. 925)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Parents are preparing children for an outdoor camp. Which statement shows they need MORE teaching on sun protection?
options: 'No sunscreen is needed on cloudy days.'
'I'll reapply it at least every 2 hours.'
'They will wear hats and long sleeves.'
questions.rationale: The sun's rays damage skin as much on cloudy, hazy days. Sunscreen is applied before exposure and reapplied at least every 2 hours, and protective clothing is worn.
explanations: Correct answer: UV rays penetrate clouds.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q744 (PDF p. 972)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement by parents of a child discharged after glomerulonephritis shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'We'll test the urine for albumin weekly.'
'She can start dance class next week.'
'We'll make sure she gets enough rest.'
questions.rationale: Children return to normal routines gradually, with adequate rest. Strenuous activity one week after discharge is too rapid. Daily BP checks and weekly urine albumin tests are appropriate.
explanations: Correct answer: too rapid an increase in activity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q768 (PDF p. 998)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 3-year-old with chickenpox scratches at night. Which statement by the mother shows the teaching worked?
options: 'I'll put cotton gloves on her at night.'
'I'll apply lots of cream all over her.'
'I'll give her warm milk at bedtime.'
'I'll keep her room warm and cozy.'
questions.rationale: Gloves stop scratching from damaging the skin. Large amounts of topical cream can cause toxicity, and a warm room worsens itching.
explanations: Correct: prevents skin damage from scratching.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q780 (PDF p. 1010)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 1-month-old is hospitalized with intussusception. Which measure BEST supports the parent-child relationship?
options: Advise the parents to rest at home
questions.rationale: Rooming-in reduces separation anxiety and preserves the parent-child bond. Sending stressed parents home does not support the relationship.
explanations: Correct: keeps parent and child together.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q893 (PDF p. 1135)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Before an infant boy's inguinal hernia repair, which parent comment needs follow-up teaching?
options: 'He may not be able to father a child someday.'
'He can go home the same day.'
questions.rationale: The location of a hernia often worries parents more than the condition itself. The concern about future fertility is a misconception that needs follow-up.
explanations: Correct answer: a misconception to address.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q894 (PDF p. 1136)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother says, 'I'm afraid my child will have another febrile seizure.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Tell me what frightens you most about seizures.'
'Most children never have a second one.'
questions.rationale: An open-ended statement lets the mother express her feelings. Promising that a seizure will not recur, or dismissing her fear, blocks communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q931 (PDF p. 1175)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of an infant with chalasia (reflux) says, 'I must be causing her to vomit.' How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Lack of bonding with the baby
questions.rationale: The vomiting is caused by a physiological problem, not by the mother. Blaming herself is an unrealistic expectation that can lower her confidence as a parent, so the nurse helps her see she is not responsible.
explanations: She accepts the problem but blames herself.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q933 (PDF p. 1177)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother of a preschooler with impetigo says, 'But my children take baths every day.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You're concerned about how she got impetigo?'
'We won't tell the day care why she's absent.'
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing the mother's statement addresses her concern. The other responses make the parent feel guilty and block communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q974 (PDF p. 1223)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother and her infant have just tested HIV-positive, and the mother is crying. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask how she was exposed to HIV
Sit quietly and listen as she talks and cries
Call the HIV counselor right away
questions.rationale: After devastating news, the client needs someone present as she begins to cope. The nurse sits with her and listens. Teaching and referral come later.
explanations: Helpful later, but not her immediate need.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1020 (PDF p. 1293)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding supports a diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome in a child?
options: Profuse watery diarrhea with daily vomiting
Diffuse abdominal pain unrelated to meals
questions.rationale: IBS causes diffuse abdominal pain unrelated to meals or activity, with alternating constipation and diarrhea. Frothy diarrhea suggests lactose intolerance; ribbon stools suggest Hirschsprung's disease.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1088 (PDF p. 1370)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is MOST typical of von Willebrand disease?
questions.rationale: Von Willebrand disease mainly causes bruising and mucous membrane bleeding (nose, mouth, GI tract), and menorrhagia in females. Joint bleeding is typical of hemophilia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1091 (PDF p. 1374)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Ely, 7, fell from a mango tree and is admitted with a head injury.
questions.stem: The nurse documents that Ely is 'obtunded.' What did the nurse observe?
options: He cannot think clearly or quickly
He does not recognize place or person
He sleeps unless aroused, with limited response
He responds only to vigorous pain
questions.rationale: An obtunded child sleeps unless aroused and, when aroused, interacts little with the environment. The other options describe confusion, disorientation, and stupor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1093 (PDF p. 1376)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Ely, 7, fell from a mango tree and is admitted with a head injury.
questions.stem: A CT scan shows a basilar skull fracture, and the physician notes Battle's sign. What will the nurse observe?
questions.rationale: Battle's sign is bruising behind the ear from blood leaking into the mastoid sinuses. 'Raccoon eyes' (periorbital bruising) is the other classic sign of basilar fracture.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1110 (PDF p. 1394)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with kidney disease has a serum sodium of 148 mEq/L. Which finding does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Hypernatremia (above 145 mEq/L) causes intense thirst, oliguria, agitation, flushed skin, edema, dry sticky mucous membranes, and nausea.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1117 (PDF p. 1401)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which laboratory finding does the nurse expect in an infant with hemolytic disease of the newborn?
questions.rationale: Hemolytic disease causes anemia (red cell production cannot keep up with destruction) and hyperbilirubinemia, made worse by the newborn liver's limited ability to process bilirubin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1118 (PDF p. 1402)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Bea, 5, has purpura and nosebleeds and is admitted for suspected idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
questions.stem: Which laboratory result is consistent with ITP?
options: A low white blood cell count
questions.rationale: ITP shows a low platelet count (usually below 20,000/mm3) as the only expected abnormality. A bone marrow exam shows normal or increased megakaryocytes.
explanations: Anemia occurs only with significant blood loss.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1137 (PDF p. 1423)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Bea, 5, has purpura and nosebleeds and is admitted for suspected idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
questions.stem: Bea is given IV immune globulin (IVIG). Which result shows the therapy is working?
options: A rapid rise in the platelet count
A drop in the white cell count
questions.rationale: IVIG usually raises the platelet count quickly by interfering with the destruction of antibody-coated platelets by macrophages.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1119 (PDF p. 1403)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which urinalysis finding does the nurse expect in a child with acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis?
options: Clear urine with no red cells
Hematuria with red cell casts and protein
Large amounts of white cell casts only
questions.rationale: Urinalysis in poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis shows hematuria with red cell casts and proteinuria. BUN and creatinine rise if renal insufficiency is severe.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1120 (PDF p. 1404)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which test primarily confirms bacterial endocarditis in a child with fever, malaise, and anorexia?
questions.rationale: Diagnosis rests mainly on a positive blood culture and vegetations seen on echocardiography. ESR and CRP may support it, and the ECG is usually not helpful.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1121 (PDF p. 1405)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY problem for a child with juvenile idiopathic arthritis during a flare?
questions.rationale: All of these problems apply, but acute pain must be managed before the others can be addressed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1136 (PDF p. 1422)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Luis, 5 weeks old, has projectile vomiting after feedings that is getting more frequent and forceful.
questions.stem: The nurse sees peristaltic waves moving left to right across his abdomen. Which condition is suspected?
questions.rationale: Pyloric stenosis causes forceful, nonbilious vomiting, constipation, visible left-to-right peristaltic waves, and sometimes an olive-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant.
explanations: Colicky infants eat well and gain weight.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1138 (PDF p. 1424)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Luis, 5 weeks old, has projectile vomiting after feedings that is getting more frequent and forceful.
questions.stem: Luis is scheduled for pyloromyotomy. Which preoperative intervention is MOST important?
options: Give enemas until returns are clear
questions.rationale: Before surgery the infant is usually NPO on IV fluids. The nurse monitors the IV, intake, output, weight, and urine specific gravity, and weighs diapers. Enemas would worsen fluid loss.
explanations: Infant is usually kept NPO preoperatively.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1159 (PDF p. 1446)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which cerebrospinal fluid result MOST supports bacterial meningitis?
options: Clear, with low protein and low glucose
Cloudy, with low protein and low glucose
Cloudy, with high protein and low glucose
questions.rationale: Bacterial meningitis shows increased pressure and cloudy CSF with high protein and low glucose, because bacteria consume glucose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1139 (PDF p. 1425)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A teacher reports that an alert, attentive 7-year-old often stares into space for a few seconds, then resumes activity. What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Absence seizures are brief (5 to 10 seconds) arrests of activity with a blank stare and loss of awareness. The child keeps their posture and resumes the activity as if nothing happened.
explanations: Presents with physical complaints before school.
Not brief staring spells with loss of awareness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1141 (PDF p. 1427)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has bilateral clubfoot. Which information should the nurse include in parent teaching?
options: Casting cures every case of clubfoot
Surgery is done in the first week of life
Casting starts at birth and lasts at least 12 weeks
Treatment waits until the child walks
questions.rationale: Casting begins at birth and continues for at least 12 weeks or until maximum correction. Corrective shoes or surgery (usually at 4 to 12 months) may follow.
explanations: Surgery is usually delayed until 4 to 12 months.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1154 (PDF p. 1441)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother asks what 'carditis' means in her child with rheumatic fever. The nurse explains that carditis is:
options: Involuntary movements of the face and limbs
Inflammation of the heart, mainly the mitral valve
Painful swelling of several large joints
A pink, ring-shaped rash on the trunk
questions.rationale: Carditis is inflammation of all parts of the heart, mainly the mitral valve. Chorea, polyarthritis, and erythema marginatum are other manifestations.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1161 (PDF p. 1448)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with Reye's syndrome is admitted. Which nursing action is the PRIORITY?
options: Keep the room quiet with dim lights
questions.rationale: Cerebral edema progresses in Reye's syndrome, so maintaining cerebral perfusion and controlling ICP is the priority. Reducing environmental stimuli lowers stress on brain tissue.
explanations: Correct: reduces stimuli that raise ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1164 (PDF p. 1451)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes cerebral palsy?
options: An infection of the central nervous system
Brain inflammation after a viral illness
Chronic difficulty controlling muscles from a motor-system abnormality
A chromosomal disorder with intellectual disability
questions.rationale: Cerebral palsy is a chronic disability with difficulty controlling the muscles because of an abnormality in the pyramidal or extrapyramidal motor system. Meningitis is an infection, and encephalitis is inflammation.
explanations: Correct: the definition of cerebral palsy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1165 (PDF p. 1452)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which characteristic is PRIMARY in autism spectrum disorder?
options: Normal social play that stops at age 5
Lack of social interaction and awareness
questions.rationale: Autism begins in infancy or toddlerhood, and its primary characteristic is a lack of social interaction and awareness. Imitation and social play are absent or abnormal, and verbal communication is impaired.
explanations: Social play is absent or abnormal from the start.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1166 (PDF p. 1453)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with leukemia is starting chemotherapy. Which intervention belongs in the care plan?
options: Check the mouth and anus each shift for breakdown
Use a firm toothbrush for oral care
questions.rationale: The mouth and anus are checked each shift for ulcers or breakdown. Rectal temperatures are avoided, and bland, nonirritating foods are given.
explanations: Rectal temperatures risk injury and infection.
Correct: early detection of mucosal breakdown.
A soft swab or brush is used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1169 (PDF p. 1456)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with leukemia has a platelet count of 20,000/mm3. Which intervention should be AVOIDED?
options: Cleaning the mouth with soft swabs
questions.rationale: With this low platelet count, the child is at risk for bleeding. Rectal temperatures and suppositories are avoided; stools are checked for blood and soft swabs are used for mouth care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1302 (PDF p. 1603)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should an infant be positioned after pyloromyotomy?
options: Prone with the head of the bed raised
questions.rationale: After pyloromyotomy, the head of the bed is raised and the infant placed prone to reduce the risk of aspiration, unless the surgeon orders otherwise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1187 (PDF p. 1479)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Rico, 10, is admitted in vaso-occlusive pain crisis from sickle cell anemia.
questions.stem: Which prescription should the nurse question?
questions.rationale: Meperidine is contraindicated for ongoing pain because of the risk of seizures. Strong opioids such as morphine or hydromorphone are used, along with fluids, oxygen, and rest.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1189 (PDF p. 1481)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which position reduces stridor in an infant with laryngomalacia?
questions.rationale: The prone position with the neck hyperextended improves breathing in laryngomalacia. A child in respiratory difficulty is never left unattended.
explanations: Without hyperextension it is less effective.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1190 (PDF p. 1482)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has an occipital encephalocele. Which item helps position the infant without pressure on the sac?
questions.rationale: A foam half-donut keeps pressure off an occipital encephalocele. The other items do not protect the lesion.
explanations: Correct: relieves pressure on the sac.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1193 (PDF p. 1485)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a child with hepatitis B calls because the jaundice seems worse. What should the nurse tell her?
options: 'Jaundice can look worse before it clears.'
'Bring your child to the ER now.'
questions.rationale: Jaundice may appear to worsen before it resolves. Parents are taught the true danger signs: changes in neurologic status, bleeding, and fluid retention.
explanations: Not needed unless danger signs appear.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1195 (PDF p. 1487)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding BEST shows that a gluten-free diet is working for a child with celiac disease?
options: The child is free of diarrhea
The child has no bloody stools
The child tolerates wheat and rye
questions.rationale: Watery diarrhea is a frequent sign of celiac disease, so its absence shows effective treatment. Bloody stools are not part of the disease.
explanations: Correct: diarrhea resolves with the diet.
Not a feature of celiac disease.
