questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1217 (PDF p. 1510)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has strabismus of the LEFT eye. Which statement shows the mother understands patching?
questions.rationale: The good (right) eye is patched to force use of the weak (left) eye. Patching works best during the preschool years.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1221 (PDF p. 1514)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which intervention in a care plan for an infant with congestive heart failure needs revision?
options: Elevate the head of the bed
Limit the time for each feeding
Wake the infant hourly to check vital signs
questions.rationale: Measures that reduce cardiac workload include elevating the head, limiting feeding time, uninterrupted rest, and oxygen during stress. Waking the infant often is not therapeutic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1247 (PDF p. 1543)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which action by a student caring for a child with a head injury needs correction?
options: Keeping the child awake as ordered
questions.rationale: Forcing fluids can cause fluid overload and raise ICP. Neurologic checks, an upright position for drainage, and keeping the child awake for assessment are appropriate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1292 (PDF p. 1593)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is associated with hydrocephalus in a 6-month-old?
questions.rationale: A bulging anterior fontanel reflects increased CSF in the ventricles. Infants also have thin, widely separated skull bones.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1332 (PDF p. 1634)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother asks what Kawasaki disease is. The nurse explains that it is:
options: A chronic autoimmune disease of connective tissue
A febrile generalized vasculitis of unknown cause
A reaction to a strep throat infection
questions.rationale: Kawasaki disease (mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a febrile generalized vasculitis of unknown cause. Its most serious complication is cardiac involvement, including coronary aneurysms.
explanations: Correct: the definition of Kawasaki disease.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1338 (PDF p. 1641)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a child with iron deficiency anemia ask which foods have iron the body absorbs MOST easily. The nurse recommends:
questions.rationale: Iron from meat, poultry, and fish is absorbed most easily. Vegetables, fruits, cereals, and breads contain iron that is harder to absorb.
explanations: Correct: heme iron is easily absorbed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1339 (PDF p. 1642)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement describes patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)?
options: A defect in the atrial septum
questions.rationale: The ductus arteriosus connects the aorta and pulmonary artery in fetal life and normally closes after birth. If it stays open, blood shunts from the high-pressure aorta to the pulmonary artery (left-to-right shunt).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1340 (PDF p. 1643)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is consistent with congenital hypothyroidism in an infant?
options: A hoarse cry and excessive sleeping
questions.rationale: Congenital hypothyroidism can cause a hoarse cry, excessive sleeping, bradycardia, constipation, a large tongue and fontanel, hypotonia, prolonged jaundice, and feeding problems.
explanations: The infant is lethargic, not irritable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1341 (PDF p. 1644)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child's tympanostomy tube falls out at home. What should the nurse tell the parent?
options: 'It's not an emergency, but call the clinic.'
'Push it back into the ear gently.'
questions.rationale: A tube falling out is not an emergency, but the provider should be notified. Parents are shown the tube's size and appearance after surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1344 (PDF p. 1647)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has a nosebleed. What should the nurse tell the parent to do?
options: Sit up, lean forward, pinch for 10 minutes
questions.rationale: The child sits upright with the head tilted forward so blood does not run into the pharynx. The soft part of the nose is pinched for a full 10 minutes, timed by a clock.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1345 (PDF p. 1648)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: When assessing a child admitted with rheumatic fever, which question is MOST significant?
options: 'Has anyone at home had a sore throat recently?'
'Has your child had a recent vaccine?'
questions.rationale: Rheumatic fever appears 2 to 6 weeks after an untreated or partly treated group A streptococcal throat infection, so the nurse asks about recent sore throats or unexplained fever in the family.
explanations: Correct: identifies a preceding strep infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1346 (PDF p. 1649)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which findings should the nurse expect in a client with abruptio placentae?
options: Uterine tenderness with abdominal and back pain
A soft, relaxed uterus between contractions
questions.rationale: Abruptio placentae is early separation of a normally implanted placenta. It causes uterine irritability with frequent low-intensity contractions, uterine tenderness, abdominal and low back pain, and nonreassuring fetal heart patterns. Painless bleeding suggests placenta previa.
explanations: The uterus is irritable and tender.
Contractions are frequent and of low intensity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q6 (PDF p. 143)

questions.stem: In the second trimester, how does fundal height usually relate to gestational age?
options: It is less than gestational age
It is greater than gestational age
It has no relation to gestational age
questions.rationale: Until the third trimester, fundal height in centimeters on average correlates with gestational age in weeks. Consistent technique, ideally by the same examiner, improves reliability.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q14 (PDF p. 152)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A laboring client feels wetness, and the nurse sees the umbilical cord at the perineum. What is the IMMEDIATE action?
options: Check the fetal heart rate first
Move her to the delivery room
questions.rationale: For cord prolapse, the nurse immediately places the client in Trendelenburg and gently holds the presenting part up to relieve cord compression. The nurse keeps this position while the physician is notified and the fetal heart rate is monitored.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q15 (PDF p. 153)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: On admission to the nursery, a newborn's anterior fontanel feels soft. How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: The anterior fontanel is diamond-shaped, about 2 to 3 cm wide and 3 to 4 cm long, and normally soft. A full or bulging fontanel may mean increased ICP; a depressed one, dehydration.
explanations: A bulging fontanel suggests increased ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q16 (PDF p. 154)

questions.stem: A pregnant client has a vaginal Candida albicans infection. What does the nurse expect to find?
questions.rationale: Candida infection causes pain, itching, and a thick white vaginal discharge. Proteinuria and hypertension suggest preeclampsia; CVA pain suggests an upper urinary tract infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q25 (PDF p. 164)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which laboratory finding supports iron deficiency anemia in a pregnant client?
questions.rationale: Iron deficiency is the main cause of pathological anemia in pregnancy and is suspected when hemoglobin falls below 11 g/dL.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q26 (PDF p. 165)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding should make the nurse suspect endometritis in a postpartum client?
options: Lochia rubra on the second day
Fever of 38°C for 2 days in a row
questions.rationale: A fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher on 2 successive days within the first 10 postpartum days, not counting the first 24 hours, indicates postpartum infection. A mildly high WBC and engorgement can be normal.
explanations: The WBC is normally elevated postpartum.
Correct: the criterion for puerperal infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q27 (PDF p. 166)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Rafael was born at 43 weeks' gestation by vaginal delivery. The amniotic fluid was meconium-stained.
questions.stem: Which physical characteristic does the nurse expect in Baby Rafael?
questions.rationale: A postterm infant (after 42 weeks) has dry, peeling, cracked, almost leathery skin (desquamation). Smooth soles, abundant lanugo, and thick vernix are signs of a preterm infant.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q28 (PDF p. 167)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Rafael was born at 43 weeks' gestation by vaginal delivery. The amniotic fluid was meconium-stained.
questions.stem: Baby Rafael develops tachypnea, grunting, retractions, and nasal flaring. What does the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Meconium aspiration syndrome is common in postterm infants and occurs when meconium in the amniotic fluid enters the lungs. RDS is a complication of preterm infants.
explanations: Correct: postterm infant with meconium-stained fluid.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q29 (PDF p. 168)

questions.stem: A client's last menstrual period began June 20, 2026. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of birth?
questions.rationale: Naegele's rule: subtract 3 months from the first day of the LMP, add 7 days, and adjust the year. June 20 minus 3 months is March 20; plus 7 days is March 27, 2027. It assumes a regular 28-day cycle.
explanations: Subtracts 7 days instead of adding them.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q92 (PDF p. 240)

questions.stem: How should the client be positioned for a fundal height measurement at 28 weeks?
questions.rationale: Fundal height is measured with the client supine, head on a pillow, and knees slightly flexed. Other positions prevent an accurate measurement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q94 (PDF p. 242)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which action prevents heat loss by CONDUCTION in a newborn?
options: Wrapping the baby in a blanket
Drying the baby with a warm towel
Placing the baby on a warmed surface
questions.rationale: Conduction is heat loss to a cold surface the baby touches, so a warmed surface prevents it. Closing doors prevents convection, and drying prevents evaporation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q103 (PDF p. 252)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding in a preterm newborn is NORMAL and not a sign of respiratory distress syndrome?
questions.rationale: RDS shows cyanosis, tachypnea or apnea, retractions, grunting, and nasal flaring. Acrocyanosis (bluish hands and feet) reflects immature peripheral circulation and is common in the first hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q108 (PDF p. 257)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which apical heart rate is normal for a newborn?
questions.rationale: The normal newborn heart rate is about 100 to 160 beats per minute, auscultated at the fourth intercostal space for a full minute.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q109 (PDF p. 258)

questions.stem: Which observation during breastfeeding suggests a problem with the infant's latch?
questions.rationale: Infant signs of breastfeeding problems include dimpled cheeks, smacking or clicking sounds, falling asleep after less than 5 minutes, refusing the breast, and tongue thrusting.
explanations: A sign of effective milk transfer.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q130 (PDF p. 280)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which newborn respiratory finding is NORMAL?
options: 46 breaths per minute while awake and quiet
questions.rationale: Normal newborn respirations are 30 to 50 per minute when not crying. They are counted for a full minute because newborns breathe periodically.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q158 (PDF p. 309)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client in the third trimester has calf pain when walking. Which sign supports superficial thrombophlebitis?
questions.rationale: Superficial thrombophlebitis shows a palpable, bumpy, hard thrombus with tenderness, pain, and warm, pinkish-red skin over it. Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs test for meningeal irritation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q159 (PDF p. 310)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: At 32 weeks, a client admitted after a road crash develops slight vaginal bleeding and mild cramps. Which action BEST supports fetal viability?
options: Insert an internal fetal scalp electrode
questions.rationale: External fetal monitoring detects changes in fetal heart rate and rhythm that show fetal jeopardy. Internal monitoring is contraindicated with vaginal bleeding, and oxygen is premature without fetal distress.
explanations: The bleeding is not enough to need IV replacement yet.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q193 (PDF p. 347)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client at 33 weeks has premature rupture of membranes. Which is a MAJOR part of her nursing care?
questions.rationale: Monitoring for infection is a major part of care in PROM. Biophysical profiles assess the fetus and amniotic fluid, and daily fetal movement counts are taught.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q245 (PDF p. 400)

questions.stem: Which statement about prenatal nutrition is accurate?
options: All pregnant women are at high nutritional risk
Calcium intake should rise from early pregnancy
Calcium is needed only in the third trimester
Iron supplements are only for anemic women
questions.rationale: Calcium is critical in the third trimester but intake must increase from the start of pregnancy. Dietary iron is usually insufficient, so supplements are routinely recommended.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q247 (PDF p. 402)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A client has hypertonic labor contractions. Which action BEST conserves her energy and promotes rest?
options: Keep the TV on for distraction
questions.rationale: Breathing and relaxation techniques help the client cope and conserve energy. A quiet, dim room promotes rest; noise and bright light do not.
explanations: Correct: helps her cope and rest.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q265 (PDF p. 422)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: At 30 weeks, why does the nurse auscultate the lower lung lobes of a pregnant client with heart disease?
questions.rationale: Blood volume peaks at 18 to 32 weeks. Crackles in the lower lobes can be an early sign of cardiac decompensation and heart failure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q286 (PDF p. 444)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.situation: Aling Marites, 38, G3P2 at 36 weeks, is admitted with severe preeclampsia.
questions.stem: Which complication should the nurse monitor her for MOST closely?
questions.rationale: Gestational hypertension can progress to preeclampsia and eclampsia, so seizures are a major complication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q293 (PDF p. 455)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.situation: Aling Marites, 38, G3P2 at 36 weeks, is admitted with severe preeclampsia.
questions.stem: Aling Marites suddenly has a seizure. What is the nurse's FIRST action?
options: Check the BP and fetal heart tones
questions.rationale: Eclampsia is marked by seizures. The first action is to establish and maintain an airway and prevent injury. The nurse never leaves the client.
explanations: Done after the airway is secured.
Done after the airway is secured.
Done after the airway is secured.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q329 (PDF p. 494)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which maternal history factor increases the newborn's risk of neonatal sepsis?
questions.rationale: Risk factors include prolonged or premature rupture of membranes (over 18 hours), poor or late prenatal care, substance use, low socioeconomic status, and poor nutrition.
explanations: Correct: prolonged rupture raises infection risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q299 (PDF p. 462)

questions.stem: Why must a client who drinks alcohol in the FIRST trimester stop right away?
options: Organs form during the first trimester
Alcohol only matters in the third trimester
It mainly affects the mother's liver
It only causes low birth weight
questions.rationale: The first trimester is organogenesis, when fetal organs and systems form, so alcohol exposure then is especially harmful.
explanations: The effects go beyond birth weight.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q300 (PDF p. 463)

questions.stem: What does the FIRST Leopold maneuver (fundal grip) determine?
questions.rationale: The first maneuver feels what occupies the fundus (head or breech), which shows the fetal lie and presentation. Descent is assessed in the fourth maneuver. Leopold maneuvers are not done during a contraction.
explanations: Correct: the fundal contents show lie and presentation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q306 (PDF p. 470)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which history supports a risk for gestational diabetes?
options: Tiredness after a day of work
questions.rationale: A history of unexplained miscarriages or stillbirths puts a client at high risk for gestational diabetes. Fatigue is normal in pregnancy, and a normal weight is not a risk factor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q328 (PDF p. 493)

questions.stem: Which equipment does the nurse routinely use to hear the fetal heart rate at 16 weeks?
questions.rationale: From near the end of the first trimester, fetal heart tones can be heard with an ultrasound (Doppler) device. Continuous monitors are for labor. The normal FHR is 120 to 160 bpm.
explanations: Used in labor or special situations.
Correct: detects FHR from about 10 to 12 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q336 (PDF p. 504)

questions.stem: Which action BEST helps prevent jaundice in a breastfed newborn?
options: No feeding until the second period of reactivity
questions.rationale: Frequent early breastfeeding helps prevent jaundice because colostrum is a natural laxative that promotes passage of meconium, and with it bilirubin.
explanations: Delaying feeding worsens jaundice and milk supply.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q351 (PDF p. 519)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A large-for-gestational-age newborn of a diabetic mother is admitted. Which test should the nurse prepare to do?
questions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is the most common problem in LGA infants, especially of diabetic mothers. Once the cord is cut, maternal glucose stops but the baby keeps producing high insulin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q356 (PDF p. 524)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has a subdural hematoma. Which assessment detects its primary sign?
options: Comparing movement of the right and left limbs
questions.rationale: A subdural hematoma presses on part of the brain and changes stimulus responses in the limbs on the opposite side of the body. Blood in the urine suggests abdominal trauma.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q376 (PDF p. 544)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client in active labor has a history of genital herpes and active lesions. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: With active herpetic lesions in labor, a cesarean delivery lowers the risk of neonatal infection. Intact membranes are another barrier. Only standard precautions are needed.
explanations: Intact membranes help protect the baby.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q412 (PDF p. 589)

questions.stem: A pregnant client who is hepatitis B positive asks if she can breastfeed. What is the nurse's BEST response?
questions.rationale: Breastfeeding is not contraindicated in hepatitis B if the infant receives prophylaxis at birth (vaccine and HBIG) and stays on the immunization schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q492 (PDF p. 684)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which position gives the BEST uteroplacental perfusion during a cesarean delivery?
questions.rationale: The pregnant uterus compresses the vena cava and aorta when the client lies supine. Surgery requires a supine position, so a wedge under the right hip displaces the uterus off the vessels.
explanations: Correct: displaces the uterus to the left.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q494 (PDF p. 687)

questions.stem: A pregnant client with a positive rubella titer asks if her toddler can get the MMR vaccine now. What should the nurse say?
options: 'Wait until the toddler is 5 years old.'
'Wait until after your baby is born.'
'Yes, children should get vaccines on schedule.'
questions.rationale: A positive titer means the mother has antibodies from past exposure. All children of pregnant women should be immunized on schedule, and there is no definitive evidence that the vaccine virus spreads person to person.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q509 (PDF p. 704)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which statement by a 17-year-old new mother shows she needs MORE teaching on infant safety?
options: 'Aluminum pots can stay in low cabinets.'
'I won't heat formula in the microwave.'
'I'll keep small objects out of reach.'
'The car seat goes in the front seat.'
questions.rationale: An infant car seat should never be placed in the front seat because of the risk of life-threatening injury on impact. Microwaves heat formula unevenly and can burn the baby.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q517 (PDF p. 712)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which action provides a safe environment for a client with preeclampsia?
options: Dim the lights and keep the room quiet
questions.rationale: Bright lights and sudden noise can trigger seizures in preeclampsia, so the client is placed in a dim, quiet, private room. Adequate fluids and sodium are needed because plasma volume is decreased.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q553 (PDF p. 754)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When MUST the nurse check the fetal heart rate during labor?
options: After ROM or a vaginal exam
questions.rationale: The FHR is checked before ambulation, right after vaginal exams, rupture of membranes, or any invasive procedure, and before oxytocin is given, because these can change the FHR.
explanations: Assessment is more frequent and event-based.
Correct: events that can alter the FHR.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q601 (PDF p. 810)

questions.stem: Which breastfeeding technique by a new mother shows she needs MORE teaching?
options: Turning the baby on his side to face her
Tilting her nipple up and pushing it into his mouth
Bringing the baby to the breast
Breaking suction with a finger before removing him
questions.rationale: Tilting the nipple or squeezing the areola and pushing it into the baby's mouth causes improper latch and poor milk flow. The other techniques are appropriate.
explanations: Correct answer: leads to improper latch.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q634 (PDF p. 852)

questions.stem: Which measure relieves heartburn in the third trimester?
questions.rationale: Heartburn relief includes frequent sips of milk or hot tea, small frequent meals, and avoiding fatty or fried foods, coffee, and cigarettes. Antacids without aspirin or sodium may be used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q649 (PDF p. 867)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a pregnant client understands UTI prevention?
options: 'I'll wear underwear with a cotton liner.'
'A bubble bath is relaxing and fine.'
questions.rationale: A cotton liner lets air circulate. Tight clothing, scented toilet paper, and bubble baths irritate the genital area and urethra.
explanations: Tight clothes trap moisture and irritate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q691 (PDF p. 912)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client with mild preeclampsia is managed at home. Which finding should she report right away?
options: Weight gain of more than 0.5 kg in a week
Mild ankle swelling at day's end
questions.rationale: She reports any rise in blood pressure, 2+ proteinuria, weight gain over 1 pound (about 0.5 kg) per week, edema of the face, hands, or sacrum, and decreased fetal activity.
explanations: Correct: a sign of worsening fluid retention.
Decreased, not increased, movement is reportable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q692 (PDF p. 913)

questions.stem: A postpartum mother with a UTI asks which drink makes her urine MORE alkaline. The nurse answers:
questions.rationale: Acidic urine slows bacterial growth. Carbonated drinks make urine more alkaline; prune, apricot, and cranberry juices acidify it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q694 (PDF p. 915)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which cord-care instruction should the nurse give a new mother?
options: Cover the cord with the diaper
Keep the cord clean and dry, diaper folded below it
Bathe the baby in a tub daily before it falls off
Expect it to take at least 21 days to fall off
questions.rationale: The cord is kept clean and dry to limit bacterial growth, with the diaper folded below it so urine and stool do not soil it. Odor, discharge, or redness is reported.
explanations: A wet diaper contaminates the cord.
Not appropriate before the cord falls off.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q696 (PDF p. 918)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which statement shows a mother understands care after her baby's circumcision?
options: 'I'll clean it hourly with baby wipes.'
'I'll check for bleeding every hour for 12 hours.'
'I'll wash it with soap at each change.'
questions.rationale: The site is checked for bleeding hourly for 8 to 12 hours and cleaned with water only. The provider is called if the baby has not voided within 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q704 (PDF p. 926)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: When should discharge planning begin for a preterm infant?
options: While the mother is in labor
Once a discharge date is set
questions.rationale: Discharge planning starts early, after the infant is stabilized, so services, supplies, and equipment can be arranged well before discharge.
explanations: The outcome of delivery is not yet known.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q724 (PDF p. 946)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which statement by a pregnant client with diabetes shows she understands the potential complications?
options: 'I have a higher risk of gestational hypertension.'
'My baby will be smaller than average.'
questions.rationale: Pregnant clients with diabetes have a higher incidence of gestational hypertension. Ultrasounds are done often to check for anomalies and growth, and hypoglycemia is a risk throughout pregnancy.
explanations: Babies of diabetic mothers are often large.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q737 (PDF p. 962)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What should the nurse teach a mother about feeding her large-for-gestational-age infant?
options: LGA babies wake themselves for feeds
He may need waking for feedings
questions.rationale: LGA infants look mature but tend to be hard to arouse, so they are woken for feedings about every 2.5 to 3 hours to support nutrition and bonding.
explanations: They are often hard to arouse.
He may not cry often enough.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q746 (PDF p. 974)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: In a prenatal class, what is the MOST effective way to promote early intervention for congenital hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Congenital hypothyroidism is a preventable cause of cognitive impairment. Newborn screening is the only means of early diagnosis, so treatment can begin immediately.
explanations: Correct: early detection allows early treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q756 (PDF p. 985)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What should the nurse tell a client about precipitous labor?
options: It may last less than 3 hours
It needs a long pushing period
questions.rationale: Precipitous labor lasts 3 hours or less from start to delivery and usually begins abruptly. Oxytocin induction is contraindicated because it overstimulates the uterus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q766 (PDF p. 995)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client is taught how to prevent another episode of preterm labor. Which statement needs correction?
questions.rationale: Dehydration is a risk factor for preterm labor, so fluids are not restricted (except alcohol and caffeine). Pelvic pressure can signal preterm labor, and intercourse can stimulate contractions.
explanations: Correct answer: dehydration can trigger preterm labor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q767 (PDF p. 997)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client who just learned she is HIV-positive is crying and very distressed. Which concern does this BEST support?
questions.rationale: A life-threatening diagnosis triggers anticipatory grief for lost future plans and diminished self-esteem.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q844 (PDF p. 1081)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client with mitral stenosis is anxious and asks about each assessment. What should the nurse do?
options: Tell her not to worry so much
Refer her to a counselor now
questions.rationale: Stress should be reduced as much as possible in a pregnant cardiac client. Honest, informed answers and explanations of nursing actions ease fear and emotional stress.
explanations: Correct: reduces stress on the heart.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q878 (PDF p. 1117)

questions.stem: A mother who had gestational diabetes asks, 'Do I still have to worry about diabetes?' Which response is BEST?
questions.rationale: She is at risk for gestational diabetes in future pregnancies and at higher risk for diabetes mellitus. She needs follow-up checks and risk reduction such as weight control.
explanations: Her risk is lifelong, not only in pregnancy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q879 (PDF p. 1118)

questions.stem: A mother is deciding whether to have her son circumcised. Which nursing action BEST supports an informed decision?
options: Tell her to ask the men in her family
Give written information and answer her questions
questions.rationale: Informed decision-making is the key. The nurse provides educational materials and answers questions, keeping personal views out of it.
explanations: Personal views should not influence teaching.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q910 (PDF p. 1153)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client was just diagnosed with sickle cell anemia. Which psychosocial intervention is MOST important now?
options: Leave her alone if she cries
Give her all the facts at once
questions.rationale: Emotional support is a key nursing role during counseling. Avoiding the topic, leaving her alone, or overwhelming her with information is nontherapeutic.
explanations: Abandons her unless she asks to be alone.
Overwhelms her while she is coping.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q919 (PDF p. 1162)

questions.stem: A mother delivered a baby with a cleft lip and palate. Which emotion must she work through FIRST before bonding can occur?
questions.rationale: A mother grieves after the birth of a child with a birth defect. Once she works through grief, she can focus on bonding. Guilt, anger, and depression are parts of grief.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q932 (PDF p. 1176)

questions.stem: A mother of an LGA newborn with facial bruising is afraid to touch him and cause pain. What should the nurse say?
options: 'Let me show you a gentle touch.'
'Let the nurses handle him for now.'
questions.rationale: Gentle touch with the fingertips is encouraged, and the bruising is temporary. Avoiding contact interferes with bonding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q937 (PDF p. 1181)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which nursing action BEST helps parents develop attachment to their preterm infant in the NICU?
options: Encouraging them to touch and talk to the baby
questions.rationale: Touch and voice start the bonding process, and active participation builds the parents' confidence in their role.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q943 (PDF p. 1188)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A laboring client with HIV says, 'I know I'll have a sick-looking baby.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You're sick, but your baby may not be.'
'You have concerns about how your baby will look?'
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing in an open-ended way invites her to voice her concerns. Babies do not look sick from HIV at birth, though their status may be uncertain for a while.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q968 (PDF p. 1216)

questions.stem: Which goal is appropriate for a mother after an intrauterine fetal death?
options: Her grieving will end within 6 months
She will not discuss the baby
She and her family will express their feelings
She will plan another pregnancy at once
questions.rationale: Appropriate goals include the family expressing feelings and discussing going home without the infant. Limiting grief to a short time is not part of normal grieving.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q922 (PDF p. 1165)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which emotional need should the nurse anticipate in a client having a precipitous labor?
options: Support in keeping a sense of control
Less pain than in a normal labor
questions.rationale: Because of its abrupt onset and quick progress, precipitous labor makes it hard for the client to keep control. She needs support to understand and adapt to the rapid changes.
explanations: Correct: rapid labor threatens her sense of control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q970 (PDF p. 1219)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a newborn with an undescended testicle ask what can happen if it is not corrected. Which complication with a psychosocial impact should the nurse mention?
questions.rationale: The testes need a temperature below body temperature to produce fertile sperm, so uncorrected cryptorchidism can cause infertility. An 'empty scrotum' can also affect self-perception.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q972 (PDF p. 1221)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a newborn with hydrocephalus says, 'I'm not sure I can care for my baby at home.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You're worried about caring for him at home?'
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing restates the mother's message and invites her to share more. The other responses minimize her concern or give false reassurance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q973 (PDF p. 1222)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Before an amniotomy, which data is the PRIORITY to assess?
questions.rationale: Fetal well-being must be confirmed before and after amniotomy by checking the FHR with a Doppler or external monitor. Scalp sampling is not possible with intact membranes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1103 (PDF p. 1387)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: At 35 weeks, a client reports a sudden gush of fluid from the vagina without contractions. What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: PROM usually shows as a sudden discharge of vaginal fluid before 37 weeks. Preterm labor shows contractions, cramping, and pressure; miscarriage shows bleeding and pain.
explanations: Presents with loss of fetal movement.
Correct: a sudden gush of fluid.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1108 (PDF p. 1392)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client with mitral valve prolapse needs anticoagulation. Which drug and route does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Heparin does not cross the placenta, so it is the safe anticoagulant in pregnancy, given subcutaneously. Warfarin crosses the placenta.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1125 (PDF p. 1409)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A postpartum client has thromboembolic disease. Which intervention MOST helps prevent pulmonary embolism?
questions.rationale: Anticoagulants prevent clots from forming and from moving to other areas, so they directly prevent pulmonary embolism. The other measures monitor but do not prevent.
explanations: Correct: prevents clot formation and movement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1145 (PDF p. 1432)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant client is admitted with worsening heart disease. Which diet should the nurse discuss with the dietitian?
options: High in fiber with enough fluids
questions.rationale: Constipation can lead to straining (Valsalva maneuver), which can overload the heart. Adequate fluid and fiber prevent constipation. Low-calorie diets are not used in pregnancy.
explanations: Leads to constipation and low blood volume.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1148 (PDF p. 1435)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The nursery is told that a newborn of an Rh-negative mother is coming. What should the nurse do first?
options: Get the baby's type and Coombs
questions.rationale: Cord blood taken at delivery gives the newborn's blood type, Rh factor, and direct Coombs test. These results guide care.
explanations: Correct: the results are needed to plan care.
RhoGAM is given to the mother, not the infant.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1172 (PDF p. 1459)

questions.stem: In the second trimester, the fetal heart rate is 100 beats per minute. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Tell the mother it is slow
questions.rationale: The normal FHR is 120 to 160 bpm. A rate of 100 needs prompt evaluation, so the provider is notified, and the finding is also documented.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1205 (PDF p. 1497)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After a gush of fluid in active labor, the monitor shows variable decelerations with each contraction. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Variable decelerations after a gush of fluid suggest cord compression from prolapse. A vaginal exam detects the cord and confirms the problem.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1181 (PDF p. 1471)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is MOST important when admitting a newborn with myelomeningocele?
questions.rationale: Increased intracranial pressure is a complication of spina bifida, and a bulging anterior fontanel is a sign of it. Temperature also matters because of infection risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1191 (PDF p. 1483)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A term infant had hypoglycemia at 1 hour of age. At 24 hours, which finding needs follow-up?
options: Weight loss of 100 g with dry, peeling skin
Glucose of 45 mg/dL before a feeding
A high-pitched cry and poor feeding
questions.rationale: Hypoglycemia causes CNS signs such as a high-pitched cry and weak feeding. Early weight loss and peeling skin are normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1216 (PDF p. 1509)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Two days after admission for gestational hypertension, which finding shows the condition is WORSENING?
questions.rationale: Headache or blurred vision means the condition is worsening and needs immediate evaluation. The other findings suggest improvement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1222 (PDF p. 1515)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The nurse encourages oral fluids during labor. Which finding shows a successful outcome?
questions.rationale: Specific gravity measures urine concentration, and the kidneys tend to concentrate urine in labor. A specific gravity of 1.020 shows adequate hydration. Ketones show inadequate intake.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1233 (PDF p. 1526)

questions.stem: The goal is 'The client will remain free of infection during her stay.' Which finding BEST shows the goal was met?
questions.rationale: Fever is the first sign of infection, so its absence suggests no infection. A temperature up to 38°C can be normal from the dehydrating effects of labor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1234 (PDF p. 1527)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a pregnant client understands the purpose of Kegel exercises?
questions.rationale: Kegel exercises strengthen the pelvic floor (pubococcygeal muscle). Pelvic tilts ease backache, and leg elevation reduces ankle edema.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1253 (PDF p. 1553)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which procedure should be AVOIDED during labor to reduce HIV transmission to the fetus?
questions.rationale: Any procedure that exposes the fetus to maternal blood or body fluids is avoided. Internal scalp electrodes break the fetal skin.
explanations: Not a transmission risk to the fetus.
Correct: exposes the fetus to maternal fluids.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1271 (PDF p. 1572)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: One hour after surfactant therapy for RDS, which finding shows the newborn is improving?
options: A slight rise in respiratory rate
Arterial pH rising to 7.35 or higher
questions.rationale: RDS causes hypoxemia and metabolic acidosis. An arterial pH rising to 7.35 or more means the acidosis is resolving.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1296 (PDF p. 1597)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should a newborn with gastroschisis be positioned before surgery?
questions.rationale: In gastroschisis the bowel is outside the abdomen with no sac. The infant is kept side-lying with the bowel supported by a blanket roll to prevent vascular compromise, kept NPO on IV fluids.
explanations: Puts pressure on the exposed bowel.
Correct: prevents twisting of the bowel.
The bowel must be covered and protected.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1331 (PDF p. 1633)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Ten days postpartum, a breastfeeding mother calls with a red, painful breast and fever. What should the nurse advise?
options: Feed only from the other breast
Call the MD; nurse both sides
Apply ice and skip a feed
questions.rationale: Fever with a red, painful breast suggests mastitis. The provider is notified so an antibiotic safe for the baby can be prescribed. The mother keeps nursing on both breasts, starting with the unaffected one.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1333 (PDF p. 1635)

questions.stem: What is the role of estrogen in pregnancy?
options: Maintains the uterine lining for implantation
Promotes uterine growth and prepares the breasts
questions.rationale: Estrogen stimulates uterine development and prepares the breasts for lactation. Progesterone maintains the uterine lining, hPL converts glucose to fat, and hCG maintains the corpus luteum.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1348 (PDF p. 1651)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How should the nurse describe imperforate anus to parents?
questions.rationale: Imperforate anus is incomplete development or absence of the anus in its normal position. Incontinence describes encopresis, and telescoping describes intussusception.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1354 (PDF p. 1657)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What is the approximate stomach capacity of a newborn?
questions.rationale: A newborn's stomach holds about 10 to 20 mL. It grows to 30 to 90 mL by 1 week and 75 to 100 mL by 2 to 3 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1355 (PDF p. 1658)

questions.stem: Which measure relieves nipple soreness in a breastfeeding mother?
options: Keep the same position to toughen the nipple
Stop nursing on the sore side
Align baby's ear, shoulder, hip, tummy to mother
Pull the baby off without breaking suction
questions.rationale: Comfort measures include proper alignment (ear, shoulder, and hip in line, baby's stomach against the mother's), rotating positions, breaking suction with a finger, nursing often, and starting on the less sore side.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1356 (PDF p. 1659)

questions.stem: Immediately after delivery, where does the nurse expect to find the fundus?
options: At or slightly below the umbilicus, midline
questions.rationale: Right after delivery, the fundus is at the umbilicus or one to three fingerbreadths below it, in the midline. A deviated fundus may mean a full bladder; a high fundus may mean clots.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1358 (PDF p. 1661)

questions.stem: Two hours after delivery, a mother's temperature is 38.9°C (102°F). What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A slight rise from dehydration is normal, but 38.9°C (102°F) suggests infection and is reported to the provider.
explanations: Not enough for this level of fever.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1359 (PDF p. 1662)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After a vaginal delivery with epidural anesthesia, a vaginal hematoma is suspected. Which finding is the BEST indicator?
questions.rationale: Under anesthesia the client cannot feel pain or pressure, so vital sign changes showing hypovolemia are the best indicator. Bruising may simply come from the delivery.
explanations: May come from the delivery itself.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1360 (PDF p. 1663)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY assessment for a postterm small-for-gestational-age newborn?
questions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is the most common metabolic complication in SGA newborns and can cause CNS damage if not corrected immediately.
explanations: Correct: hypoglycemia is the main risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1362 (PDF p. 1665)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn with Apgar scores of 1 and 4 is coming to the nursery. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: With low Apgar scores, keeping the airway open comes first, so respiratory resuscitation equipment is prepared. The other measures are lower priority.
explanations: Correct: the airway and breathing come first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1364 (PDF p. 1667)

questions.stem: Which measure relieves breast engorgement in a breastfeeding mother?
options: Warm compress or shower before feeding
Skip feedings to let breasts rest
questions.rationale: Comfort measures include massaging the breasts before feeding, alternating breasts, a warm shower or compress just before feeding, and a supportive bra at all times.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1414 (PDF p. 1720)

questions.stem: Which statement by a woman reflects a PRESUMPTIVE sign of pregnancy?
options: 'I haven't had a period in 2 months.'
questions.rationale: Presumptive signs are subjective changes the woman experiences: amenorrhea, nausea and vomiting, breast changes, urinary frequency, fatigue, and quickening.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1465 (PDF p. 1774)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Pressing on a prenatal client's shin leaves a pit about 1 inch (2.5 cm) deep. How should the nurse document it?
questions.rationale: A pit about 1 inch deep is +4 edema. A slight pit is +1, about 1/4 inch is +2, and about 1/2 inch is +3.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1537 (PDF p. 1848)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client at 30 weeks in preterm labor receives betamethasone. What is its purpose?
options: To keep the ductus arteriosus open
questions.rationale: Betamethasone increases surfactant and fetal lung maturity, reducing respiratory distress syndrome. Surfactant is not stable until after 32 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1547 (PDF p. 1859)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A toddler has swallowed a household cleaner. Which action is appropriate?
options: Lay the child flat on the back
Call poison control and check ABCs
Give milk and wait for symptoms
questions.rationale: Poison control is called before other treatment. The nurse checks airway, breathing, and circulation, identifies the substance and amount, and saves any vomitus. Vomiting is not induced for corrosive cleaners.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q529 (PDF p. 727)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A client hemorrhaging from a partial uterine inversion asks, 'What's happening? I'm bleeding. Am I dying?' What is she most likely experiencing?
questions.rationale: The unknown is the most common cause of fear, and loss of control causes anxiety. Her questions show fear rather than panic.
explanations: Requires knowing of an impending loss.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q901 (PDF p. 1144)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with gastroenteritis is watched for hypovolemic shock. Which finding indicates COMPENSATED shock?
questions.rationale: In compensated shock the child becomes tachycardic to keep up cardiac output while BP stays normal. Capillary refill may exceed 2 seconds, and the child may become irritable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1140 (PDF p. 1426)

questions.stem: The nurse finds a child's genitals swollen and suspects sexual abuse. What is of PRIMARY importance?
questions.rationale: The nurse's primary legal duty when abuse is suspected is to report it. In the Philippines, RA 7610 requires health workers to report suspected child abuse. Documenting and referring follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1192 (PDF p. 1484)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant monitored for increased ICP has an anterior fontanel that bulges only when crying. What should the nurse conclude?
options: Lower the head of the bed
questions.rationale: The anterior fontanel is normally soft and flat. A bulging fontanel may come from crying or from increased ICP, so bulging only with crying is normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q85 (PDF p. 231)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How does the nurse test a child's pharyngeal (gag) reflex?
options: Touch the back of the throat
questions.rationale: The gag reflex is tested by touching the back of the throat with a tongue depressor. Asking the child to swallow tests the swallowing reflex.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q114 (PDF p. 263)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which finding should the school nurse look for when screening for scoliosis?
questions.rationale: Signs include chest asymmetry, unequal rib heights, and lateral deviation and rotation of the vertebrae. Children 9 to 15 are screened; girls are at highest risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q618 (PDF p. 833)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How should a child stand for scoliosis screening?
questions.rationale: The child stands in underpants with weight on both feet, legs straight, and arms hanging loosely so the chest, back, and hips are seen clearly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1168 (PDF p. 1455)

questions.stem: Which statement about breast self-examination needs correction?
options: 'I can use soapy hands in the shower.'
'I check in front of a mirror.'
'I do it on the first day of my period.'
questions.rationale: BSE is done 2 or 3 days after menstruation ends, when breasts are least tender. Lumps, including in the armpit, and nipple discharge are reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q654 (PDF p. 872)

questions.stem: Two months after a right mastectomy, a client says she has not done BSE on her left breast. Which coping mechanism is she likely using?
questions.rationale: Denying or minimizing a health problem can lead to avoiding self-care such as BSE, which can be life-threatening.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q947 (PDF p. 1192)

questions.stem: Which statement about testicular self-examination needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll do it after a warm shower.'
'A cord-like part in back is normal.'
questions.rationale: TSE is done monthly. After a warm shower the scrotum is relaxed, and the spermatic cord is a normal finding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1078 (PDF p. 1360)

questions.stem: Which instruction belongs in a high school class on testicular self-examination?
options: Do it after a cold shower
questions.rationale: TSE screens for testicular cancer, common in late teens and twenties. It is done monthly after a warm shower, rolling each testicle between thumb and fingers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1369 (PDF p. 1672)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: In a pregnant client with heart disease, where is venous congestion MOST commonly seen?
questions.rationale: Venous congestion that can become varicosities is most often seen in the legs, vulva, or rectum. Edema of the fingers or eyes is not directly venous congestion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1106 (PDF p. 1390)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is a positive Kernig's sign in a child?
options: Cannot fully extend the legs supine
Hips flex when the neck flexes
questions.rationale: Kernig's sign is the inability to extend the legs fully while supine. Brudzinski's sign is hip flexion when the neck is flexed. Both suggest bacterial meningitis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1111 (PDF p. 1395)

questions.stem: Which factor should the nurse consider when teaching a child about his illness?
options: Older children have shorter attention spans
Imagination may cause more fear than truth
questions.rationale: Teaching is adjusted to the child's age and cognition. A child's imagination may create more fear than the truth, and a child may regress when ill.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q740 (PDF p. 966)

questions.stem: Which is a cause of ORGANIC erectile dysfunction?
questions.rationale: Organic causes include hypertension, vascular disease, diabetes, and alcohol. Stress, depression, and anxiety are psychogenic causes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q785 (PDF p. 1015)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which hospital safety measure is specific to infants and toddlers?
questions.rationale: Crib sides are never left down. Large, soft toys without small parts prevent choking.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q475 (PDF p. 659)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which statement about preventing burns in a toddler needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll put my coffee on the counter.'
questions.rationale: Toddlers can reach hot objects on counters. Hot drinks must be kept out of reach.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q503 (PDF p. 697)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: With which liquid should an adolescent take oral iron?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C enhances iron absorption, and tomato juice is rich in it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q611 (PDF p. 824)

questions.stem: A crying toddler won't sit still for an eye exam. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Involving the toddler in the exam reduces fear. Telling a child not to be scared tells him how to feel.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q682 (PDF p. 902)

questions.stem: A 6-year-old starts bedwetting after a new baby arrives. Which defense mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Regression is returning to an earlier form of behavior under stress.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q851 (PDF p. 1088)

questions.stem: A preschooler in traction starts bedwetting. How should the nurse explain this to the mother?
questions.rationale: Regression is common in immobilized children and usually needs no professional intervention.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q873 (PDF p. 1110)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which adolescent statement needs follow-up?
options: 'I like to be alone when stressed.'
'I've cut out all fat and lost weight.'
questions.rationale: Omitting all fat and losing weight during growth suggests poor nutrition and a possible eating disorder.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q852 (PDF p. 1089)

questions.stem: How should the nurse prepare an 11-year-old for an IV insertion?
options: Use visual aids and concrete words
questions.rationale: School-age children understand best with visual aids and concrete language.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q860 (PDF p. 1097)

questions.stem: Which statement by a hospitalized 16-year-old suggests a developmental problem?
questions.rationale: Adolescents who withdraw from peers struggle with identity development.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q867 (PDF p. 1104)

questions.stem: A 9-year-old is in traction for 2 months. What BEST promotes psychosocial development?
questions.rationale: School-age children face industry versus inferiority. Keeping up with schoolwork gives accomplishment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q939 (PDF p. 1183)

questions.stem: A 16-year-old with diabetes says, 'I'm fed up with diets and doctors!' What is the PRIORITY concern?
questions.rationale: Adolescents strive for identity and independence; the statement reflects fear of losing control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q944 (PDF p. 1189)

questions.stem: Which finding in a 12-year-old suggests disrupted self-concept development?
questions.rationale: Intimate relationships are expected in young adulthood. Friends and industry fit this age.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q962 (PDF p. 1209)

questions.stem: Which question BEST assesses a teenager's feelings about using a cane?
options: 'How do you feel about the cane?'
questions.rationale: An open-ended question about feelings elicits assessment data. The others are closed or assume feelings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1043 (PDF p. 1317)

questions.stem: A 14-year-old in skeletal traction struggles with the long stay. What helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Adolescents need to belong to a peer group. Wearing their own clothes supports this.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1202 (PDF p. 1494)

questions.stem: A 10-month-old is hospitalized for RSV. Which plan fits his development?
questions.rationale: Infants are in trust versus mistrust. A consistent routine with comfort, touch, and talking supports trust.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1163 (PDF p. 1450)

questions.stem: Which behavior shows a preschooler with scarlet fever is coping with bed rest?
questions.rationale: Play is how preschoolers adjust to life experiences; quiet play like drawing suits bed rest.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1219 (PDF p. 1512)

questions.stem: Which outcome shows a positive DEVELOPMENTAL result for a preschooler in traction?
questions.rationale: Hospitalization and immobility may cause regression. Age-appropriate behavior is the developmental outcome.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1232 (PDF p. 1525)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which parent statement about toddler temper tantrums shows understanding?
options: 'I'll say only bad kids do it.'
questions.rationale: Ignoring attention-seeking behavior extinguishes it, provided the child is safe. Time-out should be about 1 minute per year of age.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1241 (PDF p. 1534)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which diabetes task suits a newly diagnosed 9-year-old?
questions.rationale: School-age children can draw up and give insulin with supervision but lack maturity for independent dosing decisions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1252 (PDF p. 1552)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: At what age can most children begin to monitor their own insulin needs?
questions.rationale: Most children 9 years or older understand the principles of monitoring their insulin needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1080 (PDF p. 1362)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do FIRST before teaching a teenager about sexuality?
questions.rationale: Establishing a relationship and exploring prior knowledge comes first; it builds rapport and identifies learning needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q753 (PDF p. 982)

questions.stem: Which statement to parents of a stillborn baby shows effective teaching of a new nurse?
options: 'How can I help you remember your baby?'
'I don't know why this happened either.'
questions.rationale: Helping the family create memories confirms the baby's existence and helps them complete grieving.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1024 (PDF p. 1297)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which sweat test result supports cystic fibrosis?
questions.rationale: Abnormally high sweat chloride is unique to CF; a level above 60 mEq/L supports the diagnosis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q194 (PDF p. 348)

questions.stem: Which discharge instruction fits a client after abdominal hysterectomy?
questions.rationale: After abdominal hysterectomy, the client avoids heavy lifting, limits stair climbing, and walks indoors at first, gradually increasing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q361 (PDF p. 529)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A hospitalized child exposed to varicella 2 weeks ago develops a trunk rash. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Varicella incubation is 14–21 days; the child is isolated at once to prevent spread.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q559 (PDF p. 760)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which home instruction is correct for parents of a child being tested for HIV?
questions.rationale: Toothbrushes are not shared, immunizations are kept current, and blood spills are cleaned and rinsed with bleach solution.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q661 (PDF p. 880)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Why should NICU parents wash their hands properly?
questions.rationale: Proper handwashing by staff and parents prevents nursery infections and lets parents take part in care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q734 (PDF p. 959)

questions.stem: How should the nurse BEST meet the cultural needs of a child's family from another culture?
questions.rationale: Asking about specific cultural needs and treatments helps the nurse understand the family's beliefs and health practices.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q975 (PDF p. 1224)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a pregnant woman understands toxoplasmosis prevention?
questions.rationale: Infected cats shed toxoplasma in feces; pregnant women avoid litter boxes and undercooked meat.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1072 (PDF p. 1354)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which diet does a child with cystic fibrosis need?
questions.rationale: CF is managed with high-calorie, high-protein food plus pancreatic enzymes and fat-soluble vitamins. Fat is not restricted.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1073 (PDF p. 1355)

questions.stem: Which advice promotes PRIMARY prevention of cervical cancer?
questions.rationale: Early treatment of cervical infection prevents chronic cervicitis, which can lead to premalignant dysplasia. Douches are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1389 (PDF p. 1692)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 50-kg child is ordered morphine 8 mg SC q4h. The safe range is 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/dose. What should the nurse conclude?
questions.rationale: 110 lb ÷ 2.2 = 50 kg; 0.1–0.2 mg/kg = 5–10 mg. 8 mg is within range.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q113 (PDF p. 262)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How are eardrops given to an infant?
options: Pull the auricle up and back
Pull the auricle down and back
questions.rationale: For children under 3, the auricle is pulled down and back with the affected ear uppermost. Over 3, it is pulled up and back.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q394 (PDF p. 564)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How are eardrops given to a 6-year-old?
options: Pull the ear down and back
Pull the ear up and back
questions.rationale: For children over 3, the ear is pulled upward and back. Gloves are not needed for parents.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q698 (PDF p. 920)

questions.stem: Where should a mother start when bathing her newborn?
questions.rationale: Bathing starts with the cleanest area, the eyes and face, then ears and neck.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q695 (PDF p. 917)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which suction pressure is used for an infant's tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: Infants and children need smaller catheters and lower suction settings than adults; about 90 mm Hg for an infant.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1196 (PDF p. 1488)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement shows parents understand home colostomy care for Hirschsprung's disease?
questions.rationale: Parents report skin breakdown or stomal problems, such as ribbonlike stools or failure to pass flatus or stool.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1407 (PDF p. 1713)

questions.stem: Which finding supports mittelschmerz?
questions.rationale: Mittelschmerz is pelvic pain midway between periods at ovulation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q87 (PDF p. 233)

questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of endometriosis?
questions.rationale: Endometriosis is tissue resembling endometrium outside the uterus that responds to hormones during the cycle.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q88 (PDF p. 234)

questions.stem: Which statement after vasectomy needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Birth control continues until semen analysis shows no sperm; live sperm may remain in the vas.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q626 (PDF p. 843)

questions.stem: Which husband's statement on preventing infertility needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Keeping the testes cool by avoiding hot baths and tight clothing appears to improve sperm count.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q628 (PDF p. 845)

questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of laser surgery for cervical cancer?
questions.rationale: Laser therapy is outpatient, painless, and used when lesion borders are visible; no general anesthesia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1349 (PDF p. 1652)

questions.stem: When do fibrocystic breast symptoms usually worsen?
questions.rationale: Lumps and tenderness worsen before menses because of hormonal changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1370 (PDF p. 1673)

questions.stem: After radical vulvectomy, which discharge plan shows best understanding?
questions.rationale: Activity resumes slowly; walking helps, with rest when fatigued. Driving and heavy work are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1372 (PDF p. 1675)

questions.stem: After cervical cryosurgery, what discharge is expected?
questions.rationale: Discharge is clear and watery after cryosurgery; pain is mild.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1455 (PDF p. 1764)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is the pinna pulled for a tympanic temperature in a 2-year-old?
questions.rationale: For children under 3, the pinna is pulled straight back and slightly down; for adults, up and back.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tympanic Temperature (PDF p. 18)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which pulse site is routinely used for infants and children up to 3 years?
questions.rationale: The apical pulse is routine for infants and children up to 3 years.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Sites (PDF p. 19)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which pain scale suits a young child?
questions.rationale: The Faces Pain Scale is suitable for children to describe pain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessment of Pain (PDF p. 22)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which is the IM site of choice for infants 1 year and younger?
questions.rationale: The vastus lateralis is the IM site of choice for infants 1 year and younger.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IM Injection (PDF p. 28)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Using Clark's rule, what is the dose for a 30-lb child if the adult dose is 500 mg?
questions.rationale: Clark's rule: weight in lb ÷ 150 × adult dose = 30/150 × 500 = 100 mg.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Calculating Dosages (PDF p. 28)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Involuntary urination in children beyond what age is called enuresis?
questions.rationale: Enuresis is involuntary urination in children beyond 4–5 years old.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Problems (PDF p. 49)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Tetracycline should be avoided in which client?
questions.rationale: Tetracyclines are not for young children or the last half of pregnancy (tooth staining, bone effects).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-infectives (PDF p. 137)

questions.stem: Which gland secretes an alkaline fluid that neutralizes vaginal acidity?
questions.rationale: Bartholin's (paravaginal) glands secrete alkaline fluid; Skene's glands secrete lubricating mucus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, External Genitalia (PDF p. 186)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which structure is a common site for episiotomy?
questions.rationale: The fourchette, the posterior joining of the labia, is a common episiotomy site.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, External Genitalia (PDF p. 186)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which part of the uterus is most commonly cut in a cesarean section?
questions.rationale: The isthmus (lower segment) is most commonly incised for cesarean birth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Uterine Anatomy (PDF p. 187)

questions.stem: Where does fertilization usually occur?
questions.rationale: The ampulla is the longest part of the tube and the common site of fertilization and ectopic pregnancy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fallopian Tube (PDF p. 187)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which ectopic pregnancy site is MOST dangerous?
questions.rationale: The interstitial portion is the most dangerous site for ectopic pregnancy (risk of massive hemorrhage).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fallopian Tube (PDF p. 188)

questions.stem: Which male structure is the site of sperm maturation?
questions.rationale: The epididymis conducts sperm to the vas deferens and is the site of sperm maturation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Male Internal Genitalia (PDF p. 188)

questions.stem: Which hormone surge triggers ovulation?
