questions.rationale: Peaking estrogen triggers the LH surge, which coincides with ovulation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Menstrual Cycle (PDF p. 189)

questions.stem: Which phase of the menstrual cycle is constant at 14 days?
questions.rationale: The luteal phase is always about 14 days; the proliferative phase varies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Menstrual Cycle (PDF p. 189)

questions.stem: A woman has a 32-day cycle. On about which day does she ovulate?
questions.rationale: The luteal phase is 14 days, so ovulation is about 14 days before menses: 32 − 14 = day 18.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Menstrual Cycle (PDF p. 189)

questions.stem: The developing baby is called an embryo during which period?
questions.rationale: Zygote under 2 weeks, embryo 2 to under 8 weeks, fetus 8 weeks to birth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Terminologies (PDF p. 190)

questions.stem: Which is a PRESUMPTIVE sign of pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Presumptive signs are subjective: amenorrhea, nausea, breast changes, quickening. Tests and ballottement are probable; FHT is positive.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Pregnancy (PDF p. 190)

questions.stem: Which is a POSITIVE sign of pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Positive signs: fetal heart tones, fetal movement felt by examiner, fetus on ultrasound.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Pregnancy (PDF p. 191)

questions.stem: Bluish-purple discoloration of the vagina in pregnancy is:
questions.rationale: Chadwick's sign is bluish vaginal discoloration; Goodell's is cervical softening; Hegar's is lower uterine softening.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Pregnancy (PDF p. 191)

questions.stem: At 20 weeks, where is the fundus usually found?
questions.rationale: 12 weeks: symphysis; 16 weeks: halfway; 20 weeks: umbilicus; 36 weeks: xiphoid.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Landmarks (PDF p. 191)

questions.stem: When does hCG usually peak in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: hCG peaks at about 10 weeks AOG (2 months).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Probable Signs (PDF p. 191)

questions.stem: Which nursing measure helps morning sickness?
questions.rationale: Dry crackers, small frequent meals, less fatty food, ice chips, and ambulation help.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Presumptive Signs (PDF p. 190)

questions.stem: Why should the woman void before Leopold's maneuvers?
questions.rationale: An empty bladder promotes comfort and keeps fetal contour from being obscured.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leopold's Maneuver (PDF p. 192)

questions.stem: Which Leopold's maneuver locates the fetal back?
questions.rationale: The second maneuver locates the fetal back, where FHT is best heard.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leopold's Maneuver (PDF p. 192)

questions.stem: Which Leopold's maneuver determines whether the presenting part is engaged?
questions.rationale: The third maneuver checks the part at the inlet and engagement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leopold's Maneuver (PDF p. 192)

questions.stem: During the fourth Leopold's maneuver, which way does the nurse face?
questions.rationale: In the first three maneuvers the nurse faces the head; in the fourth, the foot of the bed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leopold's Maneuver (PDF p. 192)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which fetal attitude presents the smallest head diameter?
questions.rationale: Full flexion presents the suboccipitobregmatic, the smallest diameter.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Attitude (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: A woman at 30 weeks becomes dizzy lying supine. Which position helps?
questions.rationale: The uterus compresses the vena cava (supine hypotensive syndrome); left lateral relieves it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physiological Changes (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: Why does physiologic anemia occur in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Hemodilution from increased plasma volume causes physiologic anemia; iron needs rise.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hematologic Changes (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: In which position is a pregnant woman's BP LOWEST?
questions.rationale: BP is highest sitting, intermediate supine, and lowest left lateral; rest 15 minutes first.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Prenatal Clinic (PDF p. 192)

questions.stem: By how much does cardiac output increase in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Cardiac output increases 25–50% and heart rate about 10 bpm.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physiological Changes (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: A pregnant woman hyperventilates and feels tingling and light-headedness. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation causes respiratory alkalosis; rebreathing through a paper bag or cupped hands helps.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Changes (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: A pregnant woman craves and eats clay. What is this?
questions.rationale: Pica is an appetite for non-nutritive substances such as clay, chalk, or soil.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: How is gum swelling and bleeding (epulis) in pregnancy managed?
questions.rationale: Epulis is from increased estrogen; use a soft brush and avoid strong mouthwash.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: Which advice helps heartburn in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Small frequent meals, avoiding supine position after eating, and gradual ambulation help.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: Why are pregnant women prone to UTI?
questions.rationale: Hormone-induced relaxation of the renal pelvis and ureters causes urine stagnation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: Which hormone loosens the pelvic joints in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Relaxin from the placenta relaxes pelvic joints.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Musculoskeletal Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: Which measure relieves back pain from pregnancy lordosis?
questions.rationale: Pelvic rocking and lumbar pressure help; avoid supine position.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Musculoskeletal Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: Why are NSAIDs such as indomethacin avoided late in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: NSAIDs can close the ductus arteriosus prematurely and reduce fetal urine, causing oligohydramnios.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Drugs in Pregnancy (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: What should the woman do before amniocentesis?
questions.rationale: Voiding reduces bladder size and prevents accidental puncture; observe 30 minutes after.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Amniotic fluid over 1200 mL is called:
questions.rationale: Normal 800–1200 mL; oligohydramnios under 500 mL; polyhydramnios over 1200 mL.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Green-tinged amniotic fluid suggests:
questions.rationale: Green suggests meconium; strong yellow suggests blood incompatibility.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.stem: Which L:S ratio indicates fetal lung maturity?
questions.rationale: A lecithin:sphingomyelin ratio of 2:1 indicates lung maturity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.stem: How is a woman prepared for a TRANSABDOMINAL ultrasound early in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: A full bladder pushes the uterus up for better view; transvaginal needs voiding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ultrasound (PDF p. 196)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A 'snowstorm' pattern on first-trimester ultrasound suggests:
questions.rationale: H-mole shows a snowstorm appearance of fluid-filled vesicles.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ultrasound (PDF p. 196)

questions.stem: A biophysical profile score of 8–10 means:
questions.rationale: BPP 8–10 normal; 6 suspicious; 4 jeopardy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Biophysical Score (PDF p. 196)

questions.stem: Which NST result is REACTIVE (normal)?
questions.rationale: Reactive NST: two or more accelerations of 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds with movement in 20 minutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Non-Stress Test (PDF p. 197)

questions.stem: Which contraction stress test result is NORMAL?
questions.rationale: A negative CST has no late decelerations with contractions; positive (late decels) is abnormal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Contraction Stress Test (PDF p. 197)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Late decelerations appear during an oxytocin challenge test. What is FIRST?
questions.rationale: Turn left lateral, stop oxytocin, give O2 8–10 L/min, and hydrate.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Contraction Stress Test (PDF p. 197)

questions.stem: An ELEVATED maternal serum AFP suggests:
questions.rationale: Elevated AFP suggests neural tube defects; decreased suggests chromosomal disorders like Down syndrome.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alpha-fetoprotein (PDF p. 197)

questions.stem: When is chorionic villi sampling done?
questions.rationale: CVS is done at 8–10 weeks; amniocentesis at 14–16 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chorionic Villi Sampling (PDF p. 197)

questions.stem: The main psychological task in the SECOND trimester is:
questions.rationale: First trimester: accept pregnancy; second: accept the baby; third: accept parenthood.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Psychological Tasks (PDF p. 198)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which pelvis type is ideal for childbirth?
questions.rationale: The gynecoid pelvis is the normal female pelvis with a well-rounded inlet.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pelvic Dimension (PDF p. 198)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The presenting part is at the level of the ischial spines. What is the station?
questions.rationale: Station 0 (engaged) is at the ischial spines; minus is above, plus is below; +3 is crowning.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fetal Station (PDF p. 199)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: When does the posterior fontanelle close?
questions.rationale: The triangular posterior fontanelle closes at 2–3 months; the anterior at 12–18 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fetal Head (PDF p. 199)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which finding indicates TRUE labor?
options: Pain only in the lower abdomen
questions.rationale: True labor has regular, intensifying contractions starting in the back with progressive dilation and effacement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, True vs False Labor (PDF p. 200)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: In a primigravida, lightening usually occurs:
questions.rationale: Lightening occurs about 2 weeks before labor in primigravidas and at labor in multigravidas.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preliminary Signs of Labor (PDF p. 199)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: During which phase of labor is dilation 8–10 cm with contractions every 2–3 minutes?
questions.rationale: Transition: 8–10 cm, strongest contractions lasting 60–90 seconds every 2–3 minutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Labor (PDF p. 200)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Nitrazine paper turns blue with vaginal fluid. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: Blue (alkaline) indicates amniotic fluid; red (acidic) indicates urine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nitrazine Test (PDF p. 200)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A woman has a strong urge to push at 8 cm. What should the nurse tell her?
questions.rationale: Do not push before full dilation; pant-breathe with the urge to push.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Second Stage (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which sequence correctly begins the cardinal movements of labor?
questions.rationale: Mechanisms of labor: engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, external rotation, expulsion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mechanisms of Labor (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Under EINC, when is the cord clamped?
questions.rationale: EINC: immediate drying, skin-to-skin, properly timed cord clamping (after pulsations stop or 1–3 minutes), and early breastfeeding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EINC (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which sign shows the placenta has separated?
questions.rationale: Signs: Calkin's sign (firm, globular uterus), cord lengthening, sudden gush of blood, uterus rising.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: After how long is the third stage of labor considered prolonged?
questions.rationale: The third stage usually lasts 5–10 minutes; beyond 30 minutes is abnormal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: A placenta delivers with the shiny fetal side first. This is:
questions.rationale: Schultze is shiny, separates from the center, with less bleeding; Duncan is raw and red with more bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Placental Expulsion (PDF p. 201)

questions.stem: How many vessels does a normal umbilical cord have?
questions.rationale: A normal cord has two arteries and one vein (AVA).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: When is methylergonovine (Methergine) given?
questions.rationale: Ergot drugs cause strong contraction and can trap the placenta, so they are given after placental delivery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Third Stage Drugs (PDF p. 201)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why is the fourth stage of labor most risky for a woman with heart disease?
questions.rationale: Retained fluid is reabsorbed, increasing cardiac output and oxygen demand.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fourth Stage (PDF p. 202)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A woman at 10 weeks has bleeding with a closed cervix. What type of abortion is this?
questions.rationale: Threatened abortion: bleeding without cervical dilation or effacement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Abortion (PDF p. 202)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the most common predisposing factor for ectopic pregnancy?
questions.rationale: PID is the most common predisposing factor; previous surgery, IUD, and prior ectopic also increase risk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 202)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Bluish discoloration around the umbilicus in ruptured ectopic pregnancy is:
questions.rationale: Cullen's sign is periumbilical ecchymosis from hemoperitoneum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 203)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug may treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy under 3 cm?
questions.rationale: Methotrexate, given IM, destroys fast-growing trophoblast cells in small ectopics.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ectopic Pregnancy (PDF p. 203)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding suggests hydatidiform mole?
questions.rationale: H-mole shows rapid uterine enlargement, hyperemesis from high hCG, pinkish discharge, and no FHT.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydatidiform Mole (PDF p. 203)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: After D&C for H-mole, what should the woman avoid for 1 year?
questions.rationale: hCG is monitored for a year to detect choriocarcinoma; pregnancy would confuse results.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydatidiform Mole (PDF p. 203)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of habitual abortion?
questions.rationale: Premature cervical dilation (incompetent cervix) is the most common cause of habitual abortion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Cervical Dilation (PDF p. 204)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: When are McDonald cerclage sutures removed?
questions.rationale: McDonald sutures are removed at 37–38 weeks to allow vaginal delivery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Cervical Dilation (PDF p. 204)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Painless, bright red bleeding at 34 weeks suggests:
questions.rationale: Placenta previa is the most common cause of painless third-trimester bleeding; abruption is painful.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Placenta Previa (PDF p. 204)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which action is CONTRAINDICATED with painless bleeding late in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Never do pelvic or rectal exams with suspected placenta previa; they can cause hemorrhage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Placenta Previa (PDF p. 205)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Sharp fundal pain with a rigid, board-like uterus suggests:
questions.rationale: Abruption causes sharp stabbing pain, uterine rigidity, and bleeding that may be concealed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abruptio Placenta (PDF p. 205)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Blood seeping into the myometrium in central abruption causes:
questions.rationale: Couvelaire uterus is bluish, copper-colored, and atonic, often requiring hysterectomy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abruptio Placenta (PDF p. 205)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: The cord prolapses after membranes rupture. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Do not reinsert; cover with NSS-moistened gauze, give oxygen, and check FHT; prepare for delivery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, PROM (PDF p. 206)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug hastens fetal lung maturity in preterm rupture of membranes?
questions.rationale: Corticosteroids such as betamethasone hasten fetal lung maturity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, PROM (PDF p. 206)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Why is IV fluid given in preterm labor?
questions.rationale: Good hydration may stop contractions; bed rest and tocolytics are also used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Premature Labor (PDF p. 206)

questions.stem: In the BUBBLE-HE postpartum check, 'H' stands for:
questions.rationale: Breasts, Uterus, Bladder, Bowels, Lochia, Episiotomy, Homans' sign, and Emotions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Assessment (PDF p. 202)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnancy beyond how many weeks is post-term?
questions.rationale: Post-term pregnancy exceeds 42 weeks, with risks of meconium aspiration and macrosomia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Post Term Pregnancy (PDF p. 207)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Labor lasting less than 3 hours is called:
questions.rationale: Precipitate labor lasts under 3 hours and risks lacerations and fetal intracranial hemorrhage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Precipitate Labor (PDF p. 207)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Hips flexed with knees extended and buttocks presenting is a:
questions.rationale: Frank breech: hips flexed, knees extended, buttocks present. Complete: sitting position. Footling: feet present.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Breech Delivery (PDF p. 207)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Meconium-stained fluid in a breech delivery is:
questions.rationale: In breech delivery, meconium staining is expected from pressure on the fetal abdomen.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Breech Delivery (PDF p. 207)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Identical (monozygotic) twins come from:
questions.rationale: Monozygotic twins come from one ovum and one sperm and are always the same sex.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Pregnancies (PDF p. 208)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which is a complication of multiple pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Twin pregnancy raises risks of PIH, hydramnios, previa, preterm labor, anemia, and hemorrhage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Pregnancies (PDF p. 208)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which finding defines gestational hypertension?
questions.rationale: Gestational hypertension is elevated BP without proteinuria, returning to normal after birth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pregnancy Induced Hypertension (PDF p. 208)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: For a woman with mild pre-eclampsia, what salt intake is advised?
questions.rationale: Salt is not restricted, because restriction activates the renin-angiotensin system and raises BP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mild Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which assessment is essential during magnesium sulfate therapy?
questions.rationale: Check DTRs, respiratory rate, and urine output; magnesium can cause respiratory depression.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Severe Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: What is the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity?
questions.rationale: Calcium gluconate is the antidote for magnesium sulfate.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Severe Pre-eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which room environment suits a client with severe pre-eclampsia?
questions.rationale: Dim lights, limited visitors, side rails up, and suction at bedside reduce seizure risk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Eclampsia (PDF p. 209)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: HELLP syndrome stands for:
questions.rationale: HELLP: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets; RUQ pain from liver inflammation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, HELLP Syndrome (PDF p. 210)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: When is the 50-g glucose challenge done for gestational diabetes?
questions.rationale: Screening is done at 24–28 weeks; a 1-hour value above 140 mg/dL leads to a 3-hour test.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Diabetes (PDF p. 210)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which drug is used for gestational diabetes not controlled by diet?
questions.rationale: Insulin is the therapy of choice; the handout notes oral hypoglycemics may be teratogenic.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Diabetes (PDF p. 210)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A pregnant woman with heart disease has fatigue and dyspnea with ordinary activity. Which class is she?
questions.rationale: Class II: slightly compromised; ordinary activity causes fatigue, palpitations, dyspnea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gravidocardia (PDF p. 211)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Decelerations mirror contractions, starting and ending with them. What causes these?
questions.rationale: Early decelerations are from head compression; late from uteroplacental insufficiency; variable from cord compression.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Variability (PDF p. 211)

questions.topicName: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Variable decelerations appear. What is the FIRST action?
questions.rationale: Variable decelerations are from cord compression; reposition (lateral or Trendelenburg); amnioinfusion may be used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Variability (PDF p. 211)

questions.stem: A day-1 postpartum mother wants to be cared for and talks about her birth. Which Rubin phase is this?
questions.rationale: Taking-in: passive, dependent, reviews the birth experience.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Puerperium (PDF p. 212)

questions.stem: Lochia that is pinkish-brown on days 3 to 10 is:
questions.rationale: Rubra days 1–3 (red); serosa days 3–10 (pinkish/brown); alba day 10 to 3–6 weeks (white).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lochia (PDF p. 212)

questions.stem: Lochia changes from serosa back to rubra. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Lochia should never reverse; reversal suggests retained fragments. Foul odor suggests infection.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lochia (PDF p. 212)

questions.stem: How fast does the uterus normally involute after birth?
questions.rationale: Involution proceeds about 1 cm (one fingerbreadth) per day.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Puerperium (PDF p. 212)

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of early postpartum hemorrhage?
questions.rationale: Uterine atony is most common; lacerations are second. Late hemorrhage is often from retained fragments.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Problems (PDF p. 213)

questions.stem: A non-breastfeeding mother can expect menses to return in about:
questions.rationale: Non-breastfeeding: 6–10 weeks; breastfeeding: about 6 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lactation Amenorrhea (PDF p. 213)

questions.stem: Which position is used for a mother with endometritis?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's promotes drainage of lochia; antibiotics are given.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Endometritis (PDF p. 213)

questions.stem: Calf pain on dorsiflexion of the foot postpartum suggests:
questions.rationale: A positive Homans' sign suggests thrombophlebitis; heparin may be given.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Thrombophlebitis (PDF p. 213)

questions.stem: A newborn lifts only the head when prone; later the chest. Which principle is this?
questions.rationale: Development proceeds head to tail (cephalocaudal).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of G&D (PDF p. 214)

questions.stem: A 3-year-old colors best with a large crayon; a 12-year-old writes with a fine pen. Which principle?
questions.rationale: Development proceeds from gross to refined skills.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of G&D (PDF p. 214)

questions.stem: Per Freud, the toddler is in which stage?
questions.rationale: Infant oral, toddler anal (toilet training), preschool phallic, school-age latent, adolescent genital.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Freud's Stages (PDF p. 215)

questions.stem: Erikson's task for the preschooler is:
questions.rationale: Preschool: initiative vs guilt; toddler: autonomy; school-age: industry; infant: trust.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Erikson's Stages (PDF p. 215)

questions.stem: What is the main fear of a hospitalized toddler?
questions.rationale: Toddler fear: separation; preschool: mutilation; school-age: displacement from school; adolescent: from peers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: Which play type is typical of toddlers?
questions.rationale: Infants: solitary; toddlers: parallel; preschoolers: associative; school-age: competitive.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: Which toy is BEST for a toddler?
questions.rationale: Toddlers enjoy push and pull toys; infants mobiles; school-age table games.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which sign shows a toddler is ready for toilet training?
questions.rationale: Readiness includes staying dry 2 hours, waking dry from naps, removing clothes, and recognizing the urge.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toilet Training (PDF p. 216)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How should a nurse handle a toddler's negativism?
questions.rationale: Offer choices and avoid closed-ended questions that invite 'no'.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: By what age does a child usually have all 20 deciduous teeth?
questions.rationale: Children generally have all 20 primary teeth by 3 years.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Toddler (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: A preschooler believes the moon follows her because it is alive. This is:
questions.rationale: Magical thinking attributes thought and feeling to animals and objects.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preschool Period (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: What is the greatest fear of a hospitalized preschooler?
questions.rationale: Preschoolers fear mutilation and castration; use dolls and bandages to reassure.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preschool Period (PDF p. 216)

questions.stem: A school-age child sorts objects by color and size. Which Piaget stage?
questions.rationale: Concrete operations (7–12 years) include classification and reversibility.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, School-age Period (PDF p. 217)

questions.stem: An adolescent solves hypothetical problems. Which Piaget stage?
questions.rationale: Formal operations (12+) involve hypothetical and scientific reasoning.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Adolescence (PDF p. 217)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A newborn is blue at the extremities, HR 110, grimaces, has some flexion, and a weak cry. What is the APGAR?
questions.rationale: Acrocyanosis 1, HR >100 = 2, grimace 1, some flexion 1, weak cry 1 = 6.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, APGAR (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: An APGAR of 2 means the newborn needs:
questions.rationale: 1–3 poor, needs resuscitation; 4–7 fair, observe and stimulate; 8–10 good.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, APGAR (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which finding suggests a PRETERM newborn?
questions.rationale: Preterm signs: abundant lanugo, thin skin, few sole creases, flat ears, flat areola.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gestational Age (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: By what age does an infant usually TRIPLE birth weight?
questions.rationale: Birth weight doubles by 6 months and triples by 12 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: How much weight loss is normal in the first days of life?
questions.rationale: Newborns lose 5–10% of birth weight as maternal fluid-retaining hormones wear off.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What is a normal newborn head circumference?
questions.rationale: Head 33–35 cm, chest 31–33 cm; the head is the largest circumference.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Profile of a Newborn (PDF p. 218)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A Moro reflex persisting beyond 6 months may indicate:
questions.rationale: Persistence of the Moro reflex beyond 6 months may indicate brain damage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Neurologic Assessment (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which newborn vital sign is normal?
questions.rationale: Newborn apical rate 120–160, respirations 30–60.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Signs (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Scalp swelling that crosses suture lines after prolonged labor is:
questions.rationale: Caput crosses sutures and resolves in about 3 days; cephalhematoma does not cross sutures.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Assessment (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: What helps newborns produce heat?
questions.rationale: Brown adipose tissue increases metabolism to produce heat; newborns cannot shiver effectively.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Signs (PDF p. 219)

questions.stem: About how many words does a 3-year-old know?
questions.rationale: About 900 words at 3, 1500 at 4, 2100 at 5.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Language Development (PDF p. 215)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A blood collection under the scalp that does not cross sutures and resolves in weeks is:
questions.rationale: Cephalhematoma is subperiosteal blood that does not cross sutures and is absorbed in 3–6 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Head (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Until what age is strabismus considered normal?
questions.rationale: Strabismus is normal until about 6 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Eyes (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Low-set ears in a newborn may suggest:
questions.rationale: Low-set ears suggest chromosomal disorders such as trisomy 21 or kidney anomalies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Ears (PDF p. 219)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How does the nurse test a newborn for choanal atresia?
questions.rationale: Close the mouth and occlude each naris to check for distress; inability to pass a catheter confirms it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Nose (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn's abdomen looks scaphoid (sunken). This suggests:
questions.rationale: An empty or scaphoid abdomen suggests missing contents, as in diaphragmatic hernia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Newborn Abdomen (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: When does the umbilical cord usually fall off?
questions.rationale: The stump usually separates by day 6 to 10.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Umbilical Cord (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has not passed meconium in 24 hours. What should be suspected?
questions.rationale: Failure to pass meconium in 24 hours suggests imperforate anus or meconium ileus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anogenital Area (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: A female newborn has a blood-tinged vaginal discharge. This is:
questions.rationale: Maternal hormones cause pseudomenstruation and vulvar swelling, which are normal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Female Genitalia (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A urethral opening on the underside of the penis is:
questions.rationale: Hypospadias is a ventral opening; epispadias is dorsal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Male Genitalia (PDF p. 220)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A single transverse palmar crease suggests:
questions.rationale: A simian crease could signify Down syndrome.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Extremities (PDF p. 221)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A feeding tube cannot be passed into a newborn's stomach. This confirms:
questions.rationale: Failure to pass through the nares indicates choanal atresia; failure to reach the stomach indicates esophageal atresia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Congenital Anomaly Appraisal (PDF p. 221)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Why should parents not prop the baby's bottle?
questions.rationale: Propping increases aspiration and otitis media risk and deprives infants of being held.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Breastfeeding Facts (PDF p. 221)

questions.topicName: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Why is warming formula in a microwave discouraged?
options: The inner core can get very hot
questions.rationale: Microwaving heats unevenly; the inner core may grow very hot and burn the infant.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Breastfeeding Facts (PDF p. 221)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which is the most severe form of spina bifida?
questions.rationale: Myelomeningocele contains meninges, CSF, and spinal cord or nerves.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida (PDF p. 221)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is a newborn with myelomeningocele positioned before surgery?
questions.rationale: Prone positioning minimizes tension and trauma to the sac, which is covered with moist sterile nonadherent dressing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida (PDF p. 222)

questions.stem: Which supplement helps prevent neural tube defects?
questions.rationale: Folic acid supplementation, especially in the first trimester, helps prevent neural tube defects.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Spina Bifida Prevention (PDF p. 222)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 'cracked pot' sound on percussion of an infant's skull suggests:
questions.rationale: Macewen's sign in hydrocephalus results from widely separated skull bones.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 222)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which shunt is most commonly used for hydrocephalus in children?
questions.rationale: The VP shunt connecting the lateral ventricle to the peritoneum is most common.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 222)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After VP shunt insertion, how is the child positioned?
questions.rationale: Position on the unoperated side to avoid pressure on the valve, flat to avoid rapid CSF reduction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocephalus (PDF p. 223)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the FIRST nursing action when an infant is admitted with bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Isolation is the first action on admission; contacts may need prophylaxis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bacterial Meningitis (PDF p. 223)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which CSF finding supports bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Bacterial meningitis CSF is cloudy with increased protein and decreased glucose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bacterial Meningitis (PDF p. 223)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with CP has a scissor-like gait. Which type is this?
questions.rationale: Spastic CP (cortex) is most common, with a scissor gait; athetoid involves basal ganglia; ataxic the cerebellum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebral Palsy (PDF p. 224)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: White specks in the iris of a child with Down syndrome are:
questions.rationale: Brushfield spots are white iris specks seen in Down syndrome.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Down Syndrome (PDF p. 224)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Care for a child with Down syndrome is planned according to:
questions.rationale: Treatment is based on developmental rather than chronological age.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Down Syndrome (PDF p. 225)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A continuous 'machinery' murmur suggests:
questions.rationale: PDA has a machinery-like murmur; VSD has a loud systolic murmur.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Heart Defects (PDF p. 225)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which is the most common congenital heart defect?
questions.rationale: VSD is the most common CHD (about 30%), usually a left-to-right shunt.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, VSD (PDF p. 225)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant with a heart defect sweats on the scalp during feeding. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Brow or scalp sweating with feeding reflects fatigue and heart failure risk in CHD.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Defects (PDF p. 225)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the most common complication of acyanotic heart defects?
questions.rationale: CHF is the most common complication of acyanotic defects.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acyanotic Defects (PDF p. 225)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which drug may close a PDA in a premature infant?
questions.rationale: Prostaglandin inhibitors such as indomethacin or ibuprofen may close the ductus; PGE1 keeps it open.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, PDA (PDF p. 226)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Bounding radial pulses with absent femoral pulses suggest:
questions.rationale: This is the pathognomonic sign of coarctation; upper-body BP is high.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Coarctation (PDF p. 226)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which defects make up tetralogy of Fallot?
questions.rationale: Tetralogy: pulmonary stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, overriding aorta, VSD.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetralogy of Fallot (PDF p. 227)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with tetralogy of Fallot has a hypercyanotic spell. How is the infant positioned?
questions.rationale: Knee-chest (or squatting) increases systemic resistance and pulmonary blood flow.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tetralogy of Fallot (PDF p. 228)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of cyanotic heart disease?
questions.rationale: Cyanotic defects cause central cyanosis, clubbing, squatting, polycythemia (high Hct), and poor growth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cyanotic Defects (PDF p. 227)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Why is PGE1 infused in an infant with tricuspid atresia?
questions.rationale: PGE1 keeps the ductus arteriosus open to maintain oxygenation until surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tricuspid Atresia (PDF p. 228)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn becomes cyanotic when feeding but pink when crying. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Infants breathe through the nose; crying opens the mouth airway, relieving cyanosis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Choanal Atresia (PDF p. 228)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After tonsillectomy, which sign suggests hemorrhage?
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing may indicate bleeding; turn the child to the side and notify the doctor.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy (PDF p. 229)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which fluid is best after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Give clear, cool, non-citrus, non-carbonated fluids; avoid milk (coats throat) and red liquids (look like blood).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy (PDF p. 229)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is a child positioned after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Prone or side-lying facilitates drainage of secretions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy (PDF p. 229)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with epiglottitis drools and sits in a tripod position. What should the nurse AVOID?
questions.rationale: Never visualize the epiglottis with a tongue blade or take a throat culture; it may cause complete obstruction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Epiglottitis (PDF p. 229)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Rheumatic fever usually follows a strep throat by:
questions.rationale: Rheumatic fever presents 2–6 weeks after an untreated group A strep infection; glomerulonephritis 5–21 days.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillitis (PDF p. 229)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: During which situation should chest physiotherapy be withheld in asthma?
questions.rationale: CPT is not recommended during an acute exacerbation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Asthma (PDF p. 230)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Asthma that persists despite vigorous treatment is called:
questions.rationale: Status asthmaticus is a medical emergency that can cause respiratory failure.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Status Asthmaticus (PDF p. 230)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is an infant with cleft lip fed before repair?
questions.rationale: Hold upright, use an enlarged nipple, direct formula to the side and back of the mouth, and allow rests.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cleft Lip/Palate (PDF p. 230)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After cleft LIP repair, which position is AVOIDED?
questions.rationale: Avoid prone after cheiloplasty to prevent rubbing the suture line on the mattress.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cheiloplasty (PDF p. 231)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After cleft PALATE repair, what should be avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid oral suction, straws, and sharp objects near the palate; use elbow restraints.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Palatoplasty (PDF p. 231)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 5-week-old has projectile, non-bilious vomiting and an olive-shaped mass. What is suspected?
questions.rationale: Pyloric stenosis: projectile non-bilious vomiting at 4–6 weeks, visible peristalsis, olive mass.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pyloric Stenosis (PDF p. 231)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant on IV fluids only for pyloric stenosis needs:
questions.rationale: Infants receiving only IV fluids need a pacifier to meet sucking needs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pyloric Stenosis (PDF p. 231)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which dairy food is usually better tolerated in lactose intolerance?
questions.rationale: Yogurt and hard cheese contain less lactose; milk is taken with food in small amounts.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lactose Intolerance (PDF p. 232)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which grains are ALLOWED in celiac disease?
questions.rationale: Avoid BROW (barley, rye, oats, wheat); rice, corn, and millet are substitutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Celiac Disease (PDF p. 232)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 'double bubble' sign on abdominal x-ray suggests:
questions.rationale: Duodenal atresia shows a double bubble with early bilious vomiting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Duodenal Atresia (PDF p. 232)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn passes no stool in 48 hours and later has ribbon-like stools. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Hirschsprung's (aganglionic megacolon) causes delayed meconium, ribbon stools, and abdominal distention.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hirschsprung's Disease (PDF p. 233)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After Hirschsprung's surgery, what is measured daily?
questions.rationale: Abdominal girth is measured daily; NPO until bowel sounds or flatus return.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hirschsprung's Disease (PDF p. 233)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn's abdominal organs protrude through the umbilicus in a translucent sac. What is the FIRST care?
questions.rationale: Omphalocele: cover the sac immediately with sterile NSS-soaked gauze to prevent drying.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Omphalocele (PDF p. 233)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How does gastroschisis differ from omphalocele?
questions.rationale: Gastroschisis is lateral to the umbilicus with no membrane; omphalocele has a sac at the umbilicus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gastroschisis (PDF p. 233)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother wants to tape a coin over her baby's umbilical hernia. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Taping coins does not help; most umbilical hernias close by about age 3.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Umbilical Hernias (PDF p. 233)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding suggests imperforate anus?
questions.rationale: Failure to pass meconium, absent wink reflex, and inability to insert a catheter suggest imperforate anus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Imperforate Anus (PDF p. 234)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Why are clubfoot casts changed every 1–2 weeks in newborns?
questions.rationale: Rapid neonatal growth requires frequent cast changes during correction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Talipes (PDF p. 234)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which test feels the femoral head slip out of the socket in hip dysplasia?
questions.rationale: Barlow pushes the femur out (instability); Ortolani relocates it with a 'clunk'.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DDH (PDF p. 234)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How is DDH corrected in the newborn period?
questions.rationale: Positioning hips flexed and abducted (frog-leg), such as with multiple diapers or splints, deepens the acetabulum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DDH (PDF p. 235)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has fluid in the scrotum present at birth with no hernia. This is usually:
questions.rationale: Non-communicating hydrocele is trapped fluid seen at birth and needs no treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hydrocele (PDF p. 235)

questions.stem: A mother on day 4 postpartum is tearful and anxious but caring for her baby. This most likely is:
questions.rationale: Postpartum blues are common, peak at 3–7 days, and resolve without medical treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Postpartum Blues (PDF p. 271)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Bryant's traction is used for femur fractures in children younger than:
questions.rationale: Bryant's skin traction is for children under 3 (small weight).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Traction (PDF p. 452)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding during school screening suggests scoliosis?
questions.rationale: Scoliosis: uneven shoulders and hips, asymmetric rib cage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Scoliosis (PDF p. 469)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After spinal fusion for scoliosis, the child is repositioned by:
questions.rationale: Log roll every 2 hours to protect the spine and prevent pressure sores.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Scoliosis Nursing (PDF p. 469)

questions.topicName: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in a young child is:
questions.rationale: LCP: decreased blood supply to the femoral head; self-limiting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Legg-Calvé-Perthes (PDF p. 469)

questions.stem: During the preoperative interview, which information should the nurse report to the anesthesiologist as a risk factor for malignant hyperthermia?
options: The client had heat stroke after a fun run last year
The client's brother developed a very high fever during general anesthesia
The client is allergic to shellfish and iodine
The client takes paracetamol for occasional headaches
questions.rationale: Malignant hyperthermia is an inherited reaction to certain anesthetic agents (succinylcholine and inhalation agents). A family history of problems with general anesthesia is the key risk finding.
explanations: Heat stroke is an environmental heat illness, not a genetic reaction to anesthetics.
Correct: a relative's anesthesia reaction suggests an inherited susceptibility.
Relevant to contrast media, not to malignant hyperthermia.
Paracetamol use has no link to malignant hyperthermia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 192)

questions.stem: A client is on the first postoperative day after an open abdominal surgery and has a nasogastric tube to low suction. The nurse hears no bowel sounds. What should the nurse do?
options: Give sips of water to stimulate peristalsis
Clamp the nasogastric tube for one hour
Notify the surgeon of a paralytic ileus
Document the finding and keep reassessing
questions.rationale: Handling of the bowel during surgery commonly stops peristalsis for 3 to 4 days. Absent bowel sounds on day 1 is expected; the nurse documents and continues to monitor, and the client stays NPO with the NGT in place.
explanations: Oral intake is withheld until bowel sounds return.
The NGT is not clamped or removed without a prescription.
Absent bowel sounds on day 1 is an expected finding, not an emergency.
Correct: this is expected after bowel manipulation; continue monitoring.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 454)

questions.stem: On the third day after a hysterectomy, the client complains of pain in her right calf. What is the nurse's MOST appropriate action?
options: Check the calf for warmth, redness, and swelling
Massage the calf gently to relieve the cramp
Walk the client in the hallway to ease the pain
Give the PRN analgesic and reassess in 30 minutes
questions.rationale: Calf pain after pelvic surgery may signal deep vein thrombosis. The nurse first assesses the calf; massaging or ambulating could dislodge a clot, and giving an analgesic skips needed assessment.
explanations: Correct: assess for signs of DVT before any other action.
Massage can dislodge a thrombus and cause an embolism.
Ambulation can also dislodge a thrombus.
Pain relief before assessment may mask a serious complication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 156)

questions.stem: The nurse is helping a client cough and deep breathe after a thoracic surgery. Which item will make these exercises MOST effective?
options: A pillow to splint the incision
questions.rationale: Splinting the incision with a pillow reduces pain during coughing, so the client can breathe deeply and cough more effectively.
explanations: A nebulizer delivers medication; it does not support coughing.
Suction is for clients who cannot clear secretions themselves.
Correct: splinting reduces incisional pain so coughing is effective.
A resuscitation bag is for assisted ventilation in emergencies.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 418)

questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, which finding is the EARLIEST sign that Mang Ramon may be developing acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)?
questions.rationale: ARDS usually appears 24 to 48 hours after the injury. Tachypnea and dyspnea come first as the body compensates for mild hypoxemia; cyanosis, crackles, and x-ray changes appear later.
explanations: Cyanosis is a late sign of severe hypoxemia.
Correct: tachypnea is the earliest compensatory sign.
Breath sounds are usually clear early, then crackles develop.
Chest x-ray findings may be normal in the early stage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 162)

questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: When redressing the chest tube insertion site, which material should the nurse apply as the FIRST layer?
questions.rationale: Petrolatum gauze is placed directly on the site to make an occlusive seal that prevents air leaks. Gauze layers go on top, secured with strong tape.
explanations: Dry gauze is added over the first layer but does not seal the site.
An antiseptic-soaked layer does not create an airtight seal.
Transparent film does not seal around the tube itself.
Correct: petrolatum gauze creates an occlusive seal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 485)

questions.situation: Mang Ramon, a 45-year-old tricycle driver, is admitted after a road crash with blunt chest trauma. A chest tube is inserted in the emergency room, and he is transferred to the surgical ward.
questions.stem: Mang Ramon later develops a pleural effusion on the opposite side, and a thoracentesis is done. Which finding afterward should concern the nurse MOST?
options: Equal chest expansion on both sides
Respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute
Diminished breath sounds on the punctured side
Mild soreness at the puncture site
questions.rationale: After thoracentesis, diminished breath sounds, dyspnea, retractions, rising respiratory rate, or cyanosis on the affected side can mean a pneumothorax and must be reported.
explanations: Equal expansion is a normal finding.
A rate of 20 is within normal limits.
Correct: this may indicate a pneumothorax.
Mild soreness at the puncture site is expected.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 376)

questions.stem: A client in an acute asthma attack had loud wheezes on arrival. An hour later the nurse can barely hear any breath sounds, and the client is still struggling to breathe. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Severe obstruction with impending respiratory failure
A good response to the bronchodilator therapy
Lower anxiety with slower, quieter breathing
questions.rationale: Wheezing needs moving air. Breath sounds that fade while distress continues mean airflow is severely blocked, a sign of impending respiratory failure.
explanations: Correct: a silent chest in a distressed client is an emergency.
Resolution would come with easier breathing, not ongoing distress.
Improvement would show less effort and better air entry.
The client is still in distress, so this is not calming.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 184)

questions.stem: During a home visit, a client with COPD on oxygen at 2 L/min by concentrator reports more shortness of breath than usual. The respiratory rate is 22. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Raise the oxygen flow to 6 L/min
Explain that this is expected with COPD
questions.rationale: The nurse gathers more data first. Oxygen is not increased without a prescription because clients with COPD can retain carbon dioxide; calling for transfer is premature.
explanations: Higher oxygen can depress the breathing drive in COPD and needs a prescription.
Correct: more assessment is needed before acting.
False reassurance ignores a change in condition.
Premature: the client is not yet shown to be in severe distress.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 186)

questions.stem: A client is admitted in sickle cell crisis. Which intervention is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia drives red cells to sickle, so oxygen comes first, and airway and breathing take priority over circulation. Fluids and analgesics follow.
explanations: Hydration is important but follows oxygenation.
Pain relief is essential but is not the first priority.
Transfusion is not the first-line priority action.
Correct: oxygen addresses the hypoxemia causing sickling.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 339)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client discharged with a permanent pacemaker shows correct understanding of self-care?
options: 'I will check my pulse every day and report any change.'
'We have to give away our microwave oven.'
'I should stop using the electric fan at home.'
'I can never travel by airplane again.'
questions.rationale: Clients with pacemakers learn to take their pulse accurately and report changes in rate or rhythm. Grounded household appliances in good repair are safe, and air travel is allowed after informing security.
explanations: Correct: daily pulse checks detect pacemaker problems.
Grounded appliances in good repair are safe.
Household fans are safe to use.
Air travel is allowed; the client shows the pacemaker ID card at security.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 345)

questions.stem: A client with acute pericarditis has sharp chest pain that worsens on deep breathing. Which position should the nurse help the client into for comfort?
options: Flat on the back with one pillow
questions.rationale: Pericarditis pain worsens when lying supine and eases when sitting up and leaning forward, which reduces pressure on the inflamed pericardium.
explanations: Side-lying does not relieve pericardial friction.
The supine position intensifies the pain.
Correct: sitting and leaning forward eases the pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 405)

questions.stem: After angioplasty of the iliac artery, which assessment BEST detects bleeding from the procedure site?
options: Asking the client to rate the pain
questions.rationale: Bleeding from the iliac artery collects in the retroperitoneal space, which shows as increasing abdominal girth. Pulses and capillary refill show patency and perfusion, not hidden bleeding.
explanations: Correct: retroperitoneal bleeding increases abdominal girth.
Mild discomfort is expected and is not a direct measure.
Capillary refill reflects distal perfusion, not hidden bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 489)

questions.stem: Which solution should the nurse prepare for continuous bladder irrigation after a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP)?
questions.rationale: Isotonic sterile normal saline is used. Sterile water can be absorbed systemically and cause hemolysis and kidney failure; dextrose solutions are not instilled into the bladder.
explanations: Correct: isotonic saline is used for CBI.
Hypotonic water can be absorbed and cause hemolysis.
Dextrose solutions are not introduced into the bladder.
Dakin's solution is a hypochlorite wound irrigant.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 391)

questions.stem: A client's total serum calcium is 7.5 mg/dL. Which assessment finding should the nurse expect?
options: Shortened QT interval on the ECG
questions.rationale: A calcium level below 9 mg/dL is hypocalcemia, which increases neuromuscular excitability: twitching, tetany, hyperactive reflexes, positive Trousseau's and Chvostek's signs, and a prolonged QT interval.
explanations: Correct: carpal spasm with a BP cuff shows neuromuscular irritability.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 527)

questions.stem: A client with acute kidney injury is on a fluid restriction of 1,500 mL per day. Which nursing measure helps the client keep to this restriction?
options: Keep a full water pitcher at the bedside
Offer ice chips and lip balm for thirst
questions.rationale: Ice chips and lip ointment ease thirst, and removing the pitcher helps compliance. Alcohol-based mouthwash dries the mucosa, and salty food increases thirst.
explanations: A visible pitcher encourages drinking beyond the limit.
Correct: ice chips and lip balm relieve thirst within the limit.
Alcohol dries the mouth and worsens thirst.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 412)

questions.stem: Before starting a continuous IV infusion for a dehydrated client, which baseline data is MOST important for monitoring the client's fluid status?
questions.rationale: Daily weights compared against a baseline are the most sensitive and specific indicator of fluid volume change. The other data are useful but less precise.
explanations: Electrolytes are useful but do not measure volume change directly.
Correct: weight is the most sensitive indicator of fluid volume status.
I&O records are often incomplete and less precise.
Specific gravity reflects concentration, not total volume.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1380)

questions.stem: A wound culture grows methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Which precautions should the nurse put in place?
questions.rationale: Contact precautions (standard precautions plus gloves and gown) are used for draining wounds, diarrhea, and methicillin-resistant infections.
explanations: Airborne precautions are for TB, measles, and varicella.
Droplet precautions are for organisms spread by large droplets, such as influenza.
Correct: MRSA in a wound spreads by direct and indirect contact.
Reverse isolation protects an immunosuppressed client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 610)

questions.stem: A client on chemotherapy is admitted on neutropenic precautions. Which action by the nurse is appropriate?
options: Put a vase of fresh flowers in the room
Room the client with a postoperative client
Serve fresh fruit salad at lunch
Have the client wear a mask outside the room
questions.rationale: A neutropenic client is placed in a private room and wears a mask whenever leaving it. Fresh flowers and raw fruit can carry organisms.
explanations: Fresh flowers and plants can harbor organisms.
The client needs a private room.
Raw fruit and vegetables can carry microorganisms.
Correct: a mask protects the client outside the room.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 696)

questions.stem: A client with cervical cancer returns from having a radiation implant inserted. Which action is the nurse's PRIORITY?
options: Assign the client to a private room
Place the client on protective isolation
Encourage her children to visit often
questions.rationale: A client with a radiation implant is placed in a private room with limited visitors to reduce others' exposure. Pregnant women and anyone under 16 should not visit, and bed rest keeps the implant in place.
explanations: Correct: a private room limits others' radiation exposure.
Others, not the client, need protection.
Bed rest is maintained to keep the implant in place.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 741)

questions.stem: A client with multiple myeloma is receiving IV hydration at 100 mL per hour. Which finding BEST shows the treatment is working?
questions.rationale: Hydration protects the kidneys from protein, calcium, and uric acid precipitating in the tubules. Creatinine is the most accurate measure of renal function.
explanations: Weight gain may mean fluid overload, not success.
Respiratory rate is unrelated to the goal of hydration.
Correct: a normal creatinine shows protected kidney function.
Blood pressure does not measure renal protection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 458)

questions.stem: A 16-year-old asks for voluntary HIV testing at a social hygiene clinic. Under RA 11166, whose consent is needed?
questions.rationale: For persons 15 to below 18 years old, consent to voluntary HIV testing is obtained from the child without the need for parental or guardian consent.
explanations: Correct: minors 15 to 17 may consent themselves.
Not needed for this age group.
The school has no role in consent.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11166, Sec. 29(a) (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: An adult client's HIV test is reactive. Under RA 11166, to whom should the result be disclosed?
options: Only the client who was tested
questions.rationale: Results are disclosed only to the individual who submitted to the test. Disclosure to others needs written consent, except in limited cases such as DOH surveillance reporting.
explanations: Disclosure to a spouse needs the client's consent.
Correct: only to the person tested.
Community workers are not entitled to the result.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11166, Sec. 46 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Under RA 11166, which service must every HIV testing facility provide for free?
options: Hospital admission for every reactive client
Mandatory testing for all clinic visitors
questions.rationale: All HIV testing facilities must give free pre-test and post-test counseling. Testing is voluntary and needs informed consent.
explanations: Not the facility requirement in this provision.
Correct: free pre- and post-test counseling.
Admission depends on the client's condition.
Testing is non-compulsory except in limited cases.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11166, Sec. 31 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: During a variance analysis of critical paths, which finding shows the need for further action?
options: The client was discharged a day earlier than planned
The client could not walk on day 2 as the path expected
The client's pain was controlled as scheduled
The client finished discharge teaching on time
questions.rationale: A variance is a deviation from the critical path. A negative variance, such as a missed expected outcome, needs action to keep the client on track.
explanations: A positive variance; no corrective action needed.
Correct: a negative variance needs follow-up.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 643)

questions.stem: How often is variance analysis done for clients on critical paths?
options: Only on the day of discharge
questions.rationale: Variance analysis is continuous: caregivers keep comparing client outcomes with the critical path so that negative variances are caught early.
explanations: A single check misses later variances.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 677)

questions.stem: A client with Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia is to receive IV pentamidine. How should the nurse give it safely?
options: Over 1 hour with the client ambulating
Over 1 hour with the client lying supine
As a 5-minute IV push with the client seated
Over 4 hours with the client in high Fowler's
questions.rationale: Pentamidine is infused over 1 hour with the client supine to reduce the risk of severe hypotension and dysrhythmias. BP and cardiac rhythm are monitored.
explanations: Ambulating risks a fall from hypotension.
Correct: infuse over 1 hour, client supine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q17 (PDF p. 155)

questions.stem: A client takes sotalol 80 mg twice daily. Which finding suggests an ADVERSE effect of the drug?
questions.rationale: Sotalol is a beta blocker. Adverse effects include palpitations, bradycardia, irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing, signs of heart failure, and cold hands and feet.
explanations: Not an adverse effect of sotalol.
Not an adverse effect of sotalol.
Not an adverse effect of sotalol.
Correct: palpitations signal a cardiac adverse effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q20 (PDF p. 158)

questions.situation: Mr. Reyes, 50, had a liver transplant 3 months ago. He is on immunosuppressants to prevent organ rejection and comes to the transplant clinic for follow-up.
questions.stem: He takes tacrolimus daily. Which finding suggests an ADVERSE effect of the drug?
questions.rationale: Tacrolimus can cause nephrotoxicity, shown by rising serum creatinine and decreasing urine output, as well as pleural effusion. Hypertension, not hypotension, is a common side effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q22 (PDF p. 161)

questions.situation: Mr. Reyes, 50, had a liver transplant 3 months ago. He is on immunosuppressants to prevent organ rejection and comes to the transplant clinic for follow-up.
questions.stem: He is also on cyclosporine. Which laboratory finding is an adverse effect of cyclosporine?
questions.rationale: Cyclosporine adverse effects include nephrotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, infection, hypertension, tremor, hirsutism, hypomagnesemia, hyperkalemia, and hyperglycemia.
explanations: Correct: hyperkalemia can occur with cyclosporine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q100 (PDF p. 249)

questions.stem: A client on torsemide, a loop diuretic, has new lab results. Which value suggests an adverse effect of the drug?
questions.rationale: Loop diuretics can cause profound water and electrolyte loss. Normal potassium is 3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L, so 3.1 mEq/L shows depletion. The other values are within normal limits.
explanations: At the low end of normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q32 (PDF p. 171)

questions.stem: A client is receiving IV tobramycin every 8 hours. Which finding should the nurse report as a possible adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic (rising BUN and creatinine), ototoxic (tinnitus, hearing loss), and neurotoxic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q50 (PDF p. 190)

questions.stem: A client has taken a calcium channel blocker for hypertension for 2 months. Which finding suggests drug tolerance has developed?
questions.rationale: Tolerance to an antihypertensive shows as rising blood pressure readings despite therapy. The provider may adjust the dose, change the drug, or add a diuretic.
explanations: Correct: rising BP despite therapy shows tolerance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q55 (PDF p. 196)

questions.stem: IV potassium chloride is prescribed for a client with hypokalemia. Which action is correct?
options: Give it as a slow IV push
Dilute it and give it by infusion pump
Use a filter in the IV line
Apply cold compresses to the IV site
questions.rationale: Potassium chloride irritates veins and must be diluted and given with an infusion pump. It is never given by IV push or bolus, which can cause cardiac arrest.
explanations: Never give potassium by push; it can cause cardiac arrest.
Correct: dilute and use a pump.
A filter is not needed for potassium.
Cold constricts the vein and adds irritation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q110 (PDF p. 259)

questions.stem: Ondansetron is prescribed for a client receiving chemotherapy. By which route does the nurse expect it to be given for chemotherapy-induced nausea?
questions.rationale: Ondansetron comes in oral, IM, and IV forms. The IV route is used for nausea relief in clients receiving chemotherapy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q125 (PDF p. 275)

questions.stem: Which finding is a common dose-related side effect of beta-adrenergic blockers?
questions.rationale: Dose-related side effects of beta blockers include dizziness from hypotension, bradycardia, and sexual dysfunction.
explanations: Fatigue, not more energy, is common.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q156 (PDF p. 306)

questions.stem: A client with chronic kidney disease is started on epoetin alfa. Which supplement is needed for the drug to work fully?
questions.rationale: Epoetin stimulates red cell production, which needs iron. Without iron the client does not get the full benefit. Hypertension is a side effect of epoetin.
explanations: Not required for red cell production.
Not required for red cell production.
Correct: iron is needed to make red cells.
Not required for red cell production.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q190 (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: A client asks why the first dose of prazosin must be taken at bedtime. The nurse explains that the first dose may cause:
options: Sudden dizziness or fainting from low BP
questions.rationale: Prazosin, an alpha blocker, can cause a 'first-dose' hypotensive reaction with dizziness, lightheadedness, and possible fainting. It is better tolerated if the client is already in bed.
explanations: Not the reason for bedtime dosing.
Not the reason for bedtime dosing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q208 (PDF p. 363)
