questions.stem: Furosemide 40 mg IV is given to a client with dyspnea from pulmonary congestion. One hour later, which finding BEST shows the drug achieved its purpose?
questions.rationale: Here furosemide was given to reduce preload and relieve pulmonary congestion. Clear lungs show that purpose was met; more urine is expected but is not the goal itself.
explanations: Correct: shows the congestion has resolved.
Expected, but not the therapeutic goal.
Not the goal of the therapy.
Not the goal of the therapy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q215 (PDF p. 370)

questions.stem: During an IV amphotericin B infusion for histoplasmosis, the nurse should monitor closely for:
options: A sudden large increase in urine
questions.rationale: Amphotericin B is toxic. It can cause chills, fever, headache, vomiting, and impaired renal function (decreased urine output) during infusion, and it irritates veins, often causing thrombophlebitis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q233 (PDF p. 388)

questions.stem: A client on hemodialysis takes enalapril daily. When should the nurse give the dose on a dialysis day?
questions.rationale: Antihypertensives are given after hemodialysis. This prevents hypotension during dialysis and prevents the drug from being removed by dialysis.
explanations: Risks hypotension, and the drug is dialyzed out.
Risks hypotension, and the drug is dialyzed out.
Skipping a day leaves BP uncontrolled.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q257 (PDF p. 414)

questions.stem: A client on a thiazide diuretic is monitored for hypokalemia. Which ECG finding is expected?
questions.rationale: Hypokalemia (below 3.5 mEq/L) causes ST depression, inverted T waves, a prominent U wave, and heart block, plus hyporeflexia, muscle weakness, and hypoactive bowel sounds.
explanations: Correct: a classic sign of hypokalemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q268 (PDF p. 425)

questions.stem: Before giving procainamide, an antidysrhythmic, what should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Check the blood pressure and pulse
Schedule a drug level for next week
questions.rationale: BP and pulse are checked before procainamide because it can cause toxic cardiac effects. Serum levels are also monitored (therapeutic level 4 to 10 mcg/mL).
explanations: Correct: assess BP and pulse before giving it.
Levels are monitored, but this does not protect the current dose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q270 (PDF p. 427)

questions.stem: A client on digoxin has a serum level of 2.3 ng/mL. Which complaint is consistent with this level?
questions.rationale: The therapeutic range is 0.8 to 2.0 ng/mL. Toxicity causes anorexia, nausea, vomiting, drowsiness, photophobia, and visual changes such as halos around bright objects.
explanations: Correct: visual disturbance is a sign of toxicity.
Not a sign of digoxin toxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q287 (PDF p. 446)

questions.stem: A client on a heparin infusion has a PTT of 65 seconds (control 30 seconds). What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The therapeutic PTT for heparin is 1.5 to 2.5 times the control (45 to 75 seconds here), so 65 seconds is therapeutic.
explanations: The value is therapeutic, not excessive.
Protamine is for excessive anticoagulation or bleeding.
Correct: the PTT is in the therapeutic range.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q290 (PDF p. 450)

questions.stem: Aspirin is given to a client before percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA). What is its purpose?
options: To relieve pain after the procedure
To prevent fever after the procedure
questions.rationale: Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation, reducing the risk of the artery occluding during and after angioplasty.
explanations: Not the reason for giving it before PTCA.
Correct: it is an antiplatelet agent.
Aspirin does not lower blood pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q347 (PDF p. 515)

questions.stem: Acetaminophen is prescribed to be given before a topical nitrate. What is the reason?
options: Headache is a common side effect of nitrates
It prevents fever caused by the nitrate
It protects the stomach from the nitrate
questions.rationale: Nitrates dilate blood vessels, which often causes headache. Acetaminophen given beforehand prevents or lessens it. The headaches usually lessen with continued use.
explanations: It does not potentiate the nitrate.
Topical nitrates do not irritate the stomach.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q348 (PDF p. 516)

questions.situation: Mang Ernesto, 68, has atrial fibrillation and is discharged on warfarin to prevent stroke.
questions.stem: Which food should Mang Ernesto limit because of its high vitamin K content?
questions.rationale: Warfarin works against vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, so intake of vitamin K-rich foods (green leafy vegetables, broccoli, cabbage, turnips, liver, tea) is kept limited and consistent.
explanations: Oranges are high in vitamin C, not K.
Correct: broccoli is high in vitamin K.
Strawberries are high in vitamin C.
Rice is low in vitamin K.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q350 (PDF p. 518)

questions.situation: Mang Ernesto, 68, has atrial fibrillation and is discharged on warfarin to prevent stroke.
questions.stem: The nurse tells Mang Ernesto to shave with an electric razor. Which reason BEST supports this instruction?
options: Cuts and bleeding must be avoided
Blades contain metals that react with warfarin
questions.rationale: Anticoagulants increase the risk of bleeding, so clients are taught measures that prevent cuts, such as using an electric razor and a soft toothbrush.
explanations: Correct: the goal is to prevent bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q473 (PDF p. 657)

questions.stem: A client receiving cisplatin complains of ringing in the ears. The nurse recognizes this as:
options: An expected sign that the drug is working
An allergic reaction to the infusion
questions.rationale: Cisplatin, a platinum compound, can cause ototoxicity with tinnitus and hearing loss. The nurse assesses hearing during therapy.
explanations: Tinnitus is a toxic effect, not a sign of effectiveness.
Not the cause of tinnitus here.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q366 (PDF p. 534)

questions.stem: A client received atropine sulfate before surgery. Which effect should the nurse monitor for in the immediate postoperative period?
questions.rationale: Atropine is an anticholinergic. It causes tachycardia, drowsiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention. It is contraindicated in glaucoma.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q377 (PDF p. 546)

questions.stem: Flecainide is prescribed for a client with frequent runs of ventricular tachycardia. Which safety measure is MOST specific to this drug?
options: Monitoring for new or worsening dysrhythmias
Checking the blood glucose before meals
questions.rationale: Flecainide slows conduction and reduces excitability, but it can itself cause new or worse dysrhythmias (proarrhythmia). Cardiac rhythm monitoring is the key safety measure.
explanations: Standard care, not specific to flecainide.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q399 (PDF p. 569)

questions.stem: Just before an IV dose of tobramycin, the client reports dizziness and ringing in the ears. What should the nurse do?
options: Give an antiemetic with the dose
Hold the dose and notify the physician
questions.rationale: Vertigo and tinnitus suggest eighth cranial nerve damage (ototoxicity), which can become permanent hearing loss. The dose is held and the prescriber notified.
explanations: Giving the dose risks permanent hearing loss.
Treating the symptom ignores the toxicity.
Correct: hold the dose and report it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q429 (PDF p. 607)

questions.stem: Which safety measure must be in place before giving IV amiodarone for a life-threatening ventricular dysrhythmia?
questions.rationale: Amiodarone treats life-threatening ventricular dysrhythmias. The client must be on continuous cardiac monitoring, and the drug is given by infusion pump.
explanations: May be in place but is not specific to amiodarone.
Oximetry alone does not monitor rhythm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q430 (PDF p. 608)

questions.stem: A client on a heparin infusion after a myocardial infarction has an aPTT of 100 seconds. Before reporting it, which drug should the nurse make sure is available?
questions.rationale: An aPTT of 100 seconds exceeds the therapeutic range (about 60 to 70 seconds) and means a risk of bleeding. Protamine sulfate is the antidote for heparin.
explanations: FFP is used for warfarin-related bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q590 (PDF p. 798)

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a postoperative client using a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump?
options: 'Push the button before the pain becomes severe.'
'Ask your family to press it while you sleep.'
'Wait until the pain is unbearable to press it.'
'Press it every few minutes even without pain.'
questions.rationale: The client presses the button before pain becomes too great and reports nausea, vomiting, inability to void, and breakthrough pain. Only the client should press the button.
explanations: Correct: early dosing keeps pain under control.
Others pressing the button risks overdose.
Severe pain is harder to control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q515 (PDF p. 710)

questions.stem: IV foscarnet is prescribed for CMV retinitis in a client with AIDS. What should the nurse do before giving it?
options: Prepare folic acid as an antidote
Run it on a controlled infusion device
Give it as a rapid IV push
questions.rationale: Foscarnet is potentially toxic, especially to the kidneys, so it is given with a controlled infusion device and serum creatinine is checked often.
explanations: Folic acid is not an antidote for foscarnet.
Correct: controlled infusion for a toxic drug.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q548 (PDF p. 749)

questions.stem: A client with atrial fibrillation asks why long-term anticoagulants are needed. What is the BEST explanation?
options: 'Blood backs up in your legs and forms clots.'
'Blood pools in the upper heart chambers and can clot.'
'Your heart muscle is too weak to pump.'
questions.rationale: Quivering atria lose their organized contraction ('atrial kick'), so blood stagnates and can form mural thrombi. These clots can travel to the lungs or brain.
explanations: The clots form in the atria, not the legs.
Correct: atrial pooling leads to mural thrombi.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q648 (PDF p. 866)

questions.stem: A client with heart failure is starting digoxin at home. What should the nurse teach the client to do to detect early complications?
options: Check the blood pressure once a week
questions.rationale: The client takes their pulse daily and reports a rate below 60 or above 100 beats per minute to the provider.
explanations: Correct: daily pulse checks detect toxicity early.
Daily weights are better for heart failure, but the pulse is key for digoxin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q675 (PDF p. 895)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client correctly understands diltiazem therapy for Prinzmetal angina?
options: 'I will get up slowly from bed.'
'I can stop it once my chest pain goes away.'
questions.rationale: Diltiazem, a calcium channel blocker, can cause hypotension, so the client rises slowly. It is taken before meals and at bedtime. Irregular heartbeat, dyspnea, marked dizziness, or constipation are reported.
explanations: Correct: rising slowly prevents falls from hypotension.
Constipation is a side effect to report.
It is not stopped without the provider.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q677 (PDF p. 897)

questions.stem: A client with heart failure takes triamterene. Which food is the BEST choice for this client?
questions.rationale: Triamterene is potassium-sparing, so high-potassium foods (bananas, oranges, potatoes) are limited. Canned foods are often lower in potassium.
explanations: Correct: canned fruit is lower in potassium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q679 (PDF p. 899)

questions.stem: A client with breast cancer is starting cyclophosphamide. Which instruction is MOST important to prevent a serious adverse effect?
options: Drink plenty of fluids during therapy
questions.rationale: Cyclophosphamide can cause hemorrhagic cystitis, so copious fluids are needed. Hair grows back, and a sore throat may signal infection and must be reported.
explanations: A sore throat may mean infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q680 (PDF p. 900)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client on timolol, a beta blocker, shows correct understanding?
options: 'I can stop it when my BP is normal.'
'I will hold it if my pulse is below 60.'
'I may double the dose if I feel dizzy.'
questions.rationale: Clients on beta blockers check their pulse daily and hold the dose and notify the provider if it is below 60. They do not stop the drug abruptly, they change positions slowly, and they report shortness of breath.
explanations: Correct: hold for a pulse below 60 and notify the provider.
The dose is never changed by the client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q719 (PDF p. 941)

questions.stem: A client is taking benazepril, an ACE inhibitor, for hypertension. Which instruction is correct?
options: Check the BP only once a year
Get up quickly in the morning
questions.rationale: Clients on ACE inhibitors avoid salt, change positions slowly, monitor their BP weekly, and continue other lifestyle changes.
explanations: Rising quickly can cause orthostatic hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q720 (PDF p. 942)

questions.stem: Dipyridamole is prescribed for a client after heart valve replacement. What is its purpose?
options: To lower the client's blood pressure
To prevent a future heart attack
To protect the new valve from clots
To prevent a stroke in the future
questions.rationale: Dipyridamole is an antiplatelet drug often given with warfarin to protect artificial heart valves. It does not itself prevent stroke or heart attack and is not an antihypertensive.
explanations: Correct: antiplatelet protection of the valve.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q723 (PDF p. 945)

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking ketoconazole?
options: Limit alcohol to two drinks a day
Take it on an empty stomach
questions.rationale: Ketoconazole increases photosensitivity, so sun exposure is avoided. It is hepatotoxic (avoid alcohol), needs gastric acid to work (avoid antacids for 2 hours), and is taken with food.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q752 (PDF p. 981)

questions.stem: A client is started on lisinopril. Which frequent side effect should the nurse tell the client about?
questions.rationale: Cough is a frequent side effect of all ACE inhibitors. Hypertension is the reason for the drug, not a side effect.
explanations: Correct: a hallmark ACE inhibitor side effect.
This is what the drug treats.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q776 (PDF p. 1006)

questions.stem: When teaching a male client about spironolactone, which psychosocial side effect should the nurse address?
questions.rationale: Spironolactone can cause decreased libido, gynecomastia in males, and hirsutism in females, which can threaten body image and sexual identity.
explanations: Not a specific effect of spironolactone.
Correct: affects sexual function and body image.
It is a diuretic and reduces edema.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q826 (PDF p. 1061)

questions.stem: A client with a history of depression is prescribed nadolol for angina. What is MOST important to include when counseling this client?
options: Risk of a fast heart rate
questions.rationale: Beta blockers can worsen depression in clients with a history of it, so these clients are monitored closely. Beta blockers cause bradycardia, not tachycardia.
explanations: Possible, but not the most important point.
Beta blockers can mask hypoglycemia; they do not commonly cause it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q841 (PDF p. 1078)

questions.stem: A client with terminal cancer fears becoming addicted to the opioid prescribed for pain. What is the nurse's BEST response?
options: 'Wait as long as you can between doses.'
'Take it only when the pain is very severe.'
'Addiction is rare when opioids are taken for pain.'
'Ask your doctor for a weaker drug.'
questions.rationale: The nurse gives correct information: addiction is rare when medication is taken to relieve pain. Leaving the client in pain is not acceptable.
explanations: Severe pain is harder to control.
Correct: accurate reassurance while keeping pain controlled.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q906 (PDF p. 1149)

questions.stem: A client on quinidine for an atrial dysrhythmia misses a dose and remembers 4 hours later. What should the client do?
options: Take the next dose as usual
Stop the drug and call the doctor
questions.rationale: A missed quinidine dose is taken only if remembered within 2 hours; otherwise it is omitted and the normal schedule resumes. Extra or late doses are unsafe.
explanations: Too late; more than 2 hours have passed.
Correct: omit it and resume the usual schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1067 (PDF p. 1349)

questions.stem: A transplant client on cyclosporine plans breakfast. Which drink should the client avoid?
questions.rationale: Grapefruit juice blocks cyclosporine metabolism and can raise its levels by 50% to 100%, greatly increasing the risk of toxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1071 (PDF p. 1353)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client is using a nitroglycerin patch correctly?
options: 'I'll add a second patch if chest pain occurs.'
'I'll put it on a hairless part of my body.'
'I'll rub it in to make it work faster.'
'I'll use it only when I feel chest pain.'
questions.rationale: Topical nitroglycerin is applied to a nonhairy area on a scheduled basis. It is not used specifically for chest pain attacks and is not rubbed in.
explanations: Patches are not added for acute pain.
Correct: apply to a nonhairy area.
Topical nitrates are not rubbed in.
Patches are used on a schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1083 (PDF p. 1365)

questions.stem: Which instruction is appropriate for a client taking furosemide?
options: Use extra salt in hot weather
questions.rationale: Furosemide is potassium-losing and can cause orthostatic hypotension. The client changes positions slowly, avoids overheating, and discusses alcohol use with the provider.
explanations: Furosemide wastes potassium, so potassium foods are fine.
Correct: heat worsens fluid loss and hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1084 (PDF p. 1366)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client correctly understands clonidine patch use?
options: 'I'll trim the patch if an edge lifts.'
'I'll take it off whenever I bathe.'
'I'll put it on a hairy area of my chest.'
questions.rationale: The clonidine patch is changed every 7 days and left on while bathing. It is applied to a hairless site and never trimmed, which would alter the dose. A slightly loose patch is covered with the adhesive overlay.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1085 (PDF p. 1367)

questions.stem: A client with liver cirrhosis takes triamterene daily. Which finding is an adverse effect of this drug?
questions.rationale: Triamterene is potassium-retaining, so the concern is hyperkalemia, along with dehydration, hyponatremia, and lethargy.
explanations: It causes drowsiness and lethargy instead.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1102 (PDF p. 1386)

questions.stem: A client with heart failure is on long-term diuretics. Which drug puts the client MOST at risk for hypokalemia?
questions.rationale: Bumetanide is a loop diuretic that wastes potassium. Triamterene, spironolactone, and amiloride are potassium-sparing.
explanations: Correct: a loop diuretic causes potassium loss.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1128 (PDF p. 1413)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client taking prazosin for hypertension shows a need for more teaching?
options: 'I will skip doses for a few days if dizzy.'
'I will check my blood pressure at home.'
'I will report dizziness to my doctor.'
questions.rationale: Skipping prazosin can cause an abrupt rise in blood pressure. Dizziness and impotence are side effects to report, not reasons to stop on one's own.
explanations: Correct answer: skipping doses causes rebound hypertension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1131 (PDF p. 1416)

questions.stem: A client with peptic ulcer disease takes large amounts of oral antacids. Which acid-base imbalance should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: Excess antacids can cause metabolic alkalosis (pH above 7.45, HCO3 above 27 mEq/L).
explanations: Correct: excess base intake causes alkalosis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1132 (PDF p. 1417)

questions.stem: A client on furosemide and digoxin reports anorexia, nausea, and yellow vision before the morning doses. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: These symptoms suggest digoxin toxicity. The nurse checks the digoxin level first (then potassium, since low potassium worsens toxicity) and holds the drugs until the results are known.
explanations: Furosemide can lower potassium and worsen toxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1176 (PDF p. 1465)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands how to use sublingual nitroglycerin?
options: 'I'll keep the tablets in my shirt pocket.'
'I'll take one 5 to 10 minutes before activity.'
'I'll keep tablets for several years if unopened.'
'I'll store them in a pill box in the sun.'
questions.rationale: Nitroglycerin can be taken 5 to 10 minutes before an activity that triggers chest pain. It is unstable in heat, cold, and light, so it is not kept close to the body.
explanations: Tablets are discarded 3 to 6 months after opening, by the expiry date.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1213 (PDF p. 1506)

questions.stem: A client started betaxolol for hypertension. Which finding shows the drug is having its INTENDED effect?
options: Weight loss of 2 kg in 2 days
questions.rationale: Betaxolol, a beta blocker, lowers blood pressure. Bradycardia, weight gain, and edema are adverse effects that suggest heart failure.
explanations: Edema suggests heart failure, an adverse effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1223 (PDF p. 1516)

questions.stem: A client takes theophylline, a xanthine bronchodilator. Which drink is the BEST choice?
questions.rationale: Cola, coffee, and chocolate contain xanthines, which add to the cardiac and CNS side effects of theophylline.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1224 (PDF p. 1517)

questions.stem: A client with AIDS is receiving amphotericin B for a fungal lung infection. Which laboratory finding is an adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Amphotericin B can cause severe hypokalemia (worsened by renal tubular acidosis), leading to muscle weakness and ECG changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1230 (PDF p. 1523)

questions.stem: A client with hyperkalemia receives sodium polystyrene sulfonate. Which serum potassium shows the therapy is effective?
questions.rationale: Normal adult serum potassium is 3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L, so only 4.9 is normal. Hyperkalemia causes tall peaked T waves, flat P waves, and a widened QRS.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1236 (PDF p. 1529)

questions.stem: How is a client usually taught to use transdermal nitroglycerin patches?
options: A new patch once every 7 days
A new patch each morning, off at night
One patch worn for 3 days straight
A patch only during chest pain
questions.rationale: A new patch is applied each morning and left on for 12 to 16 hours as prescribed. The patch-free period helps prevent tolerance. Daily application ensures proper dosing.
explanations: Correct: a daily patch with a patch-free period.
Patches are not used for acute pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1251 (PDF p. 1550)

questions.stem: A client is on a continuous IV heparin infusion. Which finding should the nurse watch for as an adverse effect?
questions.rationale: Heparin increases the risk of bleeding: gum bleeding, ecchymoses, pink or cloudy urine, tarry stools, and occult blood in body fluids.
explanations: Not a direct effect of heparin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1277 (PDF p. 1576)

questions.stem: Chemical cardioversion is ordered for a client with atrial fibrillation. Which drug does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Amiodarone, an antidysrhythmic, can restore normal sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation. Lidocaine treats ventricular dysrhythmias. Continuous cardiac monitoring is required.
explanations: A vasodilator, not used for cardioversion.
A vasodilator, not used for cardioversion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1279 (PDF p. 1580)

questions.stem: When should blood for a serum digoxin level be drawn?
questions.rationale: Digoxin levels are usually drawn just before a dose (or 6 to 8 hours after one) so the result is not falsely high.
explanations: Correct: a trough level avoids a false high.
The level would be falsely elevated.
The level would be falsely elevated.
The level would be falsely elevated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1317 (PDF p. 1619)

questions.stem: A client with CKD is receiving epoetin alfa. Which serious adverse effect should the nurse monitor for?
questions.rationale: Hypertension and seizures are the most serious adverse effects of epoetin alfa. The drug treats anemia.
explanations: Not an adverse effect of epoetin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1384 (PDF p. 1687)

questions.stem: How should a client take amiloride 10 mg daily for hypertension?
options: At bedtime on an empty stomach
Only when the BP is high
questions.rationale: Amiloride, a potassium-sparing diuretic, is taken in the morning to avoid nocturia and with food to improve bioavailability. Sodium is restricted when it is used for hypertension.
explanations: It is taken daily, not as needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1388 (PDF p. 1691)

questions.stem: Why is diphenhydramine given to a client before a blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: Urticaria (rash with itching) is a transfusion reaction that premedication with an antihistamine can prevent. Acetaminophen is given to prevent fever and chills.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1390 (PDF p. 1693)

questions.stem: After mastectomy, a client's tumor is estrogen receptor-positive. Which follow-up treatment is commonly prescribed?
questions.rationale: Tamoxifen competes with estrogen for binding sites in breast tissue and is commonly given for years after surgery for ER-positive tumors. Estrogen would stimulate the tumor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1416 (PDF p. 1722)

questions.stem: Quinidine gluconate is prescribed. Which condition in the record is a CONTRAINDICATION?
questions.rationale: Quinidine is contraindicated in complete AV block, intraventricular conduction defects, escape rhythms, and myasthenia gravis. It is used with caution in asthma.
explanations: Not a contraindication unless it is myasthenia gravis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1462 (PDF p. 1771)

questions.stem: Which electrolyte imbalance should the nurse monitor for MOST often in a client on hydrochlorothiazide?
questions.rationale: Thiazides are potassium-losing. Other effects include hyponatremia, hypercalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, and hyperglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1472 (PDF p. 1781)

questions.stem: A client with AIDS and CMV retinitis is on ganciclovir. Which nursing action is appropriate?
options: Give it only on an empty stomach
Use bleeding precautions such as a soft toothbrush
questions.rationale: Ganciclovir frequently causes neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, so the nurse uses bleeding precautions (soft toothbrush, electric razor) and watches for bleeding.
explanations: Not a key effect of ganciclovir.
Correct: thrombocytopenia raises the bleeding risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1478 (PDF p. 1787)

questions.stem: A client on quinidine for ventricular ectopy develops diarrhea and nausea. What should the client do?
options: Stop the drug until it passes
Halve the dose on their own
Notify the provider but keep taking it
questions.rationale: GI upset and dizziness are common with quinidine and are reported, but the client never stops the drug. A sudden fall in the drug level can trigger dysrhythmias.
explanations: The dose is never changed by the client.
Correct: report it, but keep taking the drug.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1479 (PDF p. 1788)

questions.stem: A client taking cyclosporine after a kidney transplant should be MOST alert for:
questions.rationale: Immunosuppression increases the risk of infection, so the client reports signs of infection. Other effects include hypertension, hirsutism, tremors, and gingival hyperplasia.
explanations: Correct: immunosuppression raises the infection risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1484 (PDF p. 1793)

questions.stem: Which common side effect should the nurse watch for after giving preoperative scopolamine?
questions.rationale: Scopolamine is anticholinergic: dry mouth, urinary retention, decreased sweating, and dilated pupils. The distractors are the opposites of these effects.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1495 (PDF p. 1804)

questions.stem: A postoperative client complains of gas pains. Which prescribed drug should the nurse look for?
questions.rationale: Simethicone is an antiflatulent that relieves pain from excess GI gas. Droperidol treats nausea, and magnesium hydroxide is an antacid and laxative.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1508 (PDF p. 1817)

questions.stem: A man is prescribed metoprolol for hypertension. Which common side effect may affect his adherence?
questions.rationale: Impotence is a common side effect of beta blockers and may lead clients to stop the drug. Fatigue and weakness are also common.
explanations: Correct: a common reason for nonadherence.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1541 (PDF p. 1852)

questions.stem: Thirty minutes into a packed RBC transfusion, the client reports itching and chest tightness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are signs of a transfusion reaction. The nurse stops the transfusion first, then runs normal saline through new tubing, notifies the provider, and checks vital signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q314 (PDF p. 478)

questions.stem: A client with a new implanted chemotherapy port says, 'I can't handle a tube coming out of me.' What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Explain the port sits under the skin
questions.rationale: An implanted port is under the skin, not visible, and has no external tubing except when accessed. Correcting this misunderstanding comes first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q992 (PDF p. 1242)

questions.stem: IV 5% albumin is ordered for a burn client. Which history item should make the nurse call the prescriber first?
questions.rationale: Albumin, a blood derivative, is contraindicated in severe anemia, heart failure, renal insufficiency, allergic reaction, and when there is no albumin deficiency.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1295 (PDF p. 1596)

questions.stem: A client recovering from anesthesia has a single, isolated PVC on the monitor. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: An isolated PVC is not life-threatening, so the nurse keeps monitoring. Frequent PVCs may precede VT or VF and are reported.
explanations: Correct: an isolated PVC is benign.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q13 (PDF p. 151)

questions.stem: A client develops atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 150. Which effect should the nurse assess for?
questions.rationale: Rapid AF loses the atrial kick and lowers cardiac output, causing hypotension, dizziness, chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, and a pulse deficit.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q43 (PDF p. 182)

questions.stem: A client in acute heart failure (BP 85/50, pulse 96) starts digoxin. Which change shows a therapeutic response?
questions.rationale: Digoxin is positively inotropic (raises cardiac output and BP) and negatively chronotropic (slows the heart rate).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q54 (PDF p. 194)

questions.stem: How does the balloon-tipped catheter work in PTCA?
questions.rationale: In PTCA, the balloon compresses plaque against the vessel wall. A mesh device is a stent, shaving is atherectomy, and dye injection is catheterization.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q150 (PDF p. 300)

questions.stem: Sixteen hours after leg arterial bypass, pain is increasing, worse with movement, with paresthesias. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: These are classic signs of compartment syndrome (pain that intensifies with movement, paresthesias), which can compromise the vessels. The provider is notified.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q326 (PDF p. 491)

questions.situation: Aling Linda, 45, is diagnosed with Raynaud's disease. Her fingers turn pale and numb during episodes.
questions.stem: Which assessment checks for Raynaud's symptoms?
options: Look for a rash on the fingers
Feel for weak or absent pulses
questions.rationale: Raynaud's is vasospasm of small distal arteries. Diminished or absent peripheral pulses show interrupted circulation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q373 (PDF p. 541)

questions.situation: Aling Linda, 45, is diagnosed with Raynaud's disease. Her fingers turn pale and numb during episodes.
questions.stem: Which question BEST identifies what triggers her episodes?
options: 'Does cold or vibration bring them on?'
questions.rationale: Small distal arteries close in response to cold, vibration, or other external stimuli, causing pallor, coldness, numbness, and cyanosis of the fingers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q380 (PDF p. 549)

questions.situation: Aling Linda, 45, is diagnosed with Raynaud's disease. Her fingers turn pale and numb during episodes.
questions.stem: Which instruction belongs in Aling Linda's teaching plan?
questions.rationale: Preventing vasoconstriction helps. Hands and feet are kept warm and dry, and gloves and warm fabrics are worn in cold weather.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q729 (PDF p. 953)

questions.stem: Which finding does the nurse expect in pulmonary edema from left-sided heart failure?
questions.rationale: Left-sided failure backs blood into the lungs, causing respiratory signs such as crackles. Neck vein distention and peripheral edema are right-sided signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q390 (PDF p. 560)

questions.stem: Which home-safety instruction is MOST important for a client with cardiomyopathy?
questions.rationale: Orthostatic changes can occur from obstructed venous return, and sudden BP drops can cause falls.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q472 (PDF p. 656)

questions.stem: After femoral-approach cardiac catheterization, which action is a PRIORITY?
options: Flex the leg to prevent stiffness
questions.rationale: The groin is checked for bleeding, and pressure is applied if it occurs. The leg is kept straight (not flexed or hyperextended) to prevent occlusion or hemorrhage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q474 (PDF p. 658)

questions.stem: A client with left-leg DVT has severe edema and pain. Which intervention is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Care includes limb elevation, warm moist heat, analgesics, anticoagulants, and watching for pulmonary embolism. Massage can dislodge the clot.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q585 (PDF p. 790)

questions.stem: Why should a client with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) keep a diary of shocks?
options: To help the provider adjust therapy
questions.rationale: The client records the date and time of each shock, prior activity, symptoms, number of shocks, and how he felt. The provider uses this to adjust medication and therapy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q668 (PDF p. 887)

questions.stem: A client's spouse fears being shocked if the ICD fires during contact. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Families are reassured that if the device fires while they are touching the client, they may feel a slight tingle but will not be harmed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q806 (PDF p. 1040)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with an arterial ischemic leg ulcer needs correction?
options: 'I'll keep my feet clean and dry.'
'I'll raise my legs above my heart.'
questions.rationale: Foot care is the same as in diabetes, but clients with arterial disease avoid raising the legs above heart level, which reduces arterial flow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q671 (PDF p. 891)

questions.stem: After abdominal aortic aneurysm resection, which activity is appropriate at home?
questions.rationale: Walking as tolerated, including outdoors, is allowed. Pushing, pulling, straining, and lifting over 15 to 20 pounds are avoided for 6 to 12 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q678 (PDF p. 898)

questions.stem: Which risk factor should a client with Buerger's disease (thromboangiitis obliterans) modify FIRST?
questions.rationale: Buerger's disease occurs mainly in men over 40 who smoke. Smoking is consistently a risk factor, and symptoms improve with cessation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q718 (PDF p. 940)

questions.stem: Which support service BEST helps a client with Buerger's disease make needed lifestyle changes?
questions.rationale: Smoking is very harmful in Buerger's disease and must stop completely. Because it is a chemical dependency, a cessation program helps.
explanations: Correct: addresses the key risk factor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q836 (PDF p. 1072)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with peripheral arterial disease needs correction?
options: 'A heating pad will soothe my leg.'
questions.rationale: Direct heat is contraindicated. The limb may have decreased sensation and burn easily, and heat raises tissue oxygen needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q730 (PDF p. 954)

questions.stem: Which item is LOWEST in sodium for a client with hypertension?
questions.rationale: Bottled, distilled, deionized, or demineralized water can be used. Toothpaste, mouthwash, and OTC drugs such as antacids and laxatives can add sodium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q731 (PDF p. 956)

questions.stem: A client starting spironolactone may need dose adjustments if also taking which drug?
questions.rationale: Spironolactone retains potassium. Adding potassium supplements risks hyperkalemia, so potassium doses are adjusted.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q755 (PDF p. 984)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands care of the femoral site after angioplasty?
options: 'Mild soreness may be eased with paracetamol.'
questions.rationale: Mild discomfort is usually relieved by acetaminophen. Neurovascular changes, bleeding, or bruising at the site are reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q787 (PDF p. 1017)

questions.stem: A client with hypertension lists symptoms he gets. Which one is MORE likely from a sinus problem than from high blood pressure?
questions.rationale: Cerebrovascular symptoms of hypertension include early-morning occipital headaches, epistaxis, dizziness, blurred vision, and vertigo. Fullness in the head suggests sinus disease.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q789 (PDF p. 1019)

questions.stem: A client is apprehensive before a pericardiocentesis. What is the BEST plan?
options: Talk from the foot of the bed
Stay with him and explain each step
questions.rationale: A client facing a sudden complication is in situational crisis. Staying with him and giving information and encouragement builds trust.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q825 (PDF p. 1060)

questions.stem: A client with arterial leg ulcers says, 'I've had this pain for over a year. It never goes away.' What is the PRIORITY concern?
questions.rationale: The main complaint is pain lasting more than 3 months, which is defined as chronic pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q839 (PDF p. 1075)

questions.stem: Before a mechanical heart valve replacement, what is ESSENTIAL to assess?
questions.rationale: Mechanical valves carry a risk of thromboemboli, so lifelong anticoagulation with warfarin is required.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q840 (PDF p. 1076)

questions.stem: A hospitalized client with angina is very anxious. Which action BEST reduces anxiety?
options: Give him choices about his care
Keep the hallway lights on at night
questions.rationale: Providing information, social support, and control over care choices, and acknowledging feelings, reduce anxiety.
explanations: Correct: gives a sense of control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q864 (PDF p. 1101)

questions.stem: An anxious adult's ECG shows a heart rate of 90. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: The normal adult resting rate is 60 to 100, so the rate is normal. 'Don't worry' is false reassurance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q868 (PDF p. 1105)

questions.stem: Which behavior suggests depression in a client recovering from MI?
questions.rationale: Depression shows as withdrawal, lack of interest, crying, anorexia, and apathy. Insomnia suggests anxiety, ignoring limits suggests denial, and apprehension suggests anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q869 (PDF p. 1106)

questions.stem: A tense client staring at the cardiac monitor says, 'So many wires. I hope lightning doesn't hit us.' What is the BEST response?
questions.rationale: The nurse first validates the concern, then assesses the client's knowledge of the monitor so teaching can follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q887 (PDF p. 1129)

questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: Mang Pedro is very anxious. Which intervention is the PRIORITY?
options: Have family present for all care
questions.rationale: Accurate information reduces fear and builds trust. Detailed explanations can raise anxiety, so information is given simply and clearly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q911 (PDF p. 1154)

questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: On day 4, Mang Pedro refuses to dangle his legs: 'Only if my doctor says so.' What behavior is this?
questions.rationale: Dependency shows as refusing any activity unless the provider specifically approves it.
explanations: Correct: relies on the provider's approval.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q934 (PDF p. 1178)

questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: The evening before discharge, which action by Mang Pedro suggests DENIAL?
options: He asks for a sleeping pill
He eats only a quarter of supper
He walks up three flights of stairs alone
questions.rationale: Ignoring activity limits and avoiding lifestyle changes are signs of denial. Stair climbing should be supervised at this stage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q912 (PDF p. 1155)

questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: The nurse finds Mang Pedro quietly crying, with no physical cause. What is the BEST response?
options: 'Can you tell me what's upsetting you?'
questions.rationale: Clients after MI often feel anxious or afraid. An open question showing genuine interest lets him express his concerns.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q977 (PDF p. 1226)

questions.stem: A client in acute pulmonary edema is severely anxious. Which action meets his needs holistically?
options: Stay with him as much as possible
questions.rationale: Pulmonary edema brings extreme fear and a sense of impending doom. The nurse stays with the client as much as possible. Family can support him but cannot meet his physiological needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q980 (PDF p. 1229)

questions.stem: Why is reducing anxiety a key strategy in acute pulmonary edema?
questions.rationale: Falling cardiac output triggers the sympathetic fight-or-flight response, which adds to the heart's workload. Reducing anxiety helps raise cardiac output and lower fluid volume.
explanations: Correct: less sympathetic load on the heart.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1000 (PDF p. 1251)

questions.stem: A client with PVCs says, 'I'm afraid something bad will happen.' Which action gives the MOST immediate help?
options: Have staff stay with the client
questions.rationale: A calm, safe environment, appropriate reassurance, touch, and someone staying with the client ease fear.
explanations: Does not address the fear now.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q982 (PDF p. 1231)

questions.stem: A client with Raynaud's disease has a stressful job and copes poorly. Which change should the nurse suggest?
questions.rationale: Stress triggers Raynaud's vasospasm, so a stress-management program or biofeedback training can help. Quitting the job is unrealistic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q983 (PDF p. 1232)

questions.stem: During discharge teaching, a client with heart failure says, 'What's the use? I'll die anyway.' What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Anxiety and fear often develop after heart failure and can further strain the failing heart.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q990 (PDF p. 1240)

questions.stem: Which statement about thrombophlebitis care shows effective learning?
questions.rationale: Elevation uses gravity to improve venous return, lower venous pressure, and relieve edema and pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1045 (PDF p. 1319)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with a new ICD shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll avoid rough contact over the site.'
'Tight belts over the site are fine.'
'I'll show my ID card at metal detectors.'
questions.rationale: Clients avoid tight clothing or belts over the ICD, rough contact, strong electromagnetic fields, and metal detectors.
explanations: Correct answer: tight belts are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1248 (PDF p. 1544)

questions.stem: A client's ECG shows a PR interval of 0.16 seconds. How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: The normal PR interval is 0.12 to 0.20 seconds, so 0.16 is normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1263 (PDF p. 1564)

questions.stem: Which finding is an UNRELIABLE sign of antibiotic response in infective endocarditis?
questions.rationale: Once a murmur develops it does not resolve on its own, so it is the least reliable sign. Negative cultures and a normal temperature show the infection is clearing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1297 (PDF p. 1599)

questions.stem: Which assessment BEST detects the onset of heart failure in a client with valvular disease?
questions.rationale: New or increased crackles indicate fluid in the lungs from heart failure. The other findings are less reliable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1310 (PDF p. 1612)

questions.stem: After fem-pop bypass, which question BEST detects graft occlusion?
options: 'Is it like the pain before surgery?'
questions.rationale: The most frequent sign of graft occlusion is the return of pain like the preoperative pain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1312 (PDF p. 1614)

questions.stem: After lifestyle changes for hypertension, which BP reading shows the MOST success?
questions.rationale: Normal BP is below 120/80. Of the options, 128/84 is closest to normal and shows the most success.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1313 (PDF p. 1615)

questions.stem: A client has a history of intermittent claudication. Which symptom should the nurse ask about?
options: Leg pain with exercise, relieved by rest
questions.rationale: Intermittent claudication is leg pain that comes on with exercise and is relieved by rest. It is the classic sign of peripheral arterial insufficiency.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1315 (PDF p. 1617)

questions.stem: Which item should a client with a new permanent pacemaker avoid?
questions.rationale: Pacemakers are shielded from most electrical devices. Clients are warned about strong currents or magnetic fields such as store antitheft devices and airport metal detectors.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1336 (PDF p. 1639)

questions.stem: A client with frequent PVCs feels lightheaded after sitting up. What will the nurse likely hear on apical auscultation?
questions.rationale: PVCs make the rhythm irregular. The apical pulse is the most accurate way to assess rhythm; a radial pulse may miss beats.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1405 (PDF p. 1711)

questions.stem: Which intervention reduces the risk of DVT after a vaginal hysterectomy?
questions.rationale: Ambulation, pneumatic compression boots, range-of-motion exercises, and antiembolism stockings prevent DVT after major surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1421 (PDF p. 1727)

questions.stem: Which finding does the nurse expect in a client with polycythemia vera?
questions.rationale: Polycythemia vera raises blood viscosity and volume, causing a ruddy complexion, dusky red mucosa, hypertension, dizziness, headache, and fullness in the head.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1442 (PDF p. 1751)

questions.stem: Which complication should the nurse monitor for in toxic shock syndrome?
questions.rationale: TSS, often linked to tampon use, can cause DIC. Signs are reported promptly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1444 (PDF p. 1753)

questions.stem: A client has pernicious anemia. Disease of which organ affects vitamin B12 absorption?
questions.rationale: Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the ileum, so small bowel disease is a risk factor for pernicious anemia.
explanations: Correct: the site of B12 absorption.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1454 (PDF p. 1763)

questions.stem: Which finding is typical of pernicious anemia?
questions.rationale: Classic signs include weakness, mild diarrhea, and a smooth, sore, red tongue, plus neurologic signs such as paresthesias and balance problems.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1522 (PDF p. 1832)

questions.stem: Which laboratory value is elevated in sickle cell anemia?
questions.rationale: Sickle cell anemia is characterized by sickled hemoglobin (Hgb S). Two abnormal genes are needed for the disease; one gives sickle cell trait.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1458 (PDF p. 1767)

questions.stem: Which sign should the nurse monitor MOST in a client in sickle cell crisis?
questions.rationale: Sickle cell crisis causes severe bone and joint pain from microvascular occlusion. Treatment includes opioids, oxygen, and IV fluids.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1461 (PDF p. 1770)

questions.stem: Which findings are typical of a pleural effusion?
questions.rationale: A pleural effusion (fluid in the pleural space) usually causes dyspnea on exertion and a dry, nonproductive cough from bronchial irritation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q227 (PDF p. 382)

questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: When is the SAFEST time to take Mang Lando for a short walk?
questions.rationale: Activities are scheduled after respiratory treatments. After a bronchodilator he has his best oxygen exchange and tolerates activity better. After meals he tires easily.
explanations: Breathing is not improved by a nap.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q231 (PDF p. 386)

questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Mang Lando says food has lost its taste. What BEST improves his appetite?
questions.rationale: Expectorating sputum dulls taste, so oral hygiene before meals helps. Small, frequent meals are better because of dyspnea.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q385 (PDF p. 554)

questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Mang Lando gets short of breath during activity. Which action promotes his safety?
questions.rationale: Monitoring vital signs and oxygen saturation before, during, and after activity shows how he tolerates it. Pursed-lip breathing helps.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1330 (PDF p. 1632)

questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Which discharge statement by Mang Lando shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry and deep breathing continue for 6 to 8 weeks after discharge to keep the alveoli open and clear secretions.
explanations: Correct answer: keep using it for 6 to 8 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q761 (PDF p. 990)

questions.stem: After a sclerosing agent is injected through the chest tube for pleurodesis, what should the nurse do?
options: Have him cough and deep breathe
questions.rationale: The tube is clamped so the agent does not drain back out, and a repositioning schedule spreads it within the pleural space.
explanations: Correct: keeps the agent in place.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q234 (PDF p. 389)

questions.stem: Which intervention BEST promotes comfort for a client with AIDS and Pneumocystis pneumonia?
options: Raise the head of the bed
questions.rationale: Clients with breathing difficulty are usually more comfortable with the head of the bed raised. The other options monitor function rather than provide comfort.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q237 (PDF p. 392)

questions.stem: A client with empyema will have a bedside thoracentesis. What should be ready in case it is not effective?
questions.rationale: Empyema is pus in the pleural cavity. If the exudate is too thick for thoracentesis, a chest tube may be needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q239 (PDF p. 394)

questions.stem: A client with empyema is scheduled for decortication. Which fact should guide the nurse's emotional support?
options: He will be in severe pain for weeks
He'll be discharged the next day
Chest tubes may stay in a long time
questions.rationale: Chest tubes remain until the former pus-filled space is obliterated, which may take time and be discouraging.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1005 (PDF p. 1256)

questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Which action shows Mang Romy is doing pursed-lip breathing correctly?
questions.rationale: Prolonging exhalation through pursed lips reduces air trapping from narrowed airways.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q302 (PDF p. 465)

questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Mang Romy is at risk for carbon dioxide narcosis. Which oxygen flow rate should the nurse confirm?
questions.rationale: In CO2 narcosis, the drive to breathe comes from low oxygen. A low flow (2 to 3 L/min) avoids removing that stimulus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q531 (PDF p. 729)

questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Mang Romy is admitted with an exacerbation. Which factor MOST likely contributed?
questions.rationale: Dehydration thickens secretions and makes coughing ineffective. Correcting dehydration and teaching coughing technique help limit exacerbations.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q749 (PDF p. 978)

questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Romy about nutrition needs correction?
questions.rationale: Large meals distend the abdomen and push up the diaphragm, hindering breathing. Resting before meals reduces fatigue, and gas-forming foods are limited.
explanations: Correct answer: large meals impair breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q760 (PDF p. 989)

questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: What should home teaching for Mang Romy MOST importantly aim to do?
questions.rationale: COPD is airflow obstruction. Improving oxygenation and minimizing carbon dioxide retention are the primary goals; the other options support them.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q798 (PDF p. 1028)

questions.stem: The home nurse finds a client with emphysema smoking. Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'I see you never went to the clinic.'
'Have you looked at ways to quit?'
questions.rationale: The nurse avoids judgment and explores adaptive strategies without being controlling, leaving the decision with the client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q818 (PDF p. 1052)

questions.stem: A client with COPD has a respiratory rate of 35 and extreme dyspnea. Which concern is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Speaking clearly requires an intact respiratory system. Extreme dyspnea is a physical alteration that impairs speech.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q964 (PDF p. 1211)

questions.stem: A client is anxious about her first home chest physiotherapy. Which fact should reassure her?
questions.rationale: CPT mobilizes and clears secretions so breathing is more effective. It does carry some risks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q907 (PDF p. 1150)

questions.stem: A client has had hoarseness for 8 weeks. Which disorder is he at risk for?
questions.rationale: Persistent hoarseness is a common early sign of laryngeal cancer. Eight weeks is too long for acute laryngitis. Risk factors include smoking and heavy alcohol use.
explanations: Too long for an acute problem.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q395 (PDF p. 565)

questions.stem: Forty-eight hours after admission for pleurisy, the pleural friction rub is gone. What does this indicate?
questions.rationale: A friction rub is heard early, before fluid builds up. Once fluid accumulates, there is less friction and the rub disappears.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q397 (PDF p. 567)

questions.stem: Which instruction promotes comfort for a client recovering from pleurisy?
options: Take as much pain medicine as possible
questions.rationale: Splinting the chest wall during coughing and deep breathing eases pain. Shallow breaths promote atelectasis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q709 (PDF p. 931)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands how to prevent another pulmonary embolism?
options: 'I'll cross my legs to rest them.'
questions.rationale: Elastic stockings improve venous return. Adequate fluids prevent hypercoagulability, and periods of walking are mixed with sitting.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q645 (PDF p. 863)

questions.stem: A client suddenly shows signs of pulmonary embolism. Which order should the nurse carry out FIRST?
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia is the immediate threat, so oxygen comes first. An IV line for emergency drugs and an ECG follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1323 (PDF p. 1625)

questions.stem: Which findings are typical of rib fractures?
questions.rationale: Fractured ribs hurt on inspiration and palpation. Respirations are shallow, with guarding of the area.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1328 (PDF p. 1630)

questions.stem: Which breathing findings does the nurse expect with flail chest?
questions.rationale: Flail chest causes obvious respiratory distress: severe dyspnea, cyanosis, and paradoxical chest movement, with shallow, rapid, grunting respirations.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1329 (PDF p. 1631)

questions.stem: A client with a sucking chest wound has an occlusive dressing and is anxious. What BEST relieves his anxiety?
questions.rationale: Staying eases his anxiety and lets the nurse watch for a tension pneumothorax, which the dressing could cause.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q987 (PDF p. 1236)

questions.stem: After chest tube removal, which statement shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The site dressing stays in place until the provider says it may be removed. Heavy lifting is avoided for 4 to 6 weeks.
explanations: Correct answer: keep the dressing on.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1383 (PDF p. 1686)

questions.stem: Which statement before percutaneous IVC filter insertion shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The percutaneous approach uses local anesthesia. Complications are rare.
explanations: Correct answer: local anesthesia is used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1283 (PDF p. 1583)

questions.stem: Which emotional reaction in a client with silicosis needs IMMEDIATE intervention?
questions.rationale: Suicidal ideation is not a normal reaction and warrants immediate intervention. Anxiety, depression, and ineffective coping are common reactions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1373 (PDF p. 1676)

questions.stem: Which finding relates to chronic sinusitis?
questions.rationale: Chronic sinusitis causes anosmia (loss of smell), chronic cough, nasal stuffiness, purulent discharge, and headache worse on waking.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q382 (PDF p. 551)

questions.stem: Which pair of findings does the nurse expect in a client with end-stage renal disease?
questions.rationale: The kidneys maintain water balance and secrete erythropoietin, which stimulates red cell production. When they fail, edema and anemia result.
explanations: Oliguria and tachycardia are more likely.
Correct: lost water balance and erythropoietin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q175 (PDF p. 328)

questions.stem: A client is admitted with acute glomerulonephritis. Which recent history should the nurse ask about?
questions.rationale: The main cause of acute glomerulonephritis is a beta-hemolytic streptococcal infection about 3 weeks before symptoms begin, such as strep throat or impetigo.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q177 (PDF p. 330)

questions.stem: Which parameter should the nurse check DAILY in a client with nephrotic syndrome?
questions.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome causes edema, hypoalbuminemia, and proteinuria. Fluid balance is tracked daily by weight, intake and output, edema, and girth. Albumin is checked as prescribed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q183 (PDF p. 336)

questions.stem: Which item should be kept in the room of a client being evaluated for the type of kidney stone?
questions.rationale: Urine is strained until the stone passes. The stone is sent to the laboratory, and once its type is known, a prevention plan is made.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q271 (PDF p. 428)

questions.stem: What is the MOST serious complication of polycystic kidney disease?
questions.rationale: Cysts form and the kidneys enlarge. The most serious complication is ESRD, managed by dialysis or transplant. Chronic UTI is the most common complication.
explanations: The most common, not the most serious.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q363 (PDF p. 531)

questions.stem: A client newly diagnosed with polycystic kidney disease is adjusting to the illness. What should the nurse include in the discussions?
questions.rationale: Adult polycystic kidney disease is autosomal dominant, so the client and extended family should have genetic counseling. Fluid restriction is unnecessary, and hypertension is more likely.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q814 (PDF p. 1048)

questions.stem: A client returns from a left nephrectomy. Which assessment is MOST important to do hourly?
questions.rationale: Hourly urine output shows how well the remaining kidney is working and detects renal failure early. Pain, vital signs, and coughing and deep breathing are also monitored. The client is NPO at first.
explanations: The client is NPO at first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q364 (PDF p. 532)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which action protects Aling Nena's AV fistula?
options: Take BP on the right arm
Draw blood from the right arm
Check for a thrill and bruit
questions.rationale: The nurse palpates for a thrill and auscultates for a bruit every 4 hours. No BP readings, venipunctures, or IV lines go on the fistula arm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q375 (PDF p. 543)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which statement by Aling Nena about her fistula shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I won't carry heavy bags on that arm.'
questions.rationale: Clients avoid sleeping on the access arm, carrying heavy objects with it, or compressing it, and do routine range-of-motion exercises.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1082 (PDF p. 1364)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena asks how often hemodialysis is done. What is the typical schedule?
questions.rationale: Typical hemodialysis is 3 to 4 hours, 3 days a week, adjusted for body size, dialyzer type, blood flow, and client preference.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q672 (PDF p. 892)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: What should Aling Nena record daily to monitor her fluid status between treatments?
questions.rationale: Fluid status between treatments is tracked by daily intake and output and weight. Ideally she gains no more than 0.5 kg a day.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q676 (PDF p. 896)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which weight gain between dialysis sessions shows Aling Nena is following her diet and fluid limits?
questions.rationale: A limit of about 1 to 1.5 kg between treatments helps prevent the hypotension that occurs when large fluid volumes are removed during dialysis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1381 (PDF p. 1684)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena is on a fluid restriction. Which dessert choice shows she understands?
questions.rationale: Anything liquid at room temperature counts as fluid, such as gelatin, sherbet, and ice cream. Avoiding hidden fluids lets her drink more to ease thirst.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q665 (PDF p. 884)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena has itching from uremia. Which skin care item should she AVOID?
questions.rationale: Perfumes and alcohol dry the skin and worsen itching. Mild soap, bath oil, and lotion reduce dryness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q666 (PDF p. 885)

questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena is on a protein-restricted diet. Which foods are INCOMPLETE proteins?
questions.rationale: Nuts and grains are incomplete proteins. Meat, fish, milk, and eggs are complete proteins.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1353 (PDF p. 1656)

questions.stem: A client with CKD is told he needs hemodialysis and says angrily, 'I'll never be the same.' What is his PRIMARY concern?
questions.rationale: Clients may become angry over the permanence of CKD. Physical and lifestyle changes can cause an altered body image.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q809 (PDF p. 1043)

questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Which list of high-oxalate foods shows Mang Ben understood the teaching?
questions.rationale: High-oxalate foods include beets, spinach, rhubarb, black tea, cocoa, nuts, okra, and chocolate. He should also drink up to 3000 mL a day unless restricted.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q378 (PDF p. 547)

questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Mang Ben's passed stone is calcium oxalate. Which food is BEST to avoid?
questions.rationale: Foods that raise urinary oxalate include spinach, rhubarb, strawberries, chocolate, nuts, beets, tea, and okra.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q633 (PDF p. 851)

questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Two hours after morphine, Mang Ben says, 'I'm scared to death the pain will come back.' What is the PRIORITY concern?
questions.rationale: Anticipating recurring pain produces anxiety and threatens psychological integrity. No data suggest a lack of knowledge or poor coping.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q935 (PDF p. 1179)

questions.stem: A client has uric acid stones. Which food should the nurse teach him to avoid?
questions.rationale: Purines are broken down into uric acid. Organ meats such as liver are high in purines and are limited.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q642 (PDF p. 860)

questions.stem: How many glasses of water a day should a client with a nephrostomy tube drink at home?
questions.rationale: About 2000 mL a day (6 to 8 glasses) dilutes particles that could form stones and flushes the kidney and the tube.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q613 (PDF p. 826)

questions.stem: A client is admitted for ureterolithotomy. Which assessment shows readiness for surgery?
questions.rationale: As with any surgery, the client should know the procedure, the expected outcome, postoperative routines, and expected pain management.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q815 (PDF p. 1049)

questions.stem: A client with prostatitis asks why a stool softener is ordered. Which reply is BEST?
questions.rationale: Stool softeners prevent constipation, which is painful with an inflamed prostate. They do not reduce swelling directly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q652 (PDF p. 870)

questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: What should the nurse include in Mang Tonyo's discharge teaching?
options: Lift up to 20 kg after 2 weeks
questions.rationale: He reports infection, bleeding, more pain, or obstruction. Strenuous activity and lifting more than about 20 pounds (9 kg) are avoided for 4 to 6 weeks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q655 (PDF p. 873)

questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Tonyo shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Straining during defecation is avoided to prevent bleeding. Prune juice helps, and he drinks 6 to 8 glasses of fluid a day.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1066 (PDF p. 1348)

questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Mang Tonyo has continuous bladder irrigation. Which drainage color shows the flow rate is adequate?
questions.rationale: The irrigation is adjusted to keep drainage clear pale yellow or slightly pink. It is increased if drainage is cherry colored or has clots.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1238 (PDF p. 1531)

questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Which drainage color should the nurse report to the provider?
questions.rationale: Bright red drainage may mean active bleeding. Pale pink is expected. Dark pink means the irrigation rate should be increased.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1374 (PDF p. 1677)

questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: What urine color should Mang Tonyo expect for several days after going home?
questions.rationale: Urine is pink-tinged for several days. Dark red must be corrected, clear urine is not yet expected, and cloudy urine may mean infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1460 (PDF p. 1769)

questions.stem: A client asks how the prostate is removed in TURP. Through which route?
questions.rationale: TURP uses a resectoscope passed through the urethra. Suprapubic and retropubic approaches use a lower abdominal incision, and the perineal approach goes between scrotum and anus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1386 (PDF p. 1689)

questions.stem: At a prostate screening clinic, which sign of prostatism should the nurse ask about?
questions.rationale: Prostatism includes a weaker, intermittent stream, hesitancy, inability to stop quickly, a sense of incomplete emptying, and nocturia.
explanations: Inability to stop is a sign.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1377 (PDF p. 1680)

questions.stem: A client with renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney (right kidney normal) fears needing dialysis. What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: The client needs support and reassurance that a normally functioning remaining kidney can fully meet the body's metabolic needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q998 (PDF p. 1249)

questions.stem: A client with nephrotic syndrome says, 'Why bother with my diet? Nothing I do will fix my kidneys.' What is the MOST appropriate concern?
questions.rationale: Powerlessness is the belief that one's actions will not affect the outcome. Nephrotic syndrome is progressive, so the client may feel this way.
