questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q997 (PDF p. 1248)

questions.stem: After 2 days of care for nephrotic syndrome, which result shows the SMALLEST improvement?
questions.rationale: Therapy aims to heal the leaking glomerular membrane. The 0.1 g/dL rise in serum albumin is the smallest change.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1208 (PDF p. 1500)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with acute kidney injury shows a need for MORE teaching about high-quality protein?
questions.rationale: Complete proteins come from animal sources such as eggs, chicken, meat, and fish. Plant foods give incomplete proteins. With protein limited, the protein eaten should be high quality.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q656 (PDF p. 874)

questions.stem: A client recovering from acute kidney injury should limit which dietary factor?
questions.rationale: The kidneys excrete most potassium. In kidney failure, potassium is restricted (30 to 50 mEq/day), and dialysis is the main way to remove it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1210 (PDF p. 1503)

questions.stem: A client with glomerulonephritis is at risk for acute kidney injury. Which complication should the nurse monitor for?
questions.rationale: Intrarenal AKI from glomerulonephritis shows hypertension, tachycardia, oliguria, edema, and other signs of fluid overload. Prerenal AKI shows low output and low CVP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1540 (PDF p. 1851)

questions.stem: Which procedure requires surgical asepsis?
questions.rationale: Sterile technique is used for applying sterile dressings, inserting IV or urinary catheters, and tracheal suctioning. Clean technique is used for removing dressings and giving oral medicines.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q545 (PDF p. 746)

questions.stem: A chemotherapy dose seems too high, and the prescriber is away for days. What should the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: If an order seems wrong, the nurse clarifies it with the prescriber or a substitute before giving it. A pharmacist cannot change the dose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1401 (PDF p. 1705)

questions.stem: Where does the nurse palpate the apical pulse?
questions.rationale: The point of maximal impulse is normally at the fourth or fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q179 (PDF p. 332)

questions.stem: Which breath sounds does the nurse expect over the right lower lobe in a client with pneumonia there?
questions.rationale: Consolidated tissue carries bronchial sounds to the periphery, so bronchial sounds are heard over consolidation. Crackles may also be heard.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q225 (PDF p. 380)

questions.stem: A client has smoked three-fourths of a pack a day for 10 years. What is his smoking history?
questions.rationale: Pack-years equal packs per day times years smoked: 0.75 × 10 = 7.5.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q258 (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Which lab finding is MOST important to modify to lower the risk of coronary artery disease?
questions.rationale: LDL is more directly linked with CAD than other lipoproteins and predicts it better than triglycerides. Lipase is a digestive enzyme.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q689 (PDF p. 910)

questions.stem: A 39-year-old Filipino man has BP 152/92 at rest, cholesterol 180 mg/dL, and fasting glucose 90 mg/dL. Which CAD risk factor is the priority?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor. His cholesterol and glucose are normal, and age over 40 is nonmodifiable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1133 (PDF p. 1418)

questions.stem: Which assessment gives the BEST information about left-sided heart function?
questions.rationale: Left-sided failure backs fluid into the lungs, so breath sounds reflect it. Edema, hepatojugular reflux, and JVD are right-sided signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1098 (PDF p. 1382)

questions.stem: Which finding can percussion identify?
questions.rationale: Percussion assesses the size, borders, and consistency of organs and detects fluid in body cavities. Palpation assesses mobility, temperature, and resilience.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q797 (PDF p. 1027)

questions.stem: Which action by a new nurse auscultating breath sounds needs correction?
questions.rationale: Breath sounds are heard with the warmed diaphragm on bare skin while the client sits up and breathes slowly and deeply through the mouth.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1280 (PDF p. 1581)

questions.stem: After suctioning a tracheostomy, which finding BEST shows the procedure worked?
questions.rationale: Breath sounds show how well the airways were cleared of secretions. The other parameters are less precise for this purpose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1319 (PDF p. 1621)

questions.stem: Which finding is typical of herpes zoster (shingles)?
questions.rationale: Herpes zoster is reactivated varicella in the dorsal root ganglia. It causes unilateral, segmental, painful lesions, usually on the trunk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herpes Zoster (PDF p. 152)

questions.stem: A client with heart failure has magnesium 0.75 mEq/L. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Normal magnesium is 1.3–2.1 mEq/L. Hypomagnesemia affects myocardial function, so the client is monitored for dysrhythmias.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q5 (PDF p. 142)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do before starting continuous IV therapy?
options: Pad an arm board above the site
questions.rationale: IV solutions must be free of particles and within the expiration date to prevent vein trauma, thromboembolism, and infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q21 (PDF p. 160)

questions.stem: What must be written on an ABG requisition?
questions.rationale: An ABG requisition includes the time drawn, the client's temperature, whether on room air or oxygen, and ventilator settings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q31 (PDF p. 170)

questions.stem: Which ABG does the nurse expect in a client on continuous NG suction?
questions.rationale: NG suction removes acid, causing metabolic alkalosis: high pH and high bicarbonate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q40 (PDF p. 179)

questions.stem: A client on NG suction has HCO3 30. Which pH is MOST likely?
questions.rationale: Loss of gastric HCl causes metabolic alkalosis, with HCO3 above normal and an elevated pH.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q73 (PDF p. 218)

questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.43, PCO2 31, HCO3 21. Which imbalance is present?
questions.rationale: pH is normal (compensated) but on the alkaline side. Low PCO2 is the primary change, and low HCO3 is compensation.
explanations: pH is on the alkaline side.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q72 (PDF p. 217)

questions.stem: Which effect should a preoperative client expect from relaxation therapy?
questions.rationale: Relaxation decreases cognitive and physiological arousal, giving a sense of well-being and lowering heart rate, BP, and muscle tension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q42 (PDF p. 181)

questions.stem: During a first walk after abdominal surgery, which sign suggests orthostatic hypotension?
questions.rationale: Orthostatic hypotension on rising causes dizziness, nausea, tachycardia, and pallor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q83 (PDF p. 228)

questions.stem: How should the nurse prepare a client for electrophysiology studies (EPS)?
questions.rationale: EPS is invasive and induces dysrhythmias. The client is NPO 6 to 8 hours, and antidysrhythmics are usually withheld.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q127 (PDF p. 277)

questions.stem: Before a kidney CT with contrast, what is MOST important to assess?
questions.rationale: Any test with possible dye requires asking about allergies, especially to iodine or shellfish.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q137 (PDF p. 287)

questions.stem: How does the nurse check for IV infiltration?
questions.rationale: Infiltration causes edema and coolness from fluid leaking into tissue. Redness and warmth suggest phlebitis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q160 (PDF p. 311)

questions.stem: An IV dressing is damp and the tape is loose. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: The nurse checks all connections first to find the leak. If the leak is at the site, the infusion is stopped and the IV restarted.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q168 (PDF p. 321)

questions.stem: Which finding suggests a need for IV fluid and electrolyte therapy?
questions.rationale: Fluid and electrolyte imbalances such as hyponatremia, with a rapid, weak, thready pulse, signal the need for IV therapy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q172 (PDF p. 325)

questions.stem: A client with chest pain has elevated CK-MB and troponins. What do these indicate?
questions.rationale: CK-MB and troponins are sensitive markers of myocardial damage. CK-MB rises 3–6 hours after chest pain and peaks at about 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q178 (PDF p. 331)

questions.stem: A client needs three pillows to breathe while sleeping. How should this be documented?
questions.rationale: Orthopnea is difficulty breathing when lying flat and is documented by the number of pillows needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q185 (PDF p. 338)

questions.stem: Thoracentesis fluid has a high RBC count. What is the likely cause of the effusion?
questions.rationale: Pleural fluid with many RBCs may result from trauma and may need chest tube drainage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q228 (PDF p. 383)

questions.stem: Which tray should be at the bedside of a client admitted with a left pleural effusion?
questions.rationale: A significant pleural effusion is usually treated by thoracentesis, and the fluid is analyzed for the cause.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q269 (PDF p. 426)

questions.stem: How should the client breathe during indirect laryngoscopy?
questions.rationale: The vocal cords are observed during rest and phonation; the client sits upright and breathes normally.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q250 (PDF p. 407)

questions.stem: Before a renal biopsy, which result should be reported?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage is a main complication of renal biopsy. Normal PT is 11–12.5 seconds, so 15 seconds is prolonged.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q263 (PDF p. 420)

questions.stem: A client with pyelonephritis vomited all night and is due for an IV pyelogram. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: IV fluids replace losses, are needed for dye injection, and help eliminate the dye.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q266 (PDF p. 423)

questions.stem: What should the nurse tell a client about first cardiac catheterization?
questions.rationale: The client may feel sensations such as warmth or flushing with dye and palpitations. It is done in the cath lab under local anesthesia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q277 (PDF p. 434)

questions.stem: A client scheduled for pneumonectomy asks how long chest tubes will stay in. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: After pneumonectomy, chest tubes usually are not inserted; the empty cavity fills with serosanguineous fluid.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q322 (PDF p. 487)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do when moving a client from the OR table to a stretcher?
options: Check LOC and tell the client
questions.rationale: For safe transfer the nurse assesses LOC, tells the client about the transfer, and ensures enough help and locked wheels.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q416 (PDF p. 593)

questions.stem: After bronchoscopy with sedation and topical anesthetic, what is the PRIORITY?
options: Give water to soothe the throat
Keep NPO until gag reflex returns
questions.rationale: The client stays NPO until cough, gag, and swallow reflexes return (usually 1–2 hours), then starts with ice chips.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q433 (PDF p. 611)

questions.stem: Which is a MEDICAL asepsis (clean technique) action?
questions.rationale: Medical asepsis reduces and prevents the spread of microorganisms through hand hygiene, cleaning the environment, and clean gloves.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q439 (PDF p. 619)

questions.stem: After a radial ABG draw, how is bleeding prevented?
questions.rationale: Pressure over the site for 5 to 10 minutes prevents hematoma and arterial damage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q441 (PDF p. 621)

questions.stem: How is an AV fistula arm BEST protected on admission?
options: Put an allergy band on it
Place an alert band: no BP or IV
questions.rationale: No venipunctures or BP on the access arm; an alert bracelet communicates this to all caregivers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q442 (PDF p. 622)

questions.stem: A client gets dizzy sitting up for thoracentesis. Which alternate position is safest?
questions.rationale: If the client cannot sit, he lies on the unaffected side with the head elevated so fluid collects on the affected side.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q504 (PDF p. 699)

questions.stem: Which food is allowed on a low-bacteria (neutropenic) diet?
questions.rationale: Low-bacteria diets allow cooked foods such as bread, baked chicken, and well-done meat; raw produce and undercooked eggs are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q514 (PDF p. 709)

questions.stem: The nurse drops a used syringe on the floor. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Used syringes go into a sharps container immediately. Sweeping risks needlesticks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q518 (PDF p. 713)

questions.stem: What is the INITIAL action when a post-op client sits up to prepare for walking?
questions.rationale: Ambulation should not exceed tolerance, so the client is assessed for dizziness and hypotension first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q526 (PDF p. 723)

questions.stem: Which action prevents electrical shock with equipment?
questions.rationale: Use grounded three-prong plugs, check cords for fraying, and keep cords away from water.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q527 (PDF p. 725)

questions.stem: How should a home IV pump be used safely?
questions.rationale: Equipment needs grounding; extension cords are never recommended, so the client sits near a three-prong outlet.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q579 (PDF p. 784)

questions.stem: Which equipment should be at the bedside for a pleural biopsy?
questions.rationale: Complications include hemothorax and pneumothorax, so a chest tube and drainage system are kept ready.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q535 (PDF p. 733)

questions.stem: During hemodialysis, which action by a new nurse needs correction?
questions.rationale: The connection site should stay visible to check for bleeding, ischemia, and infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q536 (PDF p. 734)

questions.stem: The nurse and a dialysis client are drinking coffee during treatment. What should the manager do?
questions.rationale: Dialysis-associated hepatitis B is a risk, so no eating or drinking in the client area.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q560 (PDF p. 761)

questions.stem: What must be in place before a MUGA scan?
questions.rationale: A radioisotope is injected IV for the MUGA scan, so signed informed consent is needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q539 (PDF p. 737)

questions.stem: A nursing attendant asks how to protect herself caring for a client with chlamydial urethritis. What does the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Chlamydia is sexually transmitted; caregivers cannot catch it through care, so standard precautions suffice.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q544 (PDF p. 744)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before bronchoscopy?
questions.rationale: Bronchoscopy is invasive and requires informed consent. The client is NPO beforehand.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q554 (PDF p. 755)

questions.stem: What should the client know about shock wave lithotripsy?
options: The stone passes as fine sand in urine
questions.rationale: Lithotripsy is noninvasive; shock waves shatter the stone into fine sand passed in the urine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q565 (PDF p. 768)

questions.stem: Which home oxygen safety teaching is correct?
options: Hold the tank on your lap in the car
questions.rationale: Check the oxygen level often so it does not run out. Tanks are secured when traveling and kept away from heat and flames.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q578 (PDF p. 783)

questions.stem: Which handwashing action shows a nursing attendant needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Hands are kept lower than the forearms so water flows toward the fingertips.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q600 (PDF p. 809)

questions.stem: When is a post-op NG tube usually removed?
questions.rationale: NG tubes are removed when GI function returns, shown by passing flatus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q711 (PDF p. 933)

questions.stem: Which food should a client with uric acid stones eliminate?
questions.rationale: Organ meats, sardines, herring, and other high-purine foods are eliminated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q745 (PDF p. 973)

questions.stem: Which food choice shows a client with atherosclerosis understands the diet?
questions.rationale: The diet is low in saturated fat with less red meat and more fruits and vegetables.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q786 (PDF p. 1016)

questions.stem: Which snack is BEST for a client with hypertension?
questions.rationale: Fresh vegetables like carrots and celery are naturally low in sodium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q788 (PDF p. 1018)

questions.stem: After bronchoscopy, which statement shows the client needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Smoking is avoided. Bright red expectorated blood is reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q799 (PDF p. 1029)

questions.stem: Why does a shy client need extra support for a voiding cystourethrogram?
options: She must void in front of others
questions.rationale: Voiding in the presence of others is embarrassing and may interfere with voiding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q802 (PDF p. 1035)

questions.stem: Which explanation BEST eases anxiety about a 12-lead ECG?
questions.rationale: ECG electrodes are painless; the test takes under 5 minutes and requires lying still.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q805 (PDF p. 1039)

questions.stem: What should preoperative teaching for radical neck dissection focus on FIRST?
questions.rationale: Teaching starts by finding out what the client already knows, to correct misinformation and set a starting point.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q871 (PDF p. 1108)

questions.stem: Which statement shows POSITIVE coping with chemotherapy hair loss?
questions.rationale: Positive coping identifies feelings and plans interventions for side effects.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q913 (PDF p. 1156)

questions.stem: A client who works with the public worries about her new subclavian CVC. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: A visible CVC can create socially awkward situations and affect body image.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q961 (PDF p. 1208)

questions.stem: Why is a client told to fast and take an enema before peritoneoscopy?
options: To empty and protect the bowel
questions.rationale: A laparoscope is inserted after gas insufflation; an empty bowel reduces the risk of puncture and improves visualization.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q969 (PDF p. 1217)

questions.stem: Which plan addresses psychosocial needs before an above-knee amputation?
questions.rationale: Loss of a body part alters body image; interventions encourage expressing feelings about the change.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q979 (PDF p. 1228)

questions.stem: After consent for an IVC filter, a client says he is scared the procedure will fail. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: He names the procedure and outcome as the object, which is fear. Anxiety has no identifiable source.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q984 (PDF p. 1233)

questions.stem: A client asks if pulmonary angiography is painful and has much radiation. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary angiography involves minimal radiation and is painless except for discomfort at needle insertion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q986 (PDF p. 1235)

questions.stem: A client with AKI has trouble remembering instructions. How should the nurse communicate?
questions.rationale: Communication should be clear, simple, and understandable, repeated as needed, because of anxiety and altered lab values.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1001 (PDF p. 1252)

questions.stem: A first-time inpatient with a roommate cannot start urinating. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Lack of privacy inhibits voiding. Privacy, running water, and normal position help.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1006 (PDF p. 1257)

questions.stem: A client fears thoracentesis. Which honest information supports her?
questions.rationale: Needle insertion is painful; staying still prevents injury to the pleura and lung.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1012 (PDF p. 1263)

questions.stem: An anxious client with angina asks, 'So I had a heart attack?' What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: The nurse corrects the misconception: angina results from inadequate blood supply causing pain, without infarction.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1039 (PDF p. 1313)

questions.stem: A client on home IV antibiotics should report which finding early?
questions.rationale: Pain, drainage, and edema signal site infection; early detection prevents septicemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1064 (PDF p. 1346)

questions.stem: Which statement on a low-sodium diet needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Frozen and processed foods are often high in sodium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1070 (PDF p. 1352)

questions.stem: What is MOST important to determine before an arteriogram with contrast?
questions.rationale: Iodine or seafood allergy predicts dye reaction, and consent is needed for the invasive injection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1097 (PDF p. 1381)

questions.stem: Which sign fits dehydration from long-term diuretic use?
questions.rationale: Fluid deficit causes rapid pulse, weight loss, poor turgor, low output, and concentrated urine with high specific gravity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1107 (PDF p. 1391)

questions.stem: Allen's test checks collateral circulation of which artery?
questions.rationale: Before radial puncture, Allen's test confirms adequate ulnar circulation to prevent hand ischemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1114 (PDF p. 1398)

questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.34, PCO2 37, HCO3 19. Which imbalance is present?
questions.rationale: pH below 7.35 with HCO3 below 22 and normal PCO2 is metabolic acidosis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1116 (PDF p. 1400)

questions.stem: What is the priority after an intravenous pyelogram?
questions.rationale: Fluids help clear the dye. Activity is as tolerated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1134 (PDF p. 1419)

questions.stem: Which IV solution is isotonic?
questions.rationale: D5W is isotonic in the bag, as are 0.9% NaCl and lactated Ringer's.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1146 (PDF p. 1433)

questions.stem: What maintains the integrity of an ABG sample?
questions.rationale: ABGs use a heparinized syringe, placed on ice and sent immediately. No preservative.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1155 (PDF p. 1442)

questions.stem: After laryngectomy, oral intake starts with which food type?
questions.rationale: Oral intake begins with semisolids; liquids are added once semisolids are managed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1214 (PDF p. 1507)

questions.stem: Which ABG indicates respiratory acidosis?
questions.rationale: In respiratory acidosis, pH falls and PCO2 rises (opposite directions).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1300 (PDF p. 1601)

questions.stem: Which PaO2 shows a client's oxygen level is adequate?
questions.rationale: Normal PO2 is 80 to 100 mm Hg.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1304 (PDF p. 1606)

questions.stem: Before surgery, which medication should the nurse PRIORITIZE asking the surgeon about holding?
questions.rationale: Warfarin is often withheld before surgery to reduce bleeding risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1314 (PDF p. 1616)

questions.stem: Which observation of home oxygen use needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The concentrator needs clear space for air circulation; enclosed spaces can overheat and cause fire.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1318 (PDF p. 1620)

questions.stem: Which belongs in the plan for a client scheduled for bronchoscopy?
questions.rationale: Dentures, contact lenses, and prostheses are removed before sedation, and informed consent is signed. The client is NPO.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1324 (PDF p. 1626)

questions.stem: Which test must be positive before drawing radial ABGs?
questions.rationale: The Allen test confirms ulnar collateral flow before radial puncture.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1326 (PDF p. 1628)

questions.stem: Which finding in hypercalcemia needs follow-up?
questions.rationale: Hypercalcemia raises the risk of clots; poor capillary refill may signal impaired circulation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1350 (PDF p. 1653)

questions.stem: A client with 3 days of vomiting and diarrhea should be assessed for which sign?
questions.rationale: Dehydration causes weight loss, lethargy, sunken eyes, poor turgor, tachycardia, and hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1379 (PDF p. 1682)

questions.stem: A client is on 1200 mL/day fluid restriction. How much is usually allowed on the 7 am–3 pm shift?
questions.rationale: About half the allotment is given on the day shift when the client is most active and takes meals and medicines.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1380 (PDF p. 1683)

questions.stem: Which is a common adult bone marrow biopsy site?
questions.rationale: The iliac crest and sternum are rich in marrow and easily accessible.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1387 (PDF p. 1690)

questions.stem: A client with AKI has heavy proteinuria. Which type of kidney failure is likely?
questions.rationale: Intrinsic failure shows fixed specific gravity and proteinuria. Prerenal has high specific gravity and little protein.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1420 (PDF p. 1726)

questions.stem: Right after TURP, a client suddenly becomes confused. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Hypotonic flushing solution absorbed during TURP can cause hyponatremia, an early sign of which is confusion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1430 (PDF p. 1739)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with CKD understands potassium restriction?
questions.rationale: Boiling and discarding the water reduces potassium. Salt substitutes are high in potassium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1436 (PDF p. 1745)

questions.stem: A pale client reports fatigue and dizziness. Which lab result is the priority for planning care?
questions.rationale: Pallor, fatigue, and dizziness fit anemia, so the low hemoglobin guides care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1440 (PDF p. 1749)

questions.stem: Which sign suggests anemia after postoperative blood loss?
questions.rationale: Low hemoglobin reduces oxygen-carrying capacity, causing fatigue.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1448 (PDF p. 1757)

questions.stem: What is the most frequent cause of pain after TURP?
questions.rationale: Bladder spasms from distention or the catheter balloon are common; antispasmodics are given.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1456 (PDF p. 1765)

questions.stem: Which test detects circulating RBC antibodies when screening blood compatibility?
questions.rationale: The indirect Coombs test detects circulating RBC antibodies and is part of 'type and screen'.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1459 (PDF p. 1768)

questions.stem: A client with burns over 25% TBSA has early labs. Which value is expected?
questions.rationale: Fluid shifts out of vessels, causing hemoconcentration and a high hematocrit.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1475 (PDF p. 1784)

questions.stem: During a panic attack: pH 7.49, PCO2 31, HCO3 22. Which imbalance?
questions.rationale: pH above 7.45 with PCO2 below 35 and normal HCO3 is respiratory alkalosis from hyperventilation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1480 (PDF p. 1789)

questions.stem: Which anemia is diagnosed with a Schilling test?
questions.rationale: The Schilling test identifies the cause of vitamin B12 deficiency, which underlies pernicious anemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1500 (PDF p. 1809)

questions.stem: A client with new AKI has potassium 6.1 mEq/L. What should the nurse do IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia risks dysrhythmias and arrest; the provider is notified at once for treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1538 (PDF p. 1849)

questions.stem: What makes a burn client comfortable for hydrotherapy dressing change?
questions.rationale: Pain medication 30 to 60 minutes before the dressing change helps the client tolerate a painful procedure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q4 (PDF p. 141)

questions.stem: Paracetamol liquid 450 mg is ordered; the label reads 160 mg/5 mL. How many mL are given?
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q19 (PDF p. 157)

questions.stem: A client's BP is 146/72. What is the pulse pressure?
questions.rationale: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic: 146 − 72 = 74.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q48 (PDF p. 187)

questions.stem: Which factor helps decide if a client with respiratory disease can benefit from progressive relaxation?
questions.rationale: The choice of relaxation technique considers energy, ability to concentrate, and physical capacity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q76 (PDF p. 221)

questions.stem: Which intervention helps URGE urinary incontinence?
questions.rationale: Urge incontinence is managed with bladder retraining, scheduled toileting, and pelvic muscle exercises.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q79 (PDF p. 224)

questions.stem: What is done immediately before reinserting a cleaned nondisposable inner cannula?
questions.rationale: After washing and rinsing, the cannula is tapped dry and dried with tracheostomy pipe cleaners, then reinserted.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q131 (PDF p. 281)

questions.stem: How does the nurse start a 24-hour urine collection?
options: Have the client void and discard it
questions.rationale: The first voiding is discarded because it was stored for an unknown time; all later urine is saved.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q138 (PDF p. 288)

questions.stem: Which behavior suggests a post-op client is in pain?
questions.rationale: Behavioral pain indicators include gasping, lip biting, muscle tension, and pacing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q147 (PDF p. 297)

questions.stem: Which dressing is used on a burn fasciotomy site?
questions.rationale: The fasciotomy is left open to relieve pressure and covered with wet sterile saline dressings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q166 (PDF p. 318)

questions.stem: What does the client do as a chest tube is removed?
options: Take a deep breath and hold it
questions.rationale: A held deep breath raises intrathoracic pressure, lessening air entry into the pleural space.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q169 (PDF p. 322)

questions.stem: How is ureteral colic pain described?
questions.rationale: Stone movement through the ureter causes sharp, excruciating, wavelike pain radiating to the genitalia and thigh.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q184 (PDF p. 337)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a client uses the incentive spirometer effectively?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry reduces atelectasis, opens airways, stimulates coughing, and mobilizes secretions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q207 (PDF p. 362)

questions.stem: How should a dressing on an arterial leg ulcer be secured?
options: Kling roll taped only to itself
questions.rationale: Tape is never placed on fragile ischemic skin; a roll bandage is taped only to itself.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q209 (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: Which finding indicates a need to suction a ventilated client?
options: Mucus bubbling in the ET tube
questions.rationale: Indications include visible mucus bubbling, wet respirations, restlessness, crackles or rhonchi, and rising pulse and RR.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q219 (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: A Foley drains a very distended bladder rapidly. What may the nurse do per policy?
options: Let it all drain at once
Clamp the tubing for a short time
questions.rationale: Rapid emptying of a large volume can cause hypovolemia or bladder spasm; clamping briefly allows equilibration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q232 (PDF p. 387)

questions.stem: After bladder repair with a suprapubic catheter, how are complications prevented?
questions.rationale: Urine buildup strains sutures; the catheter must drain freely.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q235 (PDF p. 390)

questions.stem: Which belongs in care of a client with a Pleur-Evac?
options: Keep the unit above the chest
questions.rationale: Frequent position changes promote drainage; the system stays below waist level.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q241 (PDF p. 396)

questions.stem: A chest tube disconnects and the drainage unit tips and breaks. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: An underwater seal is restored first by submerging the tube end in sterile water to prevent tension pneumothorax.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q242 (PDF p. 397)

questions.stem: After ureterolithotomy with a ureteral catheter, what should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Drainage is checked on arrival and every 1–2 hours; the renal pelvis has a small capacity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q273 (PDF p. 430)

questions.stem: A 1000-mL D5W bag hung at 3 pm runs at 75 mL/hr. How much remains at 11 pm?
questions.rationale: 8 hours × 75 mL = 600 mL infused; 1000 − 600 = 400 mL remain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q278 (PDF p. 435)

questions.stem: 1000 mL NS at 100 mL/hr with a drop factor of 10 gtt/mL. What is the rate in gtt/min?
questions.rationale: 100 mL/hr × 10 gtt/mL ÷ 60 min = 16.7, rounded to 17 gtt/min.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q285 (PDF p. 443)

questions.stem: What is the first dressing layer at a chest tube insertion site?
questions.rationale: Petrolatum gauze forms an occlusive seal at the insertion site; gauze layers go on top.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q320 (PDF p. 484)

questions.stem: A clinic client's left-arm BP is 200/118. What should the nurse do NEXT?
options: Take BP in the right arm
questions.rationale: The nurse checks the opposite arm to see if the elevation is limited to one extremity, and rechecks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q327 (PDF p. 492)

questions.stem: A client due for furosemide and nifedipine requests an antacid. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Antacids interfere with absorption, so they are separated from other drugs by at least 1 hour.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q340 (PDF p. 508)

questions.stem: What is the safest way to ambulate a client with a nephrostomy tube?
options: Attach it to a leg bag
Carry the bag above the hip
questions.rationale: A leg bag allows movement while protecting tube integrity and drainage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q362 (PDF p. 530)

questions.stem: An IV drug is incompatible with the running solution. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The line is flushed with normal saline before and after the drug to prevent in-line precipitation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q393 (PDF p. 563)

questions.stem: When is a sputum culture best collected?
questions.rationale: Sputum collects in the airways during sleep, so early morning gives the best specimen, ideally before antibiotics.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q408 (PDF p. 582)

questions.stem: Where should the drainage bag be placed after inserting a Foley catheter?
questions.rationale: The bag below bladder level ensures drainage and prevents retrograde flow and infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q413 (PDF p. 590)

questions.stem: What is done before injecting heparin 5000 units subcutaneously?
questions.rationale: Changing the needle prevents leakage along the needle tract. SC heparin needs no infusion device and the site is not massaged.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q422 (PDF p. 599)

questions.stem: 1000 mL over 8 hours with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What is the rate?
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q477 (PDF p. 663)

questions.stem: Urine flows as the Foley enters the bladder. What does the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: The balloon is behind the tip, so the catheter is advanced 2.5 to 5 cm further before inflating.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q530 (PDF p. 728)

questions.stem: What is done before suctioning a tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: The client is hyperoxygenated with deep breaths, a bag, or the ventilator's sigh before suctioning, using sterile technique.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q537 (PDF p. 735)

questions.stem: How is a sputum specimen for culture collected?
questions.rationale: Culture and sensitivity specimens need sterile technique to identify organisms accurately.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q538 (PDF p. 736)

questions.stem: How is a urinalysis specimen obtained from an indwelling catheter?
questions.rationale: The closed system stays sterile; the specimen is aspirated from the port after cleansing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q551 (PDF p. 752)

questions.stem: A 1000-mL bag hung at 9 am runs at 100 gtt/min by microdrip. How much remains at 2 pm?
questions.rationale: With microdrip, gtt/min = mL/hr, so 100 mL/hr × 5 hr = 500 mL infused; 500 mL remain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q555 (PDF p. 756)

questions.stem: A peritoneal dialysis catheter dressing gets wet while bathing. What should be done?
questions.rationale: A wet dressing lets bacteria reach the site; it is changed immediately and kept dry.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q569 (PDF p. 774)

questions.stem: A client gets dizzy using the incentive spirometer. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Not breathing normally between spirometer breaths causes hyperventilation and respiratory alkalosis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q643 (PDF p. 861)

questions.stem: Which shows a client understands home Foley care?
questions.rationale: The bag stays below the bladder with tubing free of kinks; the perineum is cleaned twice daily.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q646 (PDF p. 864)

questions.stem: How should the nurse evaluate a client's learning of IV dressing care?
questions.rationale: Psychomotor skills are best evaluated by observing a return demonstration (teach-back).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q662 (PDF p. 881)

questions.stem: Which statement about an implanted port needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: An implanted port does not need pumping to stay patent.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q663 (PDF p. 882)

questions.stem: Which meat choice is BEST for a client with hypertension?
questions.rationale: Bacon, hot dogs, luncheon meats, and corned beef are high in sodium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q669 (PDF p. 888)

questions.stem: How can a home IV client prevent phlebitis and infiltration?
options: Keep the site secured and protected
questions.rationale: Protecting and securing the site keeps the catheter immobile.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q673 (PDF p. 893)

questions.stem: Which incentive spirometer action needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry is ineffective with nose breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q707 (PDF p. 929)

questions.stem: Which position helps a client with COPD breathe more easily?
questions.rationale: Sitting upright and leaning on an overbed table, or with arms on the chair arms, eases dyspnea.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q708 (PDF p. 930)

questions.stem: Give 7.5 mg IM; the label reads 10 mg/mL. How many mL?
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1184 (PDF p. 1475)

questions.stem: Which finding MOST reliably shows a post-op NG tube to suction is working?
questions.rationale: The tube decompresses the bowel; flowing drainage with no abdominal distention shows function.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1237 (PDF p. 1530)

questions.stem: An antibiotic vial makes 2 g in 5 mL after mixing. How many mL for 650 mg?
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1254 (PDF p. 1554)

questions.stem: Which finding shows the lung has fully re-expanded with a chest tube?
questions.rationale: With full expansion, no air remains to cause fluctuation (tidaling) in the water-seal chamber.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1301 (PDF p. 1602)

questions.stem: How does a woman prepare for a midstream urine culture?
questions.rationale: The perineum is cleansed front to back with antiseptic swabs; the midstream portion is collected in a sterile cup.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1397 (PDF p. 1701)

questions.stem: Which is routine chest tube care?
options: Keep the unit above the chest
questions.rationale: Coughing and deep breathing aid lung expansion; water is added to the suction chamber as needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1426 (PDF p. 1735)

questions.stem: Which items are gathered for tracheostomy care?
questions.rationale: Equipment includes a trach care kit, sterile water and saline, and a suction kit.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1434 (PDF p. 1743)

questions.stem: What is the safe wall suction range for an adult tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: The safe adult range is 80 to 120 mm Hg, with hyperoxygenation before and after.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1447 (PDF p. 1756)

questions.stem: How is an iron injection given?
questions.rationale: Parenteral iron is given deep in the gluteal muscle by Z-track to prevent staining and irritation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1453 (PDF p. 1762)

questions.stem: A client on inhaled albuterol cannot cough up secretions. What helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Increased fluids (2000–3000 mL/day unless contraindicated) thin secretions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1471 (PDF p. 1780)

questions.stem: How is a new trach tube holder checked for proper tightness?
questions.rationale: Two fingers should slide comfortably under the holder: secure but not too tight.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1506 (PDF p. 1815)

questions.stem: Which symptom does the nurse expect in newly diagnosed Hodgkin's disease?
questions.rationale: Hodgkin's typically presents with night sweats, painless enlarged nodes, fever, and malaise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q33 (PDF p. 172)

questions.stem: Which finding suggests acute rejection after a kidney transplant?
questions.rationale: Acute rejection, usually within 3 months, causes fever, hypertension, malaise, graft tenderness, and less urine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q49 (PDF p. 189)

questions.stem: Which home measure helps oral mucositis from head and neck radiation?
questions.rationale: Mucositis care includes gentle oral hygiene and frequent mild rinses such as saline; alcohol and irritants are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q53 (PDF p. 193)

questions.stem: By the rule of nines, burns to both entire legs and the perineum are about what percent?
questions.rationale: Each leg is 18% (36%) plus the perineum 1% = 37%.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q81 (PDF p. 226)

questions.stem: Which finding is MOST indicative of stage II Lyme disease?
questions.rationale: Stage II (1–3 months) includes dysrhythmias, dyspnea, dizziness, and neurologic problems. Arthritis marks stage III.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q104 (PDF p. 253)

questions.stem: Which finding is expected in stage III Lyme disease?
questions.rationale: Stage III features arthritic symptoms such as arthralgia and enlarged, inflamed joints.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1109 (PDF p. 1393)

questions.stem: Which sign is characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris?
questions.rationale: Nikolsky's sign, where the epidermis rubs off with slight friction, is a hallmark, with flaccid bullae.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q105 (PDF p. 254)

questions.stem: Which skin care shows understanding during radiation therapy?
options: Protect from heat, cold, and sun
questions.rationale: Treated skin is protected from temperature extremes, sun, and chlorinated water; markings are kept.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q189 (PDF p. 342)

questions.stem: After right radical mastectomy, which intervention is included?
options: Blood draws from the right arm
Check the back of the dressing
questions.rationale: Drainage seeps down by gravity to the posterior axillary dressing first, so it is checked. No BP or draws on the affected arm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q198 (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Where does a burn heterograft come from?
questions.rationale: Heterograft is skin from another species, most often pig. Homograft is human (cadaver); autograft is the client's own.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q216 (PDF p. 371)

questions.stem: Which describes early Kaposi's sarcoma lesions?
questions.rationale: Kaposi's sarcoma starts flat and pink and turns dark violet or black, usually bilaterally.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q226 (PDF p. 381)

questions.stem: Which discharge instruction fits a client after testicular cancer surgery?
questions.rationale: The client reports chills, fever, drainage, redness, or discharge to the provider.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q297 (PDF p. 460)

questions.stem: Which plan ensures safe cancer pain control?
questions.rationale: Safe pain control starts with low doses and titrates up to relief, alongside nondrug measures.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q468 (PDF p. 652)

questions.stem: A client with AIDS is losing weight. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: Nutrient-dense, high-calorie food in small, frequent meals supports weight gain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q617 (PDF p. 831)

questions.stem: Which statement about prostate cancer is correct?
questions.rationale: Smoking and a history of STIs raise risk; yearly digital rectal exams aid early detection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q627 (PDF p. 844)

questions.stem: After lung cancer surgery, which statement needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll handle more pain on my own.'
questions.rationale: Increasing pain should be reported; clients are not expected to manage it alone.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q658 (PDF p. 877)

questions.stem: How can a client with AIDS reduce recurrent thrush?
questions.rationale: Careful routine mouth care helps prevent overgrowth of Candida in immunosuppression.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q750 (PDF p. 979)

questions.stem: Which food should a client with AIDS avoid?
questions.rationale: Avoid raw or undercooked seafood, meat, poultry, eggs, and unpasteurized dairy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q751 (PDF p. 980)

questions.stem: Which sign suggests an opportunistic respiratory infection in AIDS?
questions.rationale: Fever and exertional dyspnea are signs of Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1094 (PDF p. 1377)

questions.stem: Which is an appropriate goal for a client with AIDS at risk for PCP?
questions.rationale: PCP causes fever, exertional dyspnea, and nonproductive cough; a goal is effective breathing without dyspnea.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1306 (PDF p. 1607)

questions.stem: A family wants hospice for a client with terminal throat cancer. What is a main goal of hospice?
questions.rationale: Hospice emphasizes caring rather than curing, with the client free of pain and distressing symptoms.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q842 (PDF p. 1079)

questions.stem: How is acute cancer pain BEST assessed?
questions.rationale: The client's perception, usually rated 0–10, is the hallmark of pain assessment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q843 (PDF p. 1080)

questions.stem: A client with AIDS feels socially isolated. What is MOST useful?
questions.rationale: The nurse encourages social contact and reduces barriers, including educating family about transmission.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q988 (PDF p. 1238)

questions.stem: A client's first HIV ELISA is positive and she cries. What should the nurse know?
options: The test is repeated and confirmed
questions.rationale: A positive ELISA is repeated because of possible false positives and confirmed with Western blot.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q994 (PDF p. 1244)

questions.stem: Before cystectomy, which statement shows FEAR?
questions.rationale: Fear has an identifiable object; here the uncertain outcome of surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q996 (PDF p. 1247)

questions.stem: Which statement during external radiation needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Lotions and powders are not applied without specific provider instructions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1077 (PDF p. 1359)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with AIDS learned energy conservation?
questions.rationale: Sitting for activities such as dressing, shaving, cooking, and bathing conserves energy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1079 (PDF p. 1361)

questions.stem: Which statement about thrush care needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Commercial mouthwashes with alcohol cause pain; warm water or saline rinses are used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1081 (PDF p. 1363)

questions.stem: Which finding fits moist desquamation from radiation?
questions.rationale: Moist desquamation destroys basal cells and exposes the dermis, which leaks serum.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1105 (PDF p. 1389)

questions.stem: How is a client positioned for intraperitoneal chemotherapy?
questions.rationale: IP chemotherapy is infused into the peritoneal cavity with the client in semi-Fowler's for comfort and breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1173 (PDF p. 1462)

questions.stem: Before bilateral orchiectomy, a 25-year-old needs priority exploration of which concern?
questions.rationale: Loss of reproductive ability is a major psychological concern and is a priority to address.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1376 (PDF p. 1679)

questions.stem: Which finding is expected in infiltrating ductal breast carcinoma?
questions.rationale: It usually presents as a single, unilateral, fixed, irregular, hard, painless mass.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1391 (PDF p. 1694)

questions.stem: After mastectomy with node dissection, which plan shows correct arm care?
options: Carry heavy bags on that arm
Have BP taken on that arm
questions.rationale: The client avoids trauma to the affected arm (gloves for gardening) to prevent edema and infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1394 (PDF p. 1698)

questions.stem: A COPD client on 2 L O2 has RR 22 and reports dyspnea. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Further assessment comes first; oxygen is not raised without validation because of CO2 retention risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1413 (PDF p. 1719)

questions.stem: Which finding is expected in systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.rationale: SLE may cause fever, aches, a butterfly facial rash, pleural effusion, lymphadenopathy, and pericarditis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1439 (PDF p. 1747)

questions.stem: A client on chemo has a falling WBC. Which precaution is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Low WBC means infection risk. Padding rails and removing sharps are bleeding precautions.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1443 (PDF p. 1752)

questions.stem: Which behavior shows the MOST difficulty adjusting after mastectomy?
options: Refuses to look at the dressing
questions.rationale: Refusing to look shows she is not ready to acknowledge the loss.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1492 (PDF p. 1801)

questions.stem: Which exercise is done in the first 24 hours after mastectomy?
questions.rationale: In the first 24 hours, the client moves fingers and hands and flexes and extends the elbow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1502 (PDF p. 1811)

questions.stem: A client on chemo has platelets of 15,000/mm³. Which precautions apply?
questions.rationale: Platelets below 20,000/mm³ place the client at risk for bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1542 (PDF p. 1854)

questions.stem: A client with a new irregular heart rate makes several comments. Which shows READINESS to learn?
questions.rationale: Readiness needs physical and emotional ability; directly asking about the disorder shows interest and motivation. Weakness shows physical inability to learn.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1308 (PDF p. 1610)

questions.stem: Which white cells arrive FIRST at a site of tissue injury?
questions.rationale: Neutrophils are first at the injury site; monocytes phagocytose in chronic injury; lymphocytes mediate immunity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Inflammation (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: Injured tissue releases substances that attract phagocytes. This process is:
questions.rationale: Chemotaxis is the magnet-like attraction of phagocytes to the injured area.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Inflammation (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: A clean surgical incision with approximated edges heals by:
questions.rationale: First intention occurs in clean-cut wounds with approximated edges and minimal scarring.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Healing Process (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: An infected wound is left open, then closed surgically days later. This is healing by:
questions.rationale: Third intention is delayed surgical closure of an infected wound.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Healing Process (PDF p. 16)

questions.stem: Which pulse site is used during cardiac arrest in an INFANT?
questions.rationale: The brachial pulse is used during infant cardiac arrest and for BP; carotid is used in adults.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Sites (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: The apical rate is 96 and the radial rate is 84 at the same time. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Pulse deficit is the difference between apical and radial rates (here 12).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Deficit (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: A pulse obliterated easily with light pressure is documented as:
questions.rationale: Scale: 0 absent, 1+ weak/thready, 2+ normal, 3+ bounding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pulse Scale (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: What is the primary chemical stimulus for breathing in healthy people?
questions.rationale: The medulla is the primary respiratory center, and CO2 is the main chemical stimulus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Center (PDF p. 19)

questions.stem: Breathing that waxes from very deep to very shallow, then stops briefly, is:
questions.rationale: Cheyne-Stokes goes from very deep to very shallow followed by temporary apnea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)

questions.stem: A shrill, harsh sound on INSPIRATION is:
questions.rationale: Stridor is a shrill, harsh inspiratory sound; wheeze is a high-pitched expiratory sound; stertor is snoring.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)

questions.stem: Which error gives a FALSELY HIGH blood pressure?
questions.rationale: A narrow or loose cuff, arm below heart level, unsupported arm, or insufficient rest give false highs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Errors in BP (PDF p. 21)

questions.stem: How fast should the BP cuff be deflated?
questions.rationale: Release the valve at 2–3 mm Hg per second to identify Korotkoff phases.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing BP (PDF p. 21)

questions.stem: Pain lasting 6 months or longer is classified as:
questions.rationale: Acute pain lasts seconds to 6 months; chronic pain lasts 6 months or longer.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Pain (PDF p. 21)

questions.stem: In PQRST pain assessment, 'R' refers to:
questions.rationale: PQRST: provoking factors, quality, radiation, severity, time.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Characteristics of Pain (PDF p. 21)

questions.stem: Percussing over an emphysematous lung produces which sound?
questions.rationale: Hyperresonance (very loud, booming) is heard over emphysematous lungs; resonance over normal lung.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion Sounds (PDF p. 22)

questions.stem: Which breath sound is soft, low-pitched, and heard over most of the lung fields?
questions.rationale: Vesicular sounds are soft, low-pitched 'gentle sighing' sounds over the bronchioles and alveoli.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Breath Sounds (PDF p. 22)

questions.stem: Foul-smelling perspiration is called:
questions.rationale: Bromhidrosis is foul-smelling sweat; hyperhidrosis is excessive sweating.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Care (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: A flat, colored spot smaller than 1 cm, like a freckle, is a:
questions.rationale: A macule is flat, circumscribed, under 1 cm; a patch is larger.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: A raised, fluid-filled lesion under 1 cm, as in chickenpox, is a:
questions.rationale: A vesicle is a small serous blister; a bulla is larger; a pustule has pus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 24)

questions.stem: A linear scratch mark exposing the dermis is a(n):
questions.rationale: An excoriation is a superficial linear or hollowed-out area exposing the dermis, such as a scratch.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 24)

questions.stem: A client disagrees with the dose of a medicine. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The nurse rechecks the medication order if the client disagrees with the dose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Medication Administration (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: Which is one of the Ten Rights of medication administration?
questions.rationale: The Ten Rights include right drug, dose, client, route, time, documentation, approach, right to know, right to refuse, and drug history.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ten Rights (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: An unexpected drug response unique to one client is a(n):
questions.rationale: Idiosyncratic effects are unexpected and individual; toxic effects come from overdose or buildup.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Medication Action (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: An order to give a drug 'immediately, once' is a:
questions.rationale: A stat order is a single dose given immediately.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Order (PDF p. 26)

questions.stem: Which tablet must NEVER be crushed?
questions.rationale: Enteric-coated and sustained-release tablets are never crushed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Route (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do before pouring a suspension?
questions.rationale: A suspension is water-based with settled particles; the bottle is shaken before use.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Drug Forms (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: Why should a sublingual tablet not be swallowed?
questions.rationale: Sublingual drugs dissolve and absorb rapidly under the tongue; if swallowed, gastric juice may inactivate them.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sublingual Route (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: At what angle is an intradermal injection given?
questions.rationale: Intradermal injections use a 25–27 gauge needle at 10–15° bevel up to form a wheal, without massage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Intradermal Injection (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: How is a glass ampule opened safely?
questions.rationale: Using gauze or an opener, the top is snapped by bending it toward you so it breaks away from yourself and others.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Ampules (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: Which needle is used to draw medicine from a glass ampule?
questions.rationale: A filter needle removes glass particles and is replaced with a regular needle before injecting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Ampules (PDF p. 28)

questions.stem: How should a vial of reconstituted medicine be mixed?
questions.rationale: Mix by rotating the vial between the palms, not by shaking.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Vials (PDF p. 29)

questions.stem: Which IV solution is hypotonic?
questions.rationale: 0.45% and 0.33% NaCl are hypotonic; NS and LR are isotonic; D5NS is hypertonic.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Solutions (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: Which IV solution can help treat metabolic acidosis?
questions.rationale: Lactate is metabolized in the liver to bicarbonate, so LR is alkalinizing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Solutions (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: Which vein should be chosen FIRST for a peripheral IV?
options: A distal vein of the non-dominant arm
A vein over the elbow joint
A vein in an injured arm
questions.rationale: Use distal veins first, on the non-dominant arm, that are soft, full, and splinted by bone; avoid flexion areas and injured limbs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vein Selection (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: An IV solution looks cloudy. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: Solutions must be clear; cloudiness is evidence of contamination.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Equipment (PDF p. 30)

questions.stem: An IV site is swollen, cool, and pale. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop and restart at another site
Apply a warm pack and continue
questions.rationale: These are signs of infiltration; the IV is disconnected and restarted at a different site, and movement limited.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: During IV therapy, a client has distended neck veins, high BP, and dyspnea. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are signs of circulatory overload; slow the rate, notify the doctor, and monitor.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: An IV vein is red, warm, and tender. After stopping the IV, what should be applied?
questions.rationale: For superficial thrombophlebitis, discontinue the IV and apply warm moist compresses; avoid the vein.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: An air embolism is suspected during IV therapy. How should the client be positioned?
questions.rationale: The client is placed on the left side (often head down) to trap air in the right heart, and the doctor is notified.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: A rapid IV push causes pounding headache, chills, and rapid pulse. What is this?
questions.rationale: Speed shock results from giving IV push drugs too rapidly.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)

questions.stem: Which blood product is used to increase oxygen-carrying capacity?
questions.rationale: Packed RBCs increase oxygen-carrying capacity; platelets treat bleeding from low platelets; FFP provides clotting factors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Products (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: Which IV solution is the ONLY one given with blood?
questions.rationale: Only normal saline is given with blood; dextrose causes hemolysis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: Within what time must a unit of blood be completely transfused?
questions.rationale: Transfusion should be completed within 4 hours of removal from refrigeration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: Which needle size is usually used for blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: Blood is usually given through an 18–20 gauge needle or catheter.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: How long can blood stay at room temperature before starting the transfusion?
questions.rationale: Blood should be at room temperature no more than 30 minutes before infusion begins.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Transfusion (PDF p. 32)

questions.stem: When is the client watched MOST closely during a transfusion?
questions.rationale: Run blood slowly the first 15 minutes and observe closely, with VS 15 minutes after starting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Transfusion (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: A client develops chills, back pain, and hypotension during a transfusion. What is the FIRST action?
questions.rationale: These suggest a hemolytic reaction; stop the transfusion, keep the line open with NS, and notify the doctor.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: A client gets mild itching and hives during a transfusion. Which reaction is this?
questions.rationale: Mild allergic reactions (to plasma proteins) cause flushing, itching, urticaria; slow or stop, notify, and give antihistamine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 33)

questions.stem: During a transfusion, an older client develops cough, crackles, and distended neck veins. How is he positioned?
questions.rationale: Circulatory overload: place upright with feet dependent, slow or stop, notify, and give diuretics and oxygen as ordered.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 34)

questions.stem: An infection that results directly from a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure is:
questions.rationale: Iatrogenic infections result directly from procedures; endogenous come from the client's own flora.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Asepsis (PDF p. 34)

questions.stem: Which agent is used to clean blood spills?
questions.rationale: Chlorine (bleach) kills bacteria, TB, spores, fungi, and viruses and is used for blood spills.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antiseptics and Disinfectants (PDF p. 34)

questions.stem: What are standard autoclave conditions?
questions.rationale: Autoclaving uses steam under pressure at 15–17 lb and 121–123°C.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Which sterilization method suits heat-sensitive items but is toxic to humans?
questions.rationale: Ethylene oxide penetrates well and suits heat-sensitive items but is toxic.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Which body fluid is exempt from standard precautions?
questions.rationale: Standard precautions apply to blood, all body fluids, secretions, and excretions except sweat.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Standard Precautions (PDF p. 35)

questions.stem: Which item needs NO special precautions after use by an infected client?
questions.rationale: Dishes require no special precautions; specimens go in leak-proof biohazard containers, sharps in puncture-resistant containers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Disposal of Equipment (PDF p. 37)

questions.stem: Accumulation of carbon dioxide in the blood is called:
questions.rationale: Hypercapnia is CO2 accumulation; hypoxemia is low blood oxygen.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Alterations (PDF p. 37)

questions.stem: How should pursed-lip breathing be done?
questions.rationale: Purse the lips as if to whistle and breathe out slowly without puffing the cheeks.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pursed-Lip Breathing (PDF p. 37)

questions.stem: In controlled coughing, why cough twice?
questions.rationale: The first cough loosens mucus; the second expels it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Controlled Coughing (PDF p. 38)

questions.stem: What is the usual sequence for chest physiotherapy?
questions.rationale: The sequence is postural drainage, percussion, vibration, then removal of secretions by coughing or suctioning.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion, Vibration and Postural Drainage (PDF p. 38)

questions.stem: Over which area is chest percussion AVOIDED?
questions.rationale: Percussion is avoided over the breasts, sternum, spinal column, and kidneys.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion (PDF p. 38)

questions.stem: When is vibration applied during chest physiotherapy?
questions.rationale: Vibrate during exhalation and stop when the client inhales.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Vibration (PDF p. 39)

questions.stem: When is postural drainage BEST scheduled?
questions.rationale: Best times are before breakfast, before lunch, late afternoon, and before bedtime, to avoid vomiting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Postural Drainage (PDF p. 39)

questions.stem: Which blanket should be used for a client on oxygen?
questions.rationale: Avoid static-generating wool and synthetic fabrics; use cotton.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oxygen Safety (PDF p. 39)

questions.stem: What oxygen concentration does a nasal cannula deliver at 2–6 L/min?
questions.rationale: A nasal cannula delivers 24–45% oxygen at 2–6 L/min.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oxygen Delivery (PDF p. 39)

questions.stem: How is the inner cannula reinserted after cleaning?
questions.rationale: The inner cannula is inserted in the direction of its curvature and locked to the outer cannula flange.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheostomy Care (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: Which dressing is used under a tracheostomy flange?
questions.rationale: Use a commercial non-raveling dressing or a folded 4x4; never cut gauze or use cotton-filled squares (fibers can be aspirated).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheostomy Care (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: Which suction catheter size is used for an adult?
questions.rationale: Adults Fr 12–18; children Fr 8–10; infants Fr 5–8.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: Which catheter is used for oropharyngeal suctioning?
questions.rationale: A Yankauer catheter is used for oropharyngeal suctioning.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 40)

questions.stem: How long should one suction pass last?
questions.rationale: Apply suction 5–10 seconds; the whole attempt lasts 10–15 seconds, and total suctioning is limited to 5 minutes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)

questions.stem: When is suction applied during catheter insertion?
questions.rationale: No suction during insertion; apply intermittent suction while rotating and withdrawing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)

questions.stem: How is an unconscious client positioned for oral suctioning?
questions.rationale: Unconscious clients are placed lateral facing the nurse to drain secretions; conscious clients semi-Fowler's.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Suctioning (PDF p. 41)

questions.stem: How far is the catheter inserted for nasopharyngeal suction in an adult?
questions.rationale: Measure from nose tip to earlobe, about 13 cm (5 in) in adults.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nasopharyngeal Suctioning (PDF p. 41)

questions.stem: How long should the nurse wait between tracheal suction passes?
questions.rationale: Allow 2–3 minutes with oxygen between suctions when possible.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tracheal Suctioning (PDF p. 42)

questions.stem: Which urine specific gravity is normal?
questions.rationale: Normal specific gravity is 1.010–1.025.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Urine Characteristics (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: An adult's normal 24-hour urine output is about:
questions.rationale: Normal adult output is 1200–1500 mL per 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Urine Characteristics (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: Urine output under 500 mL a day in an adult is called:
questions.rationale: Oliguria is low output, usually under 500 mL/day; anuria is under 100 mL/day.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Urinary Problems (PDF p. 49)

questions.stem: A woman leaks a little urine when she sneezes. Which incontinence is this?
questions.rationale: Stress incontinence is leakage (under 50 mL) with increased abdominal pressure from sneezing or coughing.
