questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1504 (PDF p. 1813)

questions.stem: A client with chronic pancreatitis starts pancrelipase. Which effect should the nurse tell the client to expect?
questions.rationale: Pancrelipase is a digestive enzyme that reduces steatorrhea and improves nutrition. It does not treat pain or heartburn and does not regulate glucose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1505 (PDF p. 1814)

questions.stem: An older client is taking cimetidine. Which side effect should the home care nurse check for?
questions.rationale: Older adults are especially prone to cimetidine's CNS effects, the most frequent being confusion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1509 (PDF p. 1818)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a client with gout is responding to colchicine?
questions.rationale: Colchicine blocks the white cell inflammatory response to urate crystals, decreasing joint pain, inflammation, and the number of attacks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1513 (PDF p. 1823)

questions.stem: What is the MOST common side effect of aluminum hydroxide antacid?
questions.rationale: Aluminum-based antacids cause constipation and can cause hypophosphatemia. They contain sodium, so they are used cautiously in hypertension and heart failure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1515 (PDF p. 1825)

questions.stem: An older client has used casanthranol, a stimulant laxative, long-term. Which lab result is an adverse effect of this use?
questions.rationale: Long-term stimulant laxative use alters fluid and electrolyte transport and can cause hypokalemia. Normal potassium is 3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1518 (PDF p. 1827)

questions.stem: What is the MOST frequent side effect of cyclobenzaprine for muscle spasms?
questions.rationale: Cyclobenzaprine, a centrally acting muscle relaxant, most often causes drowsiness, dizziness, and dry mouth, so safety is a priority.
explanations: Correct: the most frequent side effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1519 (PDF p. 1829)

questions.stem: A client with refractory myasthenia gravis asks why plasmapheresis is ordered. The nurse explains it will most likely:
questions.rationale: Plasmapheresis removes antibody-containing plasma proteins. In myasthenia gravis it is an adjunct that may give temporary relief, especially with impending respiratory failure. Usually 3 to 5 treatments are needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1525 (PDF p. 1835)

questions.stem: A client with myxedema has fatigue, cold intolerance, and facial puffiness. Lack of which hormones causes these findings?
questions.rationale: Myxedema results from inadequate thyroid hormone (T3 and T4), which lowers the basal metabolic rate and affects nearly every body system.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q64 (PDF p. 209)

questions.situation: Aling Cora, 34, is admitted with Graves' disease. She has weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, and an enlarged thyroid.
questions.stem: Which menstrual change should the nurse expect Aling Cora to report?
questions.rationale: Amenorrhea or decreased menstrual flow is common in Graves' disease (toxic diffuse goiter).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q65 (PDF p. 210)

questions.situation: Aling Cora, 34, is admitted with Graves' disease. She has weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, and an enlarged thyroid.
questions.stem: Aling Cora will receive radioactive iodine. What should the nurse tell her?
options: It destroys the whole gland in one dose
Relief of symptoms may take 6 to 8 weeks
questions.rationale: Radioactive iodine lowers thyroid hormone levels over time. Symptom relief does not occur until about 6 to 8 weeks after treatment.
explanations: It reduces, not instantly destroys, the gland.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q253 (PDF p. 410)

questions.stem: Which finding in a client with acute pancreatitis shows paralytic ileus has developed?
options: A firm mass at the right costal margin
questions.rationale: Inflammation such as pancreatitis can cause paralytic ileus, a nonmechanical obstruction. Inability to pass flatus is a sign.
explanations: Correct: a sign of paralytic ileus.
Pain in ileus is more diffuse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q181 (PDF p. 334)

questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Mang Ponso is short of breath from the ascites. What is the PRIORITY nursing measure?
options: Raise the head of the bed
questions.rationale: Ascitic fluid pushes up on the diaphragm. Raising the head of the bed uses gravity to relieve the pressure and ease breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q202 (PDF p. 356)

questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Which diet does the nurse expect for Mang Ponso?
questions.rationale: With ascites, sodium and possibly fluids are restricted. Fat stays normal, carbohydrates are sufficient, and calories are 2,000 to 3,000 a day.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q621 (PDF p. 836)

questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Ponso at discharge shows he needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is avoided in cirrhosis because it can cause fatal liver damage. Rest, nutrition, and weight monitoring are appropriate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q641 (PDF p. 859)

questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which item should be at Ate Rose's bedside after surgery?
questions.rationale: Swelling in the tracheal area after thyroidectomy can cause respiratory distress, so an emergency tracheostomy kit is kept at the bedside, along with oxygen and suction.
explanations: Thyroid surgery does not alter heat control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q259 (PDF p. 416)

questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which finding suggests the parathyroid glands were damaged during Ate Rose's surgery?
questions.rationale: Parathyroid damage lowers PTH, causing hypocalcemia and tetany. Tingling around the mouth or of the fingers and toes, and muscle twitching, are early signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q372 (PDF p. 540)

questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which statement by Ate Rose before surgery shows she understands the teaching?
options: 'I'll support my neck when I cough or move.'
'I should keep my head bent forward.'
'I can turn my head freely right away.'
questions.rationale: Supporting the neck when coughing or moving reduces tension on the incision. Removing the thyroid does not mean taking antithyroid drugs afterward.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q759 (PDF p. 988)

questions.stem: Which assessment gives the BEST data about hypothyroidism on admission?
questions.rationale: Inspecting the face reveals coarse features, puffiness around the eyes, and the blank expression typical of hypothyroidism.
explanations: The thyroid is palpated, not percussed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q301 (PDF p. 464)

questions.stem: Which finding does the nurse expect in a client with hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Low thyroid hormone slows metabolism: bradycardia, hypotension, cool dry scaly skin, low body temperature, brittle hair, and cold intolerance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q383 (PDF p. 552)

questions.stem: After transsphenoidal pituitary surgery, which assessment detects a common temporary complication?
questions.rationale: Surgical trauma can cause temporary diabetes insipidus from ADH deficiency, with polyuria of 4 to 24 L a day. Urine output and weight are monitored.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q335 (PDF p. 503)

questions.stem: Which finding should the nurse plan to manage in a client with diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: ADH deficiency causes massive urine output, poor skin turgor, dry mucous membranes, narrowed pulse pressure, tachycardia, and hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q384 (PDF p. 553)

questions.stem: Which intervention belongs in the post-hypophysectomy care plan?
questions.rationale: Diabetes insipidus or SIADH can develop, so daily weights and I&O are monitored. The head of the bed is raised. Coughing and toothbrushing are avoided because they can disrupt the surgical site and cause a CSF leak.
explanations: Coughing raises ICP and strains the site.
Avoided to protect the surgical site.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q371 (PDF p. 539)

questions.stem: Discharge teaching after a UNILATERAL adrenalectomy should include:
options: Taking steroids that will be tapered off
questions.rationale: After removal of one adrenal gland, corticosteroids are given temporarily and tapered off; lifelong replacement is not needed. Steroids also mask infection, so the client watches for its signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q337 (PDF p. 505)

questions.stem: Which question BEST elicits data about hyperparathyroidism?
options: 'Do you have joint or bone pain?'
questions.rationale: Excess PTH pulls calcium from bone, causing demineralization and bone and joint pain, along with hypercalcemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q379 (PDF p. 548)

questions.stem: Which item MUST be at the bedside after a parathyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage and swelling can compress the trachea and cause respiratory distress, so a tracheotomy set is routinely placed at the bedside.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q547 (PDF p. 748)

questions.stem: The cause of a client's acute abdominal pain is not yet known. Which order should the nurse question?
questions.rationale: Until the cause is known and the need for surgery is decided, the client is kept NPO with an IV line. A clear liquid diet would be questioned.
explanations: Correct: the client should be NPO.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q419 (PDF p. 596)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with type 1 diabetes about sick days needs correction?
options: 'I'll stop my insulin if I'm vomiting.'
'I'll call my doctor if ill more than 24 hours.'
'I'll check my sugar every 2 to 4 hours.'
questions.rationale: Insulin is continued even when vomiting and unable to eat, to prevent DKA. Blood glucose is checked every 2 to 4 hours during illness.
explanations: Correct answer: stopping insulin risks DKA.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q631 (PDF p. 848)

questions.stem: Which statement about hypoglycemia shows a client needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll take extra insulin if I feel shaky.'
questions.rationale: Insulin lowers blood glucose further and is never a treatment for hypoglycemia. The client takes 10 to 15 g of simple carbohydrate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q632 (PDF p. 850)

questions.stem: Which food should a client recovering from pancreatitis AVOID?
questions.rationale: Spicy foods, alcohol, coffee, tea, and heavy meals stimulate pancreatic secretions and can trigger attacks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q640 (PDF p. 858)

questions.stem: A client is discharged after hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS). Which teaching is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Dehydration in HHS can be severe and progress rapidly, so reporting its signs is the priority.
explanations: Part of teaching, not the priority.
Part of teaching, not the priority.
Part of teaching, not the priority.
Correct: dehydration is the main danger.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q686 (PDF p. 907)

questions.stem: When planning diabetes care for an older client, what should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Encourage family to do her care
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses self-care ability. Planning menus and relying on others promote dependence, and hands-on practice works better than video.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q687 (PDF p. 908)

questions.stem: A client with gastritis asks which pain reliever will not upset the stomach. The nurse recommends:
questions.rationale: Aspirin and NSAIDs such as naproxen and ibuprofen irritate the GI tract. Acetaminophen does not.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q717 (PDF p. 939)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with Cushing's syndrome understands discharge teaching?
options: 'I'll check my stools for dark color.'
'I'll stop steroids suddenly if I feel well.'
questions.rationale: Excess cortisol increases gastric acid, which can cause peptic ulcers and GI bleeding, so stool color is checked. Potassium-rich foods are encouraged because hypokalemia occurs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q754 (PDF p. 983)

questions.stem: A client with type 1 diabetes has a glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) of 10%. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Good control in the past week
Poor glucose control over recent weeks
questions.rationale: HbA1c reflects glucose control over the previous 6 to 8 weeks and is not affected by diet in the last day or two. A level of 10% shows poor control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q757 (PDF p. 986)

questions.stem: When is hypoglycemia MOST likely after an insulin injection?
options: At the end of its duration
questions.rationale: Reactions are most likely at peak time, when the insulin is at its maximum action. Regular insulin peaks in about 2 hours; NPH in 4 to 12 hours.
explanations: Risk is highest at the peak.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q758 (PDF p. 987)

questions.stem: Which instruction helps a client with type 1 diabetes manage the risk of hypoglycemia?
questions.rationale: Glucose tablets treat a hypoglycemic reaction. Glucagon may be prescribed if the client becomes unconscious and cannot swallow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q765 (PDF p. 994)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with peptic ulcer disease shows effective teaching?
options: 'I'll take antacids with my H2 blocker.'
questions.rationale: Eating slowly and chewing well prevent overdistention and reflux. Bedtime snacks raise night acid, aspirin and NSAIDs are avoided, and antacids interfere with H2 blockers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q781 (PDF p. 1011)

questions.stem: Which dietary statement by a client with GERD needs correction?
questions.rationale: Fluids are taken between meals to prevent overdistention and reflux. Coffee, tea, cola, and chocolate lower LES pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q783 (PDF p. 1013)

questions.stem: A client with a colostomy complains of odor. Which food helps reduce it?
questions.rationale: Yogurt, buttermilk, cranberry juice, and parsley help reduce odor. Eggs, fish, onions, cucumbers, mushrooms, and cabbage cause odor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q791 (PDF p. 1021)

questions.stem: For a client newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, which teaching is MOST important initially?
questions.rationale: Before teaching self-management, the client must understand the disease itself. Diet, glucose testing, and insulin technique follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q811 (PDF p. 1045)

questions.stem: A client with diabetes asks why the nurse wants family members at an insulin class. What is the BEST reply?
options: 'Your family is at risk for diabetes too.'
'They'll give your insulin from now on.'
'They can support you in adjusting your care.'
questions.rationale: Families are included in diabetes education to help with adjustments to the regimen. Supportive family involvement helps the client become independent in care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q813 (PDF p. 1047)

questions.stem: A client with ruptured esophageal varices and a history of alcohol abuse says, 'I deserve this.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Would you like to see the chaplain?'
'Is there some reason you feel you deserve this?'
questions.rationale: An open-ended response invites the client to talk and helps the nurse get an accurate history of alcohol intake, which a shamed client might hide.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q847 (PDF p. 1084)

questions.stem: A client with jaundice has pruritus. Which statement needs MORE teaching?
options: 'A tepid bath will ease the itch.'
'I'll keep the house warm and cozy.'
questions.rationale: Bile salts deposited in the skin cause the itching. A cool environment minimizes it; warmth worsens it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1065 (PDF p. 1347)

questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease is monitored for hyperkalemia. Which finding is MOST concerning?
questions.rationale: Low aldosterone in Addison's disease causes potassium retention. The most harmful effect of hyperkalemia is on cardiac function.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1113 (PDF p. 1397)

questions.stem: Which intervention is ESSENTIAL in the care plan after a bilateral adrenalectomy?
questions.rationale: Adrenalectomy can lead to adrenal insufficiency, and adrenal hormones are needed to respond to stress. Stress can trigger adrenal crisis.
explanations: Correct: stress can trigger adrenal crisis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1147 (PDF p. 1434)

questions.stem: Which outcome shows that nutrition care for a client with Graves' disease is successful?
options: She eats less to control appetite
She limits calories to 1,200 a day
questions.rationale: Graves' disease causes a hypercatabolic state with weight loss despite increased appetite. The goal is no further weight loss and a gradual return to ideal weight.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1239 (PDF p. 1532)

questions.stem: Which findings of thyroid storm require IMMEDIATE intervention?
questions.rationale: Excess thyroid hormone sharply raises the metabolic rate, causing fever, tachycardia, and hypertension. Quick action is needed because death can follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1257 (PDF p. 1558)

questions.stem: Which fear is a REALISTIC source of anxiety before thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: The incision is in the neck, so fear of a large scar is realistic. There are no specific dietary restrictions after discharge.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1261 (PDF p. 1562)

questions.stem: Which finding suggests perforation in a client with peptic ulcer disease?
questions.rationale: Sudden, severe abdominal pain signals perforation. The pulse becomes weak and rapid, and bowel sounds may be absent. A positive guaiac shows bleeding, not necessarily perforation.
explanations: The pulse becomes weak and rapid.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1294 (PDF p. 1595)

questions.stem: Which MODIFIABLE risk factor for colorectal cancer should the nurse emphasize?
questions.rationale: A high-fat, low-fiber diet can be changed. Age, family history, and ulcerative colitis cannot.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1395 (PDF p. 1699)

questions.stem: How should a client with GERD sleep to reduce reflux?
options: Head of bed raised about 30 degrees
questions.rationale: The client stays upright 1 to 2 hours after meals and sleeps with the head of the bed raised about 30 degrees (on 8- to 12-inch blocks). Lying flat increases reflux.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1396 (PDF p. 1700)

questions.stem: How should the client be positioned for abdominal paracentesis?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's or upright on the edge of the bed with feet supported lets the intestines float back and helps prevent laceration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1404 (PDF p. 1710)

questions.stem: A client with chronic ulcerative colitis has anemia. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.rationale: Ulcerative colitis causes repeated small blood losses during exacerbations, with bloody stools, leading to anemia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1464 (PDF p. 1773)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with diabetes understands the signs of HYPERglycemia?
options: 'I'll feel tired, have dry skin, and urinate more.'
'I'll take an extra pill if sugar is high.'
questions.rationale: Fatigue, dry skin, polyuria, and polydipsia are classic hyperglycemia signs. Sweating, shakiness, and hunger suggest hypoglycemia.
explanations: Doses are not changed by the client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1470 (PDF p. 1779)

questions.stem: A client with trigeminal neuralgia asks for a snack. Which is the BEST choice?
questions.rationale: Light touch or temperature extremes can trigger trigeminal pain, so soft, lukewarm, nutritious foods are best.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q57 (PDF p. 198)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with trigeminal neuralgia shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll avoid cold drafts on my face.'
questions.rationale: Trigeminal neuralgia causes sudden, intense facial pain that is rarely relieved by analgesics. Chewing on the unaffected side and warm mouthwash are recommended.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q764 (PDF p. 993)

questions.stem: In a client with a brainstem injury, which assessment is MOST critical along with the GCS?
questions.rationale: The respiratory center is in the brainstem, so respiratory status and cranial nerve function are critical to assess.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q62 (PDF p. 207)

questions.stem: After a supratentorial craniotomy, how is the client usually positioned?
questions.rationale: After supratentorial surgery the head is raised about 30 degrees to promote venous outflow and control intracranial pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q111 (PDF p. 260)

questions.stem: Which finding is typical of Guillain-Barré syndrome?
questions.rationale: Guillain-Barré syndrome is an acute autoimmune disorder with ascending symmetrical weakness leading to flaccid paralysis without atrophy, decreased reflexes, and possible respiratory compromise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q310 (PDF p. 474)

questions.stem: Which measure prevents footdrop in a client with a spinal cord injury?
questions.rationale: Posterior splints or high-top sneakers prevent footdrop (plantar flexion). Heel protectors protect skin, and pneumatic boots prevent DVT.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q333 (PDF p. 499)

questions.stem: After transsphenoidal surgery, what should the nurse tell the client to report?
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing or postnasal drip may indicate a cerebrospinal fluid leak. Coughing is avoided because it raises ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q338 (PDF p. 506)

questions.stem: A standing client starts a tonic-clonic seizure. What should the nurse do?
options: Guide him gently to the floor
questions.rationale: The nurse protects the client from injury by guiding him to the floor, turning him to the side, keeping the airway open, and loosening tight clothing. Restraints and tongue blades are never used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q391 (PDF p. 561)

questions.stem: A client with subarachnoid hemorrhage is on aneurysm precautions. Which intervention promotes safety?
questions.rationale: Aneurysm precautions reduce stimuli that raise ICP. Straining at stool raises ICP, so stool softeners are given and enemas avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q428 (PDF p. 605)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY in discharge teaching for a client with a spinal cord injury?
questions.rationale: Involving significant others is a priority. The client will need their support, and understanding what to expect helps both cope with the limitations.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q563 (PDF p. 765)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with Bell's palsy shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I wear an eye patch at night.'
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy affects cranial nerve VII. A liquid diet is not needed; the client chews on the unaffected side. Eye protection and facial massage are appropriate.
explanations: Correct answer: a liquid diet is not needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q763 (PDF p. 992)

questions.stem: A client with left-sided Bell's palsy says, 'I don't know how I'll live with this stroke.' What does this show?
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy is inflammation of cranial nerve VII, not a stroke. Many clients wrongly fear a stroke and believe the paralysis is permanent.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q966 (PDF p. 1214)

questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: Which outcome shows his care plan is effective?
questions.rationale: A C5 injury causes quadriplegia with no sensation below the clavicle. Maintaining intact skin is a realistic outcome; the others are not.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q770 (PDF p. 1000)

questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: While being bathed, Kuya Arnel says, 'I can't do this. I wish I were dead.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying by restating invites the client to say more. 'Why' puts him on the defensive, and the others change the subject or give false reassurance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q828 (PDF p. 1064)

questions.situation: Kuya Arnel, 28, sustained a C5 spinal cord injury in a construction fall. He is now in rehabilitation.
questions.stem: Kuya Arnel says, 'It's so depressing; I'll never have sex again.' What is the REALISTIC reply?
questions.rationale: A sexual relationship is still possible after spinal cord injury, though different from before. Sexual counseling can help with adaptation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q888 (PDF p. 1130)

questions.stem: A client with a thoracic cord injury has an unnoticed red area on the coccyx. After teaching a turning schedule, how should he check his skin?
options: Ask a relative to check daily
Use a mirror to inspect it
questions.rationale: A mirror allows independent skin self-assessment. The client cannot feel the redness, and relying on family does not promote independence.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q772 (PDF p. 1002)

questions.stem: A client with a spinal cord injury has bladder spasms and reflex incontinence. Which instruction helps prevent the problem?
options: Limit fluids to 1 L a day
questions.rationale: Caffeine contributes to bladder spasms and reflex incontinence and is eliminated from the diet. Fluid restriction does not prevent spasms.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q784 (PDF p. 1014)

questions.stem: Which statement by a woman with a T11 cord transection shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Women with spinal cord injury remain fertile, so contraception is needed if sexually active (oral contraceptives may raise thrombophlebitis risk). Limiting dairy helps prevent urinary calculi.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q794 (PDF p. 1024)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client with chronic immobility from spinal cord injury needs IMMEDIATE follow-up?
options: 'I don't want to live like this.'
questions.rationale: Expressions of hopelessness or despair need immediate attention because they may mean the client is thinking of self-harm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q834 (PDF p. 1070)

questions.stem: Which assessment BEST tests frontal lobe function in a client with dementia?
questions.rationale: Insight, judgment, and planning are frontal lobe functions. Emotions involve the limbic system, and consciousness the reticular activating system.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q848 (PDF p. 1085)

questions.stem: A relative feels guilty for not urging a client with a brain tumor to see a doctor sooner. What should the nurse include in the response?
options: Early signs are easy to spot
questions.rationale: Brain tumor symptoms vary by location (headache, vomiting, visual or personality changes) and are easily attributed to other causes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q889 (PDF p. 1131)

questions.stem: A client recovering from a head injury becomes agitated. Which action BEST calms him?
options: Give him a new task to learn
Turn on music on the TV
Tell him the behavior is bad
questions.rationale: Familiar topics and objects reduce anxiety, and fewer environmental stimuli reduce agitation. New tasks frustrate and TV adds stimuli.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q897 (PDF p. 1140)

questions.stem: A client recovering from stroke is irritable and angry about his limitations. Which approach BEST restores motivation?
options: Do tasks for him to avoid frustration
questions.rationale: Supporting and praising accomplishments motivates stroke clients. Behavior is pointed out for correction rather than ignored.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q898 (PDF p. 1141)

questions.stem: A woman with myasthenia gravis fears her husband will no longer find her attractive. Which action should the nurse encourage?
options: Share her feelings with her husband
questions.rationale: Encouraging her to share her feelings directly with her husband addresses her specific concern. The other responses block communication or avoid the issue.
explanations: Does not address her individual concern.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q938 (PDF p. 1182)

questions.stem: A client with a complete T1 cord injury says, 'I'm no good to anyone. I might as well be dead.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'I'll ask the psychologist to see you.'
'You feel you're no good to anyone?'
questions.rationale: Restating and reflecting keep communication open and invite him to explore his feelings of loss and unworthiness. Grief is a common response.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q976 (PDF p. 1225)

questions.stem: Soon after a complete T4 transection, a client insists he will walk once spinal shock resolves. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Denial is a normal early response
questions.rationale: In the first weeks after injury, denial is a normal defense that temporarily lowers anxiety. Prolonged denial can impair rehabilitation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q978 (PDF p. 1227)

questions.stem: How can the nurse help the family of an unconscious head-injured client cope?
options: Tell them to grieve outside the room
Limit their questions to the doctor
questions.rationale: The nurse explains equipment, treatments, and procedures and reinforces the provider's information. Displaying grief is normal and should not be discouraged.
explanations: Correct: reduces fear of the unknown.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1018 (PDF p. 1291)

questions.stem: Which family statement shows effective teaching for a client with Parkinson's disease?
options: 'We'll plan only a few daily activities.'
'We'll let him nap whenever he wants.'
'We'll encourage him to take part in his care.'
questions.rationale: Clients with Parkinson's disease tend to become withdrawn and depressed. Active participation in self-care and activities spread through the day prevent this.
explanations: Activities are spread throughout the day.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1022 (PDF p. 1295)

questions.stem: Which warning signs most likely occurred before a client's thrombotic stroke?
questions.rationale: Cerebral thrombosis develops over hours or days, often preceded by transient aphasia, hemiplegia, or one-sided paresthesias.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1099 (PDF p. 1383)

questions.stem: After a thrombotic stroke, a client has sudden bouts of laughing or crying. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: An expected effect of the stroke
questions.rationale: Emotional lability (sudden laughing, crying, or irritability) is a normal part of the clinical picture after a thrombotic stroke.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1123 (PDF p. 1407)

questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis has vomiting, cramps, diarrhea, hypotension, and facial twitching. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Cholinergic crisis from overmedication with anticholinesterases causes GI upset, facial twitching, miosis, and hypotension. Medications are withheld.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1135 (PDF p. 1421)

questions.stem: A client develops diabetes insipidus after cranial surgery. Which therapy does the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Diabetes insipidus causes large volumes of very dilute urine. Treatment replaces the fluid losses and gives ADH replacement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1156 (PDF p. 1443)

questions.stem: A client returns from microvascular decompression of the trigeminal nerve. Which equipment should the nurse ask the aide to place at the bedside?
questions.rationale: Care is the same as after craniotomy: hourly neurologic checks (pupils with a flashlight) and monitoring of cardiovascular and respiratory status (pulse oximetry).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1170 (PDF p. 1457)

questions.stem: A client with Guillain-Barré syndrome has paralysis ascending to the waist. Which equipment should be ready for emergencies?
questions.rationale: Ascending paralysis can cause respiratory failure, so an intubation tray is kept ready. Cardiac dysrhythmias also occur, so cardiac monitoring is needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1171 (PDF p. 1458)

questions.stem: A stroke client coughs when swallowing and now has a temperature of 38.3°C, SpO2 of 91%, confusion, and dyspnea. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: These are signs of aspiration (fever, dyspnea, low oxygen, confusion). A complication has developed, so the provider is notified.
explanations: Too late as the only action.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1198 (PDF p. 1490)

questions.situation: Mang Tomas, 52, is admitted with a leaking cerebral aneurysm and is scheduled for surgery.
questions.stem: Which intervention should the nurse implement before surgery?
questions.rationale: Aneurysm precautions keep activity minimal to prevent straining (Valsalva), which raises blood pressure and increases bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1206 (PDF p. 1498)

questions.situation: Mang Tomas, 52, is admitted with a leaking cerebral aneurysm and is scheduled for surgery.
questions.stem: Mang Tomas's daughter asks to take him to the lounge 'for just a few minutes.' What should the nurse explain?
questions.rationale: Aneurysm precautions minimize stimuli that could raise intracranial pressure and trigger bleeding or rupture. Reduced stimuli do not speed healing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1543 (PDF p. 1855)

questions.situation: Mang Tomas, 52, is admitted with a leaking cerebral aneurysm and is scheduled for surgery.
questions.stem: Which medication order should the nurse QUESTION for a client with a ruptured intracranial aneurysm?
questions.rationale: Heparin, an anticoagulant, raises the risk of rebleeding. Nicardipine manages vasospasm, docusate prevents straining, and aminocaproic acid prevents clot breakdown.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1463 (PDF p. 1772)

questions.stem: A client with Bell's palsy is upset about her face. What should the nurse tell her?
options: It often resolves in 3 to 5 weeks
questions.rationale: Clients are reassured that it is not a stroke and that symptoms often disappear on their own in about 3 to 5 weeks. Treatment is supportive.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1408 (PDF p. 1714)

questions.stem: Which finding is the PRIMARY indicator of neurologic status in a client with an acute head injury?
questions.rationale: LOC is the primary indicator. It changes before other neurologic signs or vital signs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1445 (PDF p. 1754)

questions.stem: During a seizure, a client's whole body becomes rigid, then all four limbs alternately contract and relax. How should the nurse document this?
questions.rationale: Tonic-clonic seizures begin with rigidity (tonic) followed by rhythmic contraction and relaxation (clonic). Absence seizures are brief lapses with a blank stare.
explanations: Brief lapse with a blank stare.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1450 (PDF p. 1759)

questions.stem: A client with a right-sided stroke has left-sided neglect. Which action would REINFORCE the neglect?
options: Teach him to scan to the left
Keep his items on the right side only
Place the chair on his left
Touch his left arm when talking
questions.rationale: The nurse refocuses the client's attention to the affected side. Items, the chair, and the commode are placed on the affected side, and the client is taught to scan toward it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1451 (PDF p. 1760)

questions.stem: When would continued fatigue suggest a client's myasthenia gravis drugs are not optimal?
questions.rationale: In myasthenia gravis, weakness appears after exertion and near the end of the day. If fatigue persists then despite therapy, the regimen may need adjusting.
explanations: Correct: the typical timing of weakness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1452 (PDF p. 1761)

questions.stem: Which symptom does the nurse expect in a client with trigeminal neuralgia?
options: Sudden pain along cranial nerve V
questions.rationale: Trigeminal neuralgia is abrupt-onset pain involving one or more divisions of the trigeminal nerve (cranial nerve V).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1497 (PDF p. 1806)

questions.stem: Which can trigger the pain of trigeminal neuralgia?
questions.rationale: Stimulating trigeminal nerve branches triggers pain: washing the face, brushing teeth, shaving, eating, yawning, or temperature stimuli such as a draft.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1527 (PDF p. 1837)

questions.stem: Which findings does the nurse expect in a client with Bell's palsy?
options: One-sided facial droop and trouble chewing
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy is one-sided facial paralysis from compression of cranial nerve VII. It causes facial droop, increased tearing, pain near the ear, and difficulty chewing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1528 (PDF p. 1838)

questions.stem: When taking the history of a client with Guillain-Barré syndrome, the nurse should ask about a recent:
questions.rationale: Many clients report a respiratory or GI infection 1 to 4 weeks before the onset of neurologic deficits.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1531 (PDF p. 1841)

questions.stem: Which position relieves low back pain in a client with a herniated lumbar disk?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's with the knees flexed (Williams position) relaxes the lower back muscles and relieves pressure on the spinal nerve root.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q7 (PDF p. 144)

questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which home instruction BEST prevents complications?
options: Trim the rough edges when dry
Bear weight once it feels dry
Use a hanger to scratch inside
questions.rationale: Elevation increases venous return and reduces edema, which can cause compartment syndrome. Trimmed edges can fall into the cast, and scratching damages the skin.
explanations: Pieces can fall inside the cast.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q9 (PDF p. 147)

questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which finding should make Mario seek medical attention right away?
options: A heavy, damp cast in the first day
questions.rationale: Numbness, tingling, and increased pain signal rising pressure from edema, which risks nerve damage. A cast takes up to 48 hours to dry and gives off heat while drying.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q702 (PDF p. 924)

questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which statement shows Mario understands plaster cast care?
options: 'I'll cover it with a warm blanket.'
'I'll scratch under it with a ruler.'
questions.rationale: A plaster cast must stay dry to keep its strength. Air should circulate to help it dry, and it is handled with the palms.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1209 (PDF p. 1502)

questions.stem: Which finding suggests infection under a cast?
questions.rationale: Infection under a cast shows as a musty odor, purulent drainage, or warm areas on the cast. Edema, weak pulses, and cool pale skin signal impaired circulation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q46 (PDF p. 185)

questions.stem: Which otoscopic finding does the nurse expect in mastoiditis?
questions.rationale: Mastoiditis shows a red, dull, thick, immobile tympanic membrane. The other findings are normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q68 (PDF p. 213)

questions.stem: Which finding is MOST common in inner ear disorders?
questions.rationale: Tinnitus is the most common complaint in ear disorders, especially inner ear disorders. It ranges from mild ringing to a loud roaring.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q69 (PDF p. 214)

questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: A complete neurovascular check of the affected leg includes:
questions.rationale: A neurovascular assessment covers color, sensation, movement, capillary refill, and pulses of the affected extremity.
explanations: Correct: the components of the check.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q122 (PDF p. 272)

questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: How does the nurse provide countertraction to reduce shear and friction?
options: Raise the foot of the bed slightly
Raise the head of the bed slightly
questions.rationale: The part of the bed under the traction is elevated. For leg traction, raising the foot of the bed opposes the traction force safely.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q151 (PDF p. 301)

questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: Lola Iska becomes disoriented. What is the MOST appropriate action?
questions.rationale: Inactive older adults may become disoriented from lack of sensory stimulation. Frequent reorientation, with a clock and calendar in the room, helps. Restraints worsen disorientation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q882 (PDF p. 1122)

questions.stem: Which pin-site finding is NORMAL in skeletal traction?
questions.rationale: A small amount of clear drainage ('weeping') can be expected. Loose pins, pus, redness, and swelling are reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q121 (PDF p. 271)

questions.stem: How should the nurse handle a newly applied wet arm cast during transfer?
options: Put ice on top of it
questions.rationale: Palms or flat fingers prevent dents in a wet cast, and pillows support its curves so it does not crack or flatten.
explanations: Not on top of the cast.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q123 (PDF p. 273)

questions.stem: A client asks why compartment syndrome developed after an arm fracture. What should the nurse explain?
options: A bone piece cut a nerve
questions.rationale: Bleeding and swelling inside a compartment lined by non-expanding fascia compress the nerves, muscles, and vessels within it.
explanations: Correct: pressure in a closed space.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q165 (PDF p. 317)

questions.stem: Which neurovascular finding with a new cast needs close follow-up?
questions.rationale: Normal capillary refill is under 3 seconds. Slow refill means poor circulation, and the toes or fingers will look pale or bluish.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q196 (PDF p. 350)

questions.stem: Which question helps assess for Ménière's disease?
options: 'Do you have ringing in your ears?'
questions.rationale: Ménière's disease involves excess endolymphatic fluid. It causes tinnitus, vertigo that can last for days, and one-sided sensorineural hearing loss.
explanations: Correct: tinnitus is a key sign.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q223 (PDF p. 378)

questions.stem: Which diet does the nurse expect to teach a client with Ménière's disease?
questions.rationale: Salt and fluid restrictions reduce the amount of endolymphatic fluid and are sometimes prescribed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1129 (PDF p. 1414)

questions.stem: Which intervention helps a client with Ménière's syndrome control vertigo?
questions.rationale: Slow head movements prevent worsening vertigo. Clients are advised to stop smoking entirely because of its vasoconstrictive effects.
explanations: Smoking should stop, not be reduced.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1151 (PDF p. 1438)

questions.stem: Which instruction is MOST important for home safety in a client with chronic vertigo?
options: Turn only your head when spoken to
questions.rationale: Slipping and trying to regain balance can trigger vertigo, so clutter and throw rugs are removed. The client turns the whole body and changes position slowly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q589 (PDF p. 797)

questions.stem: Which is an EARLY sign of rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.rationale: RA is a systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease. Early signs include fatigue, anorexia, weakness, low-grade fever, joint inflammation, and paresthesias. Deformities come later.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q349 (PDF p. 517)

questions.stem: Which action ensures a client's traction is safe and effective?
options: Weights hanging free off the floor
questions.rationale: Weights must hang freely, with knots kept away from the pulleys. The head of the bed is usually kept low for countertraction.
explanations: Weights must not rest on anything.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q519 (PDF p. 714)

questions.stem: On day 1 after total knee replacement, the client goes to a chair. How should the nurse protect the joint?
questions.rationale: A knee immobilizer stabilizes the joint, and the leg is elevated while sitting to minimize edema.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q574 (PDF p. 779)

questions.stem: Which surgeon's order needs clarification 2 hours after total knee surgery?
questions.rationale: Right after surgery the knee is kept in extension with a compression dressing. An order to keep it flexed needs clarification.
explanations: Correct answer: the knee is kept extended.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1382 (PDF p. 1685)

questions.stem: Which statement after a total knee replacement shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'The knee's shape may change; that's normal.'
'I'll tell caregivers about my metal implant.'
questions.rationale: Any change in the knee's shape must be reported; it is not expected. The client informs caregivers of the implant, which requires antibiotic prophylaxis for invasive procedures.
explanations: Correct answer: shape changes must be reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1494 (PDF p. 1803)

questions.stem: Which statement after total hip arthroplasty shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I won't twist my body when standing.'
'I can cross my legs when sitting.'
questions.rationale: Hip precautions include not crossing the legs past midline, avoiding bending past 90 degrees and twisting, and not sitting or standing for long periods.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q629 (PDF p. 846)

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with a below-knee amputation understands residual limb care?
questions.rationale: The residual limb is inspected daily for irritation, blisters, and breakdown. A clean woolen sock is worn daily, and alcohol is avoided because it dries the skin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q603 (PDF p. 814)

questions.stem: After LEFT eye cataract surgery, how should the client sleep?
options: On the right side or back
questions.rationale: The client sleeps on the nonoperative side or back to prevent edema. Bending below the waist or lowering the head raises intraocular pressure.
explanations: Correct: the nonoperative side or back.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q693 (PDF p. 914)

questions.stem: A client asks what happens in polymyositis. The nurse explains that:
questions.rationale: Polymyositis is a diffuse inflammatory disorder of skeletal muscle causing symmetrical weakness and atrophy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q747 (PDF p. 975)

questions.stem: Which behavior shows successful adaptation to presbycusis?
questions.rationale: Presbycusis is progressive age-related sensorineural hearing loss. Getting and regularly using a hearing aid shows good adaptation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q874 (PDF p. 1111)

questions.stem: A day after hip implant surgery, a businessman is surrounded by work papers planning a meeting. What should guide the nurse's discussion?
options: Rest is essential for bone healing
Work keeps his mind off pain
He must stop all work now
questions.rationale: Rest is essential for bone healing, and stress should be minimized. Nurses encourage clients to balance work demands rather than demanding changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q890 (PDF p. 1132)

questions.stem: A client in halo traction says, 'I can't see to the side and keep misjudging where things are.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Empathy and reflection, followed by a practical strategy, help the client adapt to limited peripheral vision.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q940 (PDF p. 1184)

questions.stem: After ventilation tubes are placed in the eardrum, which statement shows understanding?
questions.rationale: Water must be kept out of the ears. A shower cap or earplugs are used, and swimming and hair washing are avoided after surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1069 (PDF p. 1351)

questions.stem: An adult has a left earache, nausea, ear fullness, and fever. What should the nurse ask FIRST?
options: 'Do you clean your ears with cotton buds?'
questions.rationale: Adult otitis media is usually one-sided and acute, with earache, nausea, fever, and fullness. It often follows an upper respiratory infection, so the history is taken first.
explanations: Correct: URI often precedes otitis media.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1095 (PDF p. 1378)

questions.stem: A client is found on the floor after a fall, with a possible broken arm. What should the nurse do IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: A suspected fracture must be splinted before the client is moved. Vital signs follow, and the provider is called.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1201 (PDF p. 1493)

questions.stem: Which observation shows a successful outcome for a client in traction who is relearning self-care?
options: He does as much self-care as he can
He waits for staff to do it
questions.rationale: The goal is for the client to perform as much self-care as possible given the condition. The nurse promotes independence.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1243 (PDF p. 1536)

questions.stem: A client's skin at the cast edge is pink and irritated. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Petaling the cast edges with tape minimizes skin irritation. Powder can clump and cause breakdown.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1433 (PDF p. 1742)

questions.stem: What is a comminuted fracture?
questions.rationale: A comminuted fracture is a complete break across the shaft with the bone splintered into fragments. A greenstick fracture is incomplete.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1533 (PDF p. 1844)

questions.stem: Which sign in a fractured arm indicates IMPAIRED VENOUS RETURN?
questions.rationale: Increasing edema marks impaired venous return and is prevented by elevation. Weak pulses and pallor suggest arterial damage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1535 (PDF p. 1846)

questions.stem: Which task can the nurse safely delegate to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Delegation keeps accountability with the nurse. Nursing attendants are trained for noninvasive tasks such as delivering water, emptying urine bags, and taking vital signs of stable clients.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q403 (PDF p. 576)

questions.stem: Which activity is SAFE to assign to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Delegated work must match the person's expertise. Collecting specimens and taking frequent oral temperatures carry little foreseeable risk. Assessment is not delegated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q460 (PDF p. 642)

questions.stem: What should the nurse tell a nursing attendant to do for a client with acute glomerulonephritis?
questions.rationale: Acute glomerulonephritis causes fluid excess and fatigue. Care includes fluid restriction, weight and I&O monitoring, and rest. Protein is limited.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q556 (PDF p. 757)

questions.stem: Which guideline belongs in a policy on telephone and verbal orders?
options: Only the head nurse may receive them
questions.rationale: To avoid misunderstanding, the nurse clarifies any question with the prescriber and repeats the order back.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q410 (PDF p. 585)

questions.stem: A nurse finds an error in her handwritten chart entry. What should she do?
options: Draw one line and initial it
questions.rationale: A single line is drawn through the error and initialed so it stays readable. Errors are never erased, and correction fluid or markers are never used on a legal record.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q513 (PDF p. 708)

questions.stem: Which action shows a situational leadership style?
options: Asking for input on a problem
questions.rationale: Situational leaders change style with events, such as quickly delegating during an emergency. Laissez-faire leaders give up leadership; democratic leaders invite input.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q444 (PDF p. 624)

questions.stem: Which manager behavior shows an autocratic style?
questions.rationale: Autocratic leaders are task oriented and directive and decide without staff input.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q450 (PDF p. 630)

questions.stem: Which leadership style lets staff give input to decisions and best empowers them?
questions.rationale: Democratic leadership lets nurses take part in decisions and grow professionally.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q487 (PDF p. 678)

questions.stem: Which describes participative leadership?
questions.rationale: Participative leadership sits between authoritarian and democratic. The manager presents an analysis and proposals, invites comments, then makes the final decision.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q476 (PDF p. 661)

questions.stem: Which situation shows primary nursing?
options: The RN gives all care to her client
An RN leads a mixed team
Each staff does one task for all
questions.rationale: Primary nursing keeps the nurse at the bedside, giving goal-directed, individualized care. Team nursing is led by an RN; functional nursing assigns tasks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q489 (PDF p. 680)

questions.stem: The charge nurse has aides bathe clients, others pass water, and one RN give all medicines. Which model is this?
questions.rationale: Functional nursing is an assembly-line approach in which major tasks are assigned to individual staff members.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q501 (PDF p. 694)

questions.stem: Which describes team nursing?
options: An RN leads a team giving direct care
questions.rationale: In team nursing, an RN leads a team that gives direct care to a group of clients under the RN's supervision.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q562 (PDF p. 764)

questions.stem: Which statement describes case management?
options: It coordinates care and limits costs
The case manager gives all bedside care
It is done by one discipline
questions.rationale: Case management coordinates services for clients and families while keeping quality high and costs low. Case managers usually do not give direct care and work with other disciplines.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q541 (PDF p. 739)

questions.stem: Which function belongs to the unit nurse manager?
questions.rationale: The middle manager recruits and hires staff, holds staff meetings, helps staff meet unit goals, and monitors standards of practice.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q561 (PDF p. 763)

questions.stem: A staff nurse cannot meet client needs on time or prioritize care. What should the charge nurse do?
options: Ask others to do her work
Support her and find the cause
questions.rationale: Supporting the nurse and identifying the underlying cause helps reduce the problem. The other options are punitive or shift the burden to others.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q484 (PDF p. 675)

questions.stem: A preceptor watches a new nurse manage her time. Which action needs correcting?
questions.rationale: Documentation is done continuously during the day. Planning breaks, gathering supplies, and combining tasks are good time management.
explanations: Correct answer: chart as you go.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q485 (PDF p. 676)

questions.stem: Which item in the home puts a client recovering from hip surgery at risk for injury?
questions.rationale: Home injuries often come from tripping on doormats, small rugs, or clutter. Night-lights and raised seats with armrests reduce hazards.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q466 (PDF p. 649)

questions.stem: Which student statement on correcting a written chart error is CORRECT?
questions.rationale: Per agency policy, the nurse draws one line through the error, initials and dates it, then writes the correct information. Late entries are for omitted information.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1037 (PDF p. 1311)

questions.stem: The nurse finds a client on the floor beside the bed. How should the incident report describe it?
questions.rationale: An incident report gives a factual description of what the nurse observed. The nurse did not see a fall, so only the finding is recorded.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1038 (PDF p. 1312)

questions.stem: Coworkers resist a nurse's plan for a restraint-free unit. What helps her MOST as a change agent?
options: Ask the supervisor to enforce it
questions.rationale: Change is more likely when the nurse works with others to solve shared problems than when she demands change alone.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1402 (PDF p. 1707)

questions.stem: Which rehab client's needs can a nursing attendant MOST safely meet?
questions.rationale: Nursing attendants are trained to care for clients on bed rest and to maintain 24-hour urine collections, with instructions from the nurse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1449 (PDF p. 1758)

questions.stem: Which client should the nurse care for FIRST?
questions.rationale: Numb fingers under a new cast may mean compartment syndrome, an emergency. Nerve and muscle damage start within 4 to 6 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1539 (PDF p. 1850)

questions.stem: Which client can be delegated to a nursing attendant?
questions.rationale: Attendants are trained to collect specimens such as clean-catch urine. Teaching, dressing care, and assessment need a nurse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1549 (PDF p. 1862)

questions.stem: How are normal bowel sounds described?
questions.rationale: Normal bowel sounds are soft gurgles or clicks occurring irregularly 5 to 35 times a minute. Loud gurgles (borborygmi) mean hyperperistalsis; a swishing sound is a bruit.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q182 (PDF p. 335)

questions.stem: Which woman is at GREATEST risk for osteoporosis?
questions.rationale: Asian, white, small-boned, and fair-skinned women are at highest risk. Early menopause and a family history add to the risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q630 (PDF p. 847)

questions.stem: How should the nurse test for asterixis in hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.rationale: Asterixis (liver flap) is a rapid, nonrhythmic tremor of the wrists and fingers, seen when the client extends the arm, wrist, and fingers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q684 (PDF p. 905)

questions.stem: To test cranial nerve XII after a stroke, what does the nurse ask the client to do?
questions.rationale: Cranial nerve XII (hypoglossal) controls the tongue, so the nurse checks the ability to extend the tongue.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q685 (PDF p. 906)

questions.stem: Which finding is related to cranial nerve III (oculomotor) dysfunction?
questions.rationale: CN III controls pupil constriction and upper eyelid elevation; pressure on it causes ptosis. The others are early signs of a falling level of consciousness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1122 (PDF p. 1406)

questions.stem: To assess the limbic system in a client with dementia, what should the nurse assess?
questions.rationale: The limbic system governs feelings and emotions. Judgment is frontal lobe, consciousness is the reticular activating system, and eye movements are CN III, IV, and VI.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1003 (PDF p. 1254)

questions.stem: After shoulder arthroplasty, how does the nurse check the ULNAR nerve?
questions.rationale: Spreading the fingers wide against pressure tests the ulnar nerve. A grasp that tests the first and second fingers checks the median nerve.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q735 (PDF p. 960)

questions.stem: After shoulder arthroplasty, how does the nurse check the MEDIAN nerve?
questions.rationale: The client grasps the nurse's hand while the nurse notes the strength of the first and second fingers. A weak grip may mean median nerve compromise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1520 (PDF p. 1830)

questions.stem: A woman with a family history of hypertension is screened. Which finding needs teaching on stroke prevention?
questions.rationale: Oral contraceptives promote clot formation. They, along with obesity, hypertension, high cholesterol, and smoking, are modifiable stroke risk factors.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q688 (PDF p. 909)

questions.stem: Which is a NORMAL age-related concern when planning care for an older client?
questions.rationale: Older clients are at risk for dehydration, immobility complications, and loss of skin integrity. Incontinence, depression, and confusion are not normal aging.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q171 (PDF p. 324)

questions.stem: Which eye finding is a normal age-related change?
questions.rationale: Aging brings a flatter cornea (blurred vision), poor adaptation to darkness, yellowing sclera, fewer tears, and poorer color discrimination.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q612 (PDF p. 825)

questions.stem: Which factor increases an older adult's risk for hypothermia?
questions.rationale: Older adults' median oral temperature is about 36°C. Poor thermoregulation, anemia, alcohol, hypoglycemia, and burns raise hypothermia risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q620 (PDF p. 835)

questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis becomes WEAKER after an edrophonium (Tensilon) test dose. How is this interpreted?
questions.rationale: Worsening weakness after edrophonium means cholinergic crisis from overmedication. Improvement would mean myasthenic crisis.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q11 (PDF p. 149)

questions.stem: What is MOST important to assess before advancing a client from liquid to solid food?
questions.rationale: Chewing ability is assessed for safety; a soft or mechanically chopped diet may be needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q36 (PDF p. 175)

questions.stem: Which CSF finding is normally NEGATIVE in an adult?
questions.rationale: Normal CSF has no red blood cells. Protein and glucose are normally present, and a few WBCs may be seen.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q77 (PDF p. 222)

questions.stem: Which meal BEST promotes wound healing in a burn client?
questions.rationale: Wound healing needs protein (chicken, milk) and vitamin C (broccoli, strawberries).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q78 (PDF p. 223)

questions.stem: A client has a poor swallowing reflex. Which food should be removed from the diet?
questions.rationale: Raw, chunky, and stringy vegetables such as spinach, corn, and peas are excluded when swallowing is poor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q80 (PDF p. 225)

questions.stem: How should the client be positioned after a bedside liver biopsy?
questions.rationale: The client lies on the right side with a small pillow under the puncture site for about 2 hours to compress the liver and prevent bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q98 (PDF p. 246)

questions.stem: What is MOST important to assess before a liver biopsy?
questions.rationale: The client must lie still and hold the breath during needle insertion to avoid puncturing the lung or other organs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q230 (PDF p. 385)

questions.stem: Which medication is likely prescribed before an MRI for a client with a suspected brain tumor?
questions.rationale: The client must lie still in an enclosed scanner, so relaxation techniques or a sedative may be used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q124 (PDF p. 274)

questions.stem: An older client with type 1 diabetes has gastroenteritis. How should the nurse prevent dehydration?
questions.rationale: Dehydration risks DKA. Small amounts of fluid are tolerated even with vomiting and are offered frequently.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q129 (PDF p. 279)

questions.stem: Which condition LOWERS the risk of aspiration during enteral feeding?
questions.rationale: Sedation, coughing, artificial airways, suctioning, and decreased LOC raise aspiration risk. Head elevation reduces it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q148 (PDF p. 298)

questions.stem: Which GI study should be scheduled LAST?
questions.rationale: Barium may take up to 72 hours to clear and can obscure other tests, so it is done last.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q229 (PDF p. 384)

questions.stem: Which order does the nurse expect after an upper GI series?
questions.rationale: Barium is constipating and can cause obstruction, so laxatives are given routinely.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q316 (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: Which food should a client on a low-sodium diet avoid?
questions.rationale: High-sodium foods include table salt, cheeses, soy sauce, cured pork such as ham, canned foods, and cold cuts.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q272 (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY after arthroscopy?
questions.rationale: After arthroscopy, the priority is monitoring the affected area for numbness or tingling (neurovascular status).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q352 (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: Which drink should a client with a colostomy take regularly to help prevent odor?
questions.rationale: Parsley, yogurt, buttermilk, and cranberry juice help prevent colostomy odor.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q398 (PDF p. 568)

questions.stem: While bathing a client, the nurse gets an emergency phone call. What should she do?
questions.rationale: For privacy and safety, the nurse covers the client and places the call light within reach before leaving.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q404 (PDF p. 577)

questions.stem: Which finding in an older client calls for a fall-prevention protocol?
questions.rationale: Aging changes such as limited range of motion, decreased peripheral vision, and slowed nerve conduction increase accident risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q407 (PDF p. 581)

questions.stem: A home care client recovering from a mild stroke lives alone. Which assessment checks safety risk?
questions.rationale: Safety assessment includes visual acuity, gait and posture, and muscle strength because changes raise fall risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q438 (PDF p. 617)

questions.stem: How does the nurse reduce infection risk in a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: Concentrated glucose supports bacterial growth, so aseptic technique for dressing, tubing, and bag changes reduces infection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q467 (PDF p. 651)

questions.stem: A client with partial left leg hemiplegia needs more support than a straight cane. Which device fits?
questions.rationale: A tripod or quad cane gives multiple points of support for partial or complete hemiplegia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q523 (PDF p. 719)

questions.stem: How is a client moved from stretcher to bed after spinal fusion?
questions.rationale: A transfer board and four people give optimal stabilization of the spine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q528 (PDF p. 726)

questions.stem: An older client is 4 days post-ORIF for hip fracture. Which measure keeps her safe?
options: Ask her to call before getting up
questions.rationale: Age, surgery, and opioids raise fall risk, so she calls for help before getting up.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q572 (PDF p. 777)

questions.stem: A client on partial weight-bearing uses crutches. How much weight may go on the affected leg?
questions.rationale: Partial weight-bearing allows 30% to 50% of body weight on the affected limb. Touchdown allows contact without weight.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q604 (PDF p. 815)

questions.stem: Which device BEST improves bed mobility for a client in skeletal leg traction?
questions.rationale: An overhead trapeze helps the client move in bed and on and off the bedpan.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q605 (PDF p. 816)

questions.stem: How should an older client with Parkinson's tremors instill eye drops?
options: Lie down on a bed to instill
questions.rationale: Tremors make instillation hard; lying down gives stability and helps the drops reach the eye.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q608 (PDF p. 820)

questions.stem: A newly diagnosed diabetic should report glucose that is consistently above which level?
questions.rationale: Normal glucose is 70–110 mg/dL; clients report levels consistently above 250 mg/dL unless the provider says otherwise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q716 (PDF p. 938)

questions.stem: Which menu fits a low-fat diet?
questions.rationale: Skinless turkey, boiled rice, and strawberries are low in fat. Avocado, mayonnaise, butter, and red meat add fat.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q743 (PDF p. 971)

questions.stem: Which home instruction after knee arthroscopy is correct?
questions.rationale: Signs of infection are reported; strenuous exercise is avoided for a few days, but walking is usually allowed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q773 (PDF p. 1003)

questions.stem: Which drink is safe for a client with hiatal hernia?
questions.rationale: Tomato and citrus products irritate, and caffeine increases gastric acid. Apple juice is safe.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q782 (PDF p. 1012)

questions.stem: An older client with a hip fracture has periods of confusion. Which outcome MOST improves cognition?
questions.rationale: Being able to concentrate and take part in care lets the nurse work toward other outcomes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q899 (PDF p. 1142)

questions.stem: A client on TPN fears lipids will make her obese. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: The comment needs more than information at first; the nurse explores how illness affects self-concept.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q905 (PDF p. 1148)

questions.stem: A daughter feels guilty that her grieving father developed DKA despite her care. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Environment, infection, or emotional stress such as grief can trigger DKA, which eases misplaced guilt.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q914 (PDF p. 1157)

questions.stem: Why does a client on PERMANENT TPN need psychosocial support?
options: He will no longer eat orally
questions.rationale: Permanent TPN is for clients who can no longer absorb enteral nutrients, so they lose the experience of eating.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q952 (PDF p. 1197)

questions.stem: A client going home with a new colostomy says, 'I don't know how I'll do it alone.' What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The client expresses fear and helplessness; arranging home care support meets this need.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q953 (PDF p. 1198)

questions.stem: Before parathyroidectomy a client says, 'I'll have to wear a scarf after this.' Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: The statement reflects concern about appearance after surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q958 (PDF p. 1205)

questions.stem: A client treated for thyroid storm is still anxious and labile at discharge. What is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Anxiety and lability are normal after thyroid storm; the nurse helps the client cope with these changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q960 (PDF p. 1207)

questions.stem: Before discharge after HHS, a client voices worry about managing diabetes. What should the new nurse do?
