options: Suggest she move in with family
questions.rationale: Provide time, listen to concerns, and clarify feelings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1033 (PDF p. 1307)

questions.stem: How should staff speak to a hearing-impaired client?
questions.rationale: Face the client and speak clearly in a normal tone; do not shout.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1035 (PDF p. 1309)

questions.stem: After hip repair, a client keeps refusing to walk. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: An open-ended question explores factors behind the refusal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1044 (PDF p. 1318)

questions.stem: A post-op client has religious food requirements. What shows cultural consideration?
options: Ask about and honor food customs
Tell family to stop bringing food
questions.rationale: Spiritual and cultural consideration means learning and maintaining the client's familiar customs to support healing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1048 (PDF p. 1322)

questions.stem: A client speaks only a dialect the nurse doesn't know, and no interpreter is free. What is BEST before a dressing change?
questions.rationale: The ideal is a dialect-specific interpreter designated by the agency; family should not interpret medical information.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1051 (PDF p. 1327)

questions.stem: Which food should be AVOIDED for a client on a kosher diet?
questions.rationale: Kosher diets avoid pork, meat of carnivores, and fish without scales or fins.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1055 (PDF p. 1333)

questions.stem: A Muslim woman is stabilized after an assault. Which assignment is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Gender roles influence care; many Muslim women should be cared for by a female nurse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1059 (PDF p. 1339)

questions.stem: Besides food and illness beliefs, what else should the nurse consider in nutrition care across cultures?
questions.rationale: Dietary preferences, food beliefs, and cultural perception of body size must be considered.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1061 (PDF p. 1341)

questions.stem: Which measure relieves itching under a plaster cast?
options: Push a stick in with help
Blow cool air with a hair dryer
questions.rationale: Nothing is put inside a cast, and water weakens plaster. Cool air from a hair dryer can relieve itching.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1075 (PDF p. 1357)

questions.stem: An older resident returns after several GI tests. Which assessment is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: GI tests need bowel prep and NPO status, so older adults risk dehydration and poor nutrition.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1100 (PDF p. 1384)

questions.stem: Which care is correct after a bone biopsy?
questions.rationale: The site is monitored for swelling, bleeding, or hematoma; VS every 4 hours for 24 hours; the site is elevated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1199 (PDF p. 1491)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before an arthrogram with contrast?
questions.rationale: Because of contrast allergy risk, the nurse first assesses allergy to iodine or shellfish.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1200 (PDF p. 1492)

questions.stem: A head-injured client keeps pulling his feeding tube. Which restraint is BEST?
questions.rationale: Mittens prevent pulling without resistance, which could raise ICP. Wrist restraints cause resistance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1284 (PDF p. 1585)

questions.stem: A family says their father started wandering at night and got out once. What should the nurse say FIRST?
options: 'Tell me more about when this began.'
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses and collects data about the behavior change.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1288 (PDF p. 1589)

questions.stem: Which belongs in seizure precautions?
questions.rationale: Suction is ready for secretions, and the client is accompanied during activities. Nothing goes in the mouth.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1291 (PDF p. 1592)

questions.stem: Why are lipids given to a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: Fat emulsions prevent essential fatty acid deficiency and help meet caloric needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1309 (PDF p. 1611)

questions.stem: Which statement about TENS shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I must stay in hospital to use it.'
questions.rationale: TENS is portable and client-controlled; hospitalization is not required.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1352 (PDF p. 1655)

questions.stem: After EGD and vital signs, what is the nurse's next priority?
questions.rationale: The return of the gag reflex is checked first to protect the airway. Sharp pain may signal perforation and is also monitored.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1398 (PDF p. 1702)

questions.stem: Which pre-test action shows a client understands barium swallow instructions?
questions.rationale: The client removes metal objects and is usually NPO before the radiograph.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1400 (PDF p. 1704)

questions.stem: After hip prosthesis surgery, which attendant action needs intervention?
options: Seating her on a low commode
questions.rationale: The client must not flex the hip beyond 90 degrees; a low commode does this. The seat should be raised.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1435 (PDF p. 1744)

questions.stem: Which breakfast item INCREASES lower esophageal sphincter pressure in GERD?
questions.rationale: Nonfat milk increases LES pressure; coffee, chocolate, and fats decrease it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1457 (PDF p. 1766)

questions.stem: Low serum transferrin and low TIBC suggest which cause of anemia?
questions.rationale: Malnutrition lowers transferrin and TIBC. Iron deficiency usually raises TIBC.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1499 (PDF p. 1808)

questions.stem: Which statement about ERCP needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: IV sedation (not oral) is given, with an anesthetic throat spray to prevent gagging.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1503 (PDF p. 1812)

questions.stem: What must be done FIRST before a leg fracture is reduced in the casting room?
questions.rationale: Informed consent for treatment is obtained before reduction, with explanations reinforced.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1534 (PDF p. 1845)

questions.stem: Which item is allowed on a clear liquid diet?
questions.rationale: Clear liquids are transparent and liquid at body temperature: water, tea, broth, and gelatin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1546 (PDF p. 1858)

questions.stem: Which finding signals a complication of crutch walking?
questions.rationale: Forearm weakness signals radial nerve injury from crutch pressure on the axillae.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q10 (PDF p. 148)

questions.stem: What is the MOST accurate way to assess a weight loss program?
questions.rationale: Weighing the client at the same time, in the same clothes, on the same scale is most accurate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q38 (PDF p. 177)

questions.stem: Which pain description suggests a fracture after a fall?
questions.rationale: Fracture pain is sharp, continuous, and increasing. Bone pain is a dull, deep ache; muscle injury is cramping.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q39 (PDF p. 178)

questions.stem: A client on TPN has a finger-stick glucose of 425 mg/dL. What should the nurse do?
options: Slow the rate on her own
questions.rationale: Hyperglycemia is a TPN complication; abnormalities are reported to the provider.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q41 (PDF p. 180)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a nasointestinal tube is in the intestine?
questions.rationale: Gastric fluid is acidic; intestinal fluid is alkaline, so an alkaline aspirate confirms intestinal placement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q63 (PDF p. 208)

questions.stem: An NG tube stops draining. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Placement is verified first, then irrigation if prescribed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q142 (PDF p. 292)

questions.stem: A client on TPN via CVC needs an IV antibiotic. What should the nurse do?
options: Give it through the TPN line
Mix it in the TPN bag
questions.rationale: The TPN line is used only for TPN to prevent crystallization and interruption; other drugs go through a separate line.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q146 (PDF p. 296)

questions.stem: Which action is safe before a bolus NG feeding?
questions.rationale: After initial x-ray confirmation, placement is verified (tube length, aspirate) and residual checked before each feeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q152 (PDF p. 302)

questions.stem: While advancing an NG tube, the client gags. What should the nurse check?
options: Inspect the back of the throat
questions.rationale: Gagging may mean the tube coiled in the oropharynx; the nurse inspects the throat.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q153 (PDF p. 303)

questions.stem: A client develops spastic contractions during ROM exercises. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Movement is stopped at the point of spasm and gentle firm pressure applied until the muscle relaxes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q176 (PDF p. 329)

questions.stem: In which position is a bolus NG feeding given?
questions.rationale: The HOB is raised 35 to 40 degrees to prevent aspiration since the tube bypasses the gag reflex.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q180 (PDF p. 333)

questions.stem: Which foot care instruction is correct for an older client?
questions.rationale: Inspect the feet daily, including soles and between toes. Avoid knee-highs and prolonged soaking.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q188 (PDF p. 341)

questions.stem: A client on TPN reports nausea, polydipsia, and polyuria. Which data should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: These symptoms fit hyperglycemia from the high glucose load of TPN.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q201 (PDF p. 355)

questions.stem: Halfway through a cleansing enema, the client reports cramping. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The flow is stopped for 30 seconds and restarted at a slower rate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q256 (PDF p. 413)

questions.stem: Why is gastric residual checked before tube feeding?
questions.rationale: Residual shows whether the stomach empties; a large residual raises aspiration risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q262 (PDF p. 419)

questions.stem: The nurse aspirates 40 mL of formula before a feeding. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Residual contents are returned to the stomach to prevent electrolyte loss, and the feeding proceeds per policy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q274 (PDF p. 431)

questions.stem: Before teaching cane walking, what is the priority to check?
questions.rationale: Balance, strength, and confidence determine whether a cane is suitable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q284 (PDF p. 442)

questions.stem: After vomiting has stopped for 4 hours, what should the nurse offer first?
questions.rationale: Clear liquids are tolerated first, in sips of 20 to 30 mL, such as water or flat ginger ale.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q315 (PDF p. 479)

questions.stem: What does the client do as an NG tube is removed?
options: Take a deep breath and hold
questions.rationale: Breath-holding minimizes aspiration of gastric contents spilling from the tube.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q317 (PDF p. 481)

questions.stem: What should the nurse check before hanging an intralipid infusion?
questions.rationale: Separation or an oily appearance may mean spoiled or contaminated emulsion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q318 (PDF p. 482)

questions.stem: What should the nurse do FIRST when developing a diabetes teaching program?
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses clients and their needs to plan effectively.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q445 (PDF p. 625)

questions.stem: How does the nurse BEST ensure safe self-medication at home?
options: Have the client explain and demonstrate
questions.rationale: Asking the client to explain and demonstrate shows understanding and skill.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q469 (PDF p. 653)

questions.stem: Which observation shows crutches are fitted correctly?
questions.rationale: The elbow is flexed about 30 degrees on the handgrip, and the crutch top is two to three finger-widths below the axilla.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q511 (PDF p. 706)

questions.stem: Which shows correct walker use?
options: Slides it while leaning on it
Sets all four legs down, then steps
questions.rationale: The client places all four points of the walker flat about 2 feet forward before putting weight on it and stepping.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q520 (PDF p. 715)

questions.stem: An NPH insulin vial has clumps. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: NPH is uniformly cloudy; clumping or frosting means loss of potency, so a new vial is used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q546 (PDF p. 747)

questions.stem: Which catheter care direction should be given to a nursing attendant?
options: Clean the perineum with soap and water
Lift the bag above the bladder
questions.rationale: The perineal area is cleansed with mild soap and water at least three times a day and after bowel movements.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q552 (PDF p. 753)

questions.stem: A client with right-sided weakness transfers to a wheelchair. Where is the chair placed?
questions.rationale: Movement is toward the unaffected (left) side so the client can use the strong leg.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q593 (PDF p. 801)

questions.stem: A client with hypoparathyroidism has hyperphosphatemia. Which food should be avoided?
questions.rationale: High-phosphate foods include fish, eggs, milk products, whole grains, and carbonated beverages.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q623 (PDF p. 839)

questions.stem: A client weighed 75 kg on admission. Which weight shows adequate nutrition?
questions.rationale: Adequate nutrition means keeping baseline weight or losing less than about 2 kg (5 lb).
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q659 (PDF p. 878)

questions.stem: Where are crutches placed in the tripod standing position?
questions.rationale: In the tripod position, crutches are 6 to 10 inches in front of and to the side of the toes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q674 (PDF p. 894)

questions.stem: How much larger than the stoma is the colostomy appliance opening cut?
questions.rationale: 1/8 inch larger minimizes exposed skin without pressing on the stoma.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q792 (PDF p. 1022)

questions.stem: A client is confused from long bed rest and may now walk as tolerated. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The confusion comes from bed rest and low stimulation; walking in the hall increases sensory input.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q881 (PDF p. 1121)

questions.stem: A new diabetic is anxious about self-injecting insulin. What is a good FIRST step?
questions.rationale: The nurse may select the site and insert the needle, with the client pushing the plunger as a first step to self-injection.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q967 (PDF p. 1215)

questions.stem: When should crutch walking be taught for knee surgery?
questions.rationale: Crutch walking is taught before surgery because learning is hard when in pain and not fully alert.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1074 (PDF p. 1356)

questions.stem: What is the focus when assessing an older client's functional status?
questions.rationale: Functional status is the ability to perform ADLs: bathing, toileting, ambulating, dressing, and feeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1112 (PDF p. 1396)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY problem for a client in Buck's traction?
questions.rationale: Immobility poses the greatest risk of complications. Buck's is skin traction, so infection risk is low.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1124 (PDF p. 1408)

questions.stem: How is infection risk reduced for TPN via a central line?
options: Use the line for blood draws
questions.rationale: CVCs are a direct entry to the heart and circulation, so sterile technique is vital for dressing changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1143 (PDF p. 1429)

questions.stem: How does a client in a lower-extremity spica cast use the bedpan?
questions.rationale: The client cannot bend at the hips, so a low-profile fracture pan is used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1144 (PDF p. 1431)

questions.stem: Which intervention limits complications of prolonged bed rest?
questions.rationale: Immobility promotes calcium stones; limiting milk products helps prevent them. Supine positioning raises risks.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1149 (PDF p. 1436)

questions.stem: A stroke client has ROM ordered for the right side. What should the home nurse plan?
questions.rationale: All forms of ROM are considered; the client can assist in his own care, promoting independence.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1175 (PDF p. 1464)

questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before giving an NG tube feeding?
questions.rationale: NG tubes can migrate; placement is verified before anything is instilled.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1182 (PDF p. 1472)

questions.stem: After hip fixation, a client's left heel is red. Which equipment helps?
questions.rationale: The redness comes from pressure against the mattress; an alternating pressure mattress minimizes pressure points.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1186 (PDF p. 1477)

questions.stem: A client starts seizing in bed. How is aspiration prevented?
options: Turn on side, head flexed forward
questions.rationale: Side-lying with the head flexed lets the tongue fall forward and secretions drain.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1197 (PDF p. 1489)

questions.stem: Which item is essential for moving a client in leg traction?
questions.rationale: A trapeze lets the client lift straight up without altering the traction pull.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1203 (PDF p. 1495)

questions.stem: Which lab result is MOST important to report for a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: The provider uses electrolyte values to formulate the TPN solution.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1207 (PDF p. 1499)

questions.stem: Which is the BEST indicator of nutritional status during enteral feeding?
questions.rationale: Prealbumin is the most important parameter for nutritional effectiveness; it reflects recent changes.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1235 (PDF p. 1528)

questions.stem: Which exercise BEST strengthens the lower back?
questions.rationale: Walking and swimming strengthen back muscles; twisting and pulling activities do not help.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1337 (PDF p. 1640)

questions.stem: Which crutch statement needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Only crutches measured for the client are used unless adjusted to fit.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1486 (PDF p. 1795)

questions.stem: Ibuprofen 0.4 g is ordered; tablets are 200 mg. How many tablets?
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1530 (PDF p. 1840)

questions.stem: Which plan prevents skin breakdown in a client with a pelvic fracture?
questions.rationale: Pressure injury prevention includes minimizing force and friction, regular repositioning, and keeping skin clean and dry.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q93 (PDF p. 241)

questions.stem: What should a client with very dry, irritated skin apply?
questions.rationale: Emollients treat dry, cracked, irritated skin. Muscle rubs are for aches; acetic acid is for wound irrigation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1179 (PDF p. 1469)

questions.stem: A nurse with 2–3 years' experience coordinates complex care and plans well. Which Benner stage is this?
questions.rationale: Competent nurses (2–3 years) show organization and planning and coordinate multiple complex care demands.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)

questions.stem: A nurse acts because 'it felt right,' without needing rules. Which Benner stage?
questions.rationale: Experts perform fluidly without rules or maxims, often acting on intuition.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)

questions.stem: A proficient nurse (3–5 years) is characterized by which?
questions.rationale: Proficient nurses perceive situations holistically, use maxims, and focus on long-term goals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Benner's Stages (PDF p. 6)

questions.stem: Which record type groups data by problem and includes a database, problem list, plan, and progress notes?
questions.rationale: The POMR has four components: database, problem list, initial plan, and progress notes (SOAPIE).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Documentation (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which documentation tool may be written in pencil for frequently changing care details?
questions.rationale: The Kardex is a concise, quickly updated organizer that may be written in pencil.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Kardex (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: Which entry is the BEST nurses' note?
questions.rationale: Accurate notes record facts and observations, not opinions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: When should nursing care be documented?
options: At the end of the shift
As soon as possible after care
questions.rationale: No recording is done before care; documenting is done as soon as possible after assessment or intervention.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 7)

questions.stem: How should a blank space in a nurses' note be handled?
options: Draw a line through it and sign
questions.rationale: Write on every line; if a blank appears, draw a line through it and sign.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: A client refuses a treatment. What should be documented?
questions.rationale: Care omitted because of refusal is recorded with what, why, and who was notified.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guidelines for Recording (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: Which practice is correct when receiving a telephone order?
options: Write it and read it back
questions.rationale: Only RNs receive telephone orders; they write the date, time, and complete order, read it back, and question unusual orders.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Telephone Orders (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the change-of-shift report (endorsement)?
questions.rationale: Endorsement gives a quick summary of needs and care for continuity; it is not merely reciting the Kardex.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Reporting (PDF p. 8)

questions.stem: An electric fan cools a febrile child. Which heat-loss process is this?
questions.rationale: Convection is dispersion of heat by air currents. Conduction needs contact; radiation needs no contact.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Heat Loss (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: When is body temperature normally LOWEST?
questions.rationale: Diurnal variation: lowest 4–6 am, highest 4–6 pm.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Body Temperature (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A fever stays above normal but swings more than 2°C within 24 hours. Which type?
questions.rationale: Remittent fever has wide fluctuations over 2°C, all above normal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Fever (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: A client just drank hot coffee. How long should the nurse wait before taking an oral temperature?
questions.rationale: Wait 30 minutes after hot or cold drinks, food, or smoking.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: For which client is an ORAL temperature contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Oral temps are avoided with oral lesions, dyspnea, cough, vomiting, NGT or ET tubes, seizures, young children, and confusion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 17)

questions.stem: Rectal temperature is contraindicated in which client?
questions.rationale: Rectal temps are avoided with rectal conditions, diarrhea, quadriplegia, and MI (vagal stimulation).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Assessing Temperature (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: Which is correct when giving a tepid sponge bath?
questions.rationale: TSB is done by patting to avoid friction; alcohol dries and irritates the skin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tepid Sponge Bath (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: A client's temperature is 102.2°F. What is it in Celsius?
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Temperature Conversion (PDF p. 18)

questions.stem: A client in DKA has rapid, deep, labored breathing. What is it called?
questions.rationale: Kussmaul's respirations are rapid, deep, and labored, seen in metabolic acidosis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Terms (PDF p. 20)

questions.stem: What is the correct sequence for examining the abdomen?
questions.rationale: Abdominal sequence: inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation, so palpation does not alter bowel sounds.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: When should a painful abdominal quadrant be palpated?
questions.rationale: The painful quadrant is palpated last; no palpation is done with liver or kidney tumors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: How should the client be positioned for an abdominal exam?
questions.rationale: Flexing the knees relaxes the abdominal muscles during the exam.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: Where does the nurse stand to palpate the thyroid?
options: At the foot of the bed
questions.rationale: The nurse stands behind the client to palpate the neck for lymph nodes or thyroid enlargement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)

questions.stem: During a bed bath, how are the eyes cleaned?
questions.rationale: Eyes are cleaned with water only, inner to outer canthus, using a separate mitt corner for each eye.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bed Bath (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: How are the arms and legs washed during a bed bath?
options: Long firm strokes, distal to proximal
questions.rationale: Long, firm strokes from distal to proximal promote venous return.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bed Bath (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: Non-blanchable redness of intact skin over the sacrum is which pressure injury stage?
questions.rationale: Stage I is non-blanchable erythema of intact skin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pressure Ulcer (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: A pressure ulcer with exposed muscle and bone is stage:
questions.rationale: Stage IV involves full-thickness loss with damage to muscle, bone, or supporting structures.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pressure Ulcer (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent pressure ulcers?
options: Keep head of bed at 30° or less
questions.rationale: Keeping the HOB at 30° or less reduces shear. Avoid massaging bony areas and powders; turn every 2 hours or more often.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Prevention of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: Which solution is AVOIDED when cleaning a pressure ulcer?
questions.rationale: Ulcers are cleansed gently with alcohol-free cleanser; hydrogen peroxide damages tissue.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Treatment of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: Which debridement uses enzyme agents such as collagenase?
questions.rationale: Chemical debridement uses collagenase; sharp uses a scalpel; autolytic uses moisture-retaining dressings.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Treatment of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)

questions.stem: Why does the nurse avoid massaging the site after insulin injection?
questions.rationale: Massaging an insulin site speeds absorption; sites are rotated to prevent tissue damage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Subcutaneous Injection (PDF p. 27)

questions.stem: When mixing regular and NPH insulin, which is drawn up FIRST?
questions.rationale: Air is injected into NPH, then regular, and regular insulin is always withdrawn first to avoid contaminating it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Mixing Insulins (PDF p. 29)

questions.stem: Which tube is used to control bleeding esophageal varices?
questions.rationale: The triple-lumen Sengstaken-Blakemore tube treats bleeding varices; Miller-Abbott decompresses the intestine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Enteral Tubes (PDF p. 42)

questions.stem: How is NG tube length measured?
questions.rationale: Measure from the tip of the nose to the earlobe to the xiphoid process.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Why is a water-soluble lubricant used for NG insertion?
questions.rationale: Water-soluble lubricant dissolves if it enters the lungs; oil-based lubricant can cause lipid pneumonia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Once the NG tube reaches the oropharynx, how should the client position the head?
questions.rationale: Tilting the head forward helps the tube pass into the esophagus rather than the trachea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Inserting an NG Tube (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: Which aspirate pH suggests gastric placement of a feeding tube?
questions.rationale: Gastric contents are usually pH 1 to 5.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tube Feeding (PDF p. 44)

questions.stem: After a gastrostomy feeding, how long should the client stay upright?
questions.rationale: The client remains sitting or slightly elevated right lateral for 30 minutes to reduce aspiration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gastrostomy (PDF p. 44)

questions.stem: How often are enteral feeding bag and tubing replaced?
questions.rationale: The bag and tubing are replaced every 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Enteral Feeding (PDF p. 43)

questions.stem: How should TPN be discontinued?
questions.rationale: TPN is tapered slowly to prevent hyperinsulinemia and rebound hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parenteral Nutrition (PDF p. 44)

questions.stem: Which stool finding suggests upper GI bleeding?
questions.rationale: Black, tarry stool suggests upper GI bleeding; normal adult stool is brown and formed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Characteristics of Feces (PDF p. 44)

questions.stem: How high is a HIGH cleansing enema container held?
questions.rationale: High enema: 12–18 inches with position changes; low enema: no higher than 12 inches.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Enema (PDF p. 45)

questions.stem: Which enema is given mainly to expel flatus?
questions.rationale: Carminative enemas (60–80 mL in adults) expel flatus; return-flow enemas also do.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Enema (PDF p. 45)

questions.stem: How far is a rectal tube inserted in an adult for an enema?
questions.rationale: Adults: Fr 22–32 inserted 3–4 inches; children 2–3 inches; infants 1–1.5 inches.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Rectal Tube (PDF p. 46)

questions.stem: Which ostomy has liquid output with enzymes that damage skin and cannot be regulated?
questions.rationale: Ileostomy drainage is liquid, unregulated, enzyme-rich, and needs continuous appliance wear.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bowel Ostomies (PDF p. 46)

questions.stem: Colostomy irrigation is appropriate for which ostomy?
questions.rationale: Irrigation is used only for sigmoid or descending colostomies, which produce formed stool and can be regulated.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Irrigation (PDF p. 47)

questions.stem: A new stoma looks dusky purple. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A healthy stoma is red and moist; pale or dusky bluish-purple indicates impaired circulation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stoma Assessment (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: Which advice helps a client with flatulence?
questions.rationale: Limit carbonated drinks, straws, and gum (swallowed air) and gas-forming foods.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Promoting Defecation (PDF p. 47)

questions.stem: During an enema the client reports cramps. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Lower the container or clamp the tube for 30 seconds, then restart slowly.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Enema (PDF p. 46)

questions.stem: When should an ostomy pouch be emptied?
questions.rationale: Empty the pouch when one-third full; an overly full bag can loosen the skin barrier.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: Which product should be avoided when cleaning peristomal skin?
questions.rationale: Deodorant or moisturizing soaps interfere with skin barrier adhesives.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: When is the best time to change an ostomy appliance?
questions.rationale: Avoid times near meals, visiting hours, or after medications, which may stimulate evacuation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ostomy Care (PDF p. 48)

questions.stem: From which end is a stretcher pushed?
questions.rationale: Push from the head end to protect the client's head in a collision.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Safe Use of Stretcher (PDF p. 50)

questions.stem: How is the wheelchair placed for a client who has difficulty walking?
options: At a 45° angle to the bed
questions.rationale: A 45° angle lets the client pivot into the chair with less rotation; wheels are locked.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bed to Wheelchair Transfer (PDF p. 51)

questions.stem: Before a CT scan with contrast, which lab results should be checked?
questions.rationale: Kidney function (BUN, creatinine) is checked because contrast is excreted by the kidneys.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 55)

questions.stem: After a contrast CT, what should the client do?
questions.rationale: Increased fluids help eliminate the contrast medium; watch for delayed allergic reactions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 55)

questions.stem: For which client is an MRI contraindicated?
options: Client with a cast of plaster
questions.rationale: MRI is contraindicated with metal in the body and pacemakers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MRI (PDF p. 56)

questions.stem: What should the client expect during an MRI?
questions.rationale: MRI is painless but noisy, with loud banging; the client must stay still.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MRI (PDF p. 56)

questions.stem: After a PET scan, what should the client do with urine?
questions.rationale: Flush immediately after each voiding; increase fluids for 24–48 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, PET Scan (PDF p. 56)

questions.stem: How should a client prepare hair for an EEG?
options: Wash it; no sprays or creams
questions.rationale: Hair should be clean, without sprays, creams, or oils, which impair electrode contact.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)

questions.stem: How long before an EEG should caffeine be avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid caffeine-containing beverages for 8 hours before the EEG.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)

questions.stem: A client fears the EEG will shock him. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: The EEG records brain activity and does not cause electric shock.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 57)

questions.stem: How is a client positioned for lumbar puncture?
questions.rationale: The C-shaped, fetal, or knee-chest position widens the space between lumbar vertebrae (L3–L4 or L4–L5).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)

questions.stem: Which CSF finding suggests bacterial meningitis?
questions.rationale: Bacterial and TB meningitis decrease CSF glucose and increase protein and lactic acid.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)

questions.stem: When is lumbar puncture contraindicated?
questions.rationale: LP is contraindicated with infection at the site and coagulation defects, and used cautiously with increased ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)

questions.stem: After a lumbar puncture, what helps replace lost CSF?
questions.rationale: If permitted, fluids are given to replace lost CSF; the site is watched for leakage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lumbar Puncture (PDF p. 58)

questions.stem: What sensation should a client expect during EMG needle insertion?
questions.rationale: Clients feel a sensation like an intramuscular injection as the needle enters the muscle.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EMG (PDF p. 60)

questions.stem: Which is a contraindication to EMG?
questions.rationale: EMG is contraindicated with extensive skin infection, anticoagulant therapy, and infection at electrode sites.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EMG (PDF p. 60)

questions.stem: After a barium swallow, what stool change should the client expect for 2–3 days?
questions.rationale: Stools are white or light for 2–3 days; report if they do not return to normal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Barium Swallow (PDF p. 65)

questions.stem: What diet is given 2 days before a barium enema?
questions.rationale: Low-residue and clear-liquid diets 2 days before, NPO 8 hours, plus laxatives.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Barium Enema (PDF p. 65)

questions.stem: How is the client positioned for colonoscopy?
questions.rationale: Colonoscopy uses the Sims' (left lateral, knees flexed) position.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)

questions.stem: Why does the nurse ask about oral iron the week before colonoscopy?
questions.rationale: Oral iron within a week causes black, sticky stool that impairs visualization.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)

questions.stem: After colonoscopy, which sign suggests perforation?
questions.rationale: Belching and flatus are from air insufflation; pain, distention, bleeding, or fever suggest perforation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colonoscopy (PDF p. 66)

questions.stem: How many stool specimens are taken for a guaiac (occult blood) test?
questions.rationale: Three specimens on consecutive days are taken.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fecalysis (PDF p. 67)

questions.stem: How should a stool specimen for ova and parasites be handled?
questions.rationale: O&P specimens are sent immediately, fresh and warm, often to detect amoebiasis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stool Exam (PDF p. 67)

questions.stem: Which instruction applies to a 72-hour stool fat collection?
questions.rationale: Fats are included in the diet; alcohol and mineral oil are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stool for Lipids (PDF p. 67)

questions.stem: How is the client positioned for proctosigmoidoscopy?
questions.rationale: Left lateral decubitus or knee-chest position is used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Proctosigmoidoscopy (PDF p. 66)

questions.stem: After a radioactive iodine uptake test, what should the client do?
questions.rationale: Flush immediately after each voiding, wash hands well, and increase fluids for 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Radioactive Iodine Uptake (PDF p. 70)

questions.stem: Which drug may DECREASE radioactive iodine uptake results?
questions.rationale: Lugol's solution, SSKI, antithyroid drugs, and antihistamines may decrease results; lithium, estrogen, and barbiturates may raise them.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Radioactive Iodine Uptake (PDF p. 70)

questions.stem: A high TSH with low thyroid hormone suggests:
questions.rationale: TSH increases in primary and congenital hypothyroidism; it decreases in Graves' and excess replacement.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, TSH Assay (PDF p. 71)

questions.stem: Before a 24-hour urine VMA test, which food should be avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid amine-rich foods (bananas, avocados, chocolate, coffee) and vanilla for 48 hours; VMA tests for pheochromocytoma.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 71)

questions.stem: The VMA test helps diagnose which condition?
questions.rationale: VMA, a metabolite of epinephrine, helps diagnose pheochromocytoma, neuroblastoma, and ganglioneuroma.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 71)

questions.stem: How should a client prepare for an OGTT?
options: Regular diet 3 days, then NPO 8–12 hours
questions.rationale: Eat a regular diet at least 3 days before, be NPO 8–12 hours, and avoid smoking.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, OGTT (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: Glycosylated hemoglobin reflects glucose control over about how long?
questions.rationale: HbA1c reflects blood glucose levels over up to 3 months.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glycosylated Hemoglobin (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: What is the normal fasting blood glucose range?
questions.rationale: Normal FBS is 70–110 mg/dL after 8–12 hours NPO.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Fasting Blood Glucose (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: What should the client do right before paracentesis?
questions.rationale: The client voids before paracentesis to avoid bladder puncture and sits upright.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Paracentesis (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: After paracentesis, which finding is a priority to watch?
questions.rationale: Watch for hypotension and hypovolemic shock from fluid shifts; measure girth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Paracentesis (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: During needle insertion for liver biopsy, the client should:
questions.rationale: After several deep breaths, the client exhales and holds at end-expiration while the needle is inserted.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 73)

questions.stem: Before a liver biopsy, what must be available?
questions.rationale: Coagulation tests and compatible donor blood are confirmed because of bleeding risk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 72)

questions.stem: After liver biopsy, which activity is avoided for one week?
questions.rationale: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for a week; avoid coughing and straining early.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Biopsy (PDF p. 73)

questions.stem: What is the normal serum albumin level?
questions.rationale: Normal serum albumin is 4.0–5.5 g/dL; total protein 7.0–7.5 g/dL.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Protein Studies (PDF p. 73)

questions.stem: After ERCP, when may the client eat?
questions.rationale: No food or drink until the gag reflex returns, then light meals for 12–24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ERCP (PDF p. 76)

questions.stem: Which ERCP aftereffect should be reported immediately?
questions.rationale: Severe pain, fever, difficulty breathing, or blood expectoration are reported; sore throat and belching are expected.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ERCP (PDF p. 76)

questions.stem: Which teaching is specific to phenytoin?
options: Good oral hygiene and dental visits
questions.rationale: Phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia, so oral hygiene and dental visits are stressed; it is not mixed with other IV fluids.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anticonvulsants (PDF p. 110)

questions.stem: Why is carbidopa combined with levodopa?
questions.rationale: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase so more levodopa reaches the brain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-Parkinson Agents (PDF p. 110)

questions.stem: Which drug should be at the bedside of a client on pyridostigmine for myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Atropine is kept available for cholinergic crisis from cholinesterase inhibitor overdose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors (PDF p. 111)

questions.stem: When is pyridostigmine best given for myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: It is given 30–60 minutes before meals so muscle strength peaks for chewing and swallowing, with some food for gastric upset.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors (PDF p. 111)

questions.stem: Which is a serious risk of COX-2 inhibitors like celecoxib?
questions.rationale: COX-2 inhibitors carry risks of MI and stroke, plus nephrotoxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, NSAIDs (PDF p. 116)

questions.stem: Which teaching applies to a client on allopurinol for gout?
questions.rationale: Increase fluids to prevent renal calculi; avoid high-purine foods and fermented drinks.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-Gout Agents (PDF p. 117)

questions.stem: Ondansetron belongs to which class of antiemetics?
questions.rationale: Ondansetron and granisetron are serotonin (5-HT3) antagonists.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antiemetics (PDF p. 117)

questions.stem: Which side effect is expected with aluminum hydroxide antacids?
questions.rationale: Aluminum compounds cause constipation; magnesium compounds cause diarrhea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antacids (PDF p. 118)

questions.stem: Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) as an antacid may cause:
questions.rationale: Magnesium compounds cause diarrhea; aluminum compounds cause constipation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antacids (PDF p. 118)

questions.stem: How should antacids be timed with sucralfate?
questions.rationale: Avoid antacids within 30 minutes of sucralfate; give sucralfate on an empty stomach.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-PUD Drugs (PDF p. 119)

questions.stem: Omeprazole belongs to which drug class?
questions.rationale: Omeprazole and lansoprazole are PPIs; cimetidine, ranitidine, and famotidine are H2 blockers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-PUD Drugs (PDF p. 118)

questions.stem: Antidiarrheals are contraindicated in which condition?
questions.rationale: Antidiarrheals are contraindicated in ulcerative colitis (risk of toxic megacolon).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antidiarrheals (PDF p. 120)

questions.stem: Long-term mineral oil use can reduce absorption of:
questions.rationale: Intestinal lubricants such as mineral oil inhibit absorption of vitamins A, D, E, and K.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laxatives (PDF p. 120)

questions.stem: Laxatives are contraindicated with which symptom?
questions.rationale: Laxatives are contraindicated with GI obstruction, suspected appendicitis, and undiagnosed abdominal pain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Laxatives (PDF p. 120)

questions.stem: A client on thyroid replacement should report which pulse?
questions.rationale: Report a pulse over 100 and toxicity signs such as chest pain, palpitations, and nervousness.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Thyroid Agents (PDF p. 133)

questions.stem: A client on an antithyroid drug should avoid OTC products containing:
questions.rationale: Antithyroid therapy clients avoid OTC drugs containing iodine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-hyperthyroid Agents (PDF p. 133)

questions.stem: How is response to ADH (vasopressin) therapy for diabetes insipidus monitored?
questions.rationale: ADH helps reabsorb water; I&O and BP show response.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ADH (PDF p. 134)

questions.stem: Which food should a client with a colostomy limit to reduce gas?
questions.rationale: Avoid gas-forming foods: cabbage, cauliflower, nuts, carbonated drinks, gum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Diet (PDF p. 295)

questions.stem: Which substance secreted by the stomach is needed to absorb vitamin B12?
questions.rationale: Intrinsic factor from the gastric mucosa combines with dietary B12.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gastric Function (PDF p. 337)

questions.stem: Which enzyme begins starch digestion in the mouth?
questions.rationale: Salivary amylase starts starch digestion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chewing and Swallowing (PDF p. 337)

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the colon?
questions.rationale: Slow peristalsis allows water and electrolyte reabsorption.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Colonic Function (PDF p. 338)

questions.stem: During abdominal assessment, which technique is performed right after inspection?
questions.rationale: Order: inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation, to avoid altering bowel sounds.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GI Physical Examination (PDF p. 338)

questions.stem: The appendix is located in which abdominal region?
questions.rationale: Right inguinal contains the cecum, appendix, and lower ileum.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abdominal Regions (PDF p. 339)

questions.stem: Before an upper GI series, the nurse advises the client to avoid:
questions.rationale: Smoking, gum, and mints stimulate gastric motility; client is NPO from midnight.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Upper GI Series (PDF p. 339)

questions.stem: After a barium enema, the nurse should instruct the client to:
questions.rationale: Increase fluids and give laxative to evacuate barium; monitor bowel movements.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lower GI Series (PDF p. 339)

questions.stem: What is the priority nursing assessment after an EGD with sedation?
questions.rationale: Withhold food and fluids until the gag reflex returns; monitor LOC, vitals, and SpO2.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)

questions.stem: Which position is used during EGD?
questions.rationale: Left lateral position facilitates clearance of secretions and smooth scope entry.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)

questions.stem: After EGD, which finding suggests perforation?
questions.rationale: Report pain, bleeding, unusual difficulty swallowing, and rapidly rising temperature.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EGD (PDF p. 340)

questions.stem: GERD is primarily caused by:
questions.rationale: Backflow of gastric contents occurs through an incompetent LES.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GERD (PDF p. 341)

questions.stem: Which instruction helps a client with GERD?
questions.rationale: Elevate the bed, avoid eating 2 hours before bed, avoid tight clothing and lying after meals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Nursing Management (PDF p. 341)

questions.stem: Which drug class is more potent than H2 blockers for reducing gastric acid?
questions.rationale: PPIs (omeprazole) inhibit the parietal cell ATPase pump and are more potent.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Pharmacology (PDF p. 341)

questions.stem: Nissen fundoplication treats GERD by:
questions.rationale: A portion of the fundus is wrapped around the sphincter area.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GERD Surgery (PDF p. 341)

questions.stem: A client with hiatal hernia should be taught to:
options: Not recline for 1 hour after eating
questions.rationale: Small frequent feedings; do not recline 1 hour after eating; elevate head of bed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hiatal Hernia (PDF p. 342)

questions.stem: Epigastric pain 2–3 hours after meals relieved by eating suggests:
questions.rationale: Duodenal ulcer pain occurs 2–3 hours after meals and is relieved by food.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Duodenal vs Gastric Ulcer (PDF p. 342)

questions.stem: Which finding is more typical of gastric ulcer than duodenal ulcer?
questions.rationale: Gastric ulcer: pain after eating, vomiting, hematemesis, weight loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Duodenal vs Gastric Ulcer (PDF p. 343)

questions.stem: Which organism is a major cause of peptic ulcer and gastritis?
questions.rationale: H. pylori is treated with antibiotics (amoxicillin, clarithromycin) plus a PPI.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Peptic Ulcer Disease (PDF p. 343)

questions.stem: A client with gastritis develops hematemesis, tachycardia, and hypotension. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: These indicate hemorrhagic gastritis; notify the physician.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gastritis Nursing Management (PDF p. 343)

questions.stem: Severe peptic ulcers with extreme hyperacidity from a gastrin-secreting tumor is:
questions.rationale: Zollinger-Ellison: gastrinoma causing hyperacidity and severe ulcers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (PDF p. 343)

questions.stem: Sucralfate protects an ulcer by:
questions.rationale: Cytoprotectants form a viscous barrier that binds to the ulcer surface.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cytoprotectants (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: Billroth II surgery involves:
questions.rationale: Billroth II is gastrojejunostomy; Billroth I is gastroduodenostomy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, PUD Surgery (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: Thirty minutes after eating, a post-gastrectomy client has palpitations, sweating, and diarrhea. This is:
questions.rationale: Rapid gastric emptying causes dumping syndrome symptoms about 30 minutes after meals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dumping Syndrome (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent dumping syndrome?
questions.rationale: Take fluids 1 hour before or after meals, eat dry low-carbohydrate meals, and lie down after.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Dumping Syndrome (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: Diverticula most commonly occur in the:
questions.rationale: Diverticula occur most commonly in the sigmoid colon.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 344)

questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for diverticulosis without inflammation?
questions.rationale: High fiber for diverticulosis; low fiber may be needed during acute diverticulitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 345)

questions.stem: What is the diagnostic test of choice for diverticulitis?
questions.rationale: CT is the test of choice in diverticulitis and reveals abscesses.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diverticular Disease (PDF p. 345)

questions.stem: Transmural inflammation with a cobblestone appearance, mostly in the ileum, describes:
questions.rationale: Crohn's affects all layers, skip areas, fistulas, cobblestone mucosa.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Crohn's Disease (PDF p. 345)

questions.stem: Ten to 20 bloody liquid stools daily with LLQ cramping suggests:
questions.rationale: Ulcerative colitis involves mucosa of colon and rectum with bloody diarrhea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ulcerative Colitis (PDF p. 345)

questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for inflammatory bowel disease?
questions.rationale: Low residue, high protein, high calorie, with vitamins and iron.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IBD Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 346)

questions.stem: Which surgery for ulcerative colitis creates a continent internal ileal reservoir?
questions.rationale: Kock pouch is a continent ileal reservoir with a stoma.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, IBD Surgery (PDF p. 346)

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of appendicitis?
questions.rationale: The appendix is kinked or occluded by a fecalith, tumor, or foreign body.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: Pressing the LLQ causes pain in the RLQ. This is:
questions.rationale: Rovsing's sign suggests appendicitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: Pain that intensifies when pressure over the abdomen is released is called:
questions.rationale: Rebound tenderness indicates peritoneal irritation, as in appendicitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: A client with suspected appendicitis asks for a heating pad and laxative. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Heat and laxatives can promote perforation; prepare for appendectomy as soon as possible.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: Why is a pregnancy test done for a woman with RLQ pain?
questions.rationale: Ectopic pregnancy can mimic appendicitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis Diagnostics (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: After appendectomy, the client is placed in high-Fowler's position to:
questions.rationale: High-Fowler's reduces incisional and abdominal tension, easing pain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis Nursing (PDF p. 347)

questions.stem: Which teaching helps a client with hemorrhoids?
questions.rationale: High-residue diet, fluids, sitz baths, and avoiding straining.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhoids (PDF p. 348)

questions.stem: Bright red blood on toilet paper with anal itching most likely indicates:
questions.rationale: Hemorrhoids cause itching, pain, and bright red bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhoids (PDF p. 348)

questions.stem: The liver prevents ammonia toxicity by converting ammonia to:
questions.rationale: The liver converts ammonia to urea for renal excretion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatobiliary System (PDF p. 348)

questions.stem: Cirrhosis caused by chronic alcoholism and malnutrition is called:
questions.rationale: Laennec's: alcohol; biliary: bile duct disorders; post-hepatic: hepatitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Cirrhosis (PDF p. 349)

questions.stem: Dilated abdominal veins radiating from the umbilicus in cirrhosis are called:
questions.rationale: Caput medusae reflects portal hypertension.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Portal Hypertension (PDF p. 350)

questions.stem: Which daily assessment monitors ascites in portal hypertension?
questions.rationale: Measure and record abdominal girth and weight daily.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Portal Hypertension (PDF p. 350)

questions.stem: Esophageal varices are caused by:
questions.rationale: Portal hypertension dilates submucosal veins of the lower esophagus.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Esophageal Varices (PDF p. 350)

questions.stem: Which item must be at the bedside of a client with a Sengstaken-Blakemore tube?
questions.rationale: Scissors cut the tube to deflate balloons if respiratory distress occurs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Esophageal Varices (PDF p. 351)

questions.stem: Hand flapping when the arms are extended with wrists dorsiflexed in liver failure is called:
questions.rationale: Asterixis (liver flap) signals hepatic encephalopathy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Lactulose is given in hepatic encephalopathy to:
questions.rationale: Lactulose acidifies the colon, traps ammonia, and promotes its evacuation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Why is neomycin given in hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.rationale: Neomycin reduces colonic ammonia-forming bacteria.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Sweet, slightly fecal breath odor in liver failure is:
questions.rationale: Fetor hepaticus is a sign of hepatic encephalopathy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Sedatives for a client with cirrhosis should be given in conservative doses because:
questions.rationale: Impaired hepatic metabolism prolongs drug effects.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: Which is a risk factor for gallstones?
questions.rationale: Risks: obesity, female sex, multiple pregnancies, rapid weight loss, estrogen, diabetes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Disorders (PDF p. 352)

questions.stem: The client stops inhaling when the examiner presses below the right costal margin. This is:
questions.rationale: Murphy's sign indicates cholecystitis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholecystitis (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: Gallstone pain typically occurs in the RUQ and may radiate to the:
questions.rationale: Biliary colic radiates to the back near the right scapular tip.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholelithiasis (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: What is the diagnostic procedure of choice for gallstones?
questions.rationale: Ultrasound is the procedure of choice.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Diagnostics (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: Which diet should a client with cholelithiasis follow?
questions.rationale: Low-fat diet reduces gallbladder stimulation and colic.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Management (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to:
questions.rationale: UDCA dissolves small radiolucent gallstones.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Pharmacology (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: Using shock waves to fragment gallstones without incision is:
questions.rationale: ESWL is noninvasive fragmentation of stones.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Management (PDF p. 353)

questions.stem: The biliary drainage tube is clamped 1 hour before and after meals in order to:
questions.rationale: Clamping lets bile flow into the duodenum to aid fat digestion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Biliary Drainage (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Acute pancreatitis is self-digestion of the pancreas mainly by:
questions.rationale: Activated trypsin and other proteolytic enzymes digest the pancreas.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Bluish discoloration around the umbilicus in acute pancreatitis is:
questions.rationale: Cullen's: periumbilical; Grey Turner's: flank, indicating retroperitoneal bleeding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Which lab results support acute pancreatitis?
questions.rationale: Elevated amylase, lipase, and WBC; hypocalcemia may occur.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Why is a client with acute pancreatitis kept NPO?
questions.rationale: NPO inhibits pancreatic stimulation and enzyme secretion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Frothy, foul-smelling, fatty stools in chronic pancreatitis are called:
questions.rationale: Impaired fat digestion causes steatorrhea; give pancreatic enzymes with meals.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chronic Pancreatitis (PDF p. 354)

questions.stem: Chronic pancreatitis may lead to which endocrine complication?
questions.rationale: Islet cell damage causes diabetes; glucose tolerance becomes abnormal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Chronic Pancreatitis (PDF p. 355)

questions.stem: A client with a perforated ulcer has a rigid, board-like abdomen and rebound tenderness. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Peritonitis: rigidity, rebound tenderness, ileus, fever, tachycardia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Peritonitis (PDF p. 355)

questions.stem: Which position decreases pain in a client with peritonitis?
questions.rationale: Knees flexed decreases tension on abdominal organs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Peritonitis Nursing (PDF p. 356)

questions.stem: Which hormone is released by the posterior pituitary?
questions.rationale: Posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Posterior Pituitary (PDF p. 357)

questions.stem: Aldosterone acts on the kidney to:
questions.rationale: Mineralocorticoids increase sodium absorption and potassium loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenal Cortex (PDF p. 358)

questions.stem: Calcitonin from the thyroid gland:
questions.rationale: Calcitonin lowers calcium; parathormone raises it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Thyroid Gland (PDF p. 358)

questions.stem: Why is serum calcium monitored after thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Parathyroid glands may be removed or injured, causing hypocalcemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parathyroid Glands (PDF p. 358)

questions.stem: Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells:
questions.rationale: Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pancreatic Islet Cells (PDF p. 358)

questions.stem: Which hormone is produced by the kidney to stimulate RBC production?
questions.rationale: Erythropoietin increases RBC production; renin activates RAAS.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Kidney Hormones (PDF p. 359)

questions.stem: Gigantism results from excess growth hormone when:
questions.rationale: GH excess before epiphyseal closure causes gigantism; after closure, acromegaly.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gigantism (PDF p. 359)

questions.stem: A client with a GH-secreting pituitary tumor reports headache and diplopia. These are due to:
questions.rationale: Pituitary tumors press on the optic chiasm and raise ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Gigantism (PDF p. 359)

questions.stem: An adult with a protruding jaw, enlarged hands, and coarse features likely has:
questions.rationale: Acromegaly: GH excess after epiphyseal closure, causing bone and soft tissue enlargement without height gain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acromegaly (PDF p. 360)

questions.stem: After transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, clear nasal drainage should be tested for:
questions.rationale: Glucose in nasal drainage indicates CSF leak.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypophysectomy (PDF p. 360)

questions.stem: Which complication after hypophysectomy causes large volumes of dilute urine?
questions.rationale: Transient DI may follow pituitary surgery.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acromegaly Nursing Management (PDF p. 360)

questions.stem: After hypophysectomy, the client should avoid:
questions.rationale: Avoid activities that raise ICP; keep HOB elevated; deep breathing (not coughing) is taught.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypophysectomy (PDF p. 360)

questions.stem: Amenorrhea and galactorrhea in a nonpregnant woman suggest:
questions.rationale: Prolactin-secreting tumors cause amenorrhea and galactorrhea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperprolactinemia (PDF p. 361)

questions.stem: A client with lung cancer has low sodium, concentrated urine, and weight gain. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Bronchogenic carcinoma can cause SIADH with dilutional hyponatremia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, SIADH (PDF p. 361)

questions.stem: What is the key nursing intervention for SIADH?
questions.rationale: Restrict fluids; monitor weight, I&O, sodium, and neuro status.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, SIADH Management (PDF p. 362)

questions.stem: Which urine specific gravity is typical of diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: DI produces very dilute urine (SG 1.001–1.005).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetes Insipidus (PDF p. 362)

questions.stem: Which drug treats central diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: DDAVP is synthetic vasopressin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DI Management (PDF p. 362)

questions.stem: Which test differentiates central from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: Kidneys concentrate urine after ADH in central DI, not in nephrogenic DI.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DI Diagnostics (PDF p. 362)

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of endemic goiter?
questions.rationale: Endemic (simple) goiter results from iodine deficiency; prevented by iodized salt (RA 8172, ASIN Law).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Goiter (PDF p. 363)

questions.stem: Which finding is typical of Graves' disease?
questions.rationale: Hyperthyroidism: exophthalmos, heat intolerance, weight loss, tachycardia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism (PDF p. 363)

questions.stem: Lid lag when the client looks downward is called:
questions.rationale: von Graefe's: lid lag; Dalrymple's: upper lid retraction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism (PDF p. 363)

questions.stem: A client on propylthiouracil develops sore throat and fever. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Agranulocytosis is the most toxic effect; stop and get hematologic studies.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Antithyroid Medications (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: How should Lugol's solution be given?
questions.rationale: Mix in milk or juice and use a straw to prevent teeth staining.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Adjunctive Therapy (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: Why is iodine (Lugol's) given before thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Iodine decreases hormone release and thyroid vascularity, reducing blood loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Thyroidectomy (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: Which finding indicates iodism?
questions.rationale: Iodism: buccal swelling, salivation, coryza, skin eruptions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Iodism (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: Which environment suits a client with hyperthyroidism?
questions.rationale: Keep the room cool, quiet, uncluttered; use calm approach.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 365)

questions.stem: Which diet suits a client with hyperthyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hypermetabolism requires high calories and protein; avoid stimulants and spices.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperthyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 364)

questions.stem: Cold intolerance, weight gain, bradycardia, and dry skin suggest:
questions.rationale: Hypothyroidism slows metabolism.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothyroidism (PDF p. 365)

questions.stem: Why are sedatives given cautiously to a client with hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Analgesics, sedatives, and anesthetics have prolonged effects; risk of myxedema coma.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothyroidism Management (PDF p. 365)

questions.stem: When starting levothyroxine in an older client with CAD, the nurse monitors for:
questions.rationale: Thyroid replacement increases oxygen demand; watch for angina and dysrhythmias.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothyroidism Management (PDF p. 365)

questions.stem: Hyperparathyroidism commonly causes:
questions.rationale: Excess PTH causes hypercalcemia, renal calculi, bone pain, fractures.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperparathyroidism (PDF p. 366)

questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent renal calculi in hyperparathyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hydrate well, include cranberry juice, ambulate; thiazides are avoided (raise calcium).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperparathyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 367)

questions.stem: Tapping the facial nerve causes twitching of the lip after thyroidectomy. This is:
questions.rationale: Chvostek's sign indicates hypocalcemia; Trousseau's is carpopedal spasm with a BP cuff.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)

questions.stem: Which drug should be at the bedside after thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: IV calcium gluconate treats tetany from hypocalcemia; keep a tracheostomy set too.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 368)

questions.stem: Hypoparathyroidism produces which electrolyte pattern?
questions.rationale: PTH deficiency lowers calcium and raises phosphate.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)

questions.stem: Aluminum hydroxide gel is given in hypoparathyroidism to:
questions.rationale: Aluminum compounds bind phosphate for GI excretion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)

questions.stem: Paroxysmal hypertension, headache, sweating, and palpitations suggest:
questions.rationale: Pheochromocytoma secretes catecholamines: the 5 H's.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Pheochromocytoma (PDF p. 368)

questions.stem: Before a 24-hour urine VMA test, the client should avoid:
questions.rationale: Coffee, tea, bananas, chocolate, vanilla, and aspirin alter VMA results.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 368)

questions.stem: After adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma, the nurse watches for:
questions.rationale: Sudden catecholamine withdrawal can cause hypotension and hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenalectomy (PDF p. 369)

questions.stem: Bronze skin, hypotension, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia suggest:
questions.rationale: Adrenocortical insufficiency: hyperpigmentation, low Na, high K, low glucose.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Disease (PDF p. 369)

questions.stem: What is the immediate treatment for Addisonian crisis?
questions.rationale: IV hydrocortisone followed by D5NS; vasopressors if hypotension persists.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Management (PDF p. 369)

questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease has influenza. The steroid dose should be:
questions.rationale: Increase glucocorticoids during illness or stress to prevent crisis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Nursing Management (PDF p. 369)

questions.stem: Moon face, buffalo hump, and thin extremities suggest:
questions.rationale: Excess cortisol: central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, fragile skin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Disease (PDF p. 370)

questions.stem: Which lab finding is expected in Cushing's syndrome?
questions.rationale: Cortisol excess raises glucose and sodium and lowers potassium.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Diagnostics (PDF p. 370)

questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for Cushing's syndrome?
questions.rationale: High protein, calcium, vitamin D; low carbohydrate and sodium.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Nursing (PDF p. 371)

questions.stem: Which fasting plasma glucose meets the criterion for diabetes?
questions.rationale: FPG ≥126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) after 8 hours fasting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetes Criteria (PDF p. 371)

questions.stem: Type 1 diabetes results from:
questions.rationale: Autoimmune destruction of beta cells causes insulin deficiency and DKA risk.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Type 1 DM (PDF p. 371)

questions.stem: Polyuria in uncontrolled diabetes is caused by:
questions.rationale: Glucose above the renal threshold draws water into urine.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Type 1 DM (PDF p. 372)

questions.stem: Why is DKA uncommon in type 2 diabetes?
questions.rationale: Residual insulin prevents lipolysis and ketone formation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Type 2 DM (PDF p. 372)

questions.stem: Before moderate exercise, a client on insulin should:
questions.rationale: A 15-g carbohydrate snack prevents exercise hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DM Exercise (PDF p. 372)

questions.stem: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about:
questions.rationale: Glycated hemoglobin reflects 2–3 months of glucose control.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glycated Hemoglobin (PDF p. 372)

questions.stem: Which insulin is the only one approved for IV use?
questions.rationale: Regular (short-acting, clear) insulin is the only IV insulin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)

questions.stem: Which insulin has no peak and is used as a basal dose?
questions.rationale: Glargine is long-acting and peakless, lasting about 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)

questions.stem: A client gives regular insulin at 0700. Hypoglycemia is most likely around:
questions.rationale: Regular insulin peaks 2–3 hours after injection.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)

questions.stem: How can insulin lipodystrophy be prevented?
questions.rationale: Rotating sites prevents lipoatrophy and lipohypertrophy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Lipodystrophy (PDF p. 373)

questions.stem: Metformin lowers blood glucose mainly by:
questions.rationale: Biguanides inhibit hepatic glucose production and increase insulin sensitivity.
