questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Antidiabetic Agents (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: Which oral agent stimulates the pancreas to secrete insulin?
questions.rationale: Sulfonylureas (e.g., gliclazide) stimulate beta cells.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Antidiabetic Agents (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: Bedtime glucose normal, 3 AM hypoglycemia, then morning hyperglycemia. This is:
questions.rationale: Somogyi: nocturnal hypoglycemia triggers rebound hyperglycemia; reduce evening dose or add snack.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Morning Hyperglycemia (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: How is the dawn phenomenon managed?
questions.rationale: Change evening intermediate-acting insulin from dinnertime to bedtime.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Morning Hyperglycemia (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: How should the insulin vial currently in use be stored?
questions.rationale: In-use vial at room temperature; spares refrigerated; never frozen or in sunlight.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: How should a client prepare a cloudy insulin vial?
questions.rationale: Roll or gently invert to mix without bubbles; inspect for flocculation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: An NPH insulin vial shows a frosted, whitish coating inside. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Flocculation (frosted whitish coating) means the insulin is altered and should not be used.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Storing Insulin (PDF p. 374)

questions.stem: Insulin is absorbed fastest from which site?
questions.rationale: Absorption is fastest in the abdomen, then arm, thigh, hip.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Injection Sites (PDF p. 375)

questions.stem: A diabetic jogger asks where to inject insulin before running. The nurse advises avoiding:
questions.rationale: Exercising a limb speeds absorption, risking hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Injection Sites (PDF p. 375)

questions.stem: Shakiness, sweating, tachycardia, and hunger in a client on insulin indicate:
questions.rationale: Adrenergic symptoms signal mild hypoglycemia.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia (PDF p. 375)

questions.stem: A diabetic client is unconscious at home with no IV access. The family should give:
questions.rationale: Glucagon 1 mg SC or IM; never give oral fluids to an unconscious person.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia Emergency (PDF p. 376)

questions.stem: Why is IV line patency checked before giving 50% dextrose?
options: It is very irritating to veins
questions.rationale: D50W is hypertonic and irritating; infiltration damages tissue.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoglycemia Emergency (PDF p. 376)

questions.stem: Deep, rapid respirations with fruity breath in a type 1 diabetic indicate:
questions.rationale: Kussmaul breathing and acetone breath compensate for ketoacidosis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetic Ketoacidosis (PDF p. 376)

questions.stem: What is the first priority in DKA management?
questions.rationale: Start 0.9% NaCl rehydration; then insulin and potassium as needed.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Management (PDF p. 377)

questions.stem: During DKA treatment with insulin, the nurse closely monitors:
questions.rationale: Insulin and rehydration shift potassium into cells; replace once K is normal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Electrolytes (PDF p. 377)

questions.stem: Why is the first 50 mL of an insulin drip discarded through the tubing?
questions.rationale: Insulin binds to tubing; flushing saturates binding sites.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DKA Insulin (PDF p. 377)

questions.stem: An elderly type 2 diabetic has glucose 900 mg/dL, no ketones, and severe dehydration. This is:
questions.rationale: HHNS: very high glucose, hyperosmolality, minimal ketones, mainly elderly type 2.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, HHNS (PDF p. 377)

questions.stem: Which statement about DKA versus HHNS is correct?
questions.rationale: DKA: rapid onset, ketones, acidosis; HHNS: slower over days, normal pH.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, DKA vs HHNS (PDF p. 378)

questions.stem: A client with uric acid stones should limit:
questions.rationale: Uric acid stones: low-purine diet; avoid anchovies, sardines, organ meats.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Stone Types (PDF p. 382)

questions.stem: Neurons that carry impulses from receptors to the CNS are:
questions.rationale: Afferent neurons carry sensory input to the CNS.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Neurons (PDF p. 414)

questions.stem: Broca's area, controlling motor speech, is in the:
questions.rationale: Broca's (frontal) is expressive speech; Wernicke's (temporal) is comprehension.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebrum (PDF p. 414)

questions.stem: A client cannot understand spoken language after a stroke. Which area is affected?
questions.rationale: Wernicke's area in the temporal lobe controls language comprehension.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebrum (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Which brain structure controls balance and coordination?
questions.rationale: Cerebellum controls fine movement, balance, and proprioception.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cerebellum (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: The cardiac, respiratory, and vasomotor centers are located in the:
questions.rationale: The medulla contains vital centers and reflexes such as coughing and vomiting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Medulla (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Which brain structure regulates body temperature?
questions.rationale: Hypothalamus regulates temperature, food and fluid intake, and autonomic function.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothalamus (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Testing the corneal reflex assesses which cranial nerve?
questions.rationale: Trigeminal nerve: facial sensation, corneal reflex, mastication.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerves (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Asking the client to shrug the shoulders tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: CN XI innervates sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerves (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: How many pairs of spinal nerves are there?
questions.rationale: 31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Spinal Nerves (PDF p. 415)

questions.stem: Which effect is caused by sympathetic stimulation?
questions.rationale: Sympathetic: pupil dilation, tachycardia, bronchodilation, decreased peristalsis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Nervous System (PDF p. 416)

questions.stem: Parasympathetic stimulation of the urinary bladder causes:
questions.rationale: Parasympathetic contracts the detrusor and relaxes sphincters, promoting voiding.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Nervous System (PDF p. 416)

questions.stem: What is the highest possible Glasgow Coma Scale score?
questions.rationale: GCS ranges 3 (deep coma) to 15 (fully alert).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)

questions.stem: A client opens eyes to pressure, uses inappropriate words, and withdraws from pain. GCS score?
questions.rationale: Eye 2 + verbal 3 + motor 4 = 9.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)

questions.stem: Which GCS motor response is abnormal flexion?
questions.rationale: Abnormal flexion is decorticate (3); abnormal extension is decerebrate (2).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)

questions.stem: Which posture indicates more serious brain damage?
questions.rationale: Decerebrate (extension, internal rotation) is more ominous.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)

questions.stem: The Rinne and Weber tests assess cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: CN VIII: hearing (Rinne, Weber) and balance (Romberg).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)

questions.stem: Asking the client to smile, frown, and wrinkle the forehead tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: Facial nerve controls facial expression.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)

questions.stem: Eliciting the gag reflex and observing uvula rise tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: Vagus: gag reflex, symmetric uvula rise, voice.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 419)

questions.stem: Loss of the sense of smell is called:
questions.rationale: Anosmia relates to CN I.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)

questions.stem: Flexing the neck causes involuntary hip and knee flexion. This is:
questions.rationale: Positive Brudzinski's indicates meningeal irritation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)

questions.stem: In an adult, stroking the sole causes the toes to fan out. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Toes fanning is abnormal in adults, indicating upper motor neuron lesion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)

questions.stem: Before a contrast CT scan, the nurse asks about:
questions.rationale: Assess iodine allergy; warn of warm flushing and metallic taste.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 420)

questions.stem: Before an EEG, the adult client should:
questions.rationale: Sleep deprivation helps; withhold anticonvulsants, sedatives, stimulants as ordered.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 420)

questions.stem: Visual flashes and tingling of the lips before a headache indicate which migraine phase?
questions.rationale: Aura lasts under 1 hour with focal neurologic symptoms.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Migraine Phases (PDF p. 421)

questions.stem: What is the most common type of headache?
questions.rationale: Tension-type headaches are most common, chronic, and less severe.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Headaches (PDF p. 421)

questions.stem: Sumatriptan is contraindicated in clients with:
questions.rationale: Triptans cause vasoconstriction and chest pain.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-migraine Agents (PDF p. 422)

questions.stem: Which environment comforts a client during a migraine?
questions.rationale: Provide a quiet, dark room, HOB at 30 degrees, and analgesics.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Headache Nursing (PDF p. 422)

questions.stem: What is the earliest sign of increased intracranial pressure?
questions.rationale: LOC change is the earliest sign.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 422)

questions.stem: The upper limit of normal intracranial pressure is about:
questions.rationale: Normal ICP 0–10, upper limit 15 mm Hg.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 422)

questions.stem: Cushing's triad in increased ICP consists of:
questions.rationale: Cushing's triad is a late sign of rising ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 423)

questions.stem: Which action helps prevent increased ICP?
questions.rationale: Avoid straining and coughing; keep HOB elevated about 30 degrees.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ICP Nursing Management (PDF p. 423)

questions.stem: Which drug is given to reduce cerebral edema?
questions.rationale: Osmotic diuretic mannitol reduces cerebral edema.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ICP Nursing Management (PDF p. 423)

questions.stem: A transient ischemic attack typically lasts:
questions.rationale: TIA: neurologic deficit typically under 1 hour, a warning of stroke.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CVA (PDF p. 423)

questions.stem: Cardiogenic embolic stroke is most often associated with:
questions.rationale: Atrial fibrillation produces emboli.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ischemic Stroke (PDF p. 424)

questions.stem: What is the major risk factor for stroke?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is the major risk factor.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Risk Factors (PDF p. 424)

questions.stem: The most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage is:
questions.rationale: A leaking aneurysm near the Circle of Willis or AVM.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhagic Stroke (PDF p. 424)

questions.stem: A client after stroke can understand but cannot form words. This is:
questions.rationale: Expressive (Broca's): cannot form words; receptive: cannot understand.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Communication Loss (PDF p. 425)

questions.stem: Which is typical of a right hemispheric stroke?
questions.rationale: Right stroke: left weakness, spatial deficits, impulsivity, unawareness of deficits.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hemispheric Strokes (PDF p. 425)

questions.stem: A client with homonymous hemianopsia should be taught to:
options: Turn head toward the lost field
questions.rationale: Scanning toward the visual loss compensates; approach from the unaffected side.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 425)

questions.stem: When feeding a client with dysphagia after stroke, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Check gag reflex, sit upright, give soft foods on the unaffected side.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 426)

questions.stem: Which positioning prevents a common complication in a hemiplegic client?
questions.rationale: Place a pillow in the axilla to prevent adduction and contracture.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, CVA Nursing (PDF p. 425)

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of encephalitis?
questions.rationale: HSV is most common; treated with acyclovir.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Encephalitis (PDF p. 427)

questions.stem: A child stares blankly for a few seconds several times a day. This is:
questions.rationale: Absence (petit mal) seizures: brief staring, common in children.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Seizures (PDF p. 428)

questions.stem: A client picks at clothing and smacks lips with loss of awareness. This is:
questions.rationale: Complex partial (psychomotor): automatisms with loss of consciousness.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Partial Seizures (PDF p. 428)

questions.stem: During a tonic-clonic seizure, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Ease to floor, protect head, loosen clothing; never restrain or insert objects.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Seizure Nursing (PDF p. 428)

questions.stem: After a seizure, the client should be positioned:
questions.rationale: Side-lying prevents aspiration; keep suction available.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Seizure Nursing (PDF p. 428)

questions.stem: What are the earliest signs of myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Ocular weakness (ptosis, diplopia) appears first.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Myasthenia Gravis (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: Improved muscle strength after edrophonium injection indicates:
questions.rationale: Positive Tensilon test; atropine is the antidote.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tensilon Test (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: When should pyridostigmine be given to a client with myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Give before meals for chewing and swallowing strength, on schedule.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MG Nursing (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: Which drug class should be avoided in myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Avoid muscle relaxants, barbiturates, morphine, tranquilizers, neomycin.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MG Medications to Avoid (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: Cholinergic crisis in myasthenia gravis is caused by:
questions.rationale: Cholinergic crisis: excess anticholinesterase; myasthenic crisis: undermedication.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cholinergic Crisis (PDF p. 429)

questions.stem: Charcot's triad of multiple sclerosis consists of:
questions.rationale: Charcot's triad reflects demyelination.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Multiple Sclerosis (PDF p. 430)

questions.stem: Which drug is the medication of choice for spasticity in multiple sclerosis?
questions.rationale: Baclofen relieves spasticity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MS Management (PDF p. 430)

questions.stem: Which teaching is appropriate for a client with multiple sclerosis?
questions.rationale: Heat worsens symptoms and sensory loss risks burns; avoid strenuous exercise.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, MS Nursing (PDF p. 431)

questions.stem: Weakness beginning in the legs and ascending after a viral illness suggests:
questions.rationale: GBS: ascending weakness and diminished reflexes from peripheral demyelination.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Guillain-Barré (PDF p. 431)

questions.stem: What is the priority assessment for a client with Guillain-Barré syndrome?
questions.rationale: Ascending paralysis can affect the diaphragm; monitor ventilation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, GBS Nursing (PDF p. 431)

questions.stem: Parkinson's disease is associated with decreased:
questions.rationale: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Disease (PDF p. 432)

questions.stem: Which finding is characteristic of Parkinson's disease?
questions.rationale: Resting pill-rolling tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, mask-like face, festinating gait.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Manifestations (PDF p. 432)

questions.stem: Very small, illegible handwriting in Parkinson's disease is called:
questions.rationale: Micrographia results from bradykinesia and rigidity.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Manifestations (PDF p. 432)

questions.stem: Which vitamin reduces the effect of levodopa (without carbidopa)?
questions.rationale: Pyridoxine, phenothiazines, and reserpine block levodopa.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levodopa Teaching (PDF p. 433)

questions.stem: A client starting levodopa should be taught to rise slowly because of:
questions.rationale: Levodopa side effects include orthostatic hypotension, nausea, confusion.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Levodopa Side Effects (PDF p. 433)

questions.stem: Which diet helps a client with Parkinson's disease who has dysphagia?
questions.rationale: Semi-solids and thick fluids reduce aspiration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Parkinson's Nursing (PDF p. 433)

questions.stem: Riluzole is used in ALS because it:
questions.rationale: ALS involves glutamate over-excitation; riluzole is a glutamate antagonist.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ALS (PDF p. 434)

questions.stem: Spontaneous twitching of muscles seen in ALS is called:
questions.rationale: Fasciculations reflect motor neuron degeneration.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, ALS (PDF p. 434)

questions.stem: Injury at C1–C4 most threatens:
questions.rationale: High cervical injury impairs the diaphragm; airway is first priority.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Spinal Cord Injury (PDF p. 435)

questions.stem: At an accident scene with suspected spinal injury, the nurse should:
options: Immobilize and move as a unit
questions.rationale: Immobilize on a firm surface with collar; do not realign; log-roll.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, SCI Management (PDF p. 435)

questions.stem: A client with T4 injury suddenly has pounding headache, sweating, and very high BP. This is:
questions.rationale: Autonomic dysreflexia occurs with injuries above T6.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)

questions.stem: What is the first nursing action in autonomic dysreflexia?
questions.rationale: Sit upright to lower BP, then find the cause (usually a full bladder).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)

questions.stem: The most common trigger of autonomic dysreflexia is:
questions.rationale: Bladder distention; also fecal impaction and pressure ulcers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Dysreflexia (PDF p. 436)

questions.stem: Which brain changes are found in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.rationale: Amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, and cortical atrophy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's (PDF p. 436)

questions.stem: A client with Alzheimer's becomes more agitated and wanders in the late afternoon. This is:
questions.rationale: Sundowning: agitation and disorientation in afternoon and evening, middle stage.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Stages (PDF p. 437)

questions.stem: Donepezil is given in Alzheimer's disease to:
questions.rationale: Cholinesterase inhibitors increase brain acetylcholine; memantine blocks NMDA.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Management (PDF p. 437)

questions.stem: Which intervention promotes safety for a client with Alzheimer's at home?
questions.rationale: Secure doors, remove hazards, supervise, avoid restraints.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Safety (PDF p. 438)

questions.stem: At mealtime, a client with Alzheimer's is best helped by:
options: Offering one dish at a time
questions.rationale: Keep meals simple: one dish at a time, small pieces, familiar foods.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Nutrition (PDF p. 438)

questions.stem: Sudden unilateral facial paralysis with inability to close one eye suggests:
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy is CN VII inflammation causing unilateral facial weakness.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy (PDF p. 438)

questions.stem: Why are artificial tears used in Bell's palsy?
questions.rationale: Incomplete eyelid closure exposes the cornea.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy Nursing (PDF p. 439)

questions.stem: A client with Bell's palsy should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Soft diet, chew on unaffected side, avoid hot food, do facial exercises.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy Nursing (PDF p. 439)

questions.stem: Involuntary jerky movements, cognitive decline, and family history at age 40 suggest:
questions.rationale: Huntington's is inherited, with chorea and progressive dementia; genetic counseling advised.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Huntington's Disease (PDF p. 440)

questions.stem: Brief, stabbing facial pain triggered by brushing the teeth suggests:
questions.rationale: Tic douloureux: paroxysmal pain along CN V, triggered by touch.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Neuralgia (PDF p. 440)

questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used for trigeminal neuralgia?
questions.rationale: Anti-seizure agents (carbamazepine, phenytoin).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Neuralgia (PDF p. 441)

questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent attacks of trigeminal neuralgia?
questions.rationale: Avoid extreme temperatures, jarring, and vigorous facial care.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Nursing (PDF p. 441)

questions.stem: Which retinal cells are responsible for night vision?
questions.rationale: Rods: night vision; cones: color and bright light; macula: central vision.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Anatomy of the Eye (PDF p. 472)

questions.stem: A visual acuity of 20/200 means the client sees at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at:
questions.rationale: Top number is test distance; bottom is distance a normal eye sees the same line.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Snellen Chart (PDF p. 472)

questions.stem: Normal intraocular pressure is:
questions.rationale: Tonometry measures IOP; normal 10–21 mm Hg.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tonometer (PDF p. 472)

questions.stem: Which test screens for macular degeneration?
questions.rationale: Wavy or missing lines on the Amsler grid suggest macular problems.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Amsler Grid (PDF p. 473)

questions.stem: Legal blindness is best-corrected visual acuity of:
questions.rationale: Legal blindness: BCVA not exceeding 20/200 in the better eye.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Terms (PDF p. 473)

questions.stem: Removal of the entire eye and part of the optic nerve is:
questions.rationale: Evisceration removes contents; exenteration removes eye, lids, and orbit contents.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Terms (PDF p. 473)

questions.stem: How should a client manage a stye?
questions.rationale: Warm soaks promote drainage; good hygiene; do not squeeze.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Hordeolum (PDF p. 474)

questions.stem: Which compress is used for viral conjunctivitis?
questions.rationale: Cold compresses for viral; warm soaks for bacterial crusting.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Conjunctivitis (PDF p. 474)

questions.stem: What is the most important measure to prevent spread of conjunctivitis?
questions.rationale: Good hand washing prevents spread.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Conjunctivitis (PDF p. 474)

questions.stem: Which test detects corneal abrasion?
questions.rationale: Fluorescein stains epithelial defects, seen with Wood's or slit lamp.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Corneal Abrasion (PDF p. 474)

questions.stem: A client with uveitis on topical corticosteroids should have follow-up for:
questions.rationale: Corticosteroids can increase IOP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Iritis/Uveitis (PDF p. 475)

questions.stem: Gradual, painless blurring of vision with glare and a cloudy pupil suggests:
questions.rationale: Cataract: lens opacity, painless gradual loss, glare.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract (PDF p. 475)

questions.stem: After cataract surgery, which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: Avoid bending, coughing, and straining; lie on unaffected side; wear shield.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract Nursing (PDF p. 476)

questions.stem: Sudden severe eye pain and restlessness after cataract surgery may indicate:
questions.rationale: Report sudden pain with restlessness and rising pulse.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Cataract Nursing (PDF p. 476)

questions.stem: Sudden severe eye pain, halos, nausea, and a fixed semi-dilated pupil suggest:
questions.rationale: Acute angle closure is an emergency with very high IOP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Glaucoma (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: Pilocarpine treats glaucoma by:
questions.rationale: Miotics constrict the pupil and open the trabecular meshwork for outflow.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glaucoma Management (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: A client with glaucoma should avoid which drug class unless approved?
questions.rationale: Anticholinergics and corticosteroids may raise IOP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Glaucoma Teaching (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: Which finding is typical of chronic open-angle glaucoma?
questions.rationale: Open-angle glaucoma: painless, progressive peripheral field loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Open-Angle Glaucoma (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: A client with open-angle glaucoma feels fine and wants to stop eyedrops. The nurse explains:
options: Use is lifelong to prevent damage
questions.rationale: Glaucoma is chronic; IOP can damage the eye without symptoms.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Open-Angle Glaucoma Nursing (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: Floaters and a curtain-like shadow across the visual field suggest:
questions.rationale: Retinal detachment: floaters, flashes, veil; surgical emergency.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Retinal Detachment (PDF p. 478)

questions.stem: A silicone band placed around the sclera to reattach the retina is:
questions.rationale: Scleral buckle indents the sclera to bring retinal layers together.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Retinal Detachment Surgery (PDF p. 478)

questions.stem: Straight lines appearing wavy to an older adult suggests:
questions.rationale: Wet AMD: abnormal vessels leak under the retina, distorting central vision.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Macular Degeneration (PDF p. 479)

questions.stem: A client with macular degeneration is given an Amsler grid. The nurse instructs to:
options: Check one eye at a time weekly
questions.rationale: Check each eye several times weekly with glasses; report changes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, AMD Nursing (PDF p. 479)

questions.stem: A client has a metal fragment protruding from the eye. The nurse should:
options: Shield the eye, do not remove
questions.rationale: Never remove; protect with a metal shield or cup; no pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Penetrating Injuries (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: A chemical splashes into a worker's eye. The first action is:
questions.rationale: Immediately irrigate with tap water or normal saline.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Splash Injury (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: Blood in the anterior chamber of the eye after trauma is called:
questions.rationale: Hyphema is hemorrhage within the chamber.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Contusion of the Eyeball (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: Enucleation of an irreparable injured eye is done within 2 weeks to prevent:
questions.rationale: Sympathetic ophthalmia can blind the uninjured eye.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Eye Trauma (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: A normal tympanic membrane appears:
questions.rationale: Normal TM is pearly gray and translucent.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Ear Anatomy (PDF p. 480)

questions.stem: Pain when the auricle is pulled suggests:
questions.rationale: External otitis causes pain on auricle manipulation; mastoid tenderness suggests mastoiditis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Auditory Assessment (PDF p. 481)

questions.stem: In conductive hearing loss, the Weber test lateralizes to the:
questions.rationale: Conductive: Weber to affected ear, bone > air on Rinne; sensorineural: Weber to better ear.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuning Fork Tests (PDF p. 482)

questions.stem: A normal Rinne test shows:
questions.rationale: Normally air conduction is longer than bone conduction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Tuning Fork Tests (PDF p. 482)

questions.stem: Which teaching prevents otitis externa (swimmer's ear)?
questions.rationale: Avoid wetting and trauma; do not use cotton-tipped applicators.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Otitis Externa (PDF p. 482)

questions.stem: Meniere's triad consists of vertigo, tinnitus, and:
questions.rationale: Abnormal endolymph causes vertigo, tinnitus, and fluctuating sensorineural loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Disease (PDF p. 483)

questions.stem: During a vertigo attack from Meniere's disease, the client should:
options: Lie still in a safe place
questions.rationale: Lie down and stay still; recognize aura to prepare.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Nursing (PDF p. 484)

questions.stem: Which diet modification helps Meniere's disease?
questions.rationale: Limit salt, sugar, and alcohol to stabilize inner ear fluid.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Nursing (PDF p. 484)

questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used to control vertigo?
questions.rationale: Vestibular suppressants such as meclizine control vertigo.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Meniere's Management (PDF p. 483)

questions.stem: An insect is lodged in a child's ear. The nurse should first:
questions.rationale: Irrigation is contraindicated for insects; mineral oil kills and dislodges it.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Foreign Bodies (PDF p. 484)

questions.stem: Ear irrigation to remove cerumen is contraindicated with:
questions.rationale: Do not irrigate with a perforated drum or inflamed canal.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Impacted Cerumen (PDF p. 484)

questions.stem: 'If it was not charted, it was not done' emphasizes that:
options: Notes can be added later freely
questions.rationale: Records are legal protection; notes should be full, accurate, legible, prompt.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Medical Records (PDF p. 502)

questions.stem: Which theory holds that leaders are born, not made?
questions.rationale: Great man/trait theory: inborn characteristics make leaders.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Theories (PDF p. 506)

questions.stem: A head nurse inspires staff, promotes their development, and encourages creativity. This is:
questions.rationale: Transformational leaders inspire and develop followers; transactional uses rewards and punishment.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Transformational Theory (PDF p. 506)

questions.stem: Fiedler's contingency theory considers leader-member relations, task structure, and:
questions.rationale: Fiedler: leader-member relations, task structure, position power.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Contingency Theory (PDF p. 506)

questions.stem: During a code, which leadership style is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Emergencies need quick decisions and strong control.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Styles (PDF p. 507)

questions.stem: Laissez-faire leadership works best with staff who are:
questions.rationale: Little control requires self-directed, skilled members.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership Styles (PDF p. 507)

questions.stem: Who is the Father of Scientific Management?
questions.rationale: Taylor used stopwatch studies; Fayol: management process; Weber: organization/bureaucracy.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Management Theories (PDF p. 507)

questions.stem: According to Herzberg, which is a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
questions.rationale: Motivators: achievement, recognition, responsibility, growth; hygiene: policy, supervision, conditions.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Herzberg (PDF p. 508)

questions.stem: A manager believing staff dislike work and must be threatened follows:
questions.rationale: McGregor's Theory X assumes people avoid work; Theory Y assumes self-direction.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, McGregor (PDF p. 508)

questions.stem: Staff follow a senior nurse because they admire her and want to be like her. This is:
questions.rationale: Referent power comes from admiration and identification.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Power (PDF p. 508)

questions.stem: Influence based on being the mayor's daughter reflects which power?
questions.rationale: Connection power comes from links to influential people.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Power (PDF p. 509)

questions.stem: The Pareto principle states that:
questions.rationale: The 80-20 rule: focus on the vital few causes.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of Management (PDF p. 509)

questions.stem: A head nurse is an example of which management level?
questions.rationale: Head nurse: first level; supervisor: middle; chief nurse: top.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Management Levels (PDF p. 510)

questions.stem: Strategic planning typically covers:
questions.rationale: Strategic planning sets overall goals for 3–5 years by top managers.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 510)

questions.stem: A brief statement of why an organization exists is its:
questions.rationale: Mission: reason for existence; vision: future; philosophy: values.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 510)

questions.stem: A guideline allowing only one choice of action, fairly inflexible, is a:
questions.rationale: Rules allow one action; policies are broad guidelines; procedures give step sequences.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 511)

questions.stem: Daily and weekly unit plans made by head nurses are:
questions.rationale: Operational: daily/weekly, head nurses; intermediate: 6 months–2 years, supervisors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Operational Planning (PDF p. 511)

questions.stem: Purchase of a new CT scanner belongs in which budget?
questions.rationale: Capital budget covers major equipment and fixed assets.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Budgeting (PDF p. 511)

questions.stem: Which budget forces managers to justify every expense from scratch?
questions.rationale: Zero-based budgeting sets priorities and justifies costs; it is time-consuming.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Budgeting (PDF p. 512)

questions.stem: The principle that each employee reports to only one superior is:
questions.rationale: Unity of command: one superior; span of control: number reporting to a manager.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of Organizing (PDF p. 512)

questions.stem: The number of people reporting directly to a manager is the:
questions.rationale: Span of control.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Principles of Organizing (PDF p. 512)

questions.stem: An advisory department with no authority to implement its recommendations is a:
questions.rationale: Staff positions are advisory (training, research); line has direct authority.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Organization (PDF p. 512)

questions.stem: Which scheduling repeats a set pattern over a number of weeks?
questions.rationale: Cyclical scheduling is fair, saves time, and lets staff plan ahead.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Scheduling (PDF p. 513)

questions.stem: Under DOH staffing standards, how many relievers factor is used for staff working 40 hours/week?
questions.rationale: Multiply needed personnel by 0.15 (40 h/week) or 0.12 (48 h/week).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Staffing Formula (PDF p. 514)

questions.stem: Per the DOH distribution of nursing staff per shift, the AM shift receives:
questions.rationale: AM 45%, PM 37%, Night 18%.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Distribution Per Shift (PDF p. 515)

questions.stem: An incident report submitted to the nursing director is which line of communication?
questions.rationale: Upward: subordinate to superior (incident and grievance reports).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lines of Communication (PDF p. 515)

questions.stem: Shift endorsement between staff nurses is which communication line?
questions.rationale: Horizontal communication occurs between peers at the same level.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lines of Communication (PDF p. 515)

questions.stem: Which task should a head nurse not delegate?
questions.rationale: Evaluation and disciplinary action, overall accountability, and signing authority are not delegated.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Delegation (PDF p. 516)

questions.stem: One nurse gives all medications and another does all treatments. This is:
questions.rationale: Functional nursing is task-oriented and fragments care.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Functional Nursing (PDF p. 516)

questions.stem: An RN responsible 24 hours a day for 4–6 patients from admission to discharge practices:
questions.rationale: Primary nursing assures continuity and trust.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Nursing (PDF p. 517)

questions.stem: A private duty nurse caring for one patient uses which method?
questions.rationale: Case method is one-to-one (ICU, private duty).
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Case Method (PDF p. 517)

questions.stem: Planned activities that introduce new employees to the work environment are:
questions.rationale: Orientation is for new employees; in-service improves current job performance.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Staff Development (PDF p. 517)

questions.stem: Which conflict resolution strategy produces a win-win outcome?
questions.rationale: Collaboration has both parties work together to solve the problem.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Conflict Resolution (PDF p. 518)

questions.stem: Conflict between the nursing and dietary departments is:
questions.rationale: Intergroup conflict is between two groups.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Conflict (PDF p. 518)

questions.stem: What is the first step in the control process?
questions.rationale: Set standards, measure, compare, reinforce, correct.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Controlling (PDF p. 518)

questions.stem: A performance appraisal tool describing specific observed incidents of a nurse's work is:
questions.rationale: Anecdotal records describe observed experiences and behaviors.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Performance Appraisal (PDF p. 518)

questions.stem: Evaluating whether the nursing process steps were followed is which quality criterion?
questions.rationale: Structure: setting; process: steps of care; outcome: results in client.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Quality Assurance (PDF p. 519)

questions.stem: Continuously comparing a unit's performance against the best is:
questions.rationale: Benchmarking measures what exists against the best.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Benchmarking (PDF p. 519)

questions.stem: 'Doing the right thing' rather than 'doing things right' describes:
questions.rationale: Leadership focuses on purpose and the future; management on structure and the present.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Leadership vs Management (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: In Lewin's change theory, staff becoming aware of the need for change is:
questions.rationale: Unfreezing: awareness; moving: working toward change; refreezing: stabilizing.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lewin's Theory (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: A new protocol becomes part of routine practice. This is which Lewin stage?
questions.rationale: Refreezing integrates and stabilizes the change.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Lewin's Theory (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: Convincing staff with evidence that a change benefits them uses which strategy?
questions.rationale: Empirical-rational assumes people adopt justified changes that benefit them.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Change Strategies (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: Change involving mutual goal setting, equal power, and deliberateness is:
questions.rationale: Planned change has mutual goals, equal power, and deliberation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Change (PDF p. 520)

questions.stem: McClelland's theory identifies needs for achievement, affiliation, and:
questions.rationale: McClelland: achievement, power, affiliation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Motivation Theories (PDF p. 521)

questions.stem: A nurse feels underpaid compared with a colleague doing the same work. Which theory explains her motivation?
questions.rationale: Equity theory: fairness judged by comparing inputs and rewards with others.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Equity Theory (PDF p. 521)

questions.stem: A client on the psychiatric unit looks frightened and says, 'I feel like I'm losing control.' What is the nurse's MOST appropriate action?
options: Give the PRN anxiolytic right away
Take the client to a quiet room and talk
Tell the client to join the group activity
questions.rationale: A quiet setting lowers environmental stimuli, and talking lets the nurse find the cause of the feelings. Medication is used only after noninvasive approaches fail, and seclusion is for clients who are a danger to themselves or others.
explanations: Medication comes after less invasive measures fail.
Seclusion is not warranted for anxiety without danger.
Correct: reduces stimuli and opens communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 767)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client with depression asks how cognitive therapy works. Which explanation by the nurse is accurate?
options: 'It examines how your thoughts affect your feelings and mood.'
'It uncovers memories from your early childhood.'
'It rewards you each time you show a desired behavior.'
'It relies mainly on medicines to correct your mood.'
questions.rationale: Cognitive therapy examines the client's thoughts and feelings about situations and how they keep the difficulties and low mood going, then builds new coping skills.
explanations: Correct: this is the core of cognitive therapy.
Cognitive therapy is a psychotherapy, not drug treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 829)

questions.stem: Which outcome is MOST realistic in the care plan of an older client with dementia?
options: The client will be admitted to a nursing home
Staff will perform all of the client's daily care
The client will function as independently as possible
The client will recall the date on every shift
questions.rationale: Every client is encouraged to function at the highest level of independence possible, which supports a sense of control and well-being. Placement and staff-performed care are not client-centered goals.
explanations: Placement is not a client-centered outcome.
Correct: maximal independence is client-centered and realistic.
Expecting full orientation is unrealistic in progressive dementia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1026)

questions.stem: During home visits, the nurse suspects that the wife of a bedridden client is experiencing caregiver strain. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Refer the family to a social worker
Advise placing the client in a facility
Arrange a paid caregiver for the family
Gather data from both the wife and the client
questions.rationale: Before any referral, the nurse assesses the caregiver's stressors and coping abilities by collecting data from both the caregiver and the client.
explanations: Referrals wait until the assessment is complete.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 935)

questions.stem: Which activity plan is BEST for a newly admitted client with major depression?
options: Quiet, solitary activities in the room
A structured schedule of simple activities
Letting the client choose whether to join
Competitive team games to lift the mood
questions.rationale: Depressed clients are withdrawn, fatigued, and struggle to concentrate. The plan provides stimulation within a structured environment, using simple tasks the client can complete.
explanations: A depressed client will likely choose not to participate.
Competition can reinforce feelings of worthlessness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 776)

questions.stem: Which is an appropriate maintenance goal for a client being discharged with chronic anxiety?
options: Eliminating all anxiety from daily life
Calling a counselor whenever anxiety starts
Ignoring anxious feelings until they pass
questions.rationale: Recognizing triggers lets the client prepare coping strategies or avoid a specific stimulus. Anxiety cannot be eliminated, and relying on others does not build internal strengths.
explanations: It is impossible to eliminate all anxiety.
This does not develop internal coping.
Ignoring feelings does not resolve anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 796)

questions.stem: The mother of a teenager with an anxiety disorder asks what changes at home would help. Which advice is BEST?
options: Keep her home from school for a month
Stop her from seeing any friends
Limit coffee, energy drinks, and chocolate
Let her eat whatever calms her down
questions.rationale: Caffeine, chocolate, and alcohol can increase anxiety and should be limited. Isolating the teen from school and peers is unhealthy and unrealistic.
explanations: Restricting all peer contact is unreasonable.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 903)

questions.stem: A client with bipolar disorder on lithium carbonate has a serum level of 1.6 mEq/L. Which question BEST checks for early toxicity?
options: 'Have you had nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea?'
'Are you passing a lot of urine?'
questions.rationale: The maintenance range is 0.8 to 1.2 mEq/L. Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) is one of the most common early signs of mild toxicity; blurred vision and seizures occur at higher levels.
explanations: Correct: GI symptoms are early signs of toxicity.
Blurred vision appears at higher levels.
Seizures occur at much higher levels.
Polyuria can occur but is not the key early sign of toxicity.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 468)

questions.stem: A client's serum lithium level is 3.9 mEq/L. Which intervention is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: A level of 3.9 mEq/L is in the toxic range, and seizures can occur at 3.5 mEq/L and above. Seizure precautions come first.
explanations: Not the priority at this level.
Correct: seizures may occur at this level.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 759)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia is pacing, speaking rapidly, and making threatening gestures. What is the nurse's PRIORITY?
options: Ensuring the safety of the client and others
Exploring the client's anger in group therapy
Ignoring the behavior to avoid reinforcing it
questions.rationale: Signs of loss of control make safety for everyone on the unit the immediate priority. Exploring feelings comes later, and ignoring the behavior risks escalation.
explanations: Correct: safety of all clients comes first.
Not appropriate while the client is escalating.
Documentation is not the priority action.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 645)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia has visual hallucinations. Which lobe of the cerebrum is associated with this symptom?
questions.rationale: The occipital lobe processes vision and is linked to visual hallucinations. The temporal lobe processes hearing and is linked to auditory hallucinations.
explanations: The frontal lobe governs thinking, judgment, and behavior.
The temporal lobe is linked to auditory hallucinations.
The parietal lobe processes touch and sensation.
Correct: the occipital lobe processes vision.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1031)

questions.stem: A client who attempted suicide is now hallucinating and delusional. Which intervention BEST ensures the client's safety?
options: Check the client's location every 15 minutes
Ask the client to report suicidal thoughts
Keep the client in the dayroom with others
questions.rationale: Hallucinations and delusions increase unpredictable behavior, impair judgment, and raise suicide risk, so constant one-to-one supervision is needed.
explanations: Fifteen-minute checks leave gaps in supervision.
A psychotic client cannot be relied on to report.
Being among others is not the same as dedicated observation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 594)

questions.situation: Mang Lito, 50, has alcohol use disorder and wants to stay sober. His physician prescribes disulfiram.
questions.stem: Before giving the first dose, which information is MOST important for the nurse to obtain?
options: The time of his last full meal
The time of his last alcoholic drink
questions.rationale: The client must abstain from alcohol for at least 12 hours before the first dose of disulfiram, or a severe reaction can occur.
explanations: Meal timing does not affect safety here.
Correct: alcohol must be avoided for at least 12 hours before the first dose.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1796)

questions.situation: Mang Lito, 50, has alcohol use disorder and wants to stay sober. His physician prescribes disulfiram.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Lito shows he understands the teaching about disulfiram?
options: 'One bottle of beer on weekends is still okay.'
'Vinegar dips and sauces are safe to eat.'
'I will check cough syrups and mouthwash for alcohol.'
'Rubbing alcohol on my skin will not matter.'
questions.rationale: Any alcohol can trigger a disulfiram reaction, including hidden sources: vinegar and sauces, cold medicines, mouthwash, and alcohol rubs or aftershave.
explanations: Any alcohol intake causes a reaction.
Vinegars and some sauces contain alcohol.
Correct: hidden alcohol must be avoided.
Skin preparations containing alcohol can also cause a reaction.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1358)

questions.stem: A client is admitted after an attempted hanging. Which intervention is MOST important for the client's safety?
options: A staff member stays with the client at all times
The client agrees to report suicidal thoughts
The client wears a hospital gown only
The client is placed in seclusion
questions.rationale: Hanging is a serious suicide attempt, so constant observation by a staff member is necessary. The client cannot be relied on to report suicidal thoughts at this stage.
explanations: Removing clothing alone does not ensure safety.
Seclusion isolates the client without the needed observation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 780)

questions.stem: A caller tells the crisis hotline nurse that he wants to kill himself and has a loaded gun on the table. What is the BEST action?
options: Ask him to unload the gun and go to the hospital
Tell him to call back after he has calmed down
Keep him on the line while sending help
Ask why he wants to end his life
questions.rationale: In a crisis the nurse takes an authoritative, active role. Keeping the caller on the phone while getting help to him best protects his safety.
explanations: This relies on him to act alone and lacks authoritative action.
Ending the call abandons the client in crisis.
Correct: maintain contact and dispatch help.
Exploring reasons can wait until he is safe.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 781)

questions.stem: Before discharging a victim of family violence from the emergency room, what is MOST important to include in the plan?
options: A safety plan for leaving dangerous situations
A follow-up visit in one month
Advice to avoid provoking the partner
questions.rationale: In the emergency setting, the most important step is helping the victim plan how to get away from harmful situations if they arise.
explanations: Counseling may come later and is not the immediate priority.
Correct: a safety plan protects the victim now.
Follow-up is secondary to immediate safety.
This blames the victim and is inappropriate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 772)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which event is an example of a situational crisis?
questions.rationale: A situational crisis comes from an external, often unexpected event such as job loss, divorce, or death of a loved one. Retirement and childbirth are maturational crises; natural disasters are adventitious crises.
explanations: A natural disaster is an adventitious crisis.
Correct: job loss is an unanticipated external event.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 919)

questions.stem: A client becomes physically aggressive toward staff. Which action BEST protects the milieu while preserving the client's rights?
options: Lock the client in a room until calm
Try de-escalation and a sitter first
questions.rationale: Alternatives must be exhausted before restraints. If restraint becomes necessary, it requires a prescription and an explanation to the client and family.
explanations: Restraints come only after alternatives fail and need a prescription.
Chemical restraint also requires less restrictive measures first.
Seclusion without a prescription violates rights.
Correct: the least restrictive measures come first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 782)

questions.stem: A client's central venous catheter disconnects from the IV tubing, and the nurse suspects an air embolism. How should the nurse position the client immediately?
questions.rationale: Left side-lying in Trendelenburg traps air in the right atrium, away from the pulmonary outflow, where it can be aspirated if needed.
explanations: Head-up positions let air travel toward the brain and lungs.
Correct: traps air in the right atrium.
This elevates the head and does not trap the air.
Supine does not trap the air effectively.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 282)

questions.stem: A client with a suspected neck injury is unresponsive and pulseless. How should the nurse open the airway?
questions.rationale: The jaw thrust opens the airway without moving the cervical spine and is used until an x-ray confirms the spine is stable.
explanations: Correct: opens the airway while protecting the cervical spine.
Head tilt moves the neck and risks cord damage.
Not a method of opening the airway in a pulseless client.
Hyperextension can worsen a spinal injury.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 312)

questions.stem: Which findings should the nurse expect in a client developing cardiogenic shock after a myocardial infarction?
options: Warm, flushed skin and bounding pulses
Cool, clammy skin and a weak, thready pulse
Dry, hot skin and slow pulse
Pink skin and rising urine output
questions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock causes a rapid, weak, thready pulse, falling blood pressure and urine output, confusion or agitation, and cool, clammy skin.
explanations: Warm, flushed skin suggests early septic shock.
Correct: classic signs of low cardiac output.
Shock causes tachycardia, not a slow pulse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 340)

questions.stem: A client on oxygen by nasal cannula at 6 L/min has these ABGs: pH 7.29, PaCO2 49 mm Hg, PaO2 58 mm Hg, HCO3 18 mEq/L. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Switching to a partial rebreather mask
questions.rationale: The client has combined respiratory and metabolic acidosis with hypoxemia despite supplemental oxygen. When oxygen cannot maintain acceptable PaO2 and PaCO2, intubation and mechanical ventilation are needed.
explanations: A mask will not correct the ventilatory failure.
Correct: oxygen alone has failed to maintain gas exchange.
The current therapy is already failing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 308)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.situation: Nurse Paolo works in the psychiatric unit of a regional hospital and is orienting new staff on the Philippine Mental Health Act (RA 11036).
questions.stem: Within what period after admission must a service user be informed of their rights?
questions.rationale: Service users have the right to information, within 24 hours of admission to a mental health facility, about their rights.
explanations: Rights must be explained early in the stay.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 5(s) (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.situation: Nurse Paolo works in the psychiatric unit of a regional hospital and is orienting new staff on the Philippine Mental Health Act (RA 11036).
questions.stem: A new nurse asks whether admitted clients can decide on their own treatment. What is Nurse Paolo's BEST answer?
options: 'Clients are presumed to have legal capacity and must give written informed consent.'
'Admitted clients lose the right to decide on their treatment.'
'Only the family decides on treatment in a psychiatric unit.'
'Verbal consent is enough for any treatment.'
questions.rationale: Service users are presumed to have legal capacity and must give written informed consent before treatment, including physical or chemical restraint. Consent may be withdrawn.
explanations: Correct: capacity is presumed and consent is written.
Admission does not remove decision-making rights.
The client decides unless capacity is impaired.
The Act requires consent in writing.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 8 (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.situation: Nurse Paolo works in the psychiatric unit of a regional hospital and is orienting new staff on the Philippine Mental Health Act (RA 11036).
questions.stem: An emergency treatment order is given for a client in a psychiatric emergency. Within how many days must the internal review board review it?
questions.rationale: During emergencies, treatment or restraint may be given only to the extent necessary, on the order of the attending mental health professional. The internal review board reviews the order within 15 days.
explanations: Not the period set by the law.
Correct: within 15 days of the order.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 13(c) (lawphil.net)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Under RA 11036, up to how many 'supporters' may a service user designate to help in decision-making?
questions.rationale: A service user may designate up to three persons as supporters to help them make decisions about treatment.
explanations: The law allows more than one.
The law allows up to three.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 11 (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: Which nursing action BEST upholds the right to treatment in the least restrictive environment under RA 11036?
options: Placing every new admission in seclusion
Locking all clients in their rooms at night
Trying verbal de-escalation before any restraint
questions.rationale: Service users have the right to care in the least restrictive environment and manner. Facilities must minimize restrictive care, so less restrictive measures come first.
explanations: Routine seclusion violates the least restrictive principle.
Refusing medication does not justify restraint.
Correct: least restrictive measures come first.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 5(g) (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: A client's employer calls the psychiatric unit asking for the client's diagnosis. What should the nurse do?
options: Give only the diagnosis, since it is brief
Decline unless the client has given written consent
Ask the attending physician to call back with the details
Fax the discharge summary to the employer
questions.rationale: Information about service users is confidential and is not disclosed to third parties without the client's written consent.
explanations: The physician is also bound by confidentiality.
Sending records without consent violates the law.
questions.sourceLabel: RA 11036, Sec. 5(l) (lawphil.net)

questions.stem: A client tells the nurse, 'I don't want to talk to you. You're only the nurse. I'll wait for my doctor.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'I'm a licensed professional, and I know a lot.'
questions.rationale: Reflecting the client's statement sends the feeling back for validation and keeps the focus on the client's wish to talk with the doctor. Defensive replies and withdrawing block communication.
explanations: Gives an excuse and dismisses the client's need.
Withdrawal reinforces the behavior and ends communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1170)

questions.stem: A client says, 'I don't do anything right. I'm such a loser.' Which is the nurse's MOST therapeutic response?
options: 'You do things right all the time.'
'You feel you don't do anything right?'
questions.rationale: Restating the client's words gives the client a chance to say more, so the nurse learns what the client means. Reassurance, changing the subject, and generalizing close off the conversation.
explanations: False reassurance that disagrees with the client.
Correct: restating invites the client to elaborate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1173)

questions.stem: A client who has just learned of kidney failure says, 'This means I will die very soon.' Which response by the nurse is BEST?
options: 'You're worried that you are going to die soon?'
'Why do you think you will die soon?'
'Don't worry; dialysis will take care of it.'
'Many people live long lives with kidney failure.'
questions.rationale: Reflection clarifies the client's concern and encourages them to express their feelings. 'Why' questions demand explanations, and reassurance denies the client's fear.
explanations: Correct: reflection encourages expression of feelings.
'Why' questions put the client on the defensive.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 1195)

questions.stem: A client is found sitting on the floor. The nurse ensures the client's safety, completes an incident report, and notifies the physician. What should the nurse do NEXT?
options: Staple the incident report to the client's chart
Document the incident objectively in the client's record
Give the client a copy of the incident report
Write 'incident report filed' in the nurse's notes
questions.rationale: The nurse documents the event completely and objectively in the client's record. The incident report is a confidential internal quality document; it is not copied, placed in the chart, or mentioned in the notes.
explanations: The report never goes into the chart.
Correct: objective documentation in the record.
The report is internal and is not copied.
Mentioning the report in the chart is inappropriate.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 633)

questions.stem: Which entry on an incident report about a client's fall is written CORRECTLY?
options: 'The aide left the side rails down, causing the fall.'
'The client is probably confused from the new drug.'
'The client fell because the floor was poorly cleaned.'
'Client found on floor beside bed; states, I slipped.'
questions.rationale: An incident report records objective facts: what was seen, what the client said, who was involved, and what was done. It does not assign blame or give opinions.
explanations: Assumes a cause the nurse did not witness.
Correct: an objective observation plus the client's own words.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 615)

questions.stem: Which client is MOST appropriate to assign to a nursing aide (unlicensed assistive personnel)?
options: A client who needs frequent ambulation
A client who needs a sterile dressing change
A client on a bowel program needing a rectal suppository
A newly admitted client needing an initial assessment
questions.rationale: Assignments match each worker's job description and competence. Ambulation can be done by an aide; medications, sterile procedures, and assessment need a licensed nurse.
explanations: Correct: ambulation is within an aide's role.
Sterile dressing changes need a licensed nurse.
Giving medication needs a licensed nurse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 644)

questions.stem: A client with ARDS is placed on a CPAP face mask. Which action makes the therapy effective?
options: Applying the mask loosely so the client is comfortable
Fitting the mask snugly over the nose and mouth
Placing the mask over the mouth only
questions.rationale: The CPAP mask must fit snugly over the nose and mouth to keep positive pressure in the airways. A loose fit or frequent removal loses the pressure.
explanations: A loose fit loses the positive pressure.
Correct: a snug seal maintains airway pressure.
The mask must cover the nose and mouth.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 433)

questions.stem: A central venous catheter has just been inserted. Before starting the IV infusion, what is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Central line insertion can puncture the lung and cause a pneumothorax. A chest x-ray detects this and confirms catheter tip placement before IV therapy begins.
explanations: Important, but not the priority safety check.
Infection would not show this early.
Correct: rules out pneumothorax and confirms placement.
Important, but secondary to confirming placement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 200)

questions.stem: The water-seal chamber of a client's chest drainage system rises and falls with each breath. What should the nurse do?
options: Milk the tubing to remove a clot
Clamp the chest tube right away
Notify the physician of an air leak
questions.rationale: Fluctuation (tidaling) in the water-seal chamber is normal during breathing until the lung re-expands. Its absence may mean an occluded tube or a re-expanded lung; continuous bubbling suggests an air leak.
explanations: Milking is not routinely done and is not needed here.
Clamping can cause a tension pneumothorax.
Continuous bubbling, not tidaling, suggests an air leak.
Correct: tidaling is a normal finding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 323)

questions.stem: A client with depression is prescribed tranylcypromine, an MAO inhibitor. Which food should the nurse teach the client to avoid?
questions.rationale: MAO inhibitors can cause a hypertensive crisis with tyramine-rich foods: aged cheeses, figs, bananas, sauerkraut, avocados, soybeans, and fermented, smoked, or aged meats and fish.
explanations: Correct: aged cheese is high in tyramine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q12 (PDF p. 150)

questions.stem: A child is brought to the emergency room after swallowing many paracetamol (acetaminophen) tablets. Which antidote does the nurse prepare?
questions.rationale: Acetylcysteine is the antidote for acetaminophen overdose. Vitamin K reverses warfarin, protamine reverses heparin, and succimer treats lead poisoning.
explanations: Vitamin K is the antidote for warfarin.
Protamine is the antidote for heparin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q75 (PDF p. 220)

questions.stem: A client suddenly stopped long-term benzodiazepine therapy. Which findings of withdrawal should the nurse expect?
options: Excessive sleepiness and low blood pressure
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepine withdrawal causes tremor, sweating, agitation, nervousness, insomnia, anorexia, and cramps. After high-dose use it can progress to delirium, hypertension, and seizures.
explanations: Lethargy is not part of withdrawal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q195 (PDF p. 349)

questions.stem: A client is started on amitriptyline for depression. Which common side effect should the nurse monitor for?
questions.rationale: Tricyclic antidepressants commonly cause drowsiness, fatigue, and sedation, along with anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation) and hypotension.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q341 (PDF p. 509)

questions.stem: The nurse is about to inject IV hydralazine for a client in hypertensive crisis. Which item must be in place?
options: A blood pressure cuff at the bedside
A cooling blanket on the bed
questions.rationale: Hydralazine lowers blood pressure quickly, so BP and pulse are monitored frequently after it is given. A peripheral IV is enough.
explanations: A central line is not necessary.
Correct: frequent BP monitoring is required.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q436 (PDF p. 614)

questions.stem: A client on oral buspirone for anxiety says the tablets are hard to swallow. What should the nurse advise?
options: Crush the tablets before taking them
Swallow the tablet whole in applesauce
Stop the drug until the next checkup
questions.rationale: Buspirone tablets may be crushed and taken without regard to meals. There is no liquid form, and stopping the drug is not appropriate.
explanations: A whole tablet is still hard to swallow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q636 (PDF p. 854)

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking clorazepate for an anxiety disorder?
options: 'Call your doctor if you feel any drowsiness.'
'Change positions slowly, since dizziness can occur.'
'Take it with grapefruit juice for absorption.'
questions.rationale: Dizziness is a side effect, so the client rises slowly from lying to sitting to standing. Drowsiness lessens with continued use, and smoking reduces the drug's effectiveness.
explanations: Drowsiness is expected and decreases over time.
Correct: dizziness is a side effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q651 (PDF p. 869)

questions.stem: A client on clonazepam develops slurred speech, confusion, and slowed breathing. The nurse suspects:
options: An expected effect that fades in weeks
questions.rationale: Clonazepam toxicity causes slurred speech, sedation, confusion, respiratory depression, hypotension, and eventually coma. Mild drowsiness lessens with use, but these signs are not expected.
explanations: These are toxic, not expected, effects.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q722 (PDF p. 944)

questions.stem: Which statement by a client on lithium shows understanding of the home regimen?
options: 'I will keep normal salt in my diet.'
'I will keep the tablets in the refrigerator.'
'I will take extra doses when I feel low.'
questions.rationale: Lithium replaces sodium in the cells and increases sodium excretion. Clients keep a normal sodium intake and drink at least 1 to 1.5 L of fluid daily; low sodium raises lithium levels.
explanations: Fluids should be adequate, not restricted.
Correct: steady sodium intake prevents toxicity.
It is stored at room temperature.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q777 (PDF p. 1007)

questions.stem: The family of a client on an antipsychotic is taught to watch for pseudoparkinsonism. Which signs should they report?
options: Restlessness and inability to sit still
questions.rationale: Pseudoparkinsonism is an extrapyramidal effect: stooped posture, shuffling gait, masklike face, drooling, tremors, and pill-rolling. High fever suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q778 (PDF p. 1008)

questions.stem: A client on tranylcypromine asks which snack is safe. Which food can the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: On an MAO inhibitor, tyramine foods are avoided: yogurt, raisins, smoked or pickled fish and meat, beer, wine, caffeine, avocados, bananas, plums. Oranges are allowed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q779 (PDF p. 1009)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia on an antipsychotic is going home. Which health-promotion instruction should the nurse include?
options: Avoid long exposure to the sun
questions.rationale: Antipsychotics cause photosensitivity, so prolonged sun exposure is avoided. Tyramine restriction is for MAOIs, and routine blood levels are for lithium.
explanations: Antipsychotics are not used for depression here.
Blood levels are monitored for lithium.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q800 (PDF p. 1030)

questions.stem: When should a client take fluoxetine for depression?
questions.rationale: Fluoxetine is taken in the early morning without regard to meals. Taking it later can cause insomnia.
explanations: It must be taken daily, not as needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q850 (PDF p. 1087)

questions.stem: A client is admitted with panic disorder. Which benzodiazepine does the nurse expect to be prescribed?
questions.rationale: Alprazolam, a benzodiazepine anxiolytic, depresses the CNS and promotes relaxation in panic disorder. The other drugs are antidepressants.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1004 (PDF p. 1255)

questions.stem: A client on imipramine reports increasing drowsiness and fatigue. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: A sign that anxiety is decreasing
A reason to double the dose
questions.rationale: Drowsiness, lethargy, and fatigue on imipramine are adverse effects to report. Expected effects include better appetite and sleep, less anxiety, and a better sense of well-being.
explanations: The dose is never changed by the client.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1011 (PDF p. 1262)

questions.stem: A client on dextroamphetamine has trouble falling asleep. When should the client take the drug?
options: Only on nights of poor sleep
questions.rationale: Dextroamphetamine is a CNS stimulant. Taking it at least 6 hours before bedtime prevents sleep problems. Caffeine should also be avoided.
explanations: Correct: at least 6 hours before bed.
Stimulants do not treat poor sleep.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1092 (PDF p. 1375)

questions.stem: A client admitted after fainting is on olanzapine. For which condition is this drug most likely prescribed?
questions.rationale: Olanzapine is an atypical antipsychotic and a first-line treatment for schizophrenia, targeting positive and negative symptoms. It can cause orthostatic hypotension, so clients rise slowly.
explanations: Correct: an atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1260 (PDF p. 1561)

questions.stem: Which finding in a client on haloperidol is an ADVERSE effect that should be reported?
questions.rationale: Antipsychotic adverse effects include extrapyramidal symptoms such as parkinsonism (drooling), dystonia, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia. Nausea, hypotension, and blurred vision are occasional side effects.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1265 (PDF p. 1566)

questions.stem: A client with ventricular dysrhythmia receives an IV bolus of lidocaine. What should the nurse monitor MOST closely?
questions.rationale: During an IV lidocaine bolus, the nurse monitors respiratory status and blood pressure. The apical pulse is preferred over the radial.
explanations: Correct: lidocaine can depress BP and breathing.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1290 (PDF p. 1591)

questions.stem: A client with acute myocardial infarction is receiving alteplase. Which finding suggests a complication?
questions.rationale: Bleeding, superficial or internal, is the main adverse effect of thrombolytic therapy. A nosebleed is a sign of it.
explanations: Not a typical complication of alteplase.
Expected in MI; not a drug complication.
Not a typical complication of alteplase.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1357 (PDF p. 1660)

questions.stem: A client on phenelzine suddenly has a severe occipital headache, stiff neck, sweating, and very high BP. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
