questions.rationale: These are signs of an MAOI hypertensive crisis. Phentolamine given IV is the antidote.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1375 (PDF p. 1678)

questions.stem: A child with ADHD is prescribed methylphenidate. When should the mother give it?
questions.rationale: Methylphenidate is a CNS stimulant given before breakfast and before lunch. Afternoon or evening doses cause insomnia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1399 (PDF p. 1703)

questions.stem: Sertraline is prescribed for a client with depression. Which finding should make the nurse consult the prescriber first?
questions.rationale: Sertraline with an MAOI can cause serious, possibly fatal reactions. An MAOI must be stopped at least 14 days before sertraline, and vice versa.
explanations: Correct: SSRI plus MAOI is dangerous.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1422 (PDF p. 1728)

questions.stem: IV lorazepam is prescribed. Which item in the client's history should make the nurse consult the prescriber first?
questions.rationale: Lorazepam is contraindicated in narrow-angle glaucoma, coma, existing CNS depression, uncontrolled severe pain, and pregnancy or breastfeeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1429 (PDF p. 1738)

questions.stem: Which baseline laboratory tests does the nurse expect before a client starts risperidone?
questions.rationale: Baseline renal and liver function tests are done before risperidone, which is used cautiously in renal or hepatic impairment.
explanations: Lithium levels are for lithium therapy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1431 (PDF p. 1740)

questions.stem: A client has received tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). Which item should the nurse keep at hand as part of standard care?
questions.rationale: tPA dissolves clots, and bleeding is a frequent adverse effect. The nurse tests urine, stool, and NG drainage for occult blood.
explanations: Useful, but not specific to the risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1468 (PDF p. 1777)

questions.stem: The nurse has just given a dose of diazepam. What is MOST important before leaving the room?
options: Place a bedpan within easy reach
Tell the client to call for help
questions.rationale: Diazepam commonly causes dizziness, drowsiness, and lethargy, so the nurse puts safety measures in place: side rails up and assistance when getting out of bed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1473 (PDF p. 1782)

questions.stem: Which statement about buspirone should the nurse include in client teaching?
options: It carries a high risk of addiction
questions.rationale: Buspirone's side effects (dizziness, nausea, headache, lightheadedness) are usually minor. Unlike benzodiazepines, it is not addicting, tolerance does not develop, and it is not strongly sedating.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1483 (PDF p. 1792)

questions.stem: A client with Tourette's syndrome receives haloperidol decanoate. How does this drug act?
options: It blocks dopamine receptors in the brain
questions.rationale: Haloperidol decanoate is a long-acting antipsychotic that blocks dopamine at postsynaptic receptors. Fluoxetine blocks serotonin reuptake, donepezil inhibits acetylcholine breakdown, and imipramine blocks norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1490 (PDF p. 1799)

questions.stem: When should a client take a single daily dose of imipramine?
questions.rationale: Imipramine causes fatigue and drowsiness, so a single daily dose is taken at bedtime. Alcohol is avoided, and effects may take at least 2 weeks to appear.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1496 (PDF p. 1805)

questions.stem: A client is on clozapine. Which laboratory value is the PRIORITY to monitor?
questions.rationale: Clozapine can cause agranulocytosis and leukopenia. The WBC count is checked before treatment and closely during it, and the client is watched for sore throat and fever.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1545 (PDF p. 1857)

questions.stem: A client with known panic disorder arrives saying, 'Help me, I think I'm having a heart attack.' What is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Panic disorder can cause chest pain and palpitations, but a physical cause must be ruled out first. The nurse assesses the physical condition before anything else.
explanations: Correct: rule out a physiological cause first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q56 (PDF p. 197)

questions.stem: Which belief does the nurse expect to find in a client with bulimia nervosa?
options: She overeats when she loses control
questions.rationale: Bulimia involves cycles of binge eating followed by purging, which the client views as acceptable. Binge eating without purging is seen in obesity.
explanations: Correct: purging is seen as acceptable.
More typical of an obese binge eater.
More typical of an obese binge eater.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q164 (PDF p. 315)

questions.situation: Jasmine, 16, is admitted with anorexia nervosa. She is very thin and is constantly worried about gaining weight.
questions.stem: The nurse finds Jasmine doing vigorous push-ups in her room. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop her and weigh her now
Ignore it to avoid a power struggle
questions.rationale: Clients with anorexia often exercise rigorously to burn off calories. The nurse provides appropriate exercise and sets limits on excessive activity. Weighing her would reinforce her altered self-concept.
explanations: Correct: limit excess activity and offer appropriate exercise.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q167 (PDF p. 320)

questions.situation: Jasmine, 16, is admitted with anorexia nervosa. She is very thin and is constantly worried about gaining weight.
questions.stem: Which statement by Jasmine is the PRIORITY for further assessment?
questions.rationale: Exercising 3 to 4 hours daily is excessive and unrealistic for a 16-year-old and needs immediate follow-up. Daily weighing is common in anorexia.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q880 (PDF p. 1120)

questions.stem: Which finding supports a diagnosis of SEVERE depression?
questions.rationale: Severe depression typically brings weight loss and insomnia, a flat affect, and statements like 'I have no more tears.' Mild depression may bring weight gain and hypersomnia.
explanations: Severely depressed clients may have no tears left.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q309 (PDF p. 473)

questions.stem: Two days after admission for moderate depression, a client suddenly smiles and says the crisis is over. What should the nurse do?
options: Allow more time alone in room
questions.rationale: Such a quick 'cure' is unlikely. A sudden lift in mood may mean the client has decided on self-harm, so suicide precautions are needed.
explanations: Correct: a sudden mood lift may signal a suicide plan.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q414 (PDF p. 591)

questions.stem: When should the nurse add extra precautions for a client with suicidal ideation?
questions.rationale: Fewer staff are available at shift change, so precautions increase then. Nights and weekends are also high-risk times.
explanations: Weekends, not weekdays, are higher risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q415 (PDF p. 592)

questions.stem: An older adult is identified as a victim of psychological abuse at home. What is the PRIORITY nursing action?
options: Call a social worker for the family
Remove her from the abusive setting
questions.rationale: The priority is to remove the victim from the abusive environment. Treatment, reporting, and case work also follow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q425 (PDF p. 602)

questions.stem: A client admitted with suicidal ideation is about to go home. Which family statement may justify delaying discharge?
options: 'Does he know I've moved out and filed for separation?'
'I postponed my wedding so he can attend.'
'We set up his room just like before.'
questions.rationale: Separated, divorced, and widowed people have higher suicide rates. Unknown news of a separation is a serious stressor for a client with suicidal ideation.
explanations: Correct: a major new loss raises suicide risk.
Can make him feel included and valued.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q591 (PDF p. 799)

questions.stem: A client with mania comes out of her room topless, making lewd gestures. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Quietly escort her to her room to dress
Give her a time-out as a consequence
questions.rationale: Mania impairs insight, judgment, and impulse control. The nurse takes control calmly without adding stress. Confrontation or insisting may cause resistance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q803 (PDF p. 1037)

questions.stem: After witnessing a friend's murder, a client has trouble concentrating, angry outbursts, and feels 'keyed up.' What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: PTSD follows a markedly distressing event. It causes sustained anxiety, sleep problems, irritability, poor concentration, and angry outbursts.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q820 (PDF p. 1054)

questions.stem: Which therapeutic action belongs in the care plan for an 11-year-old who was physically abused?
options: Have the child confront the abuser
Provide a setting that builds trust
Teach the child to avoid abuse
Tell the child it wasn't serious
questions.rationale: Abused children need long-term support in an environment that models trust and empathy, where healing can begin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q830 (PDF p. 1066)

questions.stem: A 14-year-old with burns and bruises says, 'I'm afraid to go home; my stepfather will be angry I told.' What is the BEST response?
questions.rationale: An abused child is admitted for a full evaluation and protection. An empathic statement assures the child of safety and supports them as the victim.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q837 (PDF p. 1073)

questions.stem: Which question is MOST important when assessing a client's suicide risk?
options: 'Why do you want to hurt yourself?'
'Do you have a plan to hurt yourself?'
'Has anyone in your family died by suicide?'
questions.rationale: A client with a definite plan is at greater risk. 'Why' questions put the client on the defensive.
explanations: 'Why' puts the client on the defensive.
Correct: a plan indicates higher risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q845 (PDF p. 1082)

questions.stem: Which is an EXPECTED short-term side effect of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)?
questions.rationale: The main expected side effects of ECT are confusion, disorientation, and memory loss. Hypertension or palpitations are concerning and are reported.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q846 (PDF p. 1083)

questions.situation: Mang Danilo, 35, is admitted in the manic phase of bipolar disorder. He is restless, talks nonstop, and sleeps very little.
questions.stem: Which meal is BEST for Mang Danilo?
options: Beef stew with fruit salad and tea
Macaroni with a fork and coffee
questions.rationale: A client in mania is too active to sit through meals and often under-eats. Finger foods he can eat 'on the run' are best, and caffeine is avoided.
explanations: Needs utensils, and tea has caffeine.
Correct: high-calorie finger foods, no caffeine.
Needs utensils, and coffee has caffeine.
Needs utensils, and coffee has caffeine.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q853 (PDF p. 1090)

questions.situation: Mang Danilo, 35, is admitted in the manic phase of bipolar disorder. He is restless, talks nonstop, and sleeps very little.
questions.stem: Mang Danilo starts organizing a dance for the whole unit at suppertime. What should the nurse encourage instead?
options: Asking other staff to help organize
A quiet, solitary activity like writing
questions.rationale: A manic client is easily stimulated by the environment, so quiet, solitary activities such as writing are the best outlet for his energy. A newly admitted client is likely to have impaired judgment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q857 (PDF p. 1094)

questions.stem: An abused child copes by using repression. Which activity should the nurse include in the plan?
options: Therapeutic play to act out experiences
Telling the child to forget the past
Avoiding any talk of the abuse
questions.rationale: Therapeutic play with art, dolls, or puppets is a nonthreatening way for a child to act out frightening experiences. The other options threaten the child or force further repression.
explanations: Correct: a safe outlet for trauma.
Devalues the child and forces repression.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q854 (PDF p. 1091)

questions.stem: An older client living with family arrives with poor hygiene, contractures, and multiple pressure ulcers. Which form of victimization is suspected?
questions.rationale: Physical abuse can be battering or the subtler neglect, a failure to meet basic needs. Poor hygiene, contractures, and pressure ulcers point to neglect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q855 (PDF p. 1092)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia says, 'I am Elizabeth, the Queen of England.' What is this?
questions.rationale: A delusion is a firmly held false belief that resists change; claiming to be royalty is grandiose. An illusion misreads real stimuli, and a hallucination is a false perception.
explanations: Ideas that shift between unrelated subjects.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q856 (PDF p. 1093)

questions.stem: Why should the nurse initially allow a client with OCD to continue hand-washing rituals?
options: It lowers the risk of infection
questions.rationale: The compulsive act gives immediate relief from anxiety and is used to cope with stress. Stopping it abruptly would increase anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q858 (PDF p. 1095)

questions.stem: An anxious client is blocking the hallway, taking three steps forward and two back. How should the nurse intervene?
options: Stand beside the client: 'You're very anxious today.'
Tell the client: 'You're going to have to stop that.'
Tell other clients to walk around
Distract the client with a TV show
questions.rationale: To ease anxiety, the nurse helps the client recognize the behavior. Demands or ignoring the behavior may escalate it.
explanations: Correct: helps the client recognize the anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q861 (PDF p. 1098)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In which therapy does the client act out situations of emotional significance?
questions.rationale: Psychodrama involves acting out emotionally charged situations. Psychoanalytic and short-term dynamic therapies draw on psychoanalytic techniques.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q862 (PDF p. 1099)

questions.stem: A manic client who assaulted another client is to be secluded. What should the nurse do BEFORE seclusion?
options: Stay silent to avoid more agitation
Tell her directly why she is being secluded
questions.rationale: Seclusion removes the client to a nonstimulating room for protection and close supervision. The nurse informs the client directly of its purpose; it is never framed as punishment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q863 (PDF p. 1100)

questions.stem: A client with catatonic schizophrenia lies curled in a fetal position. Which approach BEST builds communication?
options: Leave the client alone all day
Sit in silence; ask open questions
Insist the client join group therapy
questions.rationale: Withdrawn clients need consistent, repeated contact. Sitting in silence, asking open-ended questions, and pausing for responses build communication.
explanations: Direct questions are not effective here.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q865 (PDF p. 1102)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: After a gastrostomy tube is placed, a client refuses care, avoids eye contact, and will not talk. Which coping mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Distancing is an unwillingness or inability to discuss events, shown here by withdrawal and refusal to engage.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q870 (PDF p. 1107)

questions.stem: Which is a risk factor for adolescent suicide?
questions.rationale: Risk factors include depression, a family history of mental disorders (especially depression and suicide), past attempts, family violence, substance use, poor school performance, and hopelessness.
explanations: Poor, not good, performance is a risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q872 (PDF p. 1109)

questions.stem: Which intervention is part of suicide precautions for an acutely suicidal client?
questions.rationale: Suicide precautions mean constant observation within arm's length, meal trays without glass or metal silverware, and close watch during all activities.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q875 (PDF p. 1112)

questions.stem: In which situation is seclusion CONTRAINDICATED?
options: A client who asks to be alone
A client who is very agitated
A client after a severe drug overdose
questions.rationale: Seclusion is contraindicated in unstable medical or mental conditions, delirium or dementia, severe suicidal tendencies, and severe drug reactions or overdoses that need close monitoring.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q877 (PDF p. 1115)

questions.stem: An 8-year-old who was sexually abused is withdrawn and frightened. What is the BEST plan for the first encounter?
options: Do a full exam right away
Spend time with her and move slowly
Ask her to describe the abuse
Leave her alone until she talks
questions.rationale: Child victims fear the abuse could happen again. The nurse shows a willingness to spend time and moves slowly before any activity that may feel threatening.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q883 (PDF p. 1123)

questions.stem: Two months after a sexual assault, a survivor says it feels 'like it happened yesterday.' Which response is BEST?
options: 'You should be moving on by now.'
'Tell me more about how you're feeling.'
questions.rationale: An open, unhurried, nonjudgmental invitation lets her express her feelings fully. Correcting her blocks communication, and the other replies are nontherapeutic.
explanations: Shifts the problem-solving burden to her.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q884 (PDF p. 1125)

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give staff caring for a client with paranoid personality disorder?
options: Have him sign a release form
Avoid laughing or whispering near him
questions.rationale: A paranoid client is distrustful and suspicious, and laughing or whispering nearby feeds the paranoia. The other options demand too much trust too soon.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q885 (PDF p. 1126)

questions.stem: A newly admitted client says, 'You won't have to worry about me much longer.' How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: This is a direct comment about not being around, which expresses suicidal intent. All suicidal statements are taken seriously.
explanations: Correct: a covert statement of suicide.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q886 (PDF p. 1128)

questions.stem: High school students in a crisis group are in disbelief after a classmate's suicide. What is the nurse's INITIAL action?
options: Ask how they coped with past losses
Explain the warning signs of suicide
Ask how they see the suicide
Tell them it will get easier
questions.rationale: In crisis intervention, the nurse first finds out how the students perceive the event. This identifies their appraisal of the suicide in the here and now.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q895 (PDF p. 1137)

questions.stem: Which de-escalation technique should the nurse use with an extremely angry, increasingly agitated client?
options: Avoid power struggles; give clear options
Raise your voice to be heard
questions.rationale: De-escalation uses a calm, clear voice, avoids verbal struggles, offers clear options, and preserves the client's self-esteem and dignity.
explanations: Touch may be seen as a threat.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q904 (PDF p. 1147)

questions.stem: A client with cardiomyopathy stops eating, naps for long periods, and turns away when the nurse speaks. What do these behaviors suggest?
questions.rationale: Depression is common in long-term, debilitating illness, and these behaviors fit it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q908 (PDF p. 1151)

questions.stem: After 4 weeks of outpatient care for a rape survivor, which is a REALISTIC short-term goal?
options: Fear and anxiety are fully resolved
She talks about her feelings about the rape
questions.rationale: Short-term goals cover the early stages of coping: keeping appointments, taking part in care, and starting to explore feelings. Resolving fear and anxiety is a long-term goal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q915 (PDF p. 1158)

questions.stem: Which approach belongs in the care plan for a client in acute mania?
options: Use a firm, calm approach with brief statements
questions.rationale: A client in acute mania is restless and disorganized with poor judgment. A firm, calm approach gives structure, and short, concise statements suit her short attention span.
explanations: Too much for a short attention span.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q921 (PDF p. 1164)

questions.stem: A suicidal client says, 'I was up all night. It doesn't seem worth it. Why not just end it all?' Which response BEST assesses further?
options: 'Did you sleep at all last night?'
'Tell me what you mean by that.'
questions.rationale: An open invitation lets the client say more about current thoughts. Changing the subject or giving false reassurance blocks communication.
explanations: Empathic, but does not assess further.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q930 (PDF p. 1174)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client with quadriplegia often makes lewd suggestions and swears, displacing his feelings. Which concern should the nurse identify?
questions.rationale: Displacing feelings onto the environment instead of using them constructively shows an impaired ability to adapt, which is a lack of coping skills.
explanations: Possible, but not tied to displacement.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q942 (PDF p. 1186)

questions.stem: A depressed client says, 'I should have died. I've always been a failure.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You still have a lot to live for.'
'Feeling like a failure is your illness.'
questions.rationale: Restating responds to the feelings the client expressed. The other responses minimize the experience and block exploration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q946 (PDF p. 1191)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia does not speak, although nothing is physically wrong. What is this?
questions.rationale: Mutism is the absence of speech despite an intact physical ability to speak. Verbigeration is purposeless repetition; pressured speech is rapid speech from racing thoughts.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q955 (PDF p. 1201)

questions.stem: A client with schizophrenia says, 'I am a spy. I am an eye, an eye in the sky.' Which thought disorder is this?
questions.rationale: Clang associations are words linked by similar sounds (often rhyming) and nothing else. Echolalia is parrot-like repetition of others' words.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q956 (PDF p. 1203)

questions.stem: Which question is MOST appropriate when assessing a client for suicide?
options: 'Do you wish your life was over?'
'Do you think about ending it all?'
questions.rationale: A lethality assessment needs direct communication about intent. Euphemisms are avoided.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q995 (PDF p. 1246)

questions.stem: A client in severe anxiety arrives at the emergency room. What is the PRIORITY nursing action?
options: Leave the client to calm down
questions.rationale: Left alone in severe anxiety, the client may feel abandoned and overwhelmed. A quiet room helps, but the nurse stays. Teaching is not possible until anxiety decreases.
explanations: Correct: presence prevents feelings of abandonment.
Cannot learn at this anxiety level.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1016 (PDF p. 1289)

questions.stem: A withdrawn, depressed client caused a road accident that killed a child. What is the nurse's INITIAL action?
options: Say it was only an accident
Note he seems sad; invite him to talk
questions.rationale: The nurse first encourages the client to express feelings, validating that he seems depressed, within a respectful nurse-client relationship. This also lets the nurse assess the situation.
explanations: Isolation is not the first step.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1025 (PDF p. 1298)

questions.stem: During a bed bath, the client starts to cry. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop, cover the client, and sit with them
Stop and leave the client alone
questions.rationale: The nurse stays, lets the client know it is all right to cry, and asks what they are feeling. Continuing or leaving ignores the client's feelings, and crying alone does not mean depression.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1026 (PDF p. 1299)

questions.stem: Which intervention creates a caring, therapeutic setting for a newly admitted suicidal client?
options: Limiting staff contact to give space
Focusing only on the suicide attempt
questions.rationale: Unconditional positive regard accepts the person, though not the behavior, and raises the client's sense of self-worth. A private room would reduce observation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1028 (PDF p. 1301)

questions.stem: Which activity belongs to the ORIENTATION phase of the nurse-client relationship?
options: Agreeing on a contract for time
questions.rationale: In the orientation phase, the nurse and client agree on a contract: how often to meet, how long, and when termination is expected. The other activities belong to the working phase.
explanations: Correct: the contract is set at orientation.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1031 (PDF p. 1304)

questions.stem: A client with delirium anxiously says, 'Look at the spiders on the wall.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Shall I kill the spiders for you?'
'I know you're scared, but I see no spiders.'
'There are no spiders. Go to sleep.'
questions.rationale: With hallucinations, the nurse reinforces reality while acknowledging the client's feelings. The other replies support the hallucination or dismiss the fear.
explanations: Correct: acknowledges fear and presents reality.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1040 (PDF p. 1314)

questions.stem: Which assessment focuses on the VEGETATIVE signs of depression?
questions.rationale: Vegetative signs are physiological changes in depression: appetite, weight, sleep patterns, and psychomotor activity. The others are psychological categories.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1101 (PDF p. 1385)

questions.stem: For a client with anorexia nervosa, what should health promotion PRIMARILY focus on?
questions.rationale: Health promotion helps the client identify and examine dysfunctional thoughts and the values and beliefs that maintain them. A supportive environment matters but is not primary.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1152 (PDF p. 1439)

questions.stem: Which discharge intervention gives a client who attempted suicide an IMMEDIATE resource?
options: A list of phone numbers only
questions.rationale: Crises can happen between appointments. A contract with available crisis resources gives the client responsibility and control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1153 (PDF p. 1440)

questions.stem: Which nutritional goal is appropriate for a client with dementia?
options: Feeds self with cueing in 24 hours
questions.rationale: The goal is directly tied to the client's self-care ability. Dementia impairs memory and judgment, so cueing supports self-feeding.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1157 (PDF p. 1444)

questions.stem: A shooting survivor says, 'I feel like I'm losing my mind. I keep hearing the shots.' What should the nurse do FIRST to build the relationship?
options: Ask the psychiatrist to see him
Change the topic to calm him
questions.rationale: Building a therapeutic relationship starts with acknowledging and validating the client's feelings. Relaxation teaching may help later.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1160 (PDF p. 1447)

questions.stem: Which is a major self-help organization for people with alcohol use disorder?
questions.rationale: Alcoholics Anonymous is a major self-help group for people with alcoholism. Al-Anon supports families of alcoholics.
explanations: Correct: for the person with alcoholism.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1174 (PDF p. 1463)

questions.stem: A client with OCD often misses morning activities because of a bed-making ritual. Which response is therapeutic?
options: Discuss how it looks to others
Help make the bed so it is faster
Give reflective feedback on the behavior
questions.rationale: Reflective feedback acknowledges the behavior. Disapproval increases anxiety and the need for the ritual, and helping reinforces it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1185 (PDF p. 1476)

questions.stem: After a month of family counseling, which statement by the abusive family member of an older client shows healthier coping?
options: 'I'll quit my job to care for him.'
questions.rationale: Elder abuse often comes from caregiver strain. Knowing where to turn for help with an aging relative brings relief and is a positive coping skill.
explanations: An apology, not a coping skill.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1215 (PDF p. 1508)

questions.stem: Which statement by a secluded client shows seclusion is no longer needed?
options: 'I want to be alone in my room.'
questions.rationale: A client who says they are in control may be safely released. Physical needs are met during seclusion, which is assessed every 15 to 30 minutes.
explanations: A physical need, met with a bedpan or commode.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1242 (PDF p. 1535)

questions.stem: Which behavior BEST suggests that a client at risk is contemplating suicide?
questions.rationale: Sudden happiness or contentment often means a suicide plan has been made. The others indicate depression but are less definitive.
explanations: Correct: may signal a decided plan.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1259 (PDF p. 1560)

questions.stem: Which statement about abusers in family violence is INACCURATE?
options: They are mostly from low-income families
questions.rationale: Abusers are often immature, dependent, insecure, and jealous, with low self-esteem, and use fear and intimidation. Abuse is not more common in low-income families.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1267 (PDF p. 1568)

questions.stem: Which statement by a new nurse about suicide is ACCURATE?
questions.rationale: Most people who die by suicide give definite clues or warnings. The other statements are myths.
explanations: A myth; every attempt is serious.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1269 (PDF p. 1570)

questions.stem: A client wanders into others' rooms taking things, singing and giggling for no reason. Which response is therapeutic?
options: Hug him: 'You just need a hug.'
'I can see you're very anxious today.'
questions.rationale: Regression is a defense against anxiety. Recognizing it as a sign of anxiety, and saying so, is the therapeutic response.
explanations: Ignores the anxiety behind the behavior.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1270 (PDF p. 1571)

questions.stem: Which is PRIMARY subjective data in a newly admitted psychiatric client?
options: The client says she has a headache
A relative says she got into a fight
questions.rationale: Subjective data are described by the client, who is the primary source. Measurements are objective, and reports from family or police are secondary sources.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1303 (PDF p. 1604)

questions.stem: A client wakes after electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Move the client to a wheelchair
Orient the client and check vital signs
questions.rationale: The nurse first checks vital signs, orients the client, and explains that the client just had ECT. Oxygen, suction, and emergency equipment are kept at hand.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1477 (PDF p. 1786)

questions.stem: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is suspected in a client on an antipsychotic. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?
questions.rationale: Bromocriptine, a dopamine agonist, treats neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Protamine reverses heparin, and vitamin K reverses warfarin.
explanations: Correct: a dopamine agonist for NMS.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1485 (PDF p. 1794)

questions.stem: Why is the admission physical assessment of a suicidal client a PRIORITY?
options: To look for evidence of self-harm
questions.rationale: The assessment focuses on evidence of self-harm or a plan. Clients with a history of self-harm are at greater suicide risk.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1511 (PDF p. 1820)

questions.stem: After medical treatment, what is the PRIORITY for a client who was recently sexually assaulted?
options: Securing support and a safety plan
questions.rationale: After medical treatment, the next priority is obtaining support and planning for safety. Counseling and legal guidance meet later needs.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1529 (PDF p. 1839)

questions.stem: A client's telemetry shows ventricular tachycardia. At the bedside, what should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Checking responsiveness comes first. It shows whether the drop in cardiac output from VT is affecting the client. If unresponsive and pulseless, CPR begins.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q51 (PDF p. 191)

questions.stem: A client has late-stage salicylate poisoning with metabolic acidosis. Which serum value reflects acid-base balance?
questions.rationale: In acidosis, hydrogen ions move into cells and potassium moves out, causing hyperkalemia. Potassium therefore reflects the acid-base state.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q74 (PDF p. 219)

questions.stem: A child with lead poisoning is to receive chelation therapy. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
questions.rationale: EDTA is a chelating agent for lead poisoning. Activated charcoal reduces absorption in some poisonings, and sodium bicarbonate may be used for salicylate poisoning.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q120 (PDF p. 270)

questions.stem: An IV nitroglycerin drip is started for an acute MI without an arterial line. Which bedside equipment ensures safety?
questions.rationale: Nitroglycerin dilates vessels, and its main side effect is hypotension. Without an arterial line, a noninvasive blood pressure monitor is used at the bedside.
explanations: Not specific to the drug's effect.
Not specific to the drug's effect.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q135 (PDF p. 285)

questions.stem: Concentrated IV lidocaine is ordered for ventricular tachycardia. Which solution should the nurse use to dilute it?
questions.rationale: The concentrated formulation of lidocaine must be diluted with 5% dextrose in water. Resuscitation equipment is kept available.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q145 (PDF p. 295)

questions.stem: A client suddenly has chest pain and dyspnea from a pulmonary embolus. How should the nurse position the client?
questions.rationale: Care includes semi-Fowler's position, oxygen, and IV analgesia (usually morphine). High Fowler's is avoided because extreme hip flexion slows venous return and promotes new clots.
explanations: Correct: eases breathing without hip flexion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q149 (PDF p. 299)

questions.stem: PEEP of 7 cm is added to a client's ventilator. Which expected adverse effect should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: PEEP raises intrathoracic pressure and reduces cardiac output, shown by a lower systolic BP and a compensatory rise in pulse.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q220 (PDF p. 375)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a LEFT tension pneumothorax is rapidly worsening?
options: Louder breath sounds on the left
questions.rationale: Tension pneumothorax causes tracheal deviation to the unaffected side, distended neck veins, decreased breath sounds on the affected side, worsening cyanosis, and falling BP.
explanations: Correct: shift away from the affected side.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q224 (PDF p. 379)

questions.stem: A client with flail chest has PaO2 falling from 82 to 68 and PaCO2 rising from 44 to 51 in 2 hours. Which item should be at hand?
questions.rationale: Worsening respiratory acidosis in flail chest shows that the work of breathing is failing. Intubation and mechanical ventilation may be needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q238 (PDF p. 393)

questions.stem: Before giving an opioid through an epidural catheter, the nurse aspirates 5 mL of clear fluid. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Less than 1 mL of clear fluid fits epidural placement. More than 1 mL, or blood, means the catheter may be in the subarachnoid space or a vessel, so the drug is not given.
explanations: Correct: the catheter may be misplaced.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q240 (PDF p. 395)

questions.situation: Mang Berto, 55, is rescued from a burning house and brought to the emergency room with respiratory distress.
questions.stem: Which test BEST shows whether Mang Berto has carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.rationale: Serum carboxyhemoglobin directly measures CO poisoning. CO binds hemoglobin about 200 times more readily than oxygen, so pulse oximetry can be falsely normal.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q264 (PDF p. 421)

questions.situation: Mang Berto, 55, is rescued from a burning house and brought to the emergency room with respiratory distress.
questions.stem: Mang Berto asks to remove his oxygen mask. Below which carboxyhemoglobin level can oxygen be safely removed?
questions.rationale: Oxygen may be removed once carboxyhemoglobin is below 5%. Levels of 10% to 20% cause headache, nausea, and dyspnea.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q246 (PDF p. 401)

questions.stem: A client arrives with upper GI bleeding that began 3 hours ago. What is the PRIORITY action?
questions.rationale: Vital signs show whether the client is in shock from blood loss and give a baseline to track treatment. Subjective data can wait until physical needs are met.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q254 (PDF p. 411)

questions.stem: Which intervention is standard when admitting a client with MI to the coronary care unit?
questions.rationale: Continuous cardiac monitoring is standard on CCU admission. Thrombolytics may or may not be prescribed and work best within the first 6 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q279 (PDF p. 436)

questions.stem: A client with a thoracic spinal cord injury develops spinal shock. Which IV fluid does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Isotonic normal saline stays in the vascular space and raises intravascular volume and BP. Dextran is rarely needed and has adverse effects.
explanations: Does not stay in the vascular space.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q283 (PDF p. 441)

questions.stem: Which assessment BEST shows recovery from spinal shock?
questions.rationale: Spinal shock is marked by areflexia, so the return of reflexes shows recovery. Vital signs vary with many factors.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q307 (PDF p. 471)

questions.stem: Which finding is an EARLY sign that a cerebral aneurysm has ruptured?
questions.rationale: Rupture raises intracranial pressure, and the first sign is a change in level of consciousness, even subtle drowsiness or restlessness. Vital sign changes come later.
explanations: Correct: the earliest sign of rising ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q308 (PDF p. 472)

questions.stem: A home care nurse finds a client with a history of sertraline misuse unconscious. What should the nurse assess IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: In an emergency, the nurse checks for breathing first, then pulse. Blood pressure and urine output come later.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q311 (PDF p. 475)

questions.stem: A unit of blood from the blood bank has gas bubbles in the bag. What should the nurse do?
options: Return it to the blood bank
questions.rationale: Gas bubbles suggest contamination, so the unit is returned. Nothing is ever added to blood, and filter tubing is always used.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q312 (PDF p. 476)

questions.stem: What is the SMALLEST IV catheter gauge acceptable for a blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: A 20-gauge or larger catheter prevents hemolysis of red cells and allows blood to flow without occluding the catheter.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q313 (PDF p. 477)

questions.stem: Which intervention belongs in the care plan for a client with a dissecting abdominal aortic aneurysm?
options: Teach that abdominal pain is expected
Encourage heavy lifting to regain strength
questions.rationale: The concern is rupture. The nurse checks peripheral circulation, watches for abdominal distention and lower-back ecchymoses, and has the client report abdominal pain.
explanations: Raises the pressure on the aneurysm.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q323 (PDF p. 488)

questions.stem: A client is bleeding freely from a scalp laceration after a fall. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask about the last tetanus shot
questions.rationale: The first action is to stop the bleeding with direct pressure. The wound is then cleaned, assessed for suturing, and the tetanus status checked.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q330 (PDF p. 496)

questions.situation: Rodel, 22, is brought to the emergency room after a motorcycle crash with a possible closed head injury.
questions.stem: Which assessment should the nurse perform FIRST?
questions.rationale: The nurse first ensures an adequate airway and breathing, then circulation, then neurologic status.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q332 (PDF p. 498)

questions.situation: Rodel, 22, is brought to the emergency room after a motorcycle crash with a possible closed head injury.
questions.stem: Six hours later, Rodel begins vomiting and reports dizziness and headache. What is the MOST important action?
options: Let him rest in the dark
questions.rationale: Headache, dizziness, and vomiting after a head injury suggest rising intracranial pressure, so the provider is notified at once.
explanations: Masks a sign of rising ICP.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q331 (PDF p. 497)

questions.stem: A client is admitted after an overdose of an antipsychotic. What information is MOST important to obtain first?
options: Where and when it was taken
questions.rationale: In an emergency, lifesaving facts come first. The name and amount of drug taken guide treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q343 (PDF p. 511)

questions.stem: Which is the MOST common complication after myocardial infarction?
questions.rationale: Dysrhythmias are the most common complication and cause of death after MI. The others occur less often.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q355 (PDF p. 523)

questions.stem: Which finding at an IV site suggests infiltration?
options: Warm, red skin along the vein
questions.rationale: Infiltration is IV fluid leaking into tissue. It slows the rate and causes tenderness, swelling, skin tightness, and cool, blanched skin.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q357 (PDF p. 525)

questions.stem: A client has acute cardiac and cerebral symptoms from fluid volume excess. Which measure increases comfort until therapy is ordered?
options: Raise the head of the bed to 45°
questions.rationale: Raising the head of the bed to 45 degrees reduces venous return to the heart and improves venous drainage from the brain. Oxygen needs a prescription.
explanations: Correct: reduces cardiac and cerebral load.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q360 (PDF p. 528)

questions.stem: After CABG, mediastinal chest tube drainage drops from 75 mL in hour 1 to 5 mL in hour 2. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: About 500 mL is expected in the first 24 hours, up to 100 to 150 mL per hour early on. A sudden drop suggests the tube may be occluded, which can cause cardiac tamponade.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q396 (PDF p. 566)

questions.stem: A client with silicosis has impending respiratory failure. Which equipment should be at the bedside?
questions.rationale: When compensatory mechanisms fail in respiratory failure, intubation and mechanical ventilation may be needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q434 (PDF p. 612)

questions.stem: A continuous IV regular insulin infusion is ordered for a blood glucose of 700 mg/dL. How should it be given safely?
options: Run it on an infusion pump
Give it as an IV bolus
questions.rationale: An infusion pump prevents accidental overdose and hypoglycemia. Dextrose is added only once glucose falls to about 250 mg/dL.
explanations: Counteracts the treatment at this level.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q443 (PDF p. 623)

questions.stem: Synchronized cardioversion is planned for atrial fibrillation. Which action prevents a dangerous complication?
questions.rationale: In cardioversion, the shock is synchronized with the QRS complex so it does not fall during repolarization (the T wave), which could trigger ventricular fibrillation. Less energy is used than in defibrillation.
explanations: Less energy is used than in defibrillation.
Correct: synchronize with the QRS complex.
A shock on the T wave can cause VF.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q470 (PDF p. 654)

questions.stem: Twenty-four hours after a laryngectomy, bright red blood starts draining from the tracheostomy. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: A little bleeding right after surgery is expected and resolves within hours. Later bright red bleeding may mean a vessel is about to rupture, so the surgeon is notified.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q524 (PDF p. 720)

questions.stem: A client with a C6 spinal cord injury in spinal shock is getting up to a chair. What should the nurse do?
options: Apply knee splints for the transfer
Teach locking the knees while pivoting
Raise the head gradually before rising
Stand him up quickly in one move
questions.rationale: Spinal shock often brings lower-limb vasodilation and a drop in BP on rising. A gradual increase in head elevation prevents dizziness and fainting.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q557 (PDF p. 758)

questions.stem: During a code, the physician about to defibrillate says loudly, 'CLEAR!' What should the nurse do immediately?
options: Step back from the client and bed
questions.rationale: For everyone's safety, all personnel stand back and avoid any contact with the client or bed when the shock is delivered.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q568 (PDF p. 773)

questions.stem: What starting energy range is usually used for cardioversion with a monophasic defibrillator?
questions.rationale: Cardioversion, a synchronized countershock, usually starts at 50 to 100 joules, as prescribed. The higher ranges are too high for cardioversion.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q573 (PDF p. 778)

questions.stem: A spouse manages home IV lipid infusions. What should the spouse do FIRST if an adverse reaction is suspected?
questions.rationale: Signs of a lipid reaction include chest and back pain, chills, dyspnea, fever, flushing, and nausea. The priority is to stop the infusion to limit the reaction.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q712 (PDF p. 934)

questions.stem: The family of a client in cardiogenic shock is very anxious. Which nursing action BEST supports them?
options: Insist they go home to sleep
questions.rationale: Flexible visiting hours reduce anxiety for both the client and the family. Insisting they leave is nontherapeutic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q981 (PDF p. 1230)

questions.stem: A ventilated client with respiratory failure is about to be weaned. Which comfort measure should now be LIMITED?
questions.rationale: Antianxiety drugs and opioids can suppress the respiratory drive and interfere with weaning. Distractions such as radio, TV, and family help with anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q985 (PDF p. 1234)

questions.stem: Before IV insertion, a tense preoperative client says she does not understand why she needs an IV. What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: Simple, clear information about the IV's purpose addresses her concern. Promising no pain is false, and dismissing her feelings blocks communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q991 (PDF p. 1241)

questions.stem: A ventilator's HIGH-pressure alarm sounds. Which is a possible cause?
questions.rationale: The high-pressure alarm sounds when peak pressure reaches the limit: kinked tubing, the client fighting the ventilator, secretions or a mucus plug, or the client biting the tube. Disconnection and cuff leaks trigger low-pressure alarms.
explanations: Not a cause of high pressure.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1245 (PDF p. 1538)

questions.stem: Which action helps PREVENT ventilator-associated pneumonia?
questions.rationale: Intubation bypasses upper airway defenses. Prevention includes careful hand hygiene and keeping the head of the bed raised (30 to 45 degrees) to prevent aspiration.
explanations: Suctioning should be more frequent as needed.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1268 (PDF p. 1569)

questions.stem: A client with severe radiating chest pain is restless and dyspneic. Orders include oxygen at 4 L/min, cardiac enzymes, chest x-ray, and a 12-lead ECG. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Oxygen comes first to limit damage from possible myocardial ischemia. The ECG and blood work follow shortly.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1278 (PDF p. 1579)

questions.stem: Which PVC finding after antidysrhythmic therapy shows the treatment is INEFFECTIVE?
options: PVCs falling after the T wave
questions.rationale: PVCs are dangerous when frequent (over 6 per minute), in pairs, multifocal, or falling on the T wave. The provider is notified.
explanations: PVCs on the T wave are dangerous; after it is less concerning.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1299 (PDF p. 1600)

questions.stem: A ventilated client with a fat embolus is visibly anxious. What should the nurse do?
options: Ask family to stay at all times
questions.rationale: The nurse speaks calmly and reassures the anxious client. Asking family to stay constantly burdens them, and sleep does not relieve anxiety.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1512 (PDF p. 1822)

questions.stem: The ECG complexes on the monitor are very small and hard to read. Which setting should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: The amplitude or 'gain' setting controls complex size and can be adjusted up or down.
explanations: Turns the machine on or off.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1298 (PDF p. 1599)

questions.stem: Continuous bubbling appears in the water-seal chamber of a chest drainage system. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling through inspiration and expiration means air is leaking into the system. A resolving pneumothorax causes intermittent bubbling.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1321 (PDF p. 1623)

questions.stem: The water-seal chamber fluid is below the 2-cm mark. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The water seal must be at 2 cm to keep air from re-entering the pleural space. Water evaporates, so the nurse refills it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1351 (PDF p. 1654)

questions.stem: Why is positive-pressure ventilation given during electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)?
questions.rationale: A short-acting muscle relaxant is given to prevent injury during the seizure, so ventilation is supported until it wears off, usually within 2 to 3 minutes.
explanations: Correct: the relaxant affects the breathing muscles.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1272 (PDF p. 1573)

questions.stem: Which behavior in a disaster survivor suggests post-traumatic stress disorder?
questions.rationale: PTSD is a sustained maladaptive response to trauma: flashbacks, recurrent dreams, irritability, sleep problems, detachment from others, and repressed memories.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q664 (PDF p. 883)

questions.stem: A charge nurse hears a nursing attendant shouting at a client with delirium. What is the PRIORITY action?
options: Tell the client all is well
Correct the attendant in the room
questions.rationale: The nurse first makes sure the client is safe, then talks to the attendant away from the client, who could become more confused or agitated.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q891 (PDF p. 1133)

questions.stem: A withdrawn client with end-stage heart failure won't join care. Which staff statement shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: A 'why' question asks for an explanation the client may not have, so it is nontherapeutic. The others acknowledge, explore feelings, or invite elaboration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1418 (PDF p. 1724)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which is a goal of palliative care?
questions.rationale: Palliative care is total care. It relieves pain and other distressing symptoms, supports the client to live as actively as possible, and neither hastens nor delays death.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q91 (PDF p. 239)

questions.stem: Which respiratory finding suggests that death is imminent?
questions.rationale: Imminent death shows poor gas exchange (dyspnea, cyanosis) and altered breathing such as slow, labored, irregular, or Cheyne-Stokes respiration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q154 (PDF p. 304)

questions.stem: A deceased client will donate his eyes. What care is usually prescribed?
options: Saline gauze and a small ice pack
questions.rationale: The eyes are closed and covered with saline-moistened gauze and a small ice pack. Enucleation follows within 2 to 4 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q458 (PDF p. 640)

questions.stem: Which finding is a contraindication to organ donation?
questions.rationale: A donor with hepatitis B could infect the recipient. Allergies and travel history are not contraindications.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q594 (PDF p. 802)

questions.stem: Which finding shows a brain-dead organ donor is being maintained to standard?
questions.rationale: Urine output of 100 mL/hr shows good renal perfusion. A pH of 7.32 is acidosis and a 5-second refill is too slow.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q595 (PDF p. 803)

questions.stem: After aggressive cerebral edema treatment, what is the PRIORITY to keep a donor's kidneys viable?
questions.rationale: Kidneys need about 80 mm Hg perfusion pressure. Cerebral edema treatment causes fluid deficit, so volume is restored first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q596 (PDF p. 804)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What should the nurse assess about a dying client's end-of-life wishes?
questions.rationale: End-of-life assessment includes the preferred place of death, expectations for nursing care, and wishes about comfort and spiritual care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q741 (PDF p. 967)

questions.stem: A spouse says, 'I can't keep watching her die.' What is the MOST therapeutic reply?
questions.rationale: An empathetic response acknowledges the spouse's pain and suggests time for self-care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q816 (PDF p. 1050)

questions.stem: A dying client says, 'I hope I'm worthy of heaven,' and shows fear. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Assess the nature of the fear
questions.rationale: Fear ranges from mild to overwhelming, so the nurse first assesses its nature, then helps the client express it.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q849 (PDF p. 1086)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which behavior shows ANTICIPATORY grieving in a dying client?
questions.rationale: Discussing thoughts and feelings about the loss shows anticipatory grief. The others suggest dysfunctional grieving.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q900 (PDF p. 1143)

questions.stem: A dying client is angry that her family keeps hoping for a cure. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection directs the client's feelings back to validate them.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q925 (PDF p. 1169)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which statement shows a dying client has reached ACCEPTANCE?
options: 'I want my family here when I die.'
'When my kids graduate, I'll be ready.'
questions.rationale: Acceptance is often shown by plans for death and wanting loved ones near. The others are bargaining.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q948 (PDF p. 1193)

questions.stem: How can the nurse BEST help a family cope as death nears?
questions.rationale: Open, clear communication helps decision-making and coping and preserves the family's sense of control.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1015 (PDF p. 1288)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which event BEST shows a client died with dignity?
questions.rationale: The family's response gives external validation that comprehensive, quality care was given.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1021 (PDF p. 1294)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Right after a death, the family refuses to discuss funeral plans. What should the nurse do?
options: Offer time alone with the client
questions.rationale: The family is in denial, the first stage. Offering time alone supports them as they process the death.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1029 (PDF p. 1302)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which reaction by the partner of a dying client is an EXPECTED coping response?
questions.rationale: Anger is a normal response to impending loss and is often directed at God, the dying person, or caregivers.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1030 (PDF p. 1303)

questions.stem: Which question gets the MOST thorough data about a client's recent sleep?
options: 'May we talk about your sleep lately?'
questions.rationale: An open question lets the client express thoughts and feelings. The others invite one-word answers, and one night is not a pattern.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q342 (PDF p. 510)

questions.stem: A post-op client has episodes of extreme agitation. What prevents escalation?
questions.rationale: Slow speech and movement prevent escalation; sudden moves may trigger violence. Touch may be misread.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q516 (PDF p. 711)

questions.stem: A client with hyperparathyroidism says, 'This diet is too hard for me.' What is the BEST response?
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing encourages the client to express feelings and shows the message was understood.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q810 (PDF p. 1044)

questions.stem: A retiree yells in the dining room that the turkey is dry and cold. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Asking the client to come to the kitchen respects control, removes him from the room, and allows assessment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q817 (PDF p. 1051)

questions.stem: During Allen's test, a client asks, 'No one else did that!' What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Allen's test checks collateral circulation before a radial ABG; giving information is therapeutic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q819 (PDF p. 1053)

questions.stem: A client says nurses never answer his light and don't care. Which response is empathetic?
options: 'It's hard to have to ask for help.'
questions.rationale: Empathy is perceiving how the client feels and what it means to him.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q821 (PDF p. 1056)

questions.stem: Family of a client who attempted suicide are tearful. What is MOST helpful?
options: 'I'll check when you can see her.'
questions.rationale: Addressing feelings shows empathy. The others are communication blocks: wrong timing, cliché, false reassurance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q829 (PDF p. 1065)

questions.stem: A client with hives worries about her wedding next week. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection returns the client's feelings. The others minimize fears or change the focus.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q833 (PDF p. 1069)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: The night before cancer surgery, a client says, 'I'm not having surgery. I don't have cancer.' Which defense mechanism is this?
questions.rationale: Denial blocks out painful or anxiety-provoking events to protect the ego.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q916 (PDF p. 1159)

questions.stem: A client fears not waking up from anesthesia. What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: The therapeutic response encourages the client to express concerns. The others are stereotyped reassurance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q927 (PDF p. 1171)

questions.stem: A client says the doctor gave him wrong information on purpose. Which response is therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the information and exploring whether he will talk with the provider directly supports therapeutic communication.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q945 (PDF p. 1190)

questions.stem: A man burned while drunk now needs an amputation and looks upset after signing consent. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Reflection elicits deeper awareness of feelings and validates the nurse's perception.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q965 (PDF p. 1212)

questions.stem: A client scheduled for a stress test says he is nervous. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: An open-ended response explores feelings and builds trust.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q989 (PDF p. 1239)

questions.stem: A client is anxious that his infiltrated IV must be removed. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Acknowledging the anxiety and honestly saying the IV may be restarted is giving information therapeutically.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q993 (PDF p. 1243)

questions.stem: A CABG client and spouse argue after rehab. What is BEST for the nurse to say?
questions.rationale: Acknowledging feelings without inserting values or judgment keeps communication open.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1002 (PDF p. 1253)

questions.stem: A client living alone fears complications after outpatient surgery. Which response uses reflection?
questions.rationale: Reflection directs the client's feelings back. The others give false reassurance or minimize.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1007 (PDF p. 1258)

questions.stem: Which communication method is BEST for a client with an endotracheal tube?
questions.rationale: An intubated client cannot speak; a picture or word board is simplest and needs least energy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1009 (PDF p. 1260)

questions.stem: A client on home TPN says she misses eating dinner with her family. What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Clarifying and focusing help the client explore concerns about her treatment.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1010 (PDF p. 1261)

questions.stem: A daughter says, 'If this is a stroke, it's the kiss of death.' What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: Restating lets the daughter verbalize feelings and begin coping.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1019 (PDF p. 1292)

questions.stem: A partner says, 'I thought the tube the first time would make him quit drinking.' What is BEST?
options: 'You hoped this would make him stop?'
questions.rationale: Clarifying and focusing help the partner express feelings about the chronic illness.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1032 (PDF p. 1306)

questions.stem: A client wants help to live independently. Which communication action has HIGHEST priority?
questions.rationale: Active listening and noting verbal and nonverbal cues receive the intended message and build comfort.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1036 (PDF p. 1310)

questions.stem: Which question BEST assesses adjustment to a new CAD diagnosis?
options: 'How do you feel about this diagnosis?'
questions.rationale: Exploring feelings helps determine adjustment and individualize care.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1041 (PDF p. 1315)

questions.stem: A client on crutches says, 'I'll always be crippled.' What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Clarification and validation deal with the problem from the client's perspective.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1042 (PDF p. 1316)

questions.stem: Which technique encourages a paranoid client who fears poisoned food to share his fears?
questions.rationale: Open-ended questions and silence encourage descriptive discussion of feelings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1046 (PDF p. 1320)

questions.stem: A family member says ECT won't help and causes memory loss. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Seeking data about what they know helps clarify information and address concerns.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1047 (PDF p. 1321)

questions.stem: How should the nurse address an older client from an unfamiliar culture?
questions.rationale: Using the formal name shows respect to older clients of any background; personal conversation not related to care is limited at first.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1049 (PDF p. 1324)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which factor belongs in a cultural and spiritual assessment?
questions.rationale: Cultural assessment covers nutrition, communication, high-risk behaviors, health practices, family roles, and spirituality.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1052 (PDF p. 1328)

questions.stem: A woman with headache has long red welts on her back from coin rubbing. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The nurse asks about home remedies and assesses cultural health practices; coin rubbing is a traditional remedy.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1057 (PDF p. 1335)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which death practice should the nurse expect for a dying Muslim client?
questions.rationale: Muslims desire the body to face Mecca. Hindus favor cremation within 24 hours.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1058 (PDF p. 1337)

questions.stem: Which order should wait until a comatose client is intubated?
questions.rationale: Intubation must precede gastric feeding to prevent aspiration.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1273 (PDF p. 1574)

questions.stem: A client says he goes to PT, but the record shows two missed visits. Which response uses confrontation?
options: 'I see you missed the last two visits.'
questions.rationale: Confrontation presents the facts from the record to address avoidance.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1281 (PDF p. 1582)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A young adult with sarcoidosis says there's no point learning self-care since there's no cure. Which concern applies?
questions.rationale: Powerlessness is feeling no control over the situation or outcome.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1516 (PDF p. 1826)

questions.stem: A client with paralytic ileus is upset about needing an NG tube. Which response shows empathy?
questions.rationale: Empathy shares the client's frame of reference and helps express feelings.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q903 (PDF p. 1146)

questions.stem: How is an oropharyngeal airway inserted in an adult?
questions.rationale: The airway is inserted tip up and rotated down once the flange reaches the teeth, with the neck hyperextended.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1287 (PDF p. 1587)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which statement after a stress management seminar needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Confrontation is a communication technique and may increase stress; the others are stress management techniques.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1293 (PDF p. 1594)

questions.stem: An anxious client with a finger laceration has pulse 106 and BP 158/88. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Stress triggers sympathetic stimulation causing tachycardia and high BP; stress reduction helps.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q133 (PDF p. 283)

questions.stem: A client says, 'My cancer spread; I have less than 6 months.' What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: The client is likely in shock and denial; inviting ventilation of feelings is therapeutic.
questions.sourceLabel: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1008 (PDF p. 1259)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What are the phases of Peplau's interpersonal relations model?
questions.rationale: Peplau described orientation, identification, exploitation, and resolution in the therapeutic nurse-client relationship.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Theories (PDF p. 2)

questions.stem: In the communication process, the message returned by the receiver is called:
questions.rationale: Feedback is the response returned by the receiver to the sender.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Communication (PDF p. 6)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Getting married is which type of stressor?
questions.rationale: Situational stressors are unpredictable and may be positive or negative, such as marriage, divorce, or birth.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Stress (PDF p. 15)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In Selye's GAS, the 'fight or flight' release of epinephrine and cortisol occurs in which phase?
questions.rationale: In the shock phase of the alarm reaction, the ANS releases epinephrine and cortisone for fight or flight.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, General Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In which GAS stage does the body adapt and move back toward homeostasis?
questions.rationale: In resistance, the body adapts, limits the stressor, and moves back to homeostasis.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, General Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Inflammation localized to an injured finger is an example of:
questions.rationale: In LAS, a person responds to stress through a particular body part or organ.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Local Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A wife grieves for months before her ailing husband dies. This is:
questions.rationale: Anticipatory grief is experienced before the loss occurs.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Grief (PDF p. 52)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A woman cannot openly grieve a loss society disapproves of. This is:
questions.rationale: Disenfranchised grief occurs when the loss cannot be disclosed, often a socially unacceptable loss.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Grief (PDF p. 52)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Grief suppressed for a long time and expressed much later is:
questions.rationale: Delayed grief occurs when feelings are suppressed until a much later time.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Complicated Grief (PDF p. 52)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client in the denial stage acts falsely cheerful. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: In denial, the nurse supports the client verbally but does not reinforce denial.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 52)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A dying client is angry at the nurse over small matters. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: Help the client see anger as a normal response to loss; avoid withdrawal or retaliation.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 52)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In the depression stage of grief, what helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Allow sadness, communicate nonverbally by sitting quietly, and convey caring by touch.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Kubler-Ross Stages (PDF p. 53)

questions.topicName: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which is a sign of impending death from loss of muscle tone?
questions.rationale: Loss of muscle tone includes facial relaxation (sagging jaw), difficulty swallowing, and incontinence.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Impending Death (PDF p. 53)

questions.stem: A dying client's feet are cold and mottled. Which change does this reflect?
questions.rationale: Slowing circulation causes mottling, cyanosis, and cold skin starting at the feet, with a weaker pulse and lower BP.
questions.sourceLabel: TRA Nursing Module, Signs of Impending Death (PDF p. 53)
